Rust is amazing! You have a good collection of maps to play in, and a ton of servers to play those maps on. It's not too easy to make big progress, you really have to try to be successful, or you can get lucky and make friends with someone who has already made progress and they can give you a head-start. But even when you are well off you have to continuously upgrade your base to protect your loot from other people. You can also raid people with weapons that you can craft. You can penetrate doors with c-4. When building your base you want to make sure that only you and your friends can go through your door so you can put a lock on your door and give your friend a spare key, or you can make everything easier and put a code lock on your door and tell the password to your friends, but be careful because other people can hear you so just write it on a piece of paper and give it to them. Everything will be unlocked over time by leveling up and getting xp. Rust is definitely worth it most people who have had this game for a long time have hundreds of hours on this game, it's not one of those games that you spend 5 hours on, Rust lasts. The graphics are amazing, if you are about to launch the game be sure to put graphics on fantastic but only if you have a fast computer because If not it'll run in like 2fps. If you are playing on a laptop that's not specified for gaming make sure to select "fast" in the graphics options. Rust continuously gets better because "Facepunch" will not stop updating it, improving every little detail. Rust maps are huge although there is a small map called "small".

So I seem to be in the minority here, but I will give my honest review.
DISCLAIMER: I couldn't beat the final boss. That doesn't affect my review, there are plenty of games I've never beaten that I love.
Undertale isn't a good game. It is, I might even say, a bad game. It is a bad game with a cookie cutter plot, your standard low-budget "It's cool cause it's retro" graphics, and a morality system that is your standard good guy/bad guy dichotomy. It's a bit more strict than your usual game though. I accidentally did one "bad" thing in the tutorial and it made everyone in the game mad at me forever. So that's fun.
Undertale at it's core is a completely linear adventure where the standard RPG encounters are replaced with bullet hell levels. This is a concept that works just fine for a while, but at a certain point I found myself wondering why I wasn't just playing a bullet hell game if this is all there was. I then reminded myself I hated bullet hell games and soldiered on.
I won't spoil the plot for you if you don't already know it, but it isn't a particularly new concept. There's a couple of surprises, but it doesn't break any new ground. What should be the saving grace for the game is its writing, and that is where the game will either excell for you or fall completely flat. There is a pair of comic relief skeletons, some musclebound mermen, a handful of ghosts, and other "zany" characters, but they all fit into the quirky indie charcter catalogue. They all spout dialogue designed specifically to make you call your friends and tell them about the hilarious thing this character did. "I'm such a turd" indeed, small yellow thing.
Overall this is a game that relies on witty writing to hide the lack of game, and for those who have grown up with a knowledge of media tropes, the writing won't do it for you. I hate that I didn't enjoy one of the most popular games of the year, but the fact is, it just wasn't good.

Here the old review - problems are fixed due new engine/renderer/simulation!
Bought the game on first day it went Early Access on Steam and played some hours.
First patches were ok, a lot after that were utterly crap and destroyed the game.
At the moment gameplay is "okay" but not as good as it has been at the beginning.
The main problem which really holds the game back from being real fun is:
The simulation engine ( host/server ) and render engine ( client ) are attached - just like in the ArmA games.
What does that mean:
You can have an Intel 6-core with 32GB ram and a Titan X but you will still get very bad performance in cities and big cities which definitly will destroy proper gameplay and pvp.
Why is easy to explain:
The clientside is only rendering if the client is receiving data from the host/server.
If there is not enough information incoming ( packet loss, slow / bad connection, bad / slow server with heavy load ) the client has to "wait" will not render as it could do. At this time CPU and GPU switch betweenn load and idle and the fps will drop.
Thats why you get 20-30 fps and heavy stutter when looking or running into big cities like Cherno.
This is where the server gets under heavy load and can't provide enough information.
This game need a fix for that - detach of serverside and clientside!
Bohemia knows this for years but nothing happens.
This is like cycling with a triathlon bike ( client ) behind a fat guy on a citybike (server ) and no opportunity to pass him by.
You could be a lot faster but the big dude is slowing you down and you can't do anyhting about it.

The game that keeps on giving. Borderlands 2 is a loud, colourful mess of shooting, looting, idiocy and even more idiocy, and is one of the finest multiplayer experiences I know. It's made even more addictive by the extensive RPG elements.
If you have Nvidia PhysX available, you ought to enable it because Gearbox have really made use of it in Borderlands 2. Fight scenes become a cacophonous rainbow of silliness that leave you craving more every time.
They really missed a trick when it comes to weapons though. There are countless weapons in the game but they can't really be customised with scopes, suppressors or elemental effects. If you find a weapon, you can either take it or leave it. Here's hoping Borderlands 3 will address that issue and allow players to piece together the perfect loadout for their play style.
If you are looking for realism in your shooters, try elsewhere, but if all you want is NGHGHHYEAHHH then Borderlands 2 is for you.

I do ? Fine...
If you are on the fence about the price you could wait untill its on special for around $6 as there is 6 to 10 hours of content if you take your time, In practice this is one of the games that are well worth the asking price.
Graphics & Audio make me think of early console and computer games - its a good fit for the game, and should run fine on even an intergrated/onboard video chipset.
The game is not a massive download so even those with restrictive download caps should be able to get it with minimal expense and do so fairly quickly.
On the subject of gameplay - This one of the more creative games I have played recently:
You can choose to be a murderous pyschopath slaughering everything and hunting down all that try to hide from you gaining great strength in the process leading to a darker playthrough.
You can choose the path of the pacifist and win all fights using skill & strategy.
My thoughts on the matter is the pacifist route is the superior choice - a well spoken word or an act of kindness can go a long way and frankly proving your strength without violence shows how weak your opponents are. After playing for a bit you may come to see the monsters of undertale as something else.
Having read my review the questions are:
1) Why have I not purchased this yet ?
2) Are you a Man* or a Monster ?
* Woman / Human / Person / Other - you get the idea.
The expected answers to question one is: "I didn't know about this game" & "I can't afford this game".
Well you know about it now and honestly $10 is not that much compared to the big budget AAA titles with an asking price of $50+ more offen than not. Save up for a few weeks and get your parents or a friend to purchase it or one of those steam gift cards and then go ahead and buy it.
The correct answer to question 2 is: This is one you have to decide for yourself - it will make sense after playing for a bit.

"Hope and dream fill you with determination."
Why do we like playing games? Is it because we just wanna run away from reality, or be a hero in virtual world, or just need to avoid being bored? After playing undertale, maybe you’re able to answer the question: because games fill us with determination.
Western people do value personality. Their reality shows don’t sell tragic stories, but they do tell stories, just for creating personalities. There can be a cute silly little boy, a wise elder man, a warm-hearted lady, and a mean white girl in a show. Personality is the key to make audience love a person and a show. And when I started playing undertale, the strongest feeling was “what strong personalities!”. Undertale created personality for every single character or monster, and all the personalities are strong which are so memorable. I believe it’s also the main reason why it gets so many positive comments on Steam. You may see a lot of fan art pieces on Instagram and Tumblr which is really rare for an indie game. It means a lot. Strong personalities mixing with simple graphics bring an amazing chemistry. The contrast brings bigger astonishment.
After playing games for so many years, we all have got a “pattern”: kill monsters, gain exp., level up, beat boss, end. So every time we start a new game, we just try to figure out how to attack, jump, beat enemies and what skills we will get after we up the level as soon as we can. In undertale, it seems to create the same atmosphere, and there are “EXP” and “LV” too. It tells you “EXP” stands for experience, and LV represents “LOVE”, so you have to beat monsters, gain “EXP” to rise your “LOVE”. You may meet monsters anytime, and it may be a frightened dog, a sad ghost, or a narcissistic horse. You have four choices: FIGHT, ACT, ITEM, MERCY, and in ACT, you may PET, FLIRT, TALK with monster, just like other RPG games! Your choices really mean a lot in fight, however, like the classic saying gose, you have to “stay determined”, especially when you choose MERCY, you will face a number of attack until the monster gives up fighting. Of course sparing others requires determination, dosen’t it? Sure, you can choose fight as well and kill the monster, even though it’s just an overwhelmed dog, a terrified bee. Playing so many games, we already become numb and ruthless and we don’t regard it weird to kill monsters and gain experience. That’s what we want actually, isn’t it?
You have to be responsible for your choices. In undertale, a little choice will probably result in a completely different end. At the beginning, you will meet Toriel who is gentle, patient, compassionate and lovely. She makes cinnamon pie for you, calls you to check if you’re safe, arrages a room for you... But we all know that we have to keep moving forward and leave the ivory tower she builds for us. So, we’ll start the fight with her. I had no idea how to end the fight for the first time, and I tried to spare her 2 or 3 times but it didn’t work at all. So I guessed I had no option but to kill her. My heart sank deeper and deeper when I saw her HP get lower. “Am I really about to kill her?” I felt horrible but couldn’t stop it so I just kept doing it. When my HP was 2 points, I found her attack was dodging me like a real mom by no means would hurt her child. Finally, I killed her, kept moving on sadly and was thinking about starting over again. After watching some playthrough I noticed that if I had chosen mercy for 20 times, Toriel would let me go then I could move on without killing her. Ultimately, it was all because I didn’t “stay determination”. There were so many cute characters afterwards, dream boyfriend sans, silly and cute THE GREAT PAPYRUS, brave and responsible Undyne, drama queen MTT, and really helpful professor.... The developer designed exclusive lines for every single character which made them alive and vivid. Due to the fight with Toriel, I spared PAPYRUS, gave up killing Undyne. However, it was too late, after killing Toriel, I was already in a hypocritical line. No matter what I did after that, I couldn’t reach the “true end”. In the final fight with Asgore, the developer just slapped in my face again. He told me “EX” was “Execution points” instead of experience points, LOVE represented “level of violence” instead of love itself. That moment, I had to admit it was really an excellent game and started regretting to do what I had done.
Undertale is filled with irony and black humor. It makes players feel empathetic. It wrapped its simple and thin fighting mode with abundant personalities. It’s like watching a movie more than playing a game. After finishing it, players will almost love every monster and can’t wait to play it again!(spare Toriel!) Besides, the soundtrack was amazing too. It really helped us feel immersed.
Anyways,

After hearing such rave reviews for the game, I picked it up.
While the game has some charm to it, and some pretty great music, I found myself bored throughout.
I will praise the game for its novel idea on playing the game as a pacifist. You are able to battle enemies, or try to negotiate/charm/make fun of/etc them into not fighting you.
The main issue for me was that the game just wasn't interesting... Where some people will love the dialogue, I found it almost trying too hard to be funny/quirky, where everything felt done before/predictable. Something for the internet crowd of the 2010s. It's just full of video game references, and other predictable events.
While the game has some genuinely interesting moments, some intereting twists on puzzles you've seen before, and can be very touching (if you choose to kill a character, then feel remorse for your actions), overall the game just never grabbed me.
In terms of the battle system, it is just bullet hell. If you love bullet hell, then that is what your defense is based on. And again, applauding the game, each enemy will force you to react in a new and different way... To me though, it still comes off as boring.
I felt myself constantly mashing the Z key (the "OK" button) to try and progress the game. There are times where you are constantly stopped to read text, and that was the point where I just had enough. The game almost plays itself for you, and the path is extremely linear.
There have been other rpgs that I've loved (Crono trigger), even ones that are very slowly paced (pokemon), but for me I couldn't get into this game, and really gave it a try. (Got well into the fire world).
The game has very many people who love it, so maybe you will, but for me, it just was far below expectation (given that many people were calling it revolutionary, and the best thing to hit in a long time).

First off this review is very swayed by my own personal view of the game and might be vastly different than yours. At the time I have written this I have not finished the main story line yet. When I do I will update this review to it’s fullest extent.
Quick rating at the bottom
.
Positive:
Gameplay: One of the many nice things about this game is that the gameplay is done in a way that you can play at a slower pace through sniping, doing massive amounts of damage per shot or you can play it fast pace with shot guns pistols and SMG’s. One of the games huge features is the amount of guns, there are billions of guns, and how the game plays out you want to collect them all like pokemon. Other than that it flows like any other FPS game where you can drive a car and be a relatively badass murder.
Graphics: The graphics style in borderlands is one in a million, I don’t know of one other game that has been able to successfully pull this off. The graphics are able to be beautiful and funny at the same time. I’m not going to give away the style so you're either just going to have to take my word for it, or looking in up on youtube.
Story: Reminding me of Skyrim and Fallout New Vegas the story is almost post apocalyptic but also has the vast size and detail that the Skyrim story line had. It’s funny, Exciting maybe at times has too much like MMO quests (Get the stuff, kill boss, bring back) but in the end this game’s storyline will keep you on your toes with new characters and bosses to amuse you.
Running: The system requirements are fairly low, processor and ram wise, but for video cards try and have a card that can run a newer version of directx or the game won’t even boot up. I have run this game on 4 different gaming set ups, with different processors video cards and ram. So my opinion on how and what systems it will run on, is that it all comes down to the video card and ram. obviously with a better processor the loading screens will be faster, and I do recommend a fairly good one, as the lowest speed I ran the game at was a pentium dual core running at 1.8, 4 gigs of ram and a 1gig video card (thats about 3 years old) with this set up I was getting a smooth 60 frames per second at medium to high settings.
Cons: The only thing I can think of is the directX problems I had with a video card that was way out of date (only supported directX 9.5) But really this game surprised me, even though it has been out for a while I stayed away from it and headed for more MMO games. But now that I have gotten my hands on it I can safely say it’s worth the money.
Overall rating: 9.7/10

I think the game already from day one surpassed the DayZ mod, why? Simply because of customization and zombie pathing. In the mod you could find a military base, if there was no zombie there or corpses, no players were around, it was free looting and if you were fast enough you could loot and get out before spawns even happened.
In the mod this is fixed as the zombies spawn server wide regardless of player numbers in vicinity. However because of that there are also less zombies because it is heavy on the servers.
Pro's:
- Constant fear of getting killed because you loose your gear, you end up actually trying to be a survivor. At least if you are alone.
- Zombies pathing is better and you are not safe anywhere, more difficult to run away from them too.
- More random zombies in the wilderness, need to be careful when going through the forest. ( in the mod you were more or less safe in the forest unless a player pulled zombies out there somehow.)
- More loot, alot more loot to be had.
- Physics, you have physics on things you throw for example.

Remember two things about this review.
One, it's MY opinion, therefore you might disagree, that's totally fine. This review function is for people to give their honest criticism to games they like.

Borderlands 2 boasts about ''87 bajillion guns'' in reality, all that is different between each gun is bloody stats, two guns look so simillar, It's not even funny, like at all.
The writing at times is just outright stupid and boring at times. Especially Innuendo Bot 5000, what he says is just outright unfunny.
One line he says is ''Sex sex sex sex sex sex'' and I just couldn't see why people found it funny as it wasn't at all.
Some of the community are absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s who will take everything from the loot chests or hack and ruin your save. I had my 20 Gold Keys bumped up to 123 Gold Keys, had 50 Eridium bumped up to 100 Eridium and my measly $50,000 bumped up to $9,999,999 which ruined my save file and took a few hours to get rid of.
One prick decided to scream into his mic until I closed it to LAN.
Another asshat decided to steal any sort of loot, and never used it, just sold the loot rather than give it to someone who'd like to have that certain piece of loot.
But some community members are the nicest people out there. One was not so good at the game but it was because his little brother was playing and he was teaching his little brother. Another always asked if we needed anything or was looking for any weapon type in the loot boxes so he would save that weapon for them if he found it (He would say ''Would you like me to search for Sniper, Rocket, Shotgun, Assualt Rifle, SMG or anything in particular?'')
And another would always ask to help with any side quests.
The story took me a solid 30-35 hours, the Warrior boss battle sucked, took me 16 rockets to kill and took me 3 minutes! 3 MINUTES!? Metal Gear Rising's Final Boss was 40 minutes long, Persona 3's boss was 40 minute's long. Deus Ex Human Revolution's Boss Battles took 20-ish minutes long as you would keep attempting as you could die easily.
The fact that they used memes as ''comedy'' is just ew to me. It's not funny, most memes are too old to be funny and the most the game as a whole got from me was a bloody smile.
The fact that Tiny Tina was literally only made to give the writer, Anthony Burch's sister a Voice Acting gig hurt like salt in a wound as Tiny Tina was one of the most creative characters I've seen in a game and one of my favourites altogether
The only boss I had issue with was Terramorphus, which I decided to attempt to kill at level 39 (I was level 38 when I beat the game) and the main reason I died was because he just swung his feeler once and killed me with one hit. I didn't care that my rocket launcher took only 2-3% of his health, I cared about the fact that I died in one hit.

Ingredients:
1) 2 cups Flour
2) 1/2 cup Sugar
3) 1/4 teaspoon Salt
4) 2 sticks (1 Cup) Salted Butter, Cut Into Small Cubes
5) Filling
6) 1-1/2 cup Sugar
7) 1/4 cup Flour
8) 4 whole Large Eggs
9) Zest And Juice Of 4 Medium-sized Lemons
10) Powdered Sugar, For Sifting
Directions:
1. For the crust: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Grease a 9-by-13-inch pan with butter.
2. Stir together the flour, sugar, and salt. Add the butter to the bowl and use a pastry cutter to cut it all together until the mixture resembles fine crumbs. Press into the prepared pan and bake until golden around the edges, about 20 minutes.
3. For the filling: Stir together the sugar and flour. Crack in the eggs and whisk to combine. Add the lemon zest and juice and mix until combined. Pour over the crust and bake about 20 minutes.
4. Allow to cool in the fridge for a minimum of 2 hours, then sift powdered sugar over the top before cutting into squares.
(Use an 8 x 10 pan if you'd like the layers to be a little thicker.)

So this is my third iteration of this review on 11/16/2017. Since I have heavily been into Rust again I figure I may as well give a new update.
This game is not for everyone. I know this because I have introduced a lot of friends to the game and they have all stopped playing almost immediately. It is high stress, you will lose a lot if not everything constantly. Like any job (which this game feels like at times) you will need to take lots of lumps to grow. Once you get past the lumps (after say about 200-300 hours worth of lumps, gulp) you should be fine. You will find friends whom have suffered the same abuse as you all equally as♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off looking to raid the♥♥♥♥♥♥talking squeakers off the server.
I have over a thousand hours in the game and some of the best people I've ever played with in video games I've met playing Rust. While most of the time it feels like a grind, some of the moments in Rust are well worth it. Online raiding someone (which happens few and far in between) generates some of the most adrenaline in any game I've ever played. Fending off counter raiders while simultaneously shooting the people you're raiding is an experience and a half. Some people get that same kind of high when they offline and finally reach that precious loot room, and some people groan when they realize they wasted 20 rockets to find a crate full of Improvised Balaclavas. Either way, there is some way you will have an enjoyable moment in this game.
I've played a few survival games, obviously not to the degree of Rust, but they all don't feel as polished or open as Rust does. Using the ALT key to look left or right certainly helps with your increased paranoia, and is a feature I wish were implemented in every video game. To me that is one major defining feature of Rust that separates it from other genres. Not to mention the flexibility you have in creating your bases. There's rugs, bear rugs included, lamps, chairs, pretty much a ton of things if you're into the whole role playing thing. A few things like box placement and other items needs a bit cleaned up but otherwise they've made it way more intuitive to build lately.
Now despite the mostly positive review, there are drawbacks. For one, weapon mechanics have definitely taken a step backwards. About six months ago they decided to start reworking weapon mechanics. Rust was definitely one of the more challenging games to get aiming right, but I felt after about 3-5 months I got it right. I mastered the semi auto and slaying smaller zergs was one of my favorite reasons for playing the game. However, they ditched this system in favor of a more noob, spray and pray friendly system. Instead of being that guy who could control his AK and knock people off easily from 100M or more, you'll now get randomly headshot by someone who has no idea what they're doing from the same distance 5 shot bursting. Pistols have way too much recoil now (the P2 is almost useless now) and well..just make it a point to get an AK. Almost every other gun outside of the LR and Bolt aren't really going to top an AK.  I'm definitely disappointed in the direction they've went with guns to the point where I PVP significantly less, but it's not enough to cause me to stop playing the game. With that being said, I hope they at least make it a little harder for those guys that hold mouse 1 and get instaheadshots in the future.
The pacing is also slowed down drastically with the revitalization of the BP system. Unless you are playing on a server that rarely wipes BPs (or never does) prepare to grind hard to find components. This can be seen as a good thing for about...the first 2 wipes. Then that large clan will have every BP while you probably have about 1/5th. So for 3 weeks they essentially just have to farm and find components to completely wipe everything out. And if you play on a server that wipes BPs fairly frequently...well. You're going to be grinding and finding BPs a lot. There really isn't a big advantage for either, but for me, I prefer the monthly BP wipes so you can at least have a couple wipes of having quick startups, even if you have to prepare your♥♥♥♥♥for an offline beating.
Anyways, while this game certainly can be really stressful at times, I would recommend it for anyone wanting to get into something new and different. I have thousands of hours in Counter Strike among others and was looking for a change of pace when I was introduced to Rust. Since then it has been my primary game. I absolutely recommend starting off in an empty-ish server where you can learn to build bases and farm components free of worry. Then move to 20-30 people servers or solo-duo-trio servers eventually till you get good enough (or find enough friends) to play on the big boy servers.
All in all, if this game is too hard or you think it sucks, you're probably just a beta male ♥♥♥♥♥ anyways.

I knew I was going to like Undertale - the creator's history with creating mods for my favorite game of all time, the SNES RPG Earthbound, was enough for me to be confident - and I wasn't disappointed, even though I played it after all of the hype, after it had made its way onto so many reviewers' best games of the year lists, and after the fandom had reached that critical mass where it became difficult for some people to actually see the game itself, separate from the way its fans had taken to it.
I can't say that everyone would like this game, because there are many ways in which the game could be measured as being not-good. The graphics are obviously simple, the puzzles are lackluster, and the main combat mechanic is perhaps just okay. For some people, those are the things that make up games, so if this game isn't great in those areas, how can it be a great game?
For me, this game manages to be about games in a way that is incredibly sophisticated and self-aware, while also managing to tell an incredibly meaningful and heartfelt story. It's acutally about a lot of things, and managing to have more important things to say than the vast majority of other games I've ever played. It's not just entertainment, though I did have fun playing it. I think it's worth trying, for most people, even though you may not find anything there for you. I certainly did, and it seems like a lot of other people found a lot of things, too.

I will start this off honestly with saying it hurts to place a negative on this, but there are to many issues to actually give it a positive. I really hope I can change this to a thumbs-up someday...
Don't like reading? Skip to the bottom...
Lets start with an overview. You spawn in after a long loading time. Chances are you should go eat or read or something while waiting, it will be a bit. Maybe not if you have an SSD though. You spawn in, and depending on the server either die instantly by camping snipers or run off. I suggest starting on a low population server. You will gather resources, build a house, and log off. You will get on and you got killed by a bear, in your house. While players have collision they can't get it to work with animals using the Unity game engine, so it will liekly never be fixed. If you are on a low population server you will likely do well even solo. But lets stop talking about low population servers, and focus on medium to large population servers.
Don't try to solo on these, you will fail. Not of any fault of yours, but because of that clan of 10+ players over there that just want to kill you. Why? Just to kill you even though you have nothing. So, two problems here- Toxic players, in toxic clans. Some might say its ironic because I tend to lead a large clan on the network I play on. Thing is is that we did not run around killing anything or anyone for any reason, we tried to keep toxic people off and thats it. Hence why we disband- To many people WANT to do what I just said. So don't solo, geta few friends.
The entire idea of surviving really does not hold anymore. Its really gather, kill players. Food/water is only really a first couple hours issue. There simply is not enough to make surviving rough. No massive storms you need to stay out of (Please don't add this facepunch already normal rain kills the serverwide fps). There are no NPCs to worry about unless that servers staff did alot of work and used a few plugins, and even then it is decent, not amazingly game changing. You only need to worry about one thing- other players.
"Create alliances with other players and form a town" No, just don't. This is NOT HOW THE GAME WORKS. AT least, not anymore. But I already have talked about that enough, lets go on to how it runs.
Graphics are amazing, to say the least. They have updated alot of outdated graphics and it honestly looks good. But here is the issue. Better graphics means more demending. This is a major issue with how the game is right now. 16GB of RAM is not much an issue, I just have 8GB and it never comes close to using all of that. Processor then? Again not an issue for the game, 3GHz is quite resonable. DirectX 12? It says recommeneded but you don't need that at all, the DX12 version is under "experimental" in an early access game. So what is the issue spec wise with the game? GTX 980. Yeah, you need one of those to meet recommended. Most people are not going to have that, alot of people don't even have a 900 series card or an AMD card equal to that. I have a special edition of the GTX 950. It runs the game great, almost any other player I talk to has a older card than mine and they get the same performance ingame. So honestly, I really don't think a 980 is needed. I get over 80 fps if I just am running Rust. So hardware is not an issue with the game. Its optimization and other things. Your game will run fine, you could be just standing there and the only person in the server, and then suddenly your fps drops to 5. Why? No reason. You are just standing there and have been maybe for 10 minutes. But you just got hit with a common and massive issue- the huge lag spikes. And it has no gotten better, it has gotten far FAR worse. I just upgraded my PC. Went froma  quad core at 2.3GHz to a Hexa Core at 3.5GHz, that is a massive increase. Went from DDR2 to DDR3. Before these upgrades I could already play on max graphics. I upgarded and it was amazing. But then the game got an update, and another, etc. Even though most the updates just added some small things it got worse and worse. I am from 80 fps max graphics and rarely getting a lag spike, crashing, freezing, etc to getting 45 fps on Mid-graphics and massive lag spikes dropping me down to 5 fps. Not only that, but it freezes and crashes constantly. On no other game do I have this issue. They need to stop releasing more content and overhauls on grphics and focus on fixing what they are breaking.

Do you have anger management issues? Do you often feel you are being treated unfairly? If so, I recommend Rust. You'll have a chance for growth to achieve a stoic, zen-like state where you are able to endure any frustration or setback any video game can throw at you. On the other hand, there's also a good possibility you'll achieve a total meltdown and a ride to a mental asylum, where you are given a 2x2 room of your own with padded walls, floor and ceiling. But hey, at least it's unraidable.
For an Early Access game, I think this one is surpringly mature and playable with quite interesting gathering, hunting, crafting and building mechanics and character progression. It's the so called community that makes the game unbearable for many. I say so called community, because outside co-operating groups a.k.a. clans there really is very little community. Well, that's not entirely fair as there are always players that will help you in in-game chat if you have questions about anything related to the game.
However, there is next to no community to be found in a sense that you would be likely to run into friendly neighbours and start working together. 90% of the time you'll be shot or swinged at on sight. Even of those 10% presenting themselves as friendly, 90% will eventually stab you in the back. People will not hesitate to shoot you dead with their firearms when all you have is your bare ♥♥♥, a rock and a torch. Just because they can. For some reason this game seems to bring out the worst out of people and make most of them turn into virtual bullies, always ready to prey on the weaker.
Then there are the clans I mentioned earlier that can be even 50+ players strong. In fact lone players and small groups are such underdogs to them no matter what they do, that I wouldn't be surprised to see this game go somewhere in a direction of certain number of tribes on a server, amongst which the players joining would be distributed evenly.
However, if you're able to keep in mind it's only a game, there's still plenty of fun to be had. Just remember anything you manage to gather, craft or build is only temporarily yours. It will be raided and pillaged, it's just a matter of when. As a game Rust is good if not excellent, especially given it's Early Access state. As an MP experience, depends on not only your server choice but also a lot on your own ability to tolerate losing everything over and over again, with you being able to do little or nothing about it.

TL;DR - unless you have endless free time to burn, the arduous cycle of grinding for materials only to have everything stolen/ destroyed so that you have to start entirely from scratch will get tiresome pretty quickly. Do not buy this game.
I know that saying this is going to make it sound like I'm slating the game because I'm bad at it, but this thing is way too frustrating to play to be worth buying. It works, all the mechanics are fine, there's not game breaking glitches or anything like that, and the anti-cheat is really good, so there's barely any hackers (I never saw any).
The problem is the playerbase. The whole game revolves around the player building up a base and collecting resources to upgrade weapons, armour, and building materials. It takes time and effort to get anywhere meaningful, and once you've got a base you're proud of, it feels like you've actually accomplished something. Unfortunately, there will always be someone with more time to devote to the game who can raid your base and steal everything you've worked at.
That alone would be fine - its a survival game, after all. What makes Rust such a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥♥is that no-one ever passes up the opportunity to totally ruin your experience. People won't just steal your stuff, they'll plant barricades in front of all the doors and change all the locks. They'll see you peacefully wandering the map, collecting wood or stone, and instantly kill you. They'll break down your walls and destroy your spawn point so that you can't even easily get back to your base to start over.
I know that a lot of people are going to disagree with this: "but player brutality is what adds challenge to the game", or "stop whining and just get on with it". Fine. But this review isn't for you, it's for other people, like me, who underestimated going in the amount of time this game requires you to invest to feel rewarded, and how easily all of that investment could be totally wiped out. I know that video games aren't massively productive uses of time anyway, but this game really hammers that home. I've got 30 hours on record with this game, and whereas that amount of time in, say, Fallout or Payday 2 would net me a pretty well equipped character, a decent settlement, or piles of cash, all I have in Rust is a naked guy holding a rock and a torch.
If you value your time, the feeling of accomplishment, or even just your ability to trust other human beings, do not play this game.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding lemon bars recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1) 2 cups Flour
2) 1/2 cup Sugar
3) 1/4 teaspoon Salt
4) 2 sticks (1 Cup) Salted Butter, Cut Into Small Cubes
5) Filling
6) 1-1/2 cup Sugar
7) 1/4 cup Flour
8) 4 whole Large Eggs
9) Zest And Juice Of 4 Medium-sized Lemons
10) Powdered Sugar, For Sifting
Directions:
1. For the crust: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Grease a 9-by-13-inch pan with butter.
2. Stir together the flour, sugar, and salt. Add the butter to the bowl and use a pastry cutter to cut it all together until the mixture resembles fine crumbs. Press into the prepared pan and bake until golden around the edges, about 20 minutes.
3. For the filling: Stir together the sugar and flour. Crack in the eggs and whisk to combine. Add the lemon zest and juice and mix until combined. Pour over the crust and bake about 20 minutes.
4. Allow to cool in the fridge for a minimum of 2 hours, then sift powdered sugar over the top before cutting into squares.
(Use an 8 x 10 pan if you'd like the layers to be a little thicker.)

Eh, need a little more than that? Well, fine! I just wanted to give you the chance to jump straight into the game without having any of the plot spoiled or any advanced knowledge of the gameplay. It truly is a game best played without any pretense. Such a feat is likely difficult to accomplish, however, seeing as if you've heard of the game, someone has likely already extolled its virtues and quirks. The game seems to have received quite a bit of critical acclaim and people are already talking about it, let's playing it and singing its praises from the mountaintops. However, I truly believe it is the kind of game that should just be experienced straight, without pretense or proxy. A Let's Play would ruin the intimacy of the game. A walkthrough would destroy reveals and suspense. In fact, even a review might dull the edge of the Undertale experience. However, I like this game so much that I still want to talk about it. I'll try my best to withhold anything too telling, but consider this entire paragraph a strong suggestion that if you ever feel like you should stop reading and just play it, then do so.
Undertale is a role-playing game that is inspired by the Earthbound/Mother series, a series with quite the cult following. In fact, this is not the first time someone has attempted to pay homage the strange charm of Shigesato Itoi's off-beat RPGs, however in my opinion it hasn't been properly done until now. Undertale manages to incorporate the spirit of Mother while retaining its own identity—one of a game that breaks a lot of rules and utilizes humor to distract you from the world it is building as you go. Also unique are the game mechanics that make up the puzzles and battles, making you re-think how you approach an RPG.
In Undertale, you play a young human child (whose gender is never revealed or deemed relevant) who has found themselves lost in a strange underground ruins. Greeted by some curious characters, you will discover the basic controls of the game, as well as how to approach the monsters that approach you throughout your journey. One of most obvious places where this game departs from a more direct RPG lies in the combat system. In it, you have the option to “FIGHT” offensively, “ACT” according to the situation, use an “ITEM”, or show “MERCY”. While fighting and items are fairly self-explanatory, acting can range from checking a monster to flirting with them. Mercy gives you the chance to run away or, if certain conditions are met, spare an enemy that doesn't feel like fighting anymore. If you spare an enemy, you won't get any experience, but you will get gold. How you go about your actions will affect how your game progresses.
And when I say that your actions affect the game, I mean ALL OF THEM. Okay, perhaps not every single action you make, but Undertale is programmed to account for many different decisions you make, even those that one considers to take place outside the game. I don't want to elaborate too much here, but to try to put it more clearly Undertale keeps track of not just the decisions your character makes but those you make as well. Think twice before making even the simplest of moves. ...or don't! Honestly, the hidden complexity of Undertale doesn't necessarily punish you. It simply allows you to play through the game differently. The story may grow happier or bleaker or somewhere in between , but you can still progress to a definite end without quite knowing what the next screen will provide.
Returning to the subject of battles, there is more to it than just fight or flight. When being attacked, you have the ability to evade attacks. A box appears with a heart, representing your character, that features the enemy's attack. You must navigate the heart around to dodge the projectiles that will cause damage. These attacks become more variant and complex as the game goes on, with new gimmicks being introduced to keep them fresh, while keeping in line with the monster who is producing them.
Finally there's the writing of Undertale. I don't plan on going into plot, but I can't finish a review of this game without going into its sense of humor. Undertale's characters are bright, interesting, and, more often than not, funny. The ways in which their personalities are interlinked with decisions you make in the game keep you engaged with the dialogue and give a genuine feeling of warmth as you get to know them.
That isn't to say, of course, that Undertale is nothing but situation comedy and puns. The game provides plenty of opportunities to explore the more serious side of the world below, expanding on the history between humans and monsters and what path they may find themselves on in the near future.
Everything isn't perfect, of course. There are times when the game's humor feels like it panders too much to specific internet communities or fandoms that can leave outsiders bewildered or rolling their eyes. I think that in-jokes definitely have a place in mass media, but there needs to be a very polished delivery for them to go over well without alienating some of the audience. Mostly, Undertale avoids this problem, but there are a few places that made me lightly groan.
I could easily go on all day about Undertale (and perhaps someday I will!) but for now I just wanted to touch on some of the broader concepts and components of the game. Undertale is an indie gem that I think will be remembered for some time, perhaps even with the same dedication as Earthbound/Mother has garnered over time. Okay, maybe there will never be a piece-by-piece analysis of the nuances of its translation and cultural relevance
, but the game's uniqueness and heart will win over all kinds of fans for sure. I will end by reiterating that you should really go into Undertale with as little information as possible. Don't look things up, don't try to find reviews, don't follow people's live tweet reactions... Get just enough to pique your interest and then dive in to discover your own personal Undertale.

I won't lie, Undertale's a great game. What I'm about to say has nothing to do with the game, and only the fanbase. If you have any shred of dignity, don't even glance at the fanbase. It's not worth it.
The main issue I have with it are its fanbase and how they talk about the game. They talk like the game is the best game that has ever been made, and that you're not a true fan of the game if you're not in the fandom (I hate that god-forsaken word.)
Another issue is how the fanbase is dealt with. Rust is a brutal world without mercy. The game has an amazing developpers team that push out weelky updates, monthly huge updates and communicate with the playerbase on Reddit. It has a complex building system that takes time to master perfectly. You will have adrenaline rush during PvP, you will rage when you die. You will also experience the ultime high when you outplay someone during a fight and loot their full inventory.
Rust due to certain decisions from the developpers is pushing towards mass-groups and zerging unfortunately. It used to be small crews of people playing,now you have large groups (clans) on pretty much any populated servers which rolls over the weaker playerbase without any confrontation because we simply can't defend against groups of 8 zerging you without any skills.
Recent graphic overhaul is a success, Rust is even more beautiful and alot more stable on medium-spec machines. The XP system was a try & miss, BP system was superior and will be brought back with a different more refined system from what we know.
Rust is not for casual players, not in its current state. After over 1200 hours played, best 20$ investment of my life for a video game. I just wished the game design wasn't pushing towards more groups and zerging because Rust is losing its true core gameplay.

TL;DR - unless you have endless free time to burn, the arduous cycle of grinding for materials only to have everything stolen/ destroyed so that you have to start entirely from scratch will get tiresome pretty quickly. Do not buy this game.
I know that saying this is going to make it sound like I'm slating the game because I'm bad at it, but this thing is way too frustrating to play to be worth buying. It works, all the mechanics are fine, there's not game breaking glitches or anything like that, and the anti-cheat is really good, so there's barely any hackers (I never saw any).
The problem is the playerbase. The whole game revolves around the player building up a base and collecting resources to upgrade weapons, armour, and building materials. It takes time and effort to get anywhere meaningful, and once you've got a base you're proud of, it feels like you've actually accomplished something. Unfortunately, there will always be someone with more time to devote to the game who can raid your base and steal everything you've worked at.
That alone would be fine - its a survival game, after all. What makes Rust such a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥♥is that no-one ever passes up the opportunity to totally ruin your experience. People won't just steal your stuff, they'll plant barricades in front of all the doors and change all the locks. They'll see you peacefully wandering the map, collecting wood or stone, and instantly kill you. They'll break down your walls and destroy your spawn point so that you can't even easily get back to your base to start over.
I know that a lot of people are going to disagree with this: "but player brutality is what adds challenge to the game", or "stop whining and just get on with it". Fine. But this review isn't for you, it's for other people, like me, who underestimated going in the amount of time this game requires you to invest to feel rewarded, and how easily all of that investment could be totally wiped out. I know that video games aren't massively productive uses of time anyway, but this game really hammers that home. I've got 30 hours on record with this game, and whereas that amount of time in, say, Fallout or Payday 2 would net me a pretty well equipped character, a decent settlement, or piles of cash, all I have in Rust is a naked guy holding a rock and a torch.
If you value your time, the feeling of accomplishment, or even just your ability to trust other human beings, do not play this game.

Undertale. A game I will never regret to play. NEVER. EVER.
When I first saw the trailer of this game, I expected it to be some random 8-bit game. I couldn't understand why everyone would hype this game, since the graphics are outdated. Until I downloaded it. I was instantly filled with determination!
This game has an unique battle system; every battle is different and unique at the same time. In other RPGs, you would just button smash your ♥♥♥♥ing gamepad, because you already faced that opponent a dozen times. But not in Undertale.
Every opponent has its own battle style. Your "weapon" is your SOUL, a red heart, representing your life. You can either choose to FIGHT an opponent or ACT, which includes things from simple talking to hugging an aeroplane. Because why wouldn't you wanna hug a freaking aeroplane? Not feeling up to it? That's okay, because this game's humor and puns will  leave a smile on your face as you  explore the underground. You can choose on your own whether you show some MERCY and decide to spare your monster opponents, or you just walk around killing everything and everyone who stands in your way.
Tl;dr: This game has a positive and a negative ending. Choose on your own! It's FIGHT or MERCY!
Lots of beautiful and kind characters will cross your way. You have the chance to date a skeleton, take cooking class with a fish, listen to ghost music, pet dogs and much more is waiting for you.
I highly recommend this game as it's simple designed, shares two/three endings to choose from and comes with a horde of characters helping you to feel more comfortable in the monster's world. Or not, depending on the path you decided to take. No matter which one you will take, after you finish the game, it will leave an impression in your mind. And who knows, you might have a different point of view when you kill something in your next RPG, who knows.

Rust is a survival game from the guys at Facepunch and it's the best survival game out there. I started playing back in Legacy and recently came back to see how much has changed (just yesterday they overhauled the graphics again and I love the possibility to get food and cloth from cacti now) I've played for like 100 hours overall which is very little when thinking that I've been coming back to this game again and again for like 3 years.
As a solo player I am doomed to failing over and over again since every populated server is dominated by clans that have like 20 members and ten of them online at all hours. This is the reason why I kinda rage quit every time after a few days of playing. Not surviving is infuriating and makes the game tedious but that's what makes the game difficult enough to keep me coming back. So kind of mixed feelings here. There should be somekind of incentive for playing solo to balance things but in a game like this the groups are always going to prevail 'cause even if you'd somehow lvl up faster than everyone else in the game, even if you'd have an armor and an AK47 and everyone else was running around naked with bows and arrows you just can't outfarm them in resources and you just can't kill them all if they attack.
Also, starting the game is hard 'cause no-one really cares if you just spawned. They're going to kill you. And if you manage to evade those little♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ you'll never hear someone creeping up from behind when you're gathering resourses or you'll just run into a bear which you can't outrun and which you can't really kill safely without a ranged weapon. And that means you're dead again.
So make no assumptions that you'll be better of because of your extensive background as a pro FPS player. Your MLG 360 no-scope skills only matter after you've amassed enough wealth to be the target of every other player out there.
Now after reading this you might wonder why the **** is this guy recommending the game. Well, Those things I've said before are just the reason why I play this game. I don't play the game to be the biggest and baddest out there. I play the game to see if this time I can do better than the last time. If this time I manage to get to the point again that I can realistically start raiding and robbing in the dankness of the night, if this time I'd actually succeed in building a defendable fort.
I'd play the game more if there would be more cooperation, I would love to live in a kind of a village with other players. Not as a part of an organized clan of raiders 'cause I don't give a♥♥♥♥♥♥about the contents of other peoples loot rooms. we'd retaliate if we'd be attacked but otherwise live peacefully in the center of the map surrounded by raiders, thieves and highwaymen ....Oh and the bears!
'Cause that's how it would be balanced. Raiders would need to be smaller, independent groups living in the forests and the more peaceful players would need to unite to withstand the danger lurking out there.

Ok you know what, here is a full review.
My sister bought me this game and urged me to play it, to be honest I quite frankly don't get the hype over this game and why it is so popular. To me it is just another one of those artistic pretentious indie games.
Boy was I dead wrong.
I recently finished it and I'm totally in love with this game and I will tell you why:
Let's start with the cons:
- MS Paint graphics (It is not a con for me, I don't care about graphics but maybe to others that can be a turn off.)
- Short game
- Annoying dog (JK I love you Toby)
- Expensive food items
- A spider will kill you if you don't buy said expensive food items
- There is something in my eye
Okay now with the pros:
- Beautiful storyline and writing
- Deep and meaningful plot
- It features one of the best soundtracks from the composer of Homestuck (Never read Homestuck, never will but goddamn I can't stop listening to their songs.)
- Puns and dad jokes
- Rich and 3-dimensional characters that you will love
- Bullet hell gameplay
- Your actions will impact the story in a HUGE way
- Beautiful pixel design and animation
- You will feel you're gonna have a good/bad time
This game has a message and I won't spoil that message for you but your actions will have consequences in the game unlike any other game, it deconstructs and parodies the RPG genre in a number of ways. If you like a good soundtrack, well-written characters and a very unique plot than you will love this game. Please, give it a try.
Thanks Toby.

Oooooh.
Can I just say how much do I love this game?
I went in completely blind and...just...
WOW. Everything that happened is just...wow. I didn't know that I could grew up on a game so much.
I would like to say that it's better to experience this game by yourself. Because it affects you in a personal kind of way, makes you question your intents, your morality. You can't pick it up from watching LPs.
The soundtrack is amazing. I really adds to the experince.
The game design - that being good to others makes you feel better, and being good or bad is literally YOUR choice, not the game's - is freaking brilliant. And also brilliantly executed. Characters, music, simple graphics, gameplay, all those little details - everything is placed right, and is top-notch. If it wouldn't, believe me, this game wouldn't be so popular.
Plus, there are many moments in the game that will make you genuinely smile, or laugh. Undertale is hilarious, and is a great experience overall.
Genocide run is was a great experience too. No, I'm not a trying-to-look-edgy, love-to-kill person, I'm just saying that Genocide run really made me feel like a villain. In many games, killing is a very natural thing; you don't feel really bad about about it. But in Undertale, you could see consequences of your choice - the whole atmosphere turns dark, music changes, towns are empty and you're the fault; the fight against Genocide final boss is pure gold. I was feeling like a serial killer, I was obsessed with the idea of killing him, I heard every word he said, but that wasn't enough because I went completely insane without even knowing it. It took me three days to beat him, and every day I went to bed thinking of how I'm gonna get him tomorrow.
This fight felt like a deadly date. Just two of us dancing at the end of the world.
Pretty insane, huh? No game made me feel that way before.
I honestly want to erase my memory just to experience Undertale again.

Lets just start the off with rust is not a game for the weak.
Rust is one of the best games that ive played to this date on steam. I love how every kill in the game is very rewarding because it provides you with resources that you would rather have to farm yourself, but on the other hand you could be farming for a long time and just get killed in seconds. Another issue that you can run into playing this game is groups known as Zergs. What these are, are Clans or groups containing of 4+ ganging up on one or two players. This leads to the zergs being able to surround the solo or duo players leading them to lose their gear unless they find away to kill the zerg group. Pvp in this game needs alot of work but its not bad. 1 on 1 fights come down to skill if you're using a bow or a cross bow. You have tp land 3-4 shots to down a naked and sometimes the fights last minutes or even seconds if you land a head shot, but with guns this is where I feel like pvp isnt the best currently. Because of the XP system right now you have to be level 20+ to even craft low tier guns. This means that the clans can abuse XP share to level up fast and be able to craft guns that solo players will not be able to. This means that as a solo player if your base is being raided or you're farming you will have to fight of zergs with guns and armor with only a bow or crossbow. Another point where the game shines in the light is the building aspect. You can build anything that you put your mind to in this game. You can make exhilarating building that will look amazing, but will also defend the raiders and make it hard for them to locate the TC and the loot. The last point I want to make is raiding. Today on 8/31/2016 raiding isnt the best. You have to offline raid most of the time to get the loot you want. If the the you're raiding is online then they can repair/defend the loot and even despawn the loot when they hear C4 or rockets going off. My only tip for Rust to make raiding easier is to make loot take a long time like 10 mins to depawnn. Over all I rate this game a 9.5/10 and its the only game I play other than overwatch. Would reccomend to anyone looking to play a PVE and PVP game. Just know it will take some hours of your life to start up on a server :D!

Pros:
1. Unforgiving. At one point you can be the king of the server and the next thing you notice you have nothing at all. It's like dark souls, but it's not souls you are losing. You can lose ALL your progress.
2. Addictive and rewarding gameplay. Farming, building, raiding, roaming. Choose your style.
3. The gunplay is satisfying and the primitive weapons don't lose their purpose after you reach "lategame"
4. You can enjoy the game both in solo and with friends. For a true roguelike experience, go solo.
5. Active developers. Bi-weekly update with the devs actually listening to the playerbase.
Cons:
1. The game is a memory hog and you might find yourself in trouble with even 8gb and less RAM. Atleast this was the case for me and I ended up upgrading to 16gb wich somewhat made it better.
2. Overall performance isn't that shabby. The graphics are not so well optimized, but it's an alpha so I'm sure these things will be fixed in the final product.
3. Loading times might be frustrating if you are not the most patient of people.
4. Big groups and clans dominate the servers. There is power in numbers and you might find it frustrating trying to advance if you're going solo or with a small group.
5. Animals are very glitchy, might teleport inside your base and may cause you an untimely death. Watch out for those bears!
Overall: If you are looking for a roguelike fps exeprience, this is it. The unforgivingness is a huge thrill. Best enjoyed with a group of friends, but solo is also viable.
Recommended and stay safe!

I just wanted to update my review for this game. I gave it a thumbsdown when it was first released, once again, I give it yet another thumbsdown. So, after two years, the game is still in Alpha. It's literally one guy working on it, anyway, so I don't expect him to rush it and release the full version fast. With that being said, there's still A LOT of bugs in the game. Bears and wolves glitching through walls and floors, rifles bugging out with reloads, I've even had it where I would be crafting something with an open inventory and the item never came to be AND I lost my mats doing it (it has only happened once so far).
The optimization for the game is poor, but again, take into mind there's only one developer, so it's nothing against him, it's more along the lines of because of a limited amount of resources, he can't push the game out fast enough, nor can he fix all the bugs in the game right away. After all, it's still Alpha.
Another thing I dislike are the servers. A mass majority of them wipe within 2 weeks to a single months time. The reason for this is due to clutter, AND some players are so high of a level and well established that it makes being a new player, or fresh character, almost impossible to move up, or at least take a lot longer. Some servers only wipe the map and everything you own and build, but leave XP. Some servers wipe everything. None-the-less, it's a good and also a bad thing. It's good that it makes you on even levels every few weeks, but the bad part is it makes you feel unaccomplished. Don't get me wrong, you could always get a private server and build to your hearts desire, but from my understanding is that most Rust Server Hosts require a wipe so their servers aren't cluttered.
Now, the typical game itself starts off fun; however, once you get higher level (about mid-20's and up), the game is ridiculously easy and that's including when you're PVP'ing or just doing PVE stuff. There's literally nothing challenging or exciting that happens. By the time you're level 25, majority of the time, you can build an amazing base and can make some of the top tier gear, weapons, and items. Once you're fully equipped and well armed, PVP is really, really easy. There have been servers where I be able to take out large groups of players with just a scoped Bolt Action and HV and Inc rounds. Or just fire rockets into a swarm of people. Or watch clans fight it out, hide in a mountain side, and blow rockets into the middle of all of it and go down and loot everyone after they're dead. Easy stuff. A little too easy.
One thing I've also encountered that is a pet peeve of mine is that a large amount of the servers I've been in have no problems with killing a fresh character. Personally, I always felt bad for 'em and I try to help, if I'm already established on these particular servers; however, majority of time from experience and from witnessing other players, is you could have a rock and be gathering, and some level 30+ would come around and gun them down. Rinse and repeat. To me, that's just ill taste in gameplay and a large percent of the servers I've been on do this frequently, so people who are new to Rust tend to get a bad taste for it.
I know people are complaining about the new XP system, comparing it to the old way Rust used to be upon release. Personally, I like the new XP system. I feel like it makes you strive for leveling, but there are people and entire clans that power level with each other and that's where it breaks the game. Within a day, I've seen a clan get to level 20 while most solo players were still around level 10.
When the game first launched, it was fun, but got boring fast. I hopped servers all over the place. Even got my own for a short time. The game is very repetitive and to be frank, gets dull real fast. So if you're looking for a cheap way to have a short amount of fun and like survival games, by all means, buy Rust. You'll have a blast. For those of us who wanted more, don't bother. Just wait 'till the game fully releases (as stated, it's still in Alpha).
In the end, Rust is still a better game than No Man's Sky and still a better game than anything Valve has released within the past 5 years.

I wish I could list the pros and cons of Undertale, but I really don't have any complains about this game. It is a unique experience and I would recommend this game to everyone. With that being said, these are the strongest points of Undertale:
-Memorable characters: I have played many games in my life, but after completing them and after some time, I will tend to forget the characters and their names. For Undertale it is completely different, I can see myself remembering the characters and their personalities for a long time since I feel emotionally attached to them.
-Replayability value: Everyone will have a different experience with this game based on his/her decisions within the game and dialogue selection. This games has so many different secrets, options and dialogues that you can replay this game countless of times and learn something new on each run.
-Music: THIS is the best part of Undertale in my opinion. The music is AMAZING!! I can place the soundtrack of Undertale along with the soundtrack of Ocarina of Time and Final Fantasy VII as my favorite soundtracks ever. And it´s not only good, but every song fits the situation and the character that tries to represent. If this game doesn't appeal you for some reason, I recommend checking out the soundtrack either way.
-Funny: I have never laugh so much at a videogame as I did with Undertale!! The humour of this game is very particular and it might not please everyone, but personally I love it.
-Lore/Story: It is a very good story, and the way it is told is very unique. I would like to give more details regarding this point but I don't want to spoil anything since Undertale should be played totally blind in my opinion to get the best experience.
I might undertand that the graphics may turn down someone, but this game makes everything else right that it doesn't matter, and in fact, it gives the game a unique touch.
TL,DR: Try this game!! Trust me!!

Pros:
1. Unforgiving. At one point you can be the king of the server and the next thing you notice you have nothing at all. It's like dark souls, but it's not souls you are losing. You can lose ALL your progress.
2. Addictive and rewarding gameplay. Farming, building, raiding, roaming. Choose your style.
3. The gunplay is satisfying and the primitive weapons don't lose their purpose after you reach "lategame"
4. You can enjoy the game both in solo and with friends. For a true roguelike experience, go solo.
5. Active developers. Bi-weekly update with the devs actually listening to the playerbase.
Cons:
1. The game is a memory hog and you might find yourself in trouble with even 8gb and less RAM. Atleast this was the case for me and I ended up upgrading to 16gb wich somewhat made it better.
2. Overall performance isn't that shabby. The graphics are not so well optimized, but it's an alpha so I'm sure these things will be fixed in the final product.
3. Loading times might be frustrating if you are not the most patient of people.
4. Big groups and clans dominate the servers. There is power in numbers and you might find it frustrating trying to advance if you're going solo or with a small group.
5. Animals are very glitchy, might teleport inside your base and may cause you an untimely death. Watch out for those bears!
Overall: If you are looking for a roguelike fps exeprience, this is it. The unforgivingness is a huge thrill. Best enjoyed with a group of friends, but solo is also viable.

I just wanted to update my review for this game. I gave it a thumbsdown when it was first released, once again, I give it yet another thumbsdown. So, after two years, the game is still in Alpha. It's literally one guy working on it, anyway, so I don't expect him to rush it and release the full version fast. With that being said, there's still A LOT of bugs in the game. Bears and wolves glitching through walls and floors, rifles bugging out with reloads, I've even had it where I would be crafting something with an open inventory and the item never came to be AND I lost my mats doing it (it has only happened once so far).
The optimization for the game is poor, but again, take into mind there's only one developer, so it's nothing against him, it's more along the lines of because of a limited amount of resources, he can't push the game out fast enough, nor can he fix all the bugs in the game right away. After all, it's still Alpha.
Another thing I dislike are the servers. A mass majority of them wipe within 2 weeks to a single months time. The reason for this is due to clutter, AND some players are so high of a level and well established that it makes being a new player, or fresh character, almost impossible to move up, or at least take a lot longer. Some servers only wipe the map and everything you own and build, but leave XP. Some servers wipe everything. None-the-less, it's a good and also a bad thing. It's good that it makes you on even levels every few weeks, but the bad part is it makes you feel unaccomplished. Don't get me wrong, you could always get a private server and build to your hearts desire, but from my understanding is that most Rust Server Hosts require a wipe so their servers aren't cluttered.
Now, the typical game itself starts off fun; however, once you get higher level (about mid-20's and up), the game is ridiculously easy and that's including when you're PVP'ing or just doing PVE stuff. There's literally nothing challenging or exciting that happens. By the time you're level 25, majority of the time, you can build an amazing base and can make some of the top tier gear, weapons, and items. Once you're fully equipped and well armed, PVP is really, really easy. There have been servers where I be able to take out large groups of players with just a scoped Bolt Action and HV and Inc rounds. Or just fire rockets into a swarm of people. Or watch clans fight it out, hide in a mountain side, and blow rockets into the middle of all of it and go down and loot everyone after they're dead. Easy stuff. A little too easy.
One thing I've also encountered that is a pet peeve of mine is that a large amount of the servers I've been in have no problems with killing a fresh character. Personally, I always felt bad for 'em and I try to help, if I'm already established on these particular servers; however, majority of time from experience and from witnessing other players, is you could have a rock and be gathering, and some level 30+ would come around and gun them down. Rinse and repeat. To me, that's just ill taste in gameplay and a large percent of the servers I've been on do this frequently, so people who are new to Rust tend to get a bad taste for it.
I know people are complaining about the new XP system, comparing it to the old way Rust used to be upon release. Personally, I like the new XP system. I feel like it makes you strive for leveling, but there are people and entire clans that power level with each other and that's where it breaks the game. Within a day, I've seen a clan get to level 20 while most solo players were still around level 10.
When the game first launched, it was fun, but got boring fast. I hopped servers all over the place. Even got my own for a short time. The game is very repetitive and to be frank, gets dull real fast. So if you're looking for a cheap way to have a short amount of fun and like survival games, by all means, buy Rust. You'll have a blast. For those of us who wanted more, don't bother. Just wait 'till the game fully releases (as stated, it's still in Alpha).
In the end, Rust is still a better game than No Man's Sky and still a better game than anything Valve has released within the past 5 years.

UNDERTALE.
Wow. I cannot even begin to explain the way I feel about this game. I'll try to keep it short, but I can't promise anything.
UNDERTALE has an amazing story, breathtaking soundtrack, silly humor, and hilarious characters. The game has multiple endings, which is something I've always wanted to try. It was an amazing experience.
The battle system is great. Choosing your actions based on how you want the story to unfold, and watching the characters' reactions, realizing how your actions affect others.. it's very satisfying and it feels real. The mechanics are very fun and smooth, and the framerate is nice.
The puzzles are fairly easy (by the time you play the game a second time, you should be able to complete most, if not all, of the puzzles quickly), and I wish it had a few harder ones, however I understand that puzzles are not the main focus of the game. And that's fine.
The boss battles are immensely fun and interesting. UNDERTALE seems to find a way to change it up at every boss fight, so battling constantly feels fun and it never gets old.
Once again, the soundtrack. Sometimes, I find myself sitting back and just listening to the soundtrack for a few seconds. It is truly amazing; it finds ways to implement parts of one song into another, so they all feel familiar yet new all at the same time. Not to mention the nice blend between retro-style and complex songs.
The world is vast and enjoyable. The different areas really help to contribute to the feeling that keeps the game from being stale. The colors blend nicely and the music really fits the theme.
As for age-appropriate questions, the game has some dark themes and disturbing images, but they're really not that bad.  There's no nudity, so that's not an issue. As for the humor, it's just silly fun times that will make you grin or even lose yourself in laughter. Nothing inappropriate that I can recall.
As for the length of the game, it took me less than ten hours for my first playthough, and it only got quicker after that for more Neutral Runs. However, time will vary depending on which ending you try to get. You can watch a movie that's only around two hours long and have it feel complete.  It's the same for this game. Even though it's short, it feels satisfying (ESPECIALLY when you achieve the true ending).
UNDERTALE is a masterpiece. It combines old and new mechanics and styles, making it the perfect game for someone who wants a fun and engaging RPG. And it's only ten dollars!
This game is truly amazing. If you haven't heard enough about it from the rest of the world, be my guest and read more. However, you'll get a better experience knowing as little as possible (that's why I tried to keep spoilers to a minimum here).
UNDERTALE. The RPG where you don't have to destroy anyone. Or do you? That's completely up to you.
