Rust is an intense game of survival. You are dropped into an open world sand box in a never ending pvp enviroment. You harvest resources and build house's, fortresses or compounds. You craft clothing and armor, guns and explosives. You can explore the world under a constant threat of dealth to risk coming back with amazing rewards and gear. If all thats not enough for you, then go and take whatever you like from others in heart pounding pvp fights.
This game is still in development. I personally am not a fan of the development team, primarily because they have been known to lower themselves to the same level of Rusts toxic community. That said, any hardcore pvp survival game is going to bring out strong emotions reguardless if they are good or bad.
The game is very addicting, and can become your life if you let it. I have been playing this game for years now and I very much have a love/hate relationship with it. I can not dispute that it is an amazing game and if there was a video game hall of fame, Rust would be in it. (even tho its not finished at the time of writing this)
I am sure Rust will be, and already is the flagship of its genre.
I would not recommend this game to a softcore gamer or anyone that is easily discouraged.
You can spend 80 hours progressing in this game and loose it all in the blink of an eye. Its a dog eat dog world, and Im sure you can imagine the type of rage this can bring out in the loosing party. That said, once you get the taste of victory you will keep coming back for more. This game plays on a persons ego. When your ego is hurt you will rage, and when your ego is fed you will become addicted.

I actually like this game. No, love it. It's the first time I've played a survival type of game like this, and I'm hooked. It's addicting as hell. There are negatives to this game in my eyes, but first, let's start with the positives.
The game has this original survival build-your-way-up-to-glory aspect that has finally been done with humans and realistic graphics. It's Minecraft done differently, in my opinion. Whether that's better to you is based on what you think. Me? I love it. It's Minecraft done way better. It also has this great atmosphere. You start out hopeless hitting a tree with a rock while butt naked. But once you learn the game and learn how to craft spears, tools, and clothes, you start to like it a lot more. Then you hunt for animals to throw spears at to get food and leather, then you gather lots of wood to start building your own home. At first, it feels tedious and boring, but then it gets a lot better and you get hooked. Soon, you'll be living in a stone house with guns and armor. It takes time to build up to this kind of setup, and it feels satisfying once you do. It's also way more fun if you bring some friends along with you to survive. The graphics are good, aside from the ugly tree leaves and a bit of super muddy textures on some stuff like dumpsters, which I assume is because the game is still in development. I've seen stuff about a future graphical overhaul which will be pretty sweet. The audio is also well done, especially the death screams. Whew, the chills.
Now, are there negatives? Of course. No game is perfect. The game is a bit unoptimized. Luckily, my EVGA 960 with 4GB VRAM can run this game without sacrificing a lot of visual sexiness. The game still looks pretty good with the settings I have which is great. The animals also have the ability to walk up boulders and mountains and walk through walls which is distracting and frustrating, especially when you're chasing an animal with a wooden bow and he gets away by running through a wall that you can't run through. You also can't choose your gender or race. It feels kinda PC but I think it's always been that way. Well, times have to change because I hate it. I'm forced to be a black woman. I want to be able to be a hispanic colored man in a game if I want to, and I'll proudly say that to a feminist's face.
There's also the toxic community I hear about on official servers. They always KOS (kill on sight) with no mercy, and stomp on the little guys that are trying to enjoy the game. Clans raid and slaughter everyone. To their credit, it is how the game is meant to be played, but it's no fun to any newcomers. The best way to avoid these Hitlers is to join empty servers. I always play on modded servers with little to no people on them, and I've actually made a few friends on said servers.
Now, the XP system. My opinion on it is it can work, but it's not good right now. On vanilla servers, XP takes way too long to get. It's annoying and grindy. I always make sure the modded server has at least 3x or more XP gain to get rid of the grinding. The best way to fix this is to take off new items costing XP to unlock and at least double the XP gain to make it not such a nuisence. There's also the blueprint system I hear people talk about all the time, but it honestly doesn't sound good to me.

Here's some tips I have put together to get the most out of your Rust experience:
- Empty the Parallax Mapping, Anisotropic Filtering, and the water option bars. I gained 30+ FPS by doing so. Of course, if you have a beast PC, don't worry about this.
- Join empty modded servers to get a singleplayer kind of feel. It's dumb the devs haven't added a singleplayer option like Ark and Minecraft have.
- Look for servers that have a XP multiplier plugin to get rid of the grinding.
- Servers with a map plugin are also nice, although this isn't often.
- Modded servers with a small playerbase are usually nice and don't KOS immediately. If you want a friendly server, those are the best ones to look out for.
- Don't launch the game in DX12 mode. It's laggy and the water was a solid lime color.

DON'T TRUST THE TRAILER!!!
In fact, don't even watch it. Don't even think about watching it. Undertale bears a lot of resemblance to a show called Gravity Falls. It can be serious and intense, has great characters and a lot of heart, but it also breaks the fourth wall and puts the player/viewer into ridiculous situations for laughs. And when your first impression are those ridiculous situations, without any context or without being invested in the characters, it looks dumb. But once you're actually in the game, and you've seen what it is and what it can be, these moments feel a lot more welcome. You're happy to laugh it off for a second.
The trailer doesn't show off the worst aspects of Undertale. In fact, it's funny moments are some of my favorite moments in the game. But when those funny, ridiculous moments are your first impressions of the game, when you're lead to believe the entire game is like that, it seems stupid and not worth your time. Which Undertale is not!
I mean, come on. If all you'd seen of Gravity Falls was the scene where Dipper imagines himself dancing with Wendy, would you really watch it?
So yeah. Ignore the trailer. Don't even go near it. Instead, just believe me when I tell you that Undertale is an incredible experience that will leave you wanting more. Unless you're a soulless monster, or unless the trailer put you in the wrong frame of mind.
Honestly, the game is best experienced blind, so blind you don't even know that you're playing a game when it first starts up. So just buy it and play it. I promise you won't regret it.
Also, I recommend being able to make spaghetti before playing.

1. The game is so story rich, especially when you beat it.
2. Three possible outcomes for an ending.
3. 16-bit graphics are extremely nostalgic, especially for those 80s-90s kids out there, like myself.
4. It gives you that nice, indie feel.
5. Great sense of humor.
6. Great character building.
7. Extremely engaging, as the character's are actually pretty accurate to universal personalities.
C O N S:
1. God, the fanbase. Just don't get with them, please.
2. A lot of the choppy movements seem forced.
3. The game tries too hard to be funny sometimes.
4. At some moments, the game disobeys itself and moves to 32-bit/64-bit graphics during boss battles, which ruins the feel that it's supposed to give you.
5. No difficulty options.
O V E R V I E W:
Undertale looks pretty bad on the surface. 16-bit graphics, the fanbase, and the popularity it's getting. I was in that state, looking over Undertale as I would Five Nights at Freddy's. Both games are similar. Terrible fanbase, rich story, seemingly childish story, the list goes on. Amazing game though once you get into it; it's pretty easy to learn, too. No learning curve, it goes at a good pace. Of course, no game is flawless. The combat is fairly tedious, repeatedly pushing buttons. It's unique, sure, but not an extravagant unique. You don't have to fight, and that's a great idea, but Tobyfox doesn't pull it off amazingly. Like I said, it's mashing buttons, which isn't really that different from fighting... LOVE the artstyle. Truly a beautiful game.

I think you'll be hard pressed to find someone who genuinely dislikes Undertale. The story is solid, the characters are great, and the aesthetic of the game is extremely solid for something so pixelated. The combat system is unique, and while I'm not the sort to enjoy bullet hells, I did manage to get all the way through the game and complete the True Pacifist ending.
I think what I appreciate most about this game is the sense of importance your choices make. Most games give the illusion of choice -- see the Stanley Parable for a great commentary about just that -- but only provide you with one or two endings. I was reading up on the possible endings for Undertale, and besides the big 3, there are tens of variations depending on which characters you kill. Any game developer that puts that much work into obscure endings that very few people will play is one that genuinely loves their game, and for that, as much as the game itself, Undertale is worthwhile addition to anyone's library.

To those that hate a game (or anything, for that matter) for its fanbase: Stop.
Before you drop a dump on a game because its fanbase is "cancer", actually try the game; ignore the fanbase.  Forget the game even has a fanbase.  Pretend that you are the first person ever to play that game.
After giving the game a good faith try, make your choice: like the game for the game, or hate the game for the game.
At this point, if you still hate a game, that's fair.  You tried it like that piece of nasty food when you were 4 years old or so, despite the fact that everyone else thought it was delicious.  You don't dislike the food because other people like it; you just didn't like the food.  You dislike it because YOU put it in your mouth, chewed it up, swallowed, decided it tastes bad, and possibly threw it up later.
However if you did enjoy the game, that's a different story.
If you liked the game, you might want to try your luck and join in on the fandom (or you might be weird and just want to be a recluse after all that).  Start by finding something in the fandom that you like: animation, music, artwork, etc. (Believe or not, a fandom is not just the porn-drawing, cringy fanboy/fangirl, shove-it-down-your-throat people, but literally everyone that enjoys something)  Next, plant your flag in a subject or two; either by beginning to post your own content, or by following quality content creators, widely recognized or not.  Finally, enjoy new content as it crops up; because as long as there are human beings on the planet, there will be new ideas.
CONGATULATIONS!!!  You now like something because you tried it and decided that it was good!
(Or you don't.  But don't go out of your way to post hate.  Hate with other haters, don't hate with fans)

Rust is an intense game of survival. You are dropped into an open world sand box in a never ending pvp enviroment. You harvest resources and build house's, fortresses or compounds. You craft clothing and armor, guns and explosives. You can explore the world under a constant threat of dealth to risk coming back with amazing rewards and gear. If all thats not enough for you, then go and take whatever you like from others in heart pounding pvp fights.
This game is still in development. I personally am not a fan of the development team, primarily because they have been known to lower themselves to the same level of Rusts toxic community. That said, any hardcore pvp survival game is going to bring out strong emotions reguardless if they are good or bad.
The game is very addicting, and can become your life if you let it. I have been playing this game for years now and I very much have a love/hate relationship with it. I can not dispute that it is an amazing game and if there was a video game hall of fame, Rust would be in it. (even tho its not finished at the time of writing this)
I am sure Rust will be, and already is the flagship of its genre.
I would not recommend this game to a softcore gamer or anyone that is easily discouraged.
You can spend 80 hours progressing in this game and loose it all in the blink of an eye. Its a dog eat dog world, and Im sure you can imagine the type of rage this can bring out in the loosing party. That said, once you get the taste of victory you will keep coming back for more. This game plays on a persons ego. When your ego is hurt you will rage, and when your ego is fed you will become addicted.

Undertale brought personal investment and emotion into the game, making me feel like I was part of the experience, and I'm not ashamed to say at times I cried, or fought passionately, or was terrified by what Toby Fox brought to the table. It has been a very long time since a game has touched me the way that Undertale has. I thought creativity like this had long since died, and I'm so glad to have been proven wrong.
Your choices have reverberating consequences for everyone around you, and has an effect felt throughout the underground. The emphasis on choice and consequence, as well as the storytelling techniques used, make this game best played blind.
If you're hesitant to make the purchase, I assure you the game would be a bargain at twice the price. If more game developers could capture the essence of what makes Undertale so great, I'd happily empty my wallet for the experience.
Bravo Toby Fox, Bravo. I'll be keeping my eye on you.

Out of 450 games I own I have never requested a steam refund, but this game may just change that. I was duped into buying this game from the great reviews and got the 4 pack for my girlfriend and friends. We have all pretty much stopped playing it, and do not intend to return to in its current status. The game currently as it stands is grief simulator 9000. Like many other games of its type, the fundamental issue is that there is so little to do, that as soon as people have a few weapons or even the basic gear, the game turns into pvp. I take that back, even as a fresh spawn with nothing but a rock, people run around trying to bash each other’s heads in.
There is no sense of cooperation or building relationships. Sadly the game tries to push a more social agenda by having you not be able to create a character or even pick the gender or race of who you are. But this is all wasted in the games shallow atmosphere. Working together means very little, unless you have a party and intend to build large structures and troll people. The environment does very little to challenge you and this is one the main reasons why cooperation seems meaningless. 99 out of a 100 times you see someone, even if you are bare naked they will run at you and attack you with your starting rock. Those with gear, bows, guns, etc shoot on sight.
This game is very similar to dayz in the sense that since there is no real environmental treats, PVP begins as soon people spawn, game is filled with hackers, and terrible server admins. For example, after spending several hours gather resources and leveling up, I was standing in the darkness in fear of someone seeing me with my torch or fire on. Well that didn’t stop this one person who came at me with a spear in pitch blackness. Proceeded to attack me, chase me, and kill me. Again, in pitch darkness tracking me as I ran around changing directions.
In many ways this game is far worse than dayz, because in dayz you do not gather resources, spending time bashing on a tree with a rock to gather enough wood to build your first hatchet, only to die half way through as a random person bashes your head in with a rock from the back. If you do manage to gather enough resources with a few of your friends and level up enough to begin building anything, you can look forward to getting gunned down by people already geared up. Then you rise and repeat until you and your friends say f this, let’s go play something else.. In its current state, the game can be skipped all together and nothing will be missed here.
Games like Ark offer similar gameplay but with real environmental treats that force players to be more team minded, as cooperation will lead to survival against the predators that are extremely dangerous. Given that rust is more polished than Ark, I can see great potential here; however major and I mean major changes and additions need to be made to the game to give it any longevity. The average player getting into rust will find it impossible to navigate or do anything as veterans of the server with their fortifications and sniper towers will just pick them off for fun.
My recommendation is to stay away until more is added to the game and environmental threats become a force that actually impacts the cooperation of players. Then again if you enjoy getting shot, stabbed, and bashed in the head with a rock as you attempt to gather even the most basic resources to build the most basic tools then this game is all for you.

My girlfriend recommended this game to me a week ago. It was only ten bucks so I figured, "what the heck?" You role play as a character that one day thought it'd be a good idea to climb a mountain and then falls into a sealed off underground world that is home to the fabled monsters. After meeting a few friendly characters, it becomes clear that you must journey to the castle to meet the king so you can ask him to let you out. Along this journey, you'll meet monsters that have been tasked with killing any and all humans that they come across. You'll be given a choice to either fight to the death or spare and show mercy(become besties) in your fights against them. Note that once a character is killed, they do not come back. They are gone for the rest of the game. The puzzles in the game are very simple and straightforward, I can only recall having trouble with one but that didn't last too long. I ran through the game first try as a pacifist. I didn't kill any monsters at all. I made friends with all of them instead. The characters were so funny and interesting. Then I got to the ending and the feels started. To sum it all up... for the price tag and the amount of fun you will have in this game, I highly recommend it. I'm not familiar with the neutral or genocide endings, but if you stick with a pacifist playthrough then I can promise you that the characters, the world, and the overall fun that you will have playing this game will resonate within you weeks/months later.

Rust. Some call it survival. Some call it fun. Some would even go as far as calling is "great".
I believe none of those explations do it the credit it deserves.
The word that best describes Rust is: Friendly.
The survival. The murderous animals. BUT especially the community.
Are you a new player in Rust? NO problem! Experienced and leveled players on the server will always check up on you and look after you! Whether it is showing up at your brand new, tiny, barely livable house at random times. taking your few valuable items from your boxes JUST for safe keeping, or watching over your spawn point to make sure you don't wake up too early. (Some are even known to do a little renovation and knock a few of your hard built walls down. Just to surprise you!) Rust's community is just great!
But it all seriousness. Rust in and of itself will be a great game when it is finished and is already really fun. The community just sucks and if you aren't one of the first on the servers then prepare to get murdered just for fun and your hard work destroyed just because they can. I loved the first few hours and was addicted until I had to deal with more of the players.

Rust does a lot of things good (IMO that is), like how relativly simple the crafting/building is, the minamilistic UI and the maps.
BUT, the games does a lot of things wrong, as well.
First, there's a lack of things to really, well, do aside from building. Meeting your survival needs in this game (hunger/thirst) is not difficult, so once you've got even a small stockpile of food and what not you're left with a distinct lack of stuff to do unless you plan on building some massive complex for ♥♥♥♥♥ and giggles (which is fun to do, not gonna lie).
Second, there's no easy way to play solo. You have to basically install and run your own server if you want to, and while it's not difficult, it isn't exactly intuative since you have to use SteamCMD.
Third, the game isn't really eassy for new players to get into depending on what server they decide to try first. Larger servers are often newbie gank fests with large clans running around doing nothing but trolling new players. Smaller servers are often OK, but again, you ruin into the first problem I mentioned; a lack of things to do once your done building (even when factoring in building decay).
And finally, we have how long this game's been in Early Access. It's been 4 Years already and that's kind of a long time, IMO.
So, do I recommend this game? Well, kind of. It's fun if you have a group of friends to play with, but it's also one of those games where it's going to turn people off for one reason or another. So my recomendation is to wait for a sale or it to be part of something like a Humble Bundle.

I'm checking this as free because I got it in a bundle, and instead of giving money to Garry Newman and his unfortunate lackies, I gave the money to charity. Bite me.
Let me just preface how much I hate Newman, which is quite a lot to be honest, not just for the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ attitude towards his consumers, treatment of his staff, and ungodly disgusting community he's spawned and harboured on Facepunch, wherein a clique of nerds thinks they're top dog by being the only ones able to use 12 year old outdated technology, and if you aren't in the mix already, you never can be, but mostly because his name is the same as that one fellow who wrote "Cars"
As much as I loathe Newman and his platform, this game, unfortunately, is pretty decent.
Ignore all the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t what went on behind the scenes, with developers being forced to work in awkward shifts, not recieving payments on time, and eventually being cut from the project with their content still in it (until, of course, the "legacy edition" went away)
Despite Newman's best attempts, Rust is really, honestly, an almost decent game. Granted, it's pretty early, but so are a lot of things I've played in my time, and they typically don't have the same issues, or even as many issues, as this game does.
Granted, again, I've mostly been playing on a silent community server with just myself and a couple of my jack-off friends, stuffing my labia in their faces whenever given the chance, glad beyond glad I managed to roll a female character with this asinine pick-n-mix bag of skin tones  and genitalia. She was even white, curiously enough.
Then, as if punishment for my hubris, out of said labia claws a wolf. One second, there was me, some furry with no pants, playing a game in which I was also a furry with no pants, and then, the next, there was a wolf.
It would proceed to kill me in one hit before I could even swing.
This happened four times.
I also fell out of the world once, but that's actually under par for me playing games, so I'm going to add a point for that.
Rust is, unfortunately, "plagued" by raiders, as in, all endgame content is specifically designed for raiding other players.
This means that every public lobby you jump into is going to be a boy's club of people hitting well-armed men with stones, trying to defend their 14 pieces of corn from the invading marauders that just shot down their door with an anti-tank rocket. Now, this is the natural progression of things, when the only content is guns and magazines, anyone is welcome to come and get their issue, pick a fight with the nearest naked man you're certain isn't hiding an M249
on his personage, and then repeat
The game doesn't seem to know what it wants to be, so, really it naturally becomes this, as players realize all the guns they just spent eight hours crafting can be easily pointed at another player. I mean, like, we've got boars and bears running around, makes sense, you're on some remote island that is eerily familiar of coastal Maine, complete with rusted out structures like the world ended either 40 minutes or 40 years ago, but then you've got the Super Huey flying in to blast anybody bold enough to wear clothes and a C-130 freely dropping supplies at arbitrary points on the map. Sometimes directly through the map, but, again, that kind of stuff seems to cling to me like a bad smell.
There's no real tone to it, and the cutesy cartoonish HUD elements really do a good job of working against whatever themes you're looking at, more often than not.
tl;dr
Rust is okay. I don't know what it wants to be and neither does it.
And that's also okay because I think I like it. I think.

As of now, the current state of this game is horrendous.
*The leveling system is garbage and is obviously there to make you grind even more than you already need to.
*Hunger drains way too fast and most foods only fill up around 5% of your food bar.
*Animals clip through mountains, rocks and other things that make getting food to fill your abyss of a stomach even harder.
*The amount of resources you collect and use are rediculous. Why are there stacks of 1,000 and why does making a machete require 100 pieces of metal? Following Minecraft's footsteps and making stacks small and craft requirements reasonable would be a wise decision.
*Growing food takes way too long. I end up starving to death waiting for corn to grow.
*The game's essentially made for people to greif and loot. When you leave the game, your body lays on the floor where you were last at, even when you lay down a sleeping bag. My character ended up getting looted inside of my armored house because his foot clipped outside the walls. This is incredibly annoying because my character was at the oposite side of the house from my sleeping bag, instead of just being in the bag sleeping. I understand that this is an alpha build at the moment, however it seems like these decisions were intentional. It's essentially a kick in the nuts to find out that the 7.1 hours you spent bashing a rock with a rock to get just the basics can be all for nothing because the game doesn't despawn your character when you leave the game.
I see potential in this game, however the mix of bad decisions, bad AI programming and bad balancing make me want to find a way to return the Humble Bundle I spent 5.05$ on.

Simplistic yet diverse game. Undertale is a wonderful play through regardless of your choices in the game story. It is a 16-bit JRPG with the defense in battles done in bullet hell style and all is done with rich dialogue and decent map areas. It has some wonderful soundtracks, memorable moments and characters.
Pros:
- Great value for the price.
- It has dynamic campaign that will adapt to your choices.
- Nice story and story elements with multiple play through.
- Good and funny dialogue.
- Multiple endings.
- Multiple 'bullet hell' mechanisms in the fights.
- Very wonderful soundtrack.
- Light on your system.
Cons:
- Lack of a standard settings or options menu.
- No encyclopedia or story log in the game.
- Very barebones graphics.
- Few enemy types.
- Few secrets.
- Short campaign for one finish.

Ok so I'm a newish player so this is from my perspective. First off, the game runs well and looks good. With a 1070 / 6600k I can run the game on ultra settings at around 100fps +, as long as I'm not using dx 12 version, which is experimental anyways. The gameplay feels very polished, and all the inventory management is very well done. It's also nice that custom servers are allowed to speed up game progress, as many people don't like the slow pace of the default game. Sound design is also good, nothing flashy about it, as I guess it should be. It's also easy to play with friends, and so far easy to learn. The only gripe I have is the XP system. It restricts the ability to build certain things until you get "experience" by doing stuff like crafting. I kind of like it because of the sense of achievement and the fact that it eases new players into things, but I can see how experienced players would have gripes with it. Overall, the game feels good and satisfying to play and if you are looking for a multiplayer survival game to mess around in with friends, it should do the job.

Ignore all the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t what went on behind the scenes, with developers being forced to work in awkward shifts, not recieving payments on time, and eventually being cut from the project with their content still in it (until, of course, the "legacy edition" went away)
Despite Newman's best attempts, Rust is really, honestly, an almost decent game. Granted, it's pretty early, but so are a lot of things I've played in my time, and they typically don't have the same issues, or even as many issues, as this game does.
Granted, again, I've mostly been playing on a silent community server with just myself and a couple of my jack-off friends, stuffing my labia in their faces whenever given the chance, glad beyond glad I managed to roll a female character with this asinine pick-n-mix bag of skin tones  and genitalia. She was even white, curiously enough.
Then, as if punishment for my hubris, out of said labia claws a wolf. One second, there was me, some furry with no pants, playing a game in which I was also a furry with no pants, and then, the next, there was a wolf.
It would proceed to kill me in one hit before I could even swing.
This happened four times.
I also fell out of the world once, but that's actually under par for me playing games, so I'm going to add a point for that.
Rust is, unfortunately, "plagued" by raiders, as in, all endgame content is specifically designed for raiding other players.
This means that every public lobby you jump into is going to be a boy's club of people hitting well-armed men with stones, trying to defend their 14 pieces of corn from the invading marauders that just shot down their door with an anti-tank rocket. Now, this is the natural progression of things, when the only content is guns and magazines, anyone is welcome to come and get their issue, pick a fight with the nearest naked man you're certain isn't hiding an M249
on his personage, and then repeat
The game doesn't seem to know what it wants to be, so, really it naturally becomes this, as players realize all the guns they just spent eight hours crafting can be easily pointed at another player. I mean, like, we've got boars and bears running around, makes sense, you're on some remote island that is eerily familiar of coastal Maine, complete with rusted out structures like the world ended either 40 minutes or 40 years ago, but then you've got the Super Huey flying in to blast anybody bold enough to wear clothes and a C-130 freely dropping supplies at arbitrary points on the map. Sometimes directly through the map, but, again, that kind of stuff seems to cling to me like a bad smell.
There's no real tone to it, and the cutesy cartoonish HUD elements really do a good job of working against whatever themes you're looking at, more often than not.
tl;dr
Rust is okay. I don't know what it wants to be and neither does it.
And that's also okay because I think I like it. I think.

Here's my own take on Dayz. I came into dayz during the 0.58 update so i may not have the same perspective as someone who's been here from the start. With that I havent been exposed to the same frustrations as the many others out there who now (rightly or wrongly) have serious doubts about the game. I myself can honestly say I have never experienced a game like Dayz. The situations you find yourself in are nothing like I've experienced while gaming. At times it can be a frustrating mess due to bugs and fps drops. But there's the other times when its a heart pounding, limb shaking vortex of adrenaline. You'll be freaked out at how seeing another player can turn you into an incoherent mess. Shots cracking off near you makes you want to curl up into a ball and find a happy place. After each encounter regardless of what happened you'll look back on them and laugh at how good or bad it went. This game gives you stories. Stories that make the whole mess worth it. I'm not very good at this game, in fact i'm pretty terrible. Even at my skill level i achieve enough to still enjoy the game. If you want something different in your library that you can play with a few mates I'd definietly get this. Take a bit of time to watch a few videos and engage to some degree with the community forums (reddit etc) and you'll be fine.

Borderlands 2 is a high quality, open world game with a great story with capabilities of players being alone or playing cooperatively with up to four players. The graphics are completely cartoony and unlike those of most other games. This is one of those games where you find yourself playing with friends, and completing the game time and time again.
The player has a choice of four characters, excluding the two characters you can unlock through purchasing DLC. You have your choice of being Salvador, a gunzerker capable of wielding any two weapons of your choice. Want dual rocket launchers, or an assault rifle and a shotgun? No problem! Zer0 is an assassin, capable of sending a hologram towards the enemy to cause either a distraction that can lead to your quick escape, or a sneak attack the foe won’t see coming. Axton is a skilled veteran with a deployable turret that can be the demise of any foe standing in your way. In time, with upgrades, this turret can be attached to any surface, launch missiles, heal allies, or even be upgraded so that you may have two turrets or a single turret with two guns. Lastly is Maya, with the ability to lift enemies into the sky, what you do from this point is your choice.
Being as the campaign is either solo or cooperative, you may have one of each character, four Salvadors, or just a lone vault hunter. No matter who you play as, every character has the same goal; defeat Handsome Jack. Borderlands is filled with non-stop action as well as comedy from Claptrap, a little robot that greets your character when you first step off the bus in Borderlands, as well as in the beginning of Borderlands 2. Although Borderlands 2 is rated mature, it has no strong language, and is mainly a blood filled violence game. I recommend this for everyone aged 13 and up. A fun game for friend regardless of any age, a must-have for Borderlands veterans and a great game for anyone looking to try it out. Some special details about the game; the four characters you can play as in the original Borderlands return to Borderlands 2 and make up a big part of the story. Also the entire game is not played on foot, there are several catch-a-ride machines placed throughout the game where you may obtain a vehicle to drive. In addition, Borderlands 2 has over a bazillion weapons. No two are the same. No really! It even says so on the cover!
Overall a great, fun, action-packed game. My rating is 8.75/10

I gotta a ton (almost 5000 hours) of time in this game! I run a small sever that I have learned to customize.  I enjoy programming and customizing plugins for the game.
Game Pros
• Clean menu ( servers can use plugins to add to the game HUD )
• Players can host their own servers off their computers for free, or pay to have it hosted on a shared/dedicated server
• Intricate base building system and 3rd party programs like Fortify to help design them
• Hunting/Gathering
• Day/Night Cycle
• Weather System
• Moddable ( soooo moddable )
• Frequent updates ! Dev & Community blogs
• Procedural generated world
• Gives you a sense of paranoia
• Generated Biomes (Desert, Snow, Grass)
• Sleeper servers (Even when you log off you are still in-game, and able to be killed. Pretty much forces you put in time to build a stable base before leaving the server. Or risk being killed.
Game Cons
• Game tends to lag/rubber-band if too many people are connected to the server
• Uses a lot of RAM
• KoS ( This really depends on the person and server, but what do you expect?)
• VoIP needs work (Causes a second or two of lag after letting go of the VoIP key)
• Framerate/Crashing issues at times with certain updates on AMD cards
• Runs on the Unity engine (Making it not the best for optimization, but the dev team has found lot of their way to optimize)

At this point in time I expect just about every indie game out there to be of lesser quality to some extent. I don't see the point in buying them when there's so many greater options, but then games like Undertale come along and slap me in the face. Undertale is an unforgetable game full of emotion, character, story and humor.
+Great cast of characters. It's hard not to find someone you agree with or get attached to in this game.
+Amazing soundtrack, one of my favorites.
+Great story with sub-plots that really draw you in and make the decision to kill a difficult one.
+This game has an astute awareness that there's no getting away from. It remembers your decisions beyond saves, it breaks the fourth wall, it challenges you; the player, and it does it all so seemlessly.
+Emotional ride with a highly-satisfying "true ending"
+This game is funny. I'm not the type of guy to laugh at♥♥♥♥♥♥in games, unless it's at the game. In this case it would be with it. The game has a sense of  humor that really appealed to the pun-loving geek inside me.
+Multiple endings means multiple playthroughs.
+Combat that is really unique to the RPG system. Bullet-hells with each enemy having their own type of attacks that you must catch onto quickly to survive.
+Straight to the point. No grinding, no menial tasks. Toby Fox did an excellent job in propelling the player forward ensuring there's no time for the things RPG players typically find tedious.

It's amazing how well Undertale controls your emotions. This game made me regret murdering a "goat". Resetting your save after killing that "goat" will make one of the characters mock you for that.
This game has lots of replay value. After the neutral run (the result of killing some monsters), you will probably want to be perfect the next time around, hence the pacifist run (the result of sparing everyone). After that, you become greedy and want more, hence the genocide run (the result of killing everyone). Even after you complete the 3 runs, there is still so much to do. You can encounter the "Wrong Number" song, a mystery man who is presumed to be Gaster, So Sorry, Glyde, and more. You can find secret rooms like Sans' room, Mettaton's house, the developer room, the abandoned quiche room, and much more. It doesn't stop there. There are mysteries to be solved. Secrets to be discovered. Digging into the Undertale files will reveal even more secrets, like entry number 17, Grandpa Semi, Debug Mode, and we're still discovering new secrets to this date. This isn't just a game. This is an experience.
100% worth it. Go buy it.

You have to think in milliseconds, and storm through bullet hell, but even if you're not naturally talented (admittedly I was bad) through practice and DETERMINATION, you can become the best! Borderlands 2 is a high quality, open world game with a great story with capabilities of players being alone or playing cooperatively with up to four players. The graphics are completely cartoony and unlike those of most other games. This is one of those games where you find yourself playing with friends, and completing the game time and time again.
The player has a choice of four characters, excluding the two characters you can unlock through purchasing DLC. You have your choice of being Salvador, a gunzerker capable of wielding any two weapons of your choice. Want dual rocket launchers, or an assault rifle and a shotgun? No problem! Zer0 is an assassin, capable of sending a hologram towards the enemy to cause either a distraction that can lead to your quick escape, or a sneak attack the foe won’t see coming. Axton is a skilled veteran with a deployable turret that can be the demise of any foe standing in your way. In time, with upgrades, this turret can be attached to any surface, launch missiles, heal allies, or even be upgraded so that you may have two turrets or a single turret with two guns. Lastly is Maya, with the ability to lift enemies into the sky, what you do from this point is your choice.
Being as the campaign is either solo or cooperative, you may have one of each character, four Salvadors, or just a lone vault hunter. No matter who you play as, every character has the same goal; defeat Handsome Jack. Borderlands is filled with non-stop action as well as comedy from Claptrap, a little robot that greets your character when you first step off the bus in Borderlands, as well as in the beginning of Borderlands 2. Although Borderlands 2 is rated mature, it has no strong language, and is mainly a blood filled violence game. I recommend this for everyone aged 13 and up. A fun game for friend regardless of any age, a must-have for Borderlands veterans and a great game for anyone looking to try it out. Some special details about the game; the four characters you can play as in the original Borderlands return to Borderlands 2 and make up a big part of the story. Also the entire game is not played on foot, there are several catch-a-ride machines placed throughout the game where you may obtain a vehicle to drive. In addition, Borderlands 2 has over a bazillion weapons. No two are the same. No really! It even says so on the cover!
Overall a great, fun, action-packed game. My rating is 8.75/10

Unlike many others, I can definitely see the potential in this game. Altough glitchy(haven't found THAT many to be honest) and poorly optimized, it's very addictive and fun and VERY intense sometimes. My heart rate has never been as high as when meeting two bandits and recking them. For all those folks who say it's only "W+Shift and then die", well... stop sucking at the game. You need to be VERY careful of your surroundings, and players are definitely more dangerous than zombies.
But let's be honest. I do agree it's alot of running to get to NWA(North west airfield) and then back to Elektro for some action/interaction with other players. But that can easily be fixed with more cars/bikes/boats etc, more small villages to loot instead of just vast open fields. And the thirst/hunger is seriously broken. You need to drink like 10 liters to be hydrated for a half an hour. That's ridiculous.
BUT I truly enjoy playing this game. It's supposed to be tough surviving in a zombie apocalypse. And this game is pretty tough. I really like the way you can regenerate blood if you are hydrated and have eaten enough. Never pass up a can of food! I really like the environments, altough more zombies wouldn't hurt.
Here are some things I would like to see implemented in the game, hopefully very soon:
- Military/police zombies should carry loot like ammunition and guns
- More vehicles should be added, especially small ones like bikes
- BASE BUILDING PLEASE
- More compatability among weapon parts. In a zombie apocalypse, I believe you would be able to fit a hunter scope on an M4 if you really wanted to. I think the majority of people have used duct tape and screwdrivers in their life. Food for thought
- Spray paint should be applicable to ANYTHING
- You should be able to craft together your gear. "Damn, I cant use this gun holster and this vest at the same time?" You should be able to ffs!
- Hordes of zombies. It would be awsome if suddenly you see a great big horde moving towards the city and you have to get inside, board up the place or get to high ground
- Heli crashes should carry alot more loot. But instead of finding one pristine AUG you could find a badly damaged AUG with some damaged clips and ammo that you would have to mend to use. Also, more zombies at heli crashes
That is all I can come up with as of now. I will continue to play this game, because I really do have alot of fun playing it. And for all the people who are thinking of buying it, maybe you could ask a friend who has the game to lend you his/her account and try it out first. Maybe this game is for you? Maybe not?

First off, I personally really enjoy this game. Despite the fact of its alpha state, it has been one of my most played games on steam for a while now. Whether I'm proud of that fact or not, it shows that I came back for more, multiple times, which is generally a good thing.
To anyone who has played this game, they know that, in terms of gameplay, this game can be extremely aggravating. The game always follows the concept of constantly gaining and losing loot over and over again, whatever the circumstance may be. There are many moments in the game where you could be ahead one day, but then you wake up the next morning to nothin but a raided base, or you die again and again by one large group; both of which make the game very rage inducing. From my perspective, the game is all about decision making; when to raid, when to move base, when to de-spawn all of your loot because they are blowing your door down, when to make the right move. The game is very unpredictable at times. However, with all that said, when you are on the upside of things and are raiding and/or on a hunting party or something, it can be really fun.
The game’s graphics are pretty good. Its been in alpha for a while now, but has received a lot of updates, one every Thursday I believe. I’m curious what final product they have in stock for us all, who knows what it will be.
Some Tips:
1. Playing with friends in a group is probably your best bet at getting anywhere, going solo can be pretty dang hard.
2. Don't trust anyone who is not in your group, especially nakeds.
3. There are always scheduled wipes for each server [usually around 1-2 week(s)] where everything gets deleted and you start over, and it will probably always be that way.
4. With #3 in mind, remember it's a video game, and solely that, don't allow it to overcome your life. That may sound silly, but it can be one of those games that make you pull all-nighters every night.

First of all, Facepunch, creators of Garry's Mod (Garry Newman) really REALLY gives a damn about this community, they bust their humps making sure that this game is playable and tolerable NOW. In a world (steam) full of infini-alpha games with trashdevs (hurtworld, dayz standalone, ark), Rust stands out as the leader of the pack— the example on how a dev should interact with their community.

This is a review for skeptics or people who've already convinced themselves the game is "overrated." I was like you, almost all the way to the end of my first playthrough. The game itself is really good, the end. Play the game. Ignore all outside elements.
PROS:
-Bullet hell + SMT negotiation-style battle system is unique and fun
-Scratches that Earthbound/Mother itch
-Clever use of RPG mechanics and tropes to convey story-telling through battles
-Excellent music (although not totally congruous with the game's style)
-Subsequent playthroughs are very rewarding
-Low price
-Can be laugh-out-loud funny at times
CONS:
-Way too cheeky about not having a 4th wall; this gets annoying fast, and it's a shame because the lack of 4th wall is part of the game's charm. But every now and then it'll collapse on itself with memes and self-references.
-Some of the humor is forced, possibly aimed towards a younger audience. There's one sequence in particular that involves getting a series of obnoxious text messages that made me want to stop playing the game.
-This might vary from person-to-person, but for a game this short it might take a while for you to warm up to it. As said above I didn't start really enjoying the game until its final act.
-Goddamn furries...

Undertale. It's the story of a child who falls into the Underground and whose only way out is to kill the king of this world of friendly monsters. None of them are anything more than territorial, and can be befriended in some way or another. With multiple routes depending on how you play the game, it's an experience I do not think will be soon forgotten. It even created the new toxic fandom! But is there anything I can say about this work that hasn't been said already? Actually, yeah. I think there is.
This game is an exhibiton of the fact that games are not to be judged on graphics. It's common that games with these comparitively low-res graphics are good, they don't take much energy to render, and look charming. I find it not to be a lost opportunity, rather, an exhibition of what could have been earlier in the lifespan of the miracle of video games. The graphical power for this game to be made came about just before 2006 (the year Mother 3 was released), and I don't blame the dev for taking so long; such well-composed works with this class of soundtrack and story take a very long time to come up with.
However, for what it is, I do not believe it is the best in any single aspect. There have been better stories. There have been better games. There have been better graphics. But, very few games can reach a level of each of these that meets modern standards and even thresholds for being high quality. This is what makes Undertale a good game.
+ Captivating and well-written story (this is worth probably about 10 Pros, especially if you're emotional)
+ Multiple story paths
+ Quirky, varying characters
+ Unique active battle system that makes this a step up from the gameplay of other JRPGs
+ Great soundtrack
+ Does not shatter but rethinks the fourth wall to include you as a character (no, not the character you play as, I mean you)
+ Secrets and other representations of things that further rethink the fourth wall to represent even the fandom
+ Very few items that don't have a particular use or quirk to them
- The fandom is somewhat toxic
- Graphics could have been better, to be brutally honest
- Again, to be brutally honest, a little overrated
- Doesn't spread beyond the story-based game genre for the most part
All in all, this game is unique and well-written, and certainly worth your ten dollars if you have somehow avoided playing it to this point. However, if your preference is any one aspect (all gameplay, all graphics, all story, pretty much anything other than character appeal and/or variety) then it is likely that there are better options.

This game, despite not having better graphical quality than other RPG games, it is one of the best games I've played. The fact that the game's setting which takes place in the years 5252 does not convince me much about the technological advancement as compared to the present (other than the fact that you can download your own vehicle from any catch-a-ride machine), but Gearbox's most famed game is not just an awesome game, it's beyond that. There are 3 playthrough modes, 6 characters to play on, and thousands of different variants of weapons to choose from. And then there are unique weapons, which signifies that these weapons will act in a unique way upon being fired, rather than just having its bullets fired in a straight line. Normal Mode was relaxing and enjoyable, TVHM was more intense, and UVHM (including the Overpower levels) is tougher and is recommended for hardcore gamers. I could go on, but this is truly an awesome, must-play game. Hats off to the game developers.

Dayz...hmmm. Well, if you're a fan of the whole end of times zombie genre where people are worse than the undead themselves then go ahead and add this one to your wish list but read further for why you should or should not buy it.
Pros: I think it gets the survival stuff down pretty good. While guns can be found within 15-30 min sometimes ammo is a lot more hard to find. I'm sure more seasoned players can find stuff faster but for me the ammo and magazines are somewhat tough to get I thought. Yeah, you need magazines for your guns...nice touch, or chamber one round at a time. Hunger and thirst, overall health must be maintained to keep your survival going. There's camps, crafting, and all the normal stuff you'd find in the zombie survival genre these days...but what sets it apart..? Well I feel it can be so unscripted and the pvp side of things gets interesting as you can be kidnapped, made to drink gas, robbed and skinned later for eating by your captors. This whole feeling makes my heart rush after exploring for over an hour and seeing only the wilderness and then hearing footsteps. 9/10 times you'll be killed on sight if another person spots you and sees an interest in your gear, after all...it's dog eat dog in these end of times.
This can lead to frustrating a lot of people as it is a perma-death game. If you get killed, you respawn at a random location and have to get your bearing all over again. Frustrating even more to people playing with friends and they all die and get separated only to figure out where in the ♥♥♥♥ everyone is to restart their journey together. Luckily there is a cool app (izurvive) and it's an interactive map everyone can see where they all are to meet up again...super ♥♥♥♥ing cool. If you like going through the motions, figuring out things and planning your journey only to come across some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ or gang and then have to start all over again, buy it...
There's so much more I can add, but with less than 50 hours as of this review...I feel like I've hit the big points in feel. Now for negatives...
Cons: The game runs like absolute♥♥♥♥♥♥toasted w turd butter unless you take the time to configure it. After a few days and forum reading later I have a good running game. I run textures and filtering @ very high (max) with everything else turned to low and AA off and it looks just fine to me, check out my screen shots. I can only imagine once it gets the new engine update and an optimization pass it'll be looker. So, TLDR version...don't expect the game right out of the box to be stellar even with a top end rig cuz the game it doesn't ♥♥♥♥ing care.
There's also zombies, that from what I can tell got reintroduced as of 0.59 update I believe. They are far and few with mostly being in the city type areas. So the game can use some more zombie action, that being said...if you ain't packing a firearm stay the ♥♥♥♥ away from them as melee combat is♥♥♥♥♥♥against them. So not so much a con but mostly, but there is more zombie action coming...in future updates...I'm excited for that.
Difficulty will turn a lot of people off. You'll die a lot from injuries, zombies, but mostly other♥♥♥♥♥♥head survivors looking to rob you. So it'll turn some people off working for hours on end only to killed. But also that's what the game at its heart really is truth to be told.
Lastly, it's early access so be prepared to enjoy the bugs and low frame rate dips and other oddities. But it is what it is...
Like it a lot, fun as hell and tense...if you can get through ten hours and learn the basics you'll learn to love it...good things coming ahead to the game looking at recent dev updates. Base building among them...

Borderlands 2 is a great FPS-RPG-Game, which lets you dive into a great Cel-Shaded world full of guts, glory and badassitude.
You're thrown into a cruel world named Pandora, oppressed by "Handsome Jack", the leader of Hyperion - an organization, which wants to dominate and enslave the world. To achieve his goal, Jack tries to wake up an ancient Alien Golem, referred to as "The Warrior", whose powers will eradicate all enemies in his path. Your one and only goal is to stop Jack by grouping up with the Crimson Raiders, a rebellious alliance, led by Roland from Borderlands 1. With the help of Lilith, Mordecai and Brick you'll set sails for an epic journey with a great sense of humor, which is build up by great puns, sarcastic conversations and cynic characters.
I really like the game and it has a very high replay-rate for me, because the fun at playing this game is (atleast for me) truly neverending, so I decided to buy all the DLCs to get some more events, which bright up your hours of excessive gaming.
To save some money, you should think about directly buying the "Borderlands 2 - GOTY Edition" or buy the Season Pass later, which extends your gameplay experience with new campaigns and a higher max.-level.
TL;DR: Totally worth its money - BUY THIS GAME!

The continuation of one of the best franchises ever, Borderlands 2 brings you back to Pandora with 4 new vault hunters and millions of guns. The game has countless hours of content and more easter eggs references and hidden treasures than probably every other game combined. And on top of the base game the DLC adds tons more content that will keep you involved. The game is great for all, ranging from the ones who just want the main campaign and some great side stories, to the hardened veteran of overpower level 8 taking on the invincibles. 11/10
badass!

One of my favorite games of all time. Borderlands is known for the fun and addictive gameplay, but what the first game in the series lacked in story and atmosphere, this game oozes out of every single scene. The antagonist is one of the most enjoyable characters in modern shooters and Claptrap's return is glorious.
Literally every single thing is blown up in this game compared to the first game. The action is bigger, the guns are badder and the enemies are more awesome. There's more focus on progression as well, instead of the backtracking the first game was all about. There's more areas, more bosses and the final boss isn't as unfulfilling as the boss in BL1 was.
I will recommend this game to anyone that likes shooters. Period. If you like shooters, this is for you. If you don't like shooters, this game is for you as well. Just play it.

I'm reminded of an old Meme. " I need a better sword to beat a monster, but I need to beat a monster to get a better sword. 'congrats. you've played every RPG ever' "
well,this doesnt fit that formula. In fact, the game basically PUNISHES you for FIGHTING. So, yes, it has an XP system, Weapon system, a cool skill-slider thing to determine how much damage you do.... but you are advised to IGNORE all that, and instead click talk...click something nice....repeat until you can spare them
so, compared to classic rpg's. know how battles become boring after a while, and you end up "A" spamming to get through it? Its worse than that.
Everything else is on point. Appealing visuals, great story, lovable characters, amazing diversity.... but the actual battles, im sorry to say, suck.... unless... you know... you enjoy just skipping your turn until you can run from the fight....in every fight to get a decent ending.

Undertale is a game with a beautiful story about a boy who falls down a hole.
The story is beautiful and obsorbes you into the world of monsters.
It doesn't require a computer from RAZER or ALIENWARE or any other big pc gaming brand, a simple home computer would do.
Now, the reason i'm rating this game negatively is beacause of the gameplay
(keep in mind that i am looking at this from the gameplay perspective)
undertale's gameplay is charming at first but then it gets very VERY repititive
for example i'm wandering through a stage called "water fall" and RANDOMLY an enemy comes and attacks me
and i think to myself "alright guess i have to battle or run away" and being a completionist I decided to battle
spoiler alert I die. The game restarts from my last save and I go through the same stage yet again and encouter the same enemy. This happens A LOT in Undertale.
Sure some of the bosses and other char's have different variants of the gameplay but its somewhat similar in nature.
The game itself isn't horrible but the core feature, the GAMEPLAY makes it a little...annoying
Then again the game isn't made specifically for its gameplay but for its story and that is why I IMPLORE you not to watch any videos or gameplay about it. (except the trailer)

with that I end my review on undertale by saying "if you like game's that a story driven and has an annoyingly repititve combat this is for you"

It's a very solid RPG with memorable characters, interesting mechanics and decent replayability. It plays a lot like a Mother game mixed with Shin Megami Tensei. You can choose to kill your enemies or talk your way out of battles. The moral choice is incredibly obvious, which is one of the game's greatest flaws. However, the most interesting mechanic is the fact that you have the opportunity to dodge enemy attacks in a bullet-hell minigame. Each enemy has a different variation on the mini game, and some bosses completely change up the way the mechanic works. Equipment and leveling up is pretty basic and dull, and you don't even level up if you opt to save enemies. Overall, though, it's an interesting spin on the basic indie RPG fare you see on the market.
It's also worth noting that the game remembers things that you do, regardless of whether or not you reload your save after making a bad choice. At one point, I accidentally killed a character and reloaded my game after realizing my mistake. After successfully getting past the aforementioned segment without the character dying, a character in the game mentioned that they knew that I had saved and reloaded, adding a creepy fourth wall-breaking element to the whole experience. This is one of my favorite uses of the fourth wall in the game, as it's not cheap or cheesy, but rather subverts player expectations and makes them question many of the methods we gamers use in RPGs.
The game's issues may turn some people off, however. First, if you're looking for a decent plot, look elsewhere. I'll have the rabid community breathing down my neck for this one, but the plot is incredibly standard, predictable and sometimes even goofy. The characters are what you'll want to play this game for, as they're memorable and often dynamic. Another element that's disappointing is the morality system. This game markets its morality system to hell, and even the Steam description reads, "UNDERTALE! The RPG game where you don't have to destroy anyone." Just with that, it's quite obvious what you're supposed to do to get the best ending. The other main ending in the game will only be pursued by completionists, as nobody is truly evil enough to unknowingly pursue it. The neutral endings in the game are varied, but ultimately brief and without closure. A vast majority of people are intelligent enough to get the best ending, so the neutral endings aren't going to be seen (even though they have little to offer) by many. I see people praising Undertale's morality system, and I question why it fascinates them so much. It's your average good/neutral/evil ending system that we've seen in so many games, and this isn't even the first time an RPG has let you talk your way out of a battle (Shin Megami Tensei).
In conclusion, I like Undertale. I think it has interesting gameplay mechanics and a lovable cast of characters. Most people will probably enjoy this game, but if you're looking for a good plot or interesting morality system, look elsewhere. Also, stay away from the fanbase. For your own good.

I don't recommend this game. I bought it because of all the hype, and I enjoyed the demo, but I was disappointed with my purchase. I will say that this game is
worth $10 to me.
The game is not much longer than the demo. Imagine the demo as one 'zone', you go through about 3 and a half more zones after the demo section in the full game. Pokemon is already a short game. Imagine completing the 4th gym battle, and then the game ends. That's how I felt in Undertale, going into what turned out to be the final section of the game, I figured I was maybe 25%, at worst 50% done with the game.
For example, the idea of some of the puzzles are very interesting, and you could imagine a challenging implementation of them. However the progression of the puzzles in the game go from "very easy" to "easy". Now you're thinking "I can't wait to see the next clever puzzle, I'm through the beginning of the game, so it'll probably be challenging!" and then the game ends and there are no more puzzles. In this way, something that is good about the game becomes a bad thing.
Also, the parts of the game I found enjoyable (the jokes and creativity of the fights) are a one time thing. I personally wouldn't watch a stand up comedy, and then watch it again. You already know all the jokes so it won't be anywhere near as fun.

The way this game is developed puts its potential out of the equation. It'll never feel like a full fledged game and Garry, the founder of the studio behind the game is to blame.
Core points:
. Garry has all this at his disposal and instead of spending at least some of it to help improve the development of the game, the facepunch team has kept developing Rust as if it was an indie game. In the past, Garry has been under fire for that very reason and his defense was basically "
".
There's no playtesting environment in Rust. Updates come out of the blue, many times undocumented and almost always there's something breaking the meta or the game entirely. Developers don't get to consult players before implementing features and also don't perform extensive testing from what it seems. Hotfixes however, are rare. Facepunch really sticks to the schedule with patches even if that means leaving the game broken for weeks.
You've probably heard of Unity already. It's the go-to game engine if you're a beginner in programming. It's mostly prominent among mobile games but some popular singleplayer titles have also come out of it. Well, the thing with this engine is that its toolset isn't ideal for open world FPS games. There are severe limitations and this is already showing from early access. Most importantly, server infrastructure and optimization are very, very bad and set a terrible environment for a game that requires good reflexes when interacting with other players in a competitive environment.
I have a R9 290 and an FX 8350, averaging FPS well below 60 (40is) on minimum settings (which makes the game look terrible BTW, everything is like it's made out of playdoh) with severe lag spikes that make fps. Anything in this game can cause FPS drops, even jumping causes engine lag for ♥♥♥♥s sake... Imagine having to defend yourself in FPS style combat under such conditions. And playing on official servers is just worse.
There's no infrastructure provided by the developers for a server to actually be good. There are many fans doing their best to host good servers but the cheap VPS they can afford aren't really made for gaming. The most populated servers are the game's official ones, those are stable in terms of response times but performance is just bad. As I said earlier, server infrastructure is bad. This makes it so that servers that aren't restarted every half a day or so cause huge performance drops to users playing on it. Facepunch are really inexperienced with large-scale online games and it shows by how bad their server client is.
The  direction this game is going to follow is entirely unclear. Garry has stated that he doesn't like having a roadmap; which must be because facepunch can't keep promises. Not a single one of the significant concept designes published by Rust's artists has been implemented after the initial release. Updates after 2015 have mostly been introducing minor or barely noticeable changes. After a certain point, it felt like updates stopped being worked on as much as they used to and attempts to introduced new elements always break the game (look at the recent XP update for a prime example of that).

Its amazing how a great game can go from good to bad so simply. I have had issues with alot of the new content since its adaption from Legacy. Some have been fixed others seem to remain as permanant reminders of a game that still in its alpha-beta stages. The Devs while capable programmers seemed to have lost sight on the playability of the game for small clan or solo players. Back in legacy there was only one real way to raid a base and that was to fight your way up, this worked because damage was focused on a singular path, but since the introduction of rockets you can just mow down a whole base from a safe distance and the bigger the clan the more rockets youll own thus giving even a group of three or four people no chance to make a base big enough to withstand an attack should it be raided.
Then theres the insta wall, im talking 2 story high solid stone or wood walls. Just dropped down anywhere outside a build zone as a baricade for raiders, the realism in this is so broken which in turn makes the game broken as well.
Then theres the other implementations that come and go like the xp system, ladders on any, wall able to build thatch within build zones, like really thats just offline raiding simplified. All these add up to the devs struggling to balance the game by over complicating it or bringing elements that may seem realistic but in a game  just make bad play.
Then theres the grinding, long before I gave up trying to defend a base I grew bored of grinding for materials. This review is based on single-player experience only.
Aside from being repetitive and boring, the game is plagued by some of the most obvious design flaws, that one would think would have been easily spotted and fixed so long after the game was released, but... no.
- Picking up items, cycling through weapons and collision detection are extremely glitchy and will cause countless deaths.
- Waypoint system and fast travel are awful and force you to drive or walk for hours and hours.
- Loot and enemies in an area will respawn within minutes of clearing it.
- DLC high-level areas being available since the beginning of the game: "Oh, did you accidentally press a wrong waypoint in the fast travel map, 10 minutes into the game? Well enjoy this cutscene that spoils key moments of the main storyline."
On the plus side, it is quite addictive, aesthetically pleasing, and with great voice-acting.
Overall, it should have been marketed exclusively as an MMO, because that's what it feels like, and a mediocre one at that. Then perhaps people like me who hate MMOs would avoid it, and the game in turn would avoid a negative review.

The way this game is developed puts its potential out of the equation. It'll never feel like a full fledged game and Garry, the founder of the studio behind the game is to blame.
Core points:
. Garry has all this at his disposal and instead of spending at least some of it to help improve the development of the game, the facepunch team has kept developing Rust as if it was an indie game. In the past, Garry has been under fire for that very reason and his defense was basically "
".
There's no playtesting environment in Rust. Updates come out of the blue, many times undocumented and almost always there's something breaking the meta or the game entirely. Developers don't get to consult players before implementing features and also don't perform extensive testing from what it seems. Hotfixes however, are rare. Facepunch really sticks to the schedule with patches even if that means leaving the game broken for weeks.
You've probably heard of Unity already. It's the go-to game engine if you're a beginner in programming. It's mostly prominent among mobile games but some popular singleplayer titles have also come out of it. Well, the thing with this engine is that its toolset isn't ideal for open world FPS games. There are severe limitations and this is already showing from early access. Most importantly, server infrastructure and optimization are very, very bad and set a terrible environment for a game that requires good reflexes when interacting with other players in a competitive environment.
I have a R9 290 and an FX 8350, averaging FPS well below 60 (40is) on minimum settings (which makes the game look terrible BTW, everything is like it's made out of playdoh) with severe lag spikes that make fps. Anything in this game can cause FPS drops, even jumping causes engine lag for ♥♥♥♥s sake... Imagine having to defend yourself in FPS style combat under such conditions. And playing on official servers is just worse.
There's no infrastructure provided by the developers for a server to actually be good. There are many fans doing their best to host good servers but the cheap VPS they can afford aren't really made for gaming. The most populated servers are the game's official ones, those are stable in terms of response times but performance is just bad. As I said earlier, server infrastructure is bad. This makes it so that servers that aren't restarted every half a day or so cause huge performance drops to users playing on it. Facepunch are really inexperienced with large-scale online games and it shows by how bad their server client is.
The  direction this game is going to follow is entirely unclear. Garry has stated that he doesn't like having a roadmap; which must be because facepunch can't keep promises. Not a single one of the significant concept designes published by Rust's artists has been implemented after the initial release. Updates after 2015 have mostly been introducing minor or barely noticeable changes. After a certain point, it felt like updates stopped being worked on as much as they used to and attempts to introduced new elements always break the game (look at the recent XP update for a prime example of that).

9/10 this game is incredible.
Rust is one of the most enjoyable and dynamic survival games available right now and it shows as soon as you enter the game. Going from a naked spawn with a rock to an armored badass with an AK takes time, patience, a lot of effort, and a lot of skill. Keeping your stuff after you've acquired it is an even further challenge. All of this makes rust a fast-paced, adrenaline fueled race to the top of the item chain, with much much more to do in between. Just watch out for the bears.

Rust is a survival game. You start with a rock and a torch. Where you came from, what you did before is unknown, but now you stand on a beach on an island. You obviously weren't an engineer in your past life. you have little knowledge of how to build much more than a fireplace. Your goal? Is it to hunt down other similiarly stranded people and take everything they have? No. is it to run to the nearest civilization because there are blueprints in trashcans that will teach you how to build rocket launchers? no. Your first priority is food and shelter. Cause you know, this is a survival game. Off in the distance you see a bear but it hasnt seen you. Probably a good idea to avoid it. Ah. some mushrooms on the ground. Not a steak dinner, but it is calories and energy. Because, you know...this is a survival game.
30 minutes later: You chipped away at a free trees with your rock. You knocked off some stone shards from a rocky outcropping. After some trial and error ( levelling to level 3) you manage to craft a makeshift stone axe and pickaxe. Gathering is much easier now. You have also slaughtered a pig. As night falls following your first day on this remote island, you do not have an automatic rifle. you do not have a towering stone structure to hide in. You do not have a dozen c4. Neither does any of the other people you've come across.
No. you have a 2x2 log cabin. A bow that, after some practice you've become proficient with, you have a campfire and some bacon. All in all, not bad for a few hours of work.
Knock knock knock. someone is at the door to your log cabin. You are at a crossroads. Do you greet the stranger? He is after all your fellow human, trapped in the same situation as you. What if he lacks the basic survival skills you have? What if he is still chasing chickens with a rock and about to starve? Or.. is he out there with a buddy, one with a bow and one with a salvaged sword he found in an old gun crate? Risk/reward. Realizing you have little to gain by greeting the stranger, and everything to lose. You decide to ignore the knock.
After some time, day 2 dawns. Goals for today? A makeshift furnace, smelting down some of those metal fragments you found, and securing that wooden door by replacing it with (an armored door? nope.. you've been on this island for 24 hours) a sheet metal door. No one is going to burn THAT down.
Rust is a game that is survival at its core. Whereas in the past the game was entirely focused on pvp, it has shifted into a true survival game, and I think that's fantastic.
