Here are some very good reasons why this game is absolutely horrible:
1. Player:
In DayZ you play as an autistic man with the stomach the size of a walnut. Your main goal is to find a can of food every five seconds, and if you can't keep up with this rate of 1 can per five seconds, you will die of starvation.
Your player also cannot eat while crouching or lying down. You must be at a full upright position to eat your food.
The player must also conquer the great fences. He must jam the jump key well before the fence is in site, and even then you might not jump them, but if you do you must go into a crouching postion and crawl over the fence, then proceed back to a crouching position.
2. Map
This map is uneccesarily big. You can play on a server with 64 people for at least 10 hours and maybe only find two of these people, and chances are they are going to kill you no matter what.
Let's look at an equation real quick. Take Town A, for example. You spawn there. You want to get to Town B. Well, don't even calculate anything. Just forget that nonesense because it's going to be twenty minutes of your fingers on shift + w (forward and sprint) while you wait to get to a town that might have a box of cereal in it. Wooo!
This game was actually meant to be played with a treadmill plugged in as the controller so the community could lose weight while playing a game.
3. Items
This game has more useless items in it than it does usable items. I mean, sit down and think about it. When they were developing this game, someone actually suggested they put useless ♥♥♥♥ing ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t into the game. That's not all, these bumbos put those useless items into the game. What am I going to do with a box of nails? Oh! I know I can open the box and---nope nevermind. You can't even open the box.
4. Updates
Imagine you wanna go get some fast food, so you hop in your car and head to McDonald's. You pull through the drive through lane and ask for a Big Mac, small fries, and a large sweet tea. The employee tells you your total and you pull up to the next window. She opens her window and throws in half the head of a moose, two eggs, a scalpel, the toothbrush she uses to clean her ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, and a half chewed piece of gun stuck to a melted plastic bottle cap. This is how the developers listen to the community.
5. Optimization/Graphics
I believe my four year old cousin did the concept art for this. It looks like picasso had Parkinsons Disease mixed with autism, causing him to shake and hold his brush backwards. I HIGHLY recommend throwing all of your live savings into a super nice gaming rig that can run Fallout 4 on max at 1,000 fps just to see if it can get at least 10 fps on DayZ. Seriously, it's like I'm running eight or nine different games in the background while I play this one. The frame rate should not be this low. I run Fallout 4 on max at a smooth 60fps, and could keep a game of Civ cooking in the background at at least 60 frames, then maybe have Skyrim at max with realism mods. What does DayZ give me? 18-25 frames in a city the size of the palm of my hand. What the ♥♥♥♥.
All in all. This game just sucks♥♥♥♥♥ I've put over 200 hours into it and half of them have been pressing forward + sprint while I wait for my character to sprint to a town where there might be some decent loot that I will eventually lose to the game updating or the server crashing. This game used to be very promising and now it never will become the beauty in which its potential held.
Edit: It's 2017. This game still costs more than H1Z1. Don't buy this ♥♥♥♥ing game. It is♥♥♥♥♥♥

If you're a fan of Earthbound or Mother 3, you will almost certainly enjoy this game. It's got lots of humor, puzzles and moments that tug at your heart strings. The battle system is kinda weird for an RPG, turning into a bullet hell game, and it may remind you of Touhou. It's unique because there actually are consequences for killing mons without thinking anything of it, and the game remembers that you did that in a previous run. If you're starting a genocide run (or if you kill any of the bosses on the neutral route), it will make you feel like a horrible person. You'd be surprised how a game manages to make you feel bad for killing something you know is just pixels.
The soundtrack is awesome enough to justify being a paid item on Steam and supporting the creator. My favorites are The Core, Death by Glamour, Another Medium, Megalovania, and Asgore. Spear of Justice is an honorable mention.
Start to finish, it feels kinda short, especially if you do 2 or more playthroughs in a short span of time, which I would not recommend.

You use the wood and stone from the trees and rocks to make tools.  You use the tools to gather more rock and tree.  You gather hemp to get cloth.  You combine to make bows to kill animals.  You harvest animals to get cloth, leather, meat, and bone.  You gather more.  You find other people in the game who are similar to yourself.  You work together to use harvested stone, and wood to build big bases.  You melt sulfur and metal down to make explosives.  You use explosives to raid other people's base, and once inside, take their resources to cart back to your base.  You cover your base with artwork, showing who you and your people are.
Get a microphone and strap in.  People complaining about the XP System and playing solo have not played long enough to know that this game is ever changing.  The devs are active and they have not stopped working on this amazing game.  I thouroughly have enjoyed my time spent playing this "game".

If you're a fan of Earthbound or Mother 3, you will almost certainly enjoy this game. It's got lots of humor, puzzles and moments that tug at your heart strings. The battle system is kinda weird for an RPG, turning into a bullet hell game, and it may remind you of Touhou. It's unique because there actually are consequences for killing mons without thinking anything of it, and the game remembers that you did that in a previous run. If you're starting a genocide run (or if you kill any of the bosses on the neutral route), it will make you feel like a horrible person. You'd be surprised how a game manages to make you feel bad for killing something you know is just pixels.
The soundtrack is awesome enough to justify being a paid item on Steam and supporting the creator. My favorites are The Core, Death by Glamour, Another Medium, Megalovania, and Asgore. Spear of Justice is an honorable mention.

I normally don't write reviews cause nothing ever gets me motivated enough to do so, but this game...
I played the "predecessor" Dayz Mod for Arma 2 for over 300h and had probably the greatest amount of fun in my gaming life, in that most ridiculous game ever created. Gathering resources for hours, fighting for life with crazy odds of survival, being triumphant and ecstatic over every little success only to die over bug while trying to crouch in a confined space... None of that could discourage me one bit. I just respawned, tried to gather my stuff back before the server reset and continue doing the same futile routine. With implementation of Epoch, having the possibilty to build yourself a base, preserve the resources You tried so hard to gather was probably the greatest simple idea ever. Tons of vehicles, and AI that on hardcore servers made You crawl, more often than not... In four words: mature, prudent, intelligent gameplay; with remarkable amount of fun...
But why am I expatiating like this about a game that's not the subject of this review?
Well I was really impatient to put my hands on the successor but 28 EUR seemed a bit much for a game still largely in development state. But when I got it gifted from a good friend, I immidietely immersed myself in what I thought will be unforgettable gaming experience. Eh... You know where I'm headin' with this...
Okey, let's go... Let's divide it into pros and cons for Your sake of not reading more crap:
Cons:
- Optimazation - 15 FPS most of the time on lowest settings (on GeForce 970 GTX, 16 GB DDR3 Ram, AMD 1100T)
- "No vehicles" - they're adding some on experimental servers but boy... Just imagine how much fun it is to find a wheelless truck/bus/sedan in a village with probably 10 wheels spawned on the entire map with 40 people to divide it onto. Remember to carry car battery as well cause hell... You sure want to spent next 12h repairing a car, dragging wheels from across the map just to get owned around next corner... I didn't know that post-apocalyptic world is a place where cars don't have wheels. I guess people are building wheelo-effigies or something... Priceless...
- No interactions - I mean... There is nothing to do here... Like, nothing... Get stuff, find other player, kill him, or be killed... Or befriend him and get killed by other group, or kill them and yeah...
- The Development team... I don't want this to be personal but damn... It really is You know? When people pay 30 EUR and then wait months to get a freakin' weapon mountable flashlight or a new model of sheep You know someone's taking a♥♥♥♥♥♥ I don't give a banana peel about new look of a refrigerator! If You plan to add all this "stuff" be my guest, but in the meantime give something that You can actually enjoy! And those constant assurances every other month, that the new stable fully packed update with vehicles and many other amazing features being just around the corner and then coming up empty, is a joke...
Pros:
- You don't die when trying to put new pants on.
To summarize... I am a bit mad about how it all turned out. I really, really hoped to have a good time here.
Maybe someday the game will be what they promised it to be. I'm just scared I might be a bit too old to have a desire to emulate this game on Windows 16.
And I would get by with all the missing features if the game would be optimized enough for a smooth experience but... What I hate most, is how the devs are having a blast watching us throwing our money away, giving us the minimum to keep the business going.
But then again... Can I blame them? Most of us would probably do the same. It's just sad we realize it too late.

This game tore me away from 2 faithful seasons on League of Legends faster than MC Hammer lost his fame.
Delicious FPS-based MMO that will totally fool you into thinking its not an MMO for the first 2/3 of the story quests.  Then as soon as Sanctuary lifts off you get 352101349582345 side quests that are made available.  That put me off and made me rush the story-mode then buy DLC in a hurry.
The characters are well portrayed throughout the story quests and side-missions, leading to a very entertaining story that is wrapped by the neat bow which is their social attitude towards murder, greed, envy, revenge and lust.
The visual aesthetic of this game's design never gets boring, especially the unique environments, stylized 3d characters that looked like they jumped out of a graphic novel (pen lines and all) and ad-hoc fortresses constructed by Hyperion or Bandits.  Yes, just as in all MMOs, the mobs basically repeat themselves with different names, slightly stronger attacks (Shock Nomadic, Caustic Goliath) but the variations on the theme are hardly boring; hell one of the best parts of the battle gameplay is letting a Goliath kick the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of everything you run into and then turn around and unload on them all.
I look forward to hitting 50+ in this game, currently lvl 34 Axton and loving every minute of it.  BUY THIS GAME.

Rust is a demanding game. If you can live with its demands,  you'll have a blast. If not, you're either going to be disappointed, or you're going to find yourself at a serious disadvantage against everyone who can (which, depending your attitude towards masochism, could actually be a huge plus).
Here's what Rust demands from you:
1) That you play regularly, preferably at least 2-3 hours daily
2) That you play with a group, not solo. If you're adamant about lone-wolfing, prepare for regular heartbreak.
3) That you be able to handle regular, consistent griefing, raiding and KOS, accepting it all as part of the game
4) That you accept that it is a work in progress, and are ready to stay on top of its regular updates.
If you can accept these demands, what awaits you is challenging, rewarding and ultimately fun experience.
My overall rating: 8,5/10

I figured it would be a good idea to write a quick review.
I bought this game a year ago, maybe one and a half, not quite sure though.
Pro's first:
The idea of the game is great, so is the flora and fauna with the new renderer coming, it should be even more enjoyable.
You have lots of items, lots of crafting, and an insanely big, open-world map.
Now the con's:

Bug fixes, renderer, yeah even the Beta itself has been promised for the end of 2015, now look what we got!
I am really disappointed by now, and I wish I could get my money back, but as you can see, I have played lots of hours in this game.
But thats more because I am in a group of people, and for a period of a few months, the game was quiet enjoyable and we played almost every day cause it was fun.
Long story short:
I do not recommend this game in the current state, wait until the Beta is released, which will only take until 2025 as the developers most likely throw new content like weapons and stuff in there, instead of just maintain the game's performance.
They should focus on building a solid foundation, instead of putting more flowers into the garden.
With all the con's erased, DayZ has the potential of beeing a great, and I mean a real ♥♥♥♥ing great game.
It can be real fun, but right now, its disappointment about the games progress.
This was my first review, I hope it was helpful.

If you read one review, make sure it's this one.
Liked the Arma 2: DayZ Mod? Well, me too! However I was wrong in thinking that the Standalone would be a step in the right direction. When I purchased this game, I'd waited so long for it to be released, and knew it was still in development, so I didn't mind the bugs, glitches, or clunky gameplay. This was just a part of the Alpha stage, and to be expected.
As time passed, I watched the development blogs on Youtube to see what was being improved upon or fixed... but for three years I've been sorely disappointed. Core issues have not been addressed, bugs have been left alone, glitches ignored, while secondary issues have been focused upon. In a game that barely functions at times, adding extra content, shiny visual effects, and worst of all, modeling characters to look like the developers themselves, isn't very good at all is it? No, it's not. It's shockingly unacceptable.
This should not still be an "Early Access" Alpha, when the gears of development have grinded to a halt. Customers have been let down, money has been wasted, and the hopeful gamers who bought it, have been pretty much betrayed by the development team that seem to have run away with our money and gone into exile in a far off land, away from the angry mobs.
That's as polite as I can be.

DayZ is one of the most mentionworthy PC games ever created.  No title, early access or otherwise, will have produced the sheer quantity of laughs, tense moments, tears of rage and game-until-dawn sessions that DayZ has in it's lifetime.  More so, because it's real life hasn't officially even started yet.  Everyone has either played DayZ, or heard of DayZ, because it's a PC gaming phenomenon.  It is a bellweather for a PC gaming movement which has been long in the waiting for many gamers, like me.
If you're reading reviews because you *really* don't know what DayZ is all about and are considering purchasing it, I will give a little detail.  It's a brutal survival simulator where you must keep your equipment dry, find food and water, keep from getting ill, or find medicine, bandage your wounds before you lose consciousness, administer a (correctly typed) blood-bag to your friend if they're dying, craft your own clothes from tanned skins, save your rotted plants for fertilized in your next crop, build a secret cache and make cautious missions to collect goodies and all the while, keep eyes in the back of your head because if you are seen by another player, they WILL come for you.
If all of that sounds good, yes, buy this game and don't look back.  Welcome to Chernarus, prepare to die.
The state of the game is pretty good, really, but there are many planned features still on the way over the next year, and many existing features which are temporarilty turned off, for the sake of the alpha.  Weather, diseases etc are either off or operating in a very limited sense, while new features are debugged.  The performance is still not great, but if you have a decent gaming rig you will find it mostly runs just fine.  (I have a GTX780, 16GB ram and a 3.3GHz hex core, don't hate).
Final and most compelling piece of evidence for why DayZ is a must play?  Take a look at the endless list of negative reviews and tally up those who have logged over 100 hours in-game before posting the ASCII guy pooping with "DayZ suxx."  That's what happens.  100 hours later you're♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥because you died, but at 300 hours you're in love with it again.. Fall out of love at 375 hours, and so on..
Me?  550 hours and still think DayZ has potential to continue to be the most engaging game ever made.

You harvest animals to get cloth, leather, meat, and bone.  You gather more.  You find other people in the game who are similar to yourself.  You work together to use harvested stone, and wood to build big bases.  You melt sulfur and metal down to make explosives.  You use explosives to raid other people's base, and once inside, take their resources to cart back to your base.  You cover your base with artwork, showing who you and your people are.
Get a microphone and strap in.  People complaining about the XP System and playing solo have not played long enough to know that this game is ever changing.  The devs are active and they have not stopped working on this amazing game.  I thouroughly have enjoyed my time spent playing this "game".

I really, really love Undertale, ever since I played it until the end. And now that I got to a certain ending, I believe it's best for me to not disturb their peace anymore.
On to the review:
Gameplay: 9/10
The way the game plays, is that it allows you to either go play the game peacefully, or kill anything in your way, whatever fancies you. When you're being attacked, which in other games, you'd simply get hit, or sometimes miss. But in Undertale, you can avoid enemy attacks in a Bullet-Hell fashion. It does give you a better feeling of 'avoiding attacks', which in other games, you simply get hit, or if you're lucky, they miss or you block. The game even states the things that you've done in your previous save, even when you "reset" your progress. Not only that, but most of your decisions, including the enemy's fate, can change the outcome of the game. The only bad for the gameplay I can think of, is that it does get a little irittating to repeat the game over again just to see different results, but I can only say that as a minor thing, as there's not 105 endings or whatever, just only 3 endings.
Characters: 9.5/10
Most of the characters are funny, but are all well-written. Nothing much to say. The only downside is that I personally think that Sans is overrated, you know, the punny skeleton fella. He's not bad or anything, he's a great character, he's just... overrated. Again, nothing much at all. On to the next one.
Story: 9/10
Depending on what choices you did, you can go through the game with 3 routes: Genocide, Neutral, and True Pacifist. As the names suggest, one of those endings will trigger depending on what you do to the enemies. Genocide triggers when you kill everything, True Pacifist triggers when you don't kill any enemies, befriend all the characters and do certain tasks meet the requirements, and Neutral is to simply go through the game by killing few enemies, or no one at all, but not do any of the tasks. Unless you go Genocide, the game literally remembers EVERYTHING you've done, even after resetting the entire game. Would explain why and how, but I don't want to spoil too much.
Soundtrack: 10/10
Arguably, in my opinion, the best part about the game. There are a LOT of times where the music fits the mood in certain places. Remember the different routes? Well, depending on which route you go through, it will sound different. For example, Genocide will have a very eerie tone on most of the music. It's pretty good, and it fits in most of the moods, especially depending on your actions.
Overall, it's really good, but I feel as if the majority of the community ruined the game. Overrated is something I would say about the game, but it's just good.
Verdict:
9/10

Rust is a demanding game. If you can live with its demands,  you'll have a blast. If not, you're either going to be disappointed, or you're going to find yourself at a serious disadvantage against everyone who can (which, depending your attitude towards masochism, could actually be a huge plus).
Here's what Rust demands from you:
1) That you play regularly, preferably at least 2-3 hours daily
2) That you play with a group, not solo. If you're adamant about lone-wolfing, prepare for regular heartbreak.
3) That you be able to handle regular, consistent griefing, raiding and KOS, accepting it all as part of the game
4) That you accept that it is a work in progress, and are ready to stay on top of its regular updates.
If you can accept these demands, what awaits you is challenging, rewarding and ultimately fun experience.
My overall rating: 8,5/10

DayZ is one of the most mentionworthy PC games ever created.  No title, early access or otherwise, will have produced the sheer quantity of laughs, tense moments, tears of rage and game-until-dawn sessions that DayZ has in it's lifetime.  More so, because it's real life hasn't officially even started yet.  Everyone has either played DayZ, or heard of DayZ, because it's a PC gaming phenomenon.  It is a bellweather for a PC gaming movement which has been long in the waiting for many gamers, like me.
If you're reading reviews because you *really* don't know what DayZ is all about and are considering purchasing it, I will give a little detail.  It's a brutal survival simulator where you must keep your equipment dry, find food and water, keep from getting ill, or find medicine, bandage your wounds before you lose consciousness, administer a (correctly typed) blood-bag to your friend if they're dying, craft your own clothes from tanned skins, save your rotted plants for fertilized in your next crop, build a secret cache and make cautious missions to collect goodies and all the while, keep eyes in the back of your head because if you are seen by another player, they WILL come for you.
If all of that sounds good, yes, buy this game and don't look back.  Welcome to Chernarus, prepare to die.
The state of the game is pretty good, really, but there are many planned features still on the way over the next year, and many existing features which are temporarilty turned off, for the sake of the alpha.  Weather, diseases etc are either off or operating in a very limited sense, while new features are debugged.  The performance is still not great, but if you have a decent gaming rig you will find it mostly runs just fine.  (I have a GTX780, 16GB ram and a 3.3GHz hex core, don't hate).
Final and most compelling piece of evidence for why DayZ is a must play?  Take a look at the endless list of negative reviews and tally up those who have logged over 100 hours in-game before posting the ASCII guy pooping with "DayZ suxx."  That's what happens.  100 hours later you're♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥because you died, but at 300 hours you're in love with it again.. Fall out of love at 375 hours, and so on..
Me?  550 hours and still think DayZ has potential to continue to be the most engaging game ever made.

Forever loading. From the moment I pressed 'Play" in my Steam client to the moment after the map is done loading and I'm able to move around without lag is around 10-15 minutes. Even then, moving to a new area causes more loading. All that after having to force close the game because it stopped responding, twice.
The Stories. I'm sure you saw some stories on the internet about some crazy battle happening at the air base or someone escaping from their would-be captors; none of that happens. What happens is, you either get killed by a player after spawning or you run across the map for a long time finding bits and pieces of good loot and by then you're bored of the game.

Unfortunately, the developers have decided to move this game in a direction that forces a specific type of play and makes it very difficult for new players to become involved with the game. The constant focus on rewarding large clans and groups, while nerfing the early game for new players is ruining what made rust great. The flexibility to play the game the way you want.
Most recently with the new XP system and changes to early game weapons they made it so a new player literally has no way to defend themselves when they start. They must farm or gather to get enough resources to level up and craft a spear. Usually just to give up these resources to other players before they can even craft a spear. This is made even worse by the fact that the XP system clearly rewards larger groups who can coordinate the XP sharing to quick level their members.
I honestly hope this game turns around because it is one of my top games of all time. Let's hope the developers pull their head out of the sand long enough to see they have something that can be great.

Undertale is a nothing short of a beautiful artistic piece that breaks traditional RPG elements and tests the morality of the player better than almost any other game before it.
Its combat is unique, thrilling and not once was it boring, and the characters are so likeable and engaging that killing them is simply unthinkable (to me, at least). Initially, when I began my first playthrough, I decided I liked Undertale and I would return to it after the credits rolled to attempt the 'genocide run'. Little did I know how much i would come to adore every character in this entire experience (bar one, and those who have played the game will know exactly who I'm talking about).
Because that's what this game is: an EXPERIENCE. It is important to EXPERIENCE this game for yourself while knowing nothing about it beforehand.
If I had any gripes with the game at all, it would be that a character named Alphys talks WAY too much in one of the later stages, breaking the immersion a little and causing me to say out loud, "Jeez, could you shut the f*ck up?".
So if you are intrigued by this little indie title, don't look anything up about it. Just buy the game ASAP, boot it up and enjoy the cr*p out of it, because this is one game that I can safely say:
This is absolutely worth your time.
Overall Score: 9/10

Undertale has been a big internet phenomenon for a while now. Every detail of the game has fanwork and has many analyzes on it. To be honest, when I first saw the storepage it didn't looked that special to me. Now that I have played it I can say my view on the game has changed.
The game is an old school RPG with bullethell gameplay. You, the main character, have fallen into a world of monster, which you have to escape. On your journey you will encounter many monster that you can choose to kill or spare through silly interactions.
Story and narrative are the biggest part of this game. The storytelling is done through conversations, gameplay and interactions with objects. What I really enjoy about the story is that even though the premise of escaping a place full of monsters is cliché, the game progresses in really unexpected ways.
The whole game has this charming, kid-friendly humour, making fun of the characters and you the player. The use of humour had me exploring everything that I could just so that I could find something new and funny. Even though the story is filled with humour, there are still enough serious parts to keep it interesting. The game kept referencing my previous actions in-game, amazing me with how well connected everything is. Every character you encounter really shows a lot of their own personality, making each one memorable. This means that I am sure to play this game again in the future with a different playstyle, because not only does it have a different ending but the adventure changes based on your playstyle.  ( I have heard that the monsters will even remember things from your previous playthroughs! )
Gameplay comprises of walking around and encountering various monsters. When you are in a fight with a monster you can choose to attack them using timing or you can choose to act to try to get them to stop attacking you. When you are getting attacked by the monsters you play as a hearth, dodging projectiles. While this doesn't sounds that interesting, it is really creative and outside the box. Additionally the monster attacks really suits the monster's character. Apart from these core mechanics the game also includes puzzles, mostly to add variety as it doesn't really add much else. The choice of graphical style really suits the game and adds to the charm.
The sound design is another really strong part of the game , which contributes to the overall feel. Each piece of music suits every character and its situation. I found the music so catchy that after I finished the game I still wanted to listen to them. There are also  small, subtle sound effects that really add to the charm of the environments and  the interactions.
There is no option menu in Undertale, just a single option whether to have the game fullscreen or in window mode. Also the game is only able to be viewed as a square, so there are borders on widescreen. I guess this is due to how the old school RPGs were.
The amount of value this game gives means I can say it is really worth its asking price. The game takes around 10 hours to complete and with the different experiences resulting from different playstyles it really adds to the replay value. Even though I have only played once through, I can already say it is worth the price for the amount of enjoyment
In conclusion, even though Undertale didn't catch me when I first saw it, I have totally fallen in love with it, and is one of the rare games I definitely be playing again. The game is just filled with charm, creativity and everything is amazingly well connected. What I still have trouble believing is that the game was, for the most part, made by one person (even the soundtrack!).

Love it or hate it, Day Z has many issues. I was going to take a wait and see approach with this game as it is still in alpha. But the last straw for me was the malware that comes along with this game. On 1/14/16 I launched the game and Steam told me that the game failed to launch. My AV popped up and warned me that Trojan.gen.SMH was detected in the dayz.be.exe file. This file has to do with the Battle eye anti cheat service that Day Z uses. While my AV was removing this file it did what trojans do, It tried to access my AV files and alter them through EVGA precision X. Precision X has never tried to access any files on my computer before this incident and has not tried to again since my AV got rid of the dayz.be.exe file.
I went to the Day Z official site and was directed by the moderator to run the Steam validation tool and did so. Immediately my AV popped up when the tool tried to reinstall the dayz.be.exe file, and immediately my EVGA Precision X program tried to access the files for my AV. This is not a false positive. from my AV. When you are alerted of a Trojan and your AV files are attacked there is no explanation for this other than it being what your AV says it is. Malware.
For that reason alone. I can not recommend this game to anyone. For those who would say: "My AV didn't see anything wrong, your AV sucks." Just because your AV didn't catch the malware, doesn't mean that you are not effected by it. You may not notice anything wrong with your computer, but that's the point isn't it? Effective malware isn't going to send avatar's dancing accross your screen to taunt you. It's going to try to stay undetected for as long as possible.
I will never buy another Bohemia Interactive product again.

It is then obvious that the game has been destroyed by not only the developers of the game but mostly from the community (us) who form huge clans. So, for me, typing a review for this game is rather hard.
I've played so many hours, and enjoyed the hell out of it, however i can't say it doesn't have it's shortcomes. For those who are lazy and dont want to read the whole bloody thing, i'd give it a 8,5-9 out of 10.
So, kicking it off with art style, shall we?
Having played the original borderlands -not so much, but yeah-, i found the art style familiar. The comic-ish way of presenting items, the character and monster design, they look familiar and i blent in fast. However the quallity was far superior to this of the original borderlands, making it a nice place to look at.
But that was simply the first view...  When the game finaly opened up, and i took a look arround every place and every map, i was like, "Damn. This, is trully some next level sh*t". Every area is somehow unique, it rewards you if you explore, and it's damn a pleasure to do so. All of the enviroments are pretty, the lighting looks pretty good, and the day-night cycle make the game come to life.
Gameplay wise, now.
The shooting mechanics are rather... Odd, in Borderlands 2. Different weapon manifactures give different handling, creating a huge world of guns to check, loot, and shoot. The weapon system has a lot of depth, but mainly works like this:
The main body, depending on the company and the rarity level, is the main factor. White: Low damage Green: Higher Damage (including handling and everything) Blue: Even higher damage, Purple: Even bloody higher damage, Orange: Damn high damage, Ciel: Damn hell damage.
All of those work with the help of a grip, a barrel that changes the way bullets behave, so on and so forth. Add elemental damage, and you get a huge ammount of depth and searching to do.
Now, compare this games system with the originals, i have to admit i preffered the other one. I mean, this way weapons are balanced so on and so forth, but with the old random system, you could get this one gun that would keep up for so damn many levels, something that doesn't happen here. But i guess that's a complaint i personally have, well.
Now, on the skill trees. What can i say...
I have played alot of the siren and some of the mechromancer class, and i had some fun with both.
Now, why there is no skill system i don't get, meaning that there is only 1 active skill while all of the others are passive. One excuse would be that it had to be played on consoles where you dont have enough keys to bind, but still, that's not a good enough of an excuse. This is the pc port, to begin with, and that is something that i don't accept. One active skill on a 2012 game is rather dissapointing. The passive skills and all of the general upgrades are fun, making every character unique and fun to play. Some of them may need a change of gear, a change of approach, so on and so forth. Every skill tree requires different player skill levels and techiiques, which make it fun. Also, some may seem weaker than others -zero's deception for example-, but given the right player, the character is stil viable and strong, even without his active.
Now, to the characters themselfs.
Borderlands actually has one of the fullest casts i've seen in a game, with a character for everyone. I got to love Mr Torgue, not to mention Gaige, and of course an all time favorite Tiny Tina. The voice acting is decent, writing is damn good and funny in too many points. Followed by many refferences, jokes, and a helluva lot more jokes, Borderlands 2 is one of the best written games for me in the past few years.
Now, moving to the "open world" feature of the game.
Side quests, roaming... All of those things are in borderlands 2, and complete one of the best packs i've had fun with, like, ever. Those side quests give depth and flesh pandora's universe out, they create a back story for most characters, and also give some feedback on what happened in the years between the original and this one.
What that does is, making this game much more addictive, and turning you somehow into a perfectionist without even realising it. Now, thought, a thing that may annoy some, is the fact that some quests are clearly story driven, and dont make any sence if you dont really care about the lore. Well, some, are morons.
Now, to the economy system... That's rather funny to discuss.
There are two currencies in pandora: Edirium, and Dolars. Eridium gives you the ability to buy upgrades, mainly for the space of your invertory and ammount of bullets you can carry.
Dollars work as a currency to buy anything else. Bullets themselfs, weapons, grenades, mods, so on and so forth.
Now gear in general.
I talked about the weapon system before, so lets talk about what you can have in the Borderlands Universe.
There are a few things you can carry, really. There is a grenade mod, that makes your grenades behave in different ways. From grenades that follow enemies, explode, and come back to replenish your health, to grenades that gather nearby enemies and explode in a small radius arround them, but dealing massive ammounts of damage, grenade mods make for a fun addition, sometimes even necessary piece of equipment.
Shields, is what basically keep you alive. Shields are somewhat like an extra bar of regenerating health, and have their own special abilities. From ones with huge capacity but reducing your overal health, to ones that once they are depleted they can make your meele attacks create explossions (!), Shields are fun to mess with, but once they are depletted you will usually die since your health is going down pretty fast.
After that, there are relics. Relic gives small bonuses, over a few minor things, such as pistol damage, clip capacity, so on and so forth.
Now, there are also the class mods. Those are intresting, since they change the way your skills, passive and active work, but basically work in the way of simply buffing some of the stuff, reducing some of the depth they would create.
All of those items are droppable, and have rarities exatcly like weapons do, that make them rather fun to loot too.
Now, overally, borderlands 2 is a pretty awsome game. It's worth the 30$ price tag to the fullest extend, and the DLC's -i have only played Tiny tina's attack on Dragon keep- are fully worth their price as well.
Going on to enemy types, since i dont want to spoil anything, i will say a few things. All of the mobs in this game have a critical point, that deals double damage. Between creatures those differ, and on some it might be hard to find them. THere is a huge variety on how they scale in level, inteligence, and weapons. In general, the AI might sometimes leave you short handed because most of the enemies lie out of cover, but usually so do you. So not taking advantage in FPS elements like cover is rather a viable option, since you can rely on the RPG nature of it.
Now, a last thing i will mention, is the death system. Once both your health and shields are depletted, you fall into "second wind mode". Basically, you can't take this damage in this mode, but you have a certain timer. If some other players comes over and revives you, or you kill an enemy in this time, you get a "second wind", which actually deploys your shields and some of your health. If you die multiple times in a small ammount of time, than your time in "second wind mode" is reduced significantly.
Now, if you haven't played borderlands 2, and are intrested is on RPG's, that BUY THIS GAME! I love it, played hours of it, and will keep playing. So, no matter some issues this game has, it's still one of the best games i've played in the past years.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

Undertale is great game for any player, RPG fan or not. The choice of fight or mercy is also a new and innovative evolution to RPG gameplay and may likely be featured in other games in the near future. That's not the only typical choice in Undertale however, your choices and actions within the game greatly interfere with the games story and can drastically change the games ending. Although choices and effect in games isn't new, Toby Fox takes it to the next level by setting it as a 'route' or 'run' feature, allowing pacifist, nuetral or genocide. The game's story is also extremely engrossing to the player, it's wacky and goofy on the outside, hiding a dark and ominous game underneath. That may not be new to RPGs either but it works well with this game, a touch of light heartedness in a dark land greatly changes the effect it has on the player. The game also shocks you with strange reveals such as LvL/LOVE actually meaning 'Level of Voilence' and ExP/EXPERIENCE POINTS actually meaning 'execution points'. I recommend this game to anyone who's prepared to have a good and challenging RPG experience and I also recommend it to people looking for something cheap, new and unique to play.

Undertale is great game for any player, RPG fan or not. The choice of fight or mercy is also a new and innovative evolution to RPG gameplay and may likely be featured in other games in the near future. That's not the only typical choice in Undertale however, your choices and actions within the game greatly interfere with the games story and can drastically change the games ending. Although choices and effect in games isn't new, Toby Fox takes it to the next level by setting it as a 'route' or 'run' feature, allowing pacifist, nuetral or genocide. The game's story is also extremely engrossing to the player, it's wacky and goofy on the outside, hiding a dark and ominous game underneath. That may not be new to RPGs either but it works well with this game, a touch of light heartedness in a dark land greatly changes the effect it has on the player. The game also shocks you with strange reveals such as LvL/LOVE actually meaning 'Level of Voilence' and ExP/EXPERIENCE POINTS actually meaning 'execution points'. I recommend this game to anyone who's prepared to have a good and challenging RPG experience and I also recommend it to people looking for something cheap, new and unique to play.

First of all, this game is not even near of a finished game and honestly, I've lost my faith; I don't believe this game will ever leave early access. In conclusion, as a game I wouldn't recommend DayZ at this current state, maybe wait some time before buying it. But if you have some friends who are interested in playing this buggy mess, go ahead. You can squeeze some fun hours out of it with friends. At least I did.

I had originally given this game a negative review when the devs replaced the old blueprint system with an experience system, that was both grindy, repetitive, and made everyone want to kill themselves out of boredom. Now that it is out for good and replaced with a component based system where you actually have to look for the parts to build weapons and armor, I can finally give Rust the positive review it deserves.
Keep in mind, when you first start playing, you will have a tough time with a steep learning curve. That's ok though, since we've all been there. Eventually, through trial and error, you will hearn how to build and fight effectively enough to come out on top.
Always make sure you come out on top. Other players will not even hesitate to wipe you off the map and KoS, so don't cry on the forums when you yelled friendly at someone and they mowed you down anyways. Always make sure you're armed too.
Weapons in this game are pretty good, but recoil can be pretty tricky to control. Aiming a bow in the game is very similar to how you'd aim one in real life. The devs went through a lot of details on the guns too. There are even ricochet sounds when you shoot a rock, small sonic cracks when they zoom by you, and they even whizz through the air if one goes by you.
Overall I highly recommend Rust.

A very fun FPSRPG, with a good 2-5hrs playtime on First Playthrough, increasing to 6-10hrs and 15+hrs for True Vault Hunter (New Game+) and Ultimate Vault Hunter (New Game++, requires DLC) respectively. An Infinite amount of weaponry ranging from traditional single shot sniper-rifles,  to Legendary Class Shotguns that has exploding buckshot that explodes again. A decent variety of terrains ranging from snow, desert, and grasslands, to name a few.
My main issue with the game is the lack of enemy types, to lovingly steal a line from Yahtzee, all it seems to be is "shooting Jason Voorhees in the face" (Ignoring the quest that requires you to simply: Shoot this guy in the face.). The other problem that I have with the game is that the playable DLC (Only extra Campaigns or areas) seems to be hit or miss, but more frequently a miss. Captain Scarlett and Her Pirate's Booty and Sir Hammerlock's Big Game Hunt are both big misses because the main quest lines are boring and uninteresting and the side quests are tedious, whereas Mr. Torgue's Campaign of Carnage and Tiny Tina's Assault on Dragon Keep are sidesplittingly funny and have interesting main quest lines.

After playign this game for 30(+) hours, I can safely say that this is one of, if not the best survival game i have ever played. HOWEVER-It's core gameplay is held back by 3 things-game crashing bugs( as this is an alpha), graphical errors, where textures will look like they came off a PS2, and the abrasive community. At it's very best, Rust is an excellent survival game with smart crafting and Exp mechanics, where you find satisfaction in every inch of progress you make whether alone, or with friends that you've made. The world is beautiful and interesting, while also being frightening and hostile. You have dynamic interactions with other players ,where you have to talk and act as you would in real life in order to make allies, save your own skin, or kill to survive. I've been holding back on making this review for a long time. But, I feel like this game has proved stable and worthy enough by now.
First off, I have to say that this game is BY FAR the best multiplayer game I have EVER played. I play this game whenever I can and it never disappoints. I have been playing since October of 2015, and hopefully for many more to come. Let me get into the positives and experiences.
My Experiences-
This game is unique. You decide when you beat the game or succeed. For me, succeeding is building the best 5 layer honeycombed, double-stacked, 6x6 possible, raiding the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Zerg on the server, duo style, and then taking the crown. For you, winning could simply be succeeding in making a furnished 2x2 on a 300 pop server. I also just want to add a disclaimer that this game is VERY possible as a solo player. About 400 of my hours are from being solo on vanilla at a 120 pop server, you just have to be good and experienced. I also want to say that the community is in fact pretty ♥♥♥♥ing toxic, but I have also met a ton of awesome people from playing. Now for the professional standard of the review.
PROS-
•Best building mechanics out of ANY survival game
•Amazing gunplay, could use some balancing but for the most part very smooth
•Very nice devs. They continue to listen to the community and they are always hard at work
•PVE is starting to get rolling with elements such as chopper and animals
•Crafting system is very simple and easy to get used to. The components system is getting refined in every devblog and continues to be ironed out
•Community is a half/half. If you want to hold hands with everyone and make cottage in a meadow, join a PVE server or gtfo
•Farming is not as hard at everyone makes it out to be. Just spend 30 minutes straight of farming resources every day and you'll be more than fine
•Beautiful scenery and graphics
•Maps are very nice, especially for procedural standards
CONS-
•Can be very buggy at times aswell as exploits are getting out frequently, but that's what you sign up for when buying an early access title
•Raiding is a bit unbalanced, making it impossible for a solo or duo player survive when being pitted against a 10 man Zerg
•Animal AI is pretty ♥♥♥♥ed right now, but progress is being made big time
•Optimization is a piece of♥♥♥♥♥♥ but they try
------
Overall I defiantly recommend this game for people interested in survival/pvp games. If I wanted to rate it I would probably I've a 9/10, maybe a 10/10 when it gets to full release :)

TL;DR: A good stylistic shooter with a lot of humor and heart that is great for Co-Op, still good enough for solo. A couple of annoying problems.
=================================
I played about two hours of the first borderlands on a controller with a friend a couple of years ago and wasn't nearly as impressed with it that he was. There was some comedy there, especially with the voice acting, but I found the looting to be a little 'meh' and didn't appreciate having to open a dozen containers to get some ammo. I never picked it back up, and so wasn't expecting too much with BL2. Turns out either it's better than the first game or I didn't give its predecessor enough playtime.
I played the sequel with at least one other person, sometimes two, throughout most of the game. I think I'd like playing it solo too as the writing, voice-acting and missions are humorous enough. It's better with more than one person, though, for all the reasons a good co-op game shines. There's plenty to do and a reasonably open world in which to do it. The weapons and shields are varied beyond a few stat differences with some nice extra effects that combine with a skill tree to define characters quite a bit. Two people can have the same class of character and yet specialize in such a way to have very different play styles. There's a lot of visual customization as well if you are willing to unlock things. I'd warn that playing solo is fine for the first playthorough but becomes ridiculously hard if you don't have the right build during a subsequent harder playthrough (TVH mode).
There are some problems with the game, and most is related to the co-op, though the controls (especially for vehicles) are also awkward. Dialogue, one of the shining points of the game, can often be cut off when another player does something to activate another script (like clicking on an NPC). This can happen accidentally or if someone doesn't want to bother waiting, but there should be a way for a player to listen to major dialogues again via a log or something. Looting most things spreads them among the players, which feels right, but really good items are still up for grabs and can be ninja-ed, putting a bit of an annoying element in the co-op. I'm not sure if this is a solvable problem, and at least there is a fairly painless way to trade items. The enemies are fun and have different tactics, some less suicidal than others.
The main villian is very well done (though it would have been better for him to make some physical appearances before the end), but the plot is servicable at best with too many moving parts that make it feel overcomplicated. It barely starts before it ends, and has uneven progression. Luckily there are sidequests a plenty and the real meat of the game is in its mechanics and dialogue, not the plot per se. Dying is easy in the beginning but just costs money to undo; unless your whole team dies, you can keep sending bodies into the fray. It gets pretty expensive later on, but by then hopefully it doens't happen quite as much. More annoying were the bugs that would glitch a player through something solid and result in their death. Rare, but it happened at least twice to me over the course of a campaign. The 'second wind' capability also tends to glitch and get shortened to nothing sometimes for no reason.
There are a couple major missteps I noticed after playing the game quite a bit. The first is the flying and disappearing enemies are terrible and almost game-breaking for some builds, although a respec can help. The second may seem small but it's a really awful "puzzle" in the Tiny Tina expansion. The game lampshades previous puzzles but plays this one infuriatingly straight. It's completely unacceptable to have a crappy platform puzzle that results in death when the game penalizes the player for failing by depleting their bank account. For one reason or another a lot of deaths in this game feel unfair, especially playing solo. Leaving the "play area" that is not clearly marked, for example...
That aside, if you like stylistically goofy FPS games, it's a good pick, especially with people you know. If you don't like the genre at all or prefer realistic games, maybe not, but it wouldn't be a bad game to try at a reasonable price.

I had originally given this game a negative review when the devs replaced the old blueprint system with an experience system, that was both grindy, repetitive, and made everyone want to kill themselves out of boredom. Now that it is out for good and replaced with a component based system where you actually have to look for the parts to build weapons and armor, I can finally give Rust the positive review it deserves.
Keep in mind, when you first start playing, you will have a tough time with a steep learning curve. That's ok though, since we've all been there. Eventually, through trial and error, you will hearn how to build and fight effectively enough to come out on top.
Always make sure you come out on top. Other players will not even hesitate to wipe you off the map and KoS, so don't cry on the forums when you yelled friendly at someone and they mowed you down anyways. Always make sure you're armed too.
Weapons in this game are pretty good, but recoil can be pretty tricky to control. Aiming a bow in the game is very similar to how you'd aim one in real life. The devs went through a lot of details on the guns too. There are even ricochet sounds when you shoot a rock, small sonic cracks when they zoom by you, and they even whizz through the air if one goes by you.
Overall I highly recommend Rust.

The XP update has made clans way to too strong. The clans were already very powerful and pretty much dominated any server you played on but now tht there is an xp system that is "shared" between your whole group, clans are able to build ridiculous bases and be fully equipped with AK47's, Bolt Action Sniper Rifles, Pump Shotguns, C4, and Rockets. While you, as a solo or co-op player will have bows and at best a water pipe shotgun (if youre lucky) to defend against 5-10 people who are fully geared and prepared to raid you within 12 hours of a fresh server wipe with the best guns and armour in the game. And If you kept trying to play on that server as they got more and more powerful, it is then it is obviously hopeless as they will have so much more than you it is actually ridiculous and very salt-inducing. I have played over 150+ hours of this game and I ♥♥♥♥ing love this game, but now that the XP update now makes clans even stronger than they already were, it makes them nearly impossible to stop unless your join or form a clan of your own, which isn't in everyone's best intrest of how they want to play the game. AND SINCE WE BOUGHT THE GAME WE SHOULD BE ABLE TO PLAY IT HOW WE WANT TOO, RIGHT? WRONG. The majority of Rust players are solo or with a friend, the other 10-20% are clan members which ruin and domintate ever server they play on. They already have a MASSIVE ADVANTAGE because of their STRENGTH IN NUMBERS and now Facepunch is going to weaken primitive tools (i.e. bows, crossbows, spears) too make it eaiser for clans to get all the items in the game at an obcene rate. Oh, and expect a metal fortress with walls within 12 hours of the fresh server wipe. With this power they choose to abuse it, therefore they should'nt possess this type of power. With this power, they will kill everyone who isn't their friend or slave for absoultely no provacation or reason at all. The game is fun at first and you can really get into it, however as soon as you seen one of the massive clan bases after a fresh server wipe, and they already have guns, armour, and explosives, while you have your rock, torch, and underpowered bows, you will quickly see exactly what I'm talking about. When you have to grind for hours to level up just to get a certain item (i.e. metal door and code lock) while the clans are all 10-15 levels ahead of you with about a quarter of the effort you put into your grind, simply because of the broken shared XP system. This is a clearly unfair concept and makes clan even stronger, it then seems like the Developers don't even realize that the majority of players are solo or co-op players and thus are not willing to form a 5-10 man team just to stay alive, own a house for more than a day, and have a chance at getting good weapons and armour. You do all the work for youself, by yourself, and then they come along (they always do, no matter where you live or what you live in) and they will kill you multiple times, take everything you own, grief your house, and leave you even more behind than you already were. It's simply ridiculous. If you think I'm kidding then buy the game and see for yourself what I am talking about, the only good reviews are before the XP update, and also from clan members who don't have to do anything compared to solo and co-op players who suffer a grueling grind just to live in a house that will be raided as soon as its found by a scout by one of the clans. I only recommend this game if the XP system is fixed and solo/co-op players get some sort of adavantage or at least somewhat of a level playing field against the clans whom are already pretty much impossible to stop due to their sheer numbers and newly formed XP adavantage. If you have a clan in mind to play this game with, then sure go for it, you probably will have fun, but know that you will be aiding to the very destruction of this potentially great community and fantastic game simply for your own selfish purposes and self-gain by stepping on all the weaklings just because you obviously can. It should be renamed: Rust: A Clan's Game, as it is the only group of people who can truly enjoy Rust. TL;DR: A good stylistic shooter with a lot of humor and heart that is great for Co-Op, still good enough for solo. A couple of annoying problems.
=================================
I played about two hours of the first borderlands on a controller with a friend a couple of years ago and wasn't nearly as impressed with it that he was. There was some comedy there, especially with the voice acting, but I found the looting to be a little 'meh' and didn't appreciate having to open a dozen containers to get some ammo. I never picked it back up, and so wasn't expecting too much with BL2. Turns out either it's better than the first game or I didn't give its predecessor enough playtime.
I played the sequel with at least one other person, sometimes two, throughout most of the game. I think I'd like playing it solo too as the writing, voice-acting and missions are humorous enough. It's better with more than one person, though, for all the reasons a good co-op game shines. There's plenty to do and a reasonably open world in which to do it. The weapons and shields are varied beyond a few stat differences with some nice extra effects that combine with a skill tree to define characters quite a bit. Two people can have the same class of character and yet specialize in such a way to have very different play styles. There's a lot of visual customization as well if you are willing to unlock things. I'd warn that playing solo is fine for the first playthorough but becomes ridiculously hard if you don't have the right build during a subsequent harder playthrough (TVH mode).
There are some problems with the game, and most is related to the co-op, though the controls (especially for vehicles) are also awkward. Dialogue, one of the shining points of the game, can often be cut off when another player does something to activate another script (like clicking on an NPC). This can happen accidentally or if someone doesn't want to bother waiting, but there should be a way for a player to listen to major dialogues again via a log or something. Looting most things spreads them among the players, which feels right, but really good items are still up for grabs and can be ninja-ed, putting a bit of an annoying element in the co-op. I'm not sure if this is a solvable problem, and at least there is a fairly painless way to trade items. The enemies are fun and have different tactics, some less suicidal than others.
The main villian is very well done (though it would have been better for him to make some physical appearances before the end), but the plot is servicable at best with too many moving parts that make it feel overcomplicated. It barely starts before it ends, and has uneven progression. Luckily there are sidequests a plenty and the real meat of the game is in its mechanics and dialogue, not the plot per se. Dying is easy in the beginning but just costs money to undo; unless your whole team dies, you can keep sending bodies into the fray. It gets pretty expensive later on, but by then hopefully it doens't happen quite as much. More annoying were the bugs that would glitch a player through something solid and result in their death. Rare, but it happened at least twice to me over the course of a campaign. The 'second wind' capability also tends to glitch and get shortened to nothing sometimes for no reason.
There are a couple major missteps I noticed after playing the game quite a bit. The first is the flying and disappearing enemies are terrible and almost game-breaking for some builds, although a respec can help. The second may seem small but it's a really awful "puzzle" in the Tiny Tina expansion. The game lampshades previous puzzles but plays this one infuriatingly straight. It's completely unacceptable to have a crappy platform puzzle that results in death when the game penalizes the player for failing by depleting their bank account. For one reason or another a lot of deaths in this game feel unfair, especially playing solo. Leaving the "play area" that is not clearly marked, for example...
That aside, if you like stylistically goofy FPS games, it's a good pick, especially with people you know. If you don't like the genre at all or prefer realistic games, maybe not, but it wouldn't be a bad game to try at a reasonable price.

This game is in Alpha....  so for any review that comments on glitches, bugs, lags, lack of content, etc....   write to the developers as feedback... that's what early access Alpha is about... otherwise... just wait until it's released as a finished product..
But, for those of you that already grasp this concept....  This game only gets better... I have had it for almost two years. Yes, that is a long time for it to be in development... but, as it has progressed, it's almost as if I've had several different games to play, some more engrossing than others... i've set it down for a few months, and then been blown away when I pick it up again later...
Whether this game is worth the purchase is entirely up to your ability to enjoy the mechanics, development, fundamentals and implementation of game engine particulars....   and how much of a need you depend on from your gameplay for direction, reward, status indicators and other micro gratification and basically ego stroking.....
For those of you that get all geared up and then avoid all interaction.... I'm actually an advocate of fresh-spawning players every time they log in...  For those of you that kill anyone you meet without any interaction, I like the idea of keeping a stat record of players kills on other players on non-pvp servers and after too many violations, either barring entry to that server type or an in-game indicator of your location to all other players.
And to all those who feel the game is missing something...  just wait... it only gets better...
This is a game about survival... not killing other players... when they implement the dynamics that reward you for positive interaction and hinder you for random killing, this game will really unfold its potential.

Back in December of 2015 I bought this game on sale. I gave it a quick try for a couple hours and then stopped playing. It stayed in my library for many months before I tried it again and stuck with it. It ended up being one of the best games I've every played. It was intense, had great pvp, and it had what other survival games didn't. There were just so many aspects and things never seen before in any game let alone other survival games.  If you didn't want to grind and farm you didn't have to. If you wanted to play solo that was totally possible as well. You could play however you wanted to with several different styles to do so. I added more friends to my steam friends list from this game than all other games combined in my library in just a few months. Everything was really awesome about this game.... And then they put in the XP system. Even before they added it most people including myself protested and claimed we didn't want a grind element to the game. Not only do people starting out now have no chance to fight back but to add insult to injury I almost decided to give it one more try and put up with the xp system only I then found out they completely ruined the crossbow and waterpipe shotgun on top of it. They greatly reduced the pull out time for the waterpipe and made it so you completely can not move while reloading the crossbow. They were the only 2 weapons of defense that most of us had against these big clans that were the only people with actual guns. Facepunch recently polled twitter asking which system everyone liked better. 54 percent voted blueprints with 46 voting xp. Hopefully they revert back or fix the current system and re buff the xbow and waterpipe because as of now the game is a mess.  I'm holding onto faith that they will and if that happens then I will change this review to recommended. I understand the game is in alpha and I'm confident the devs will fix what was broken. Until then though I cannot reccomend the game. Keep an eye on the reviews and once they go back to positive pick the game up. Hopefully we can go back to raiding each other soon instead of playing mining simulator 2016.

Rust is a game that is constantly changing . As a player this makes it highly frustrating as the developers sometimes remove or change the mechanics that already work fine . The single biggest problem with Rust at the moment is that it has become somewhat of a "Battle Royale " with basebuilding. Servers dont hold their population like they used to. (In mid to late 2015, Servers would last a good 2 weeks with very few people quitting).
In my opinion this is down to a somewhat overcomplication of the key elements of rust. One of these elements being the maps. The maps in 2015 were far from perfect but what they did offer was 3 distinct biomes, Desert , Forest and Arctic . The former and latter being a place were the large groups would build their base and the forest biome being a place were smaller groups and solos would fight it out . On top of that there used to be only a few monuments and a few small radtowns on the map. This was ideal because it meant there was many areas in the map that would be secluded , but also guaranteed areas to get some good loot or have some PvP.
The new maps , while full of beautiful massive radtowns and small monuments, are flat , extremely repetitive and crowded. You could easily go to a dungeon and not see anybody and yet not find any good loot either , they are simply too big . ( Also a cause of poor performance). Hopefully in the future they give server owners the option of having the old style of proc gen maps.

After playign this game for 30(+) hours, I can safely say that this is one of, if not the best survival game i have ever played. HOWEVER-It's core gameplay is held back by 3 things-game crashing bugs( as this is an alpha), graphical errors, where textures will look like they came off a PS2, and the abrasive community. At it's very best, Rust is an excellent survival game with smart crafting and Exp mechanics, where you find satisfaction in every inch of progress you make whether alone, or with friends that you've made. The world is beautiful and interesting, while also being frightening and hostile. You have dynamic interactions with other players ,where you have to talk and act as you would in real life in order to make allies, save your own skin, or kill to survive. At its worst, Rust is an uneven, ugly cluster**** of more powerful players mowing down noobs before they can even begin building a base, all while your framrate drops and your character stops moving i nthe middle of a firefight right as you crash. This game is VERY frustrating, however once you push through the first few hours or so on a single server, and you begin building yourself up, you begin to see the fun in everything you do-the pulse pounding stress of whether your base is going to be raided-the race against tiem when you went out with all your gear and a helicopter shows up-the fight against a bear who happened to be near an airdrop with life-saving resources and weapons. All of these make the game so unique, in that you never know whats going to happen next. Overall, I say get it now, or if you're skeptical wait until it's on sale. Overall, I give it an 8 1/2 out of 10.

After finishing Undertale completely I knew I had to write a review about it. I have never written a review (with effort) before but I’m going to try to describe the game for you as objectively as possible. There will be some subjective parts but it should be obvious when I talk about my personal opinion.
Undertale is an indie RPG made by toby fox and released on 15 September 2015. It started its life as a kickstarter project on 13 June 2013. Toby fox asked for only 5000$ to make the project reality yet he received 10 times that amount. The main mechanic of this RPG is that you don’t have to kill anyone, but you can if you wish.
I want to start off with the community because it seems that this is the main reason why people are discouraged from this game. Lots of people call the Undertale fandom toxic and although it’s not the best community I’ve ever seen it’s by no means as bad as people say it is.
Yes, there are a lot of memes and♥♥♥♥♥♥posts and sometimes Undertale is being mentioned for no reason but there are also some amazing people who try to expand the story after the game ends or create amazing fan art. What I think the main reason is that the Undertale community is treated as toxic is because most people don’t realise that if someone didn’t play the game yet that they won’t understand the jokes that are being told. I can clearly see why this would be annoying but saying the community is toxic because they make references to certain moments in the game that you just don’t know about (yet) is idiotic.
At the end of the day though you shouldn’t even consider the community as a reason for not liking / not playing the game. Especially considering this is a single player game, you won’t have any interaction with the community within the game itself.
This is the main selling point for Undertale. It’s story. Here is a brief part of it to get you started: ‘Long ago, two races ruled over Earth: humans and monsters. One day, war broke out between the two races. After a long battle, the humans were victorious. They sealed the monsters underground, under Mt. Ebott, with a magic spell. After many years legends say that those who climb the mountain never return. You, the player, climb the mountain and you fall in a pit where you end up in “The underground” the place where the monsters were sealed away. Your objective? To find a way back to the surface.’
The story is perfectly designed to make any interaction the player may take feel important. Even when in battle it always feels like you are progressing the story instead of you just getting interrupted to fight someone. The characters have their own personalities and this even includes some of the random NPC’s and normal enemies. All of the characters are really likable, even if you may find some annoying at first. Some of the characters their backstories are really deep and some characters don’t even show any of their backstory making them very mysterious.
Throughout your adventure you will be faced with certain choices, the biggest and most obvious one being that you can either kill or spare your enemies. This is a very important aspect of this game. When you kill someone they are actually dead. You may have certain species of monsters that keep on reappearing but the monster that you previously killed isn’t coming back.
Almost all of the decisions you can possibly make will change the story. There are three major endings to this game: Neutral, Pacifist and Genocide. All of these endings will explain different parts of the story.
When you try to immerse yourself into the story you will be blown away by it, multiple times. I have cried when playing this game and there is no shame to it. The story is just that good. I would love to tell you at which points this happens but obvious spoiler warning. You will just have to trust me on this one.
When it comes to gameplay you have two major situations. In-battle and out-battle.
Out-battle you will run around trying to solve various puzzles to progress, interact with characters to further the story, try to find new items and better equipment. Pretty standard RPG stuff.
The puzzles are fun. Although they’re neither easy nor difficult they are still interesting to do.
In-battle you have two ways of defeating your enemies, by killing them or by sparing them.
When it comes to sparing the enemies, fights will become puzzles themselves. You will have to perform different kind of acts in order to make the enemy not wanting to fight you any longer. You will have to understand what every enemy expects out of you in order to make them merciful. Don’t worry you don’t have to search up what kind of hidden numbers of characteristics each enemy has. It all becomes obvious during the fighting itself.
If you wish to slaughter your enemies then you can do that however admittedly this is a pretty weak part of this game. Unlike other RPG where you have many different attacks and spells all with their unique stats and effects. In Undertale, you only have one way of inflicting damage. The amount of damage that you deal is based on your timing in pressing a button but other than that, actually hurting the enemy doesn’t really change that much. (You do get different timing patterns with different weapons but overall it will be very similar)
There is something really interesting though about this game and I wish that a lot more RPG’s would use a mechanic like this. In a traditional RPG, when it is your enemies turn you simply have to take the damage and hope it doesn’t kill you. In Undertale, if an enemy attacks you, you will have to dodge the attacks yourself in order to survive. You will be a small heart that you can move around to avoid the projectiles that the enemy shoots at you. It’s basically a bullet-hell. The game will start off easy on you but the dodging can become really difficult later on in the game. The great part about this is that you can improve your own skills when fighting the enemy instead of mindless grinding to boost your characters stats.
If you don’t like chiptune then you probably won’t like the songs ON THEIR OWN. You see we are talking about a game with a retro style so the chiptune fits in. However more importantly is that the songs always seem to match the situations in the game perfectly. Yea I know that that is what video game music has to do but I have never seen so perfectly done as in Undertale. When it comes to the soundtrack that you can buy separately I’ll admit that it is a bit overprized.

Undertale has become my favourite single player game of all time and for good reasons. The fighting elements are interesting and skillful and the story will make you curious and wanting to get more. The game is also decently large with an average of 21 hours of gameplay to beat all three major endings. With it only costing 10 euros I don’t see a reason not to buy it. Even now that it's has become a year old it's still a great story to be part off. If you still aren’t sure about purchasing this game then you can still try out the demo. You can download the demo on the
.
The best way to play this game is to be as blind as possible. The character you are controlling shouldn’t be played like you would with, let’s say, Mario. In Mario games you pretend to be Mario and save the princess but in Undertale you are playing as yourself.
