I've been holding back on making this review for a long time. But, I feel like this game has proved stable and worthy enough by now.
First off, I have to say that this game is BY FAR the best multiplayer game I have EVER played. I play this game whenever I can and it never disappoints. I have been playing since October of 2015, and hopefully for many more to come. Let me get into the positives and experiences.
My Experiences-
This game is unique. You decide when you beat the game or succeed. For me, succeeding is building the best 5 layer honeycombed, double-stacked, 6x6 possible, raiding the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Zerg on the server, duo style, and then taking the crown. For you, winning could simply be succeeding in making a furnished 2x2 on a 300 pop server. I also just want to add a disclaimer that this game is VERY possible as a solo player. About 400 of my hours are from being solo on vanilla at a 120 pop server, you just have to be good and experienced. I also want to say that the community is in fact pretty ♥♥♥♥ing toxic, but I have also met a ton of awesome people from playing. Now for the professional standard of the review.
PROS-
•Best building mechanics out of ANY survival game
•Amazing gunplay, could use some balancing but for the most part very smooth
•Very nice devs. They continue to listen to the community and they are always hard at work
•PVE is starting to get rolling with elements such as chopper and animals
•Crafting system is very simple and easy to get used to. The components system is getting refined in every devblog and continues to be ironed out
•Community is a half/half. If you want to hold hands with everyone and make cottage in a meadow, join a PVE server or gtfo
•Farming is not as hard at everyone makes it out to be. Just spend 30 minutes straight of farming resources every day and you'll be more than fine
•Beautiful scenery and graphics
•Maps are very nice, especially for procedural standards
CONS-
•Can be very buggy at times aswell as exploits are getting out frequently, but that's what you sign up for when buying an early access title
•Raiding is a bit unbalanced, making it impossible for a solo or duo player survive when being pitted against a 10 man Zerg
•Animal AI is pretty ♥♥♥♥ed right now, but progress is being made big time
•Optimization is a piece of♥♥♥♥♥♥ but they try
------
Overall I defiantly recommend this game for people interested in survival/pvp games. If I wanted to rate it I would probably I've a 9/10, maybe a 10/10 when it gets to full release :)

Improving in some areas over the original, Borderlands 2 tries to revel in the ridiculous, but ultimately feels disappointingly similar.
Whilst it's unfair to criticise Borderlands 2 for 'not being innovative enough', it fairly quickly smacks of being very similar to its predecessor. Obviously random loot will pay a part in that and whilst there are different weapons to pick up compared to the original, it's hard to differentiate between two sets of random. There's a much bigger emphasis on story, with a central villain who communicates with you throughout, as well as more attention paid to a vivid cast of increasingly insane characters, but it all feels very much the same. You're still chasing The Vault, you're still collecting weapons, some of which you might keep with you for a bit longer, some you might ditched 10 minutes later and you're still trapsing round environments to complete fairly mundane quests.
This time around it feels like, weirdly, there's just too much effort put in to trying to please the audience. Some weapon varities were removed in the name of balance, but whilst I had an assortment of different types of weapons in BL1, in BL2 I felt I was sticking to the same weapon types that simply had different stats or elemental effects about them. Some of the fun variations seem to be completely missing instead of being balanced and the result is that I never really felt that I had a favourite weapon, they were just there to serve the means of killing enemies and even though that's all you did in the first game, there's something about loot games that makes me connected to certain items (obviously putting them aside when something clearly superior comes along) but there's no real sense of attachment to something.
More of your inventory is subject to randomisation, up from weapon and grenade types, but it all feels very much the same and in fact with certain unique items, it often felt more rewarding to grind out enemies or areas to try and get certain powerful combinations as opposed to making do with what you had. Obviously shield and class modifications don't give so much feedback as to what they do as well, altogether making some loot just down-right boring to the point of upgrading simply because you can rather than wanting to.
It's not just the loot that seems to be at fault either as the characters, dialogue and plot is all dialled up. Whilst BL1 wasn't exactly rooted in reality, the sense of depression oozing out of the environment made all the killing sort of fit in, with the odd few characters you converse with mostly being sane, but traumatized by the environment. In this sequel, everyone seems to be an exaggeration of their former selves and the whole thing just seems over-the-top ridiculous. Spread out and utilised not too often, this is fine, but the seemingly constant bombardment of it can leave character interactions and dialogue just seeming a bit jarring, boring or at worst annoying to suffer through.
Some of the mistakes of the original seep through as well. The opening takes a pointlessly long amount of time given it's a game about shooting things where those things can drop items that let you shoot things better. The user interface, especially when managing inventory, isn't exactly great and whilst I warmed up to it while playing, it felt a bit needlessly awkward. The plot, while trying to be more serious, or at the very least focused, is just as ridiculous and the few attempts at poignant, emotional moments are ruined by the insanity going on around.
My overall problem with the game is that I never really felt a great sense of satisfaction out of what I was doing. Things were better, but they weren't necessarily more fun.

I wanted it to be a positive review, I did, But I cannot. This game requires way too much time, The community is horrible and just about everything in this game caters to bigger groups of players.
Heres the 2 main factors of this game -
Time: You need to sink several hours into this game a day to maintain a healthy, decent base which keeps all your hard earned work safe. If you don't have 6+ hours a day to play this game, Don't have a group of players who can help maintain your base while you are offline, Just forget about this game already, Especially now with the recently added XP System which makes it even more time consuming, If you don't have the time, You simply won't be able to even unlock most of the items before servers reset. Example : I've grinded 20+ Hours in the past 2 days and I'm barely level 17, And I still haven't unlocked the good stuff yet and it continues to get harder to grind through the ranks. Theres 30+ levels in total to unlock and I'm 2 days into the wipe. (1 week wipe cycle). Chances are, I probably won't even unlock the Rocket launcher before the wipe.
Numbers: DO NOT and I repeat, DO NOT even think about purchasing this game if you plan on playing this game alone, You will be eaten alive by the trolls, Griefers and general asshats that make up for the majority of the community. People will go to any extent to make your experience terrible. Just don't. This game caters to clans (Groups of 3+) who will absoloutly rip you to pieces and stop at nothing to do exactly that. If you do somehow survive the first few days solo, Somehow manage to get a decent base going, You can count on a clan of 5-6 people pulling up at your doorstep and taking everything you own with no problem. Chances are, You probably won't even have weapons to defend yourself against 5 armed opponents as they blow your base to rubble and steal everything you owned.
Conclusion,
Do you have a big group of friends who'd join you? Do you have countless hours a day to put into this game? If so, You might actually enjoy this game. Give it a shot, You can always refund it if you don't. Otherwise, I would not reccommend this game.
Lastly, I'd just like to give the developers some praise, They do an excellent job at updating their game and have great communication with their fans, Constant updates in game, Updated Dev Blogs and great communication via Reddit also.
These guys should set an example as to what an early access should be.

TL;DR - Game has so much potential, Team largely incompetent, #BringBackRocket
I've poured so much time and effort into this game, and have for years considered it my favorite game of all time. I started playing the early alpha vanilla DayZ mod in July 2012, and I was blown away by the scale, realism, immersion, and uniqueness of the gameplay. The game has been in development for nearly 4 years now (standalone development started spring of 2012). It has sold nearly 3.5 million copies and has brought in $90million+ in revenue for the developer, Bohemia Interactive Studios.
However, despite these facts, I am deeply saddened by the progress the development team has shown. The game still is burdened by the same bugs it was plagued by in its standalone release over 2 years ago (weapon glitches, game-breaking desync, etc), and script kiddie issues in addition to terrible game performance has NEVER been worse. Nearly 4 years into active development, and the devs have little to show for their progress besides a few new guns, glitchy vehicles, and some new boonie hat colors. The new game engine that promised fixes for these issues is nowhere in sight, and the dev team refuses to give and deliver promised features on hard dates (go see their timeline for 2014 and you can tell nothing substantial was accomplished this year despite their promises).
When I compare this game's early alpha progress to its peers like SQUAD, VERDUN etc, it is not a stretch to call the DayZ dev team completely INCOMPETENT when they are unable to deliver half the progress that teams 1/10 their size have accomplished. This is not meant as an attack on management at Bohemia, but rather I want them and the members of the DayZ community to wake up and demand more from this game's development.
I implore the dev team: shakeup your approach to development and find a NEW competent Project Lead (#BringBackRocket). I implore you the gamer: think twice before buying this game.

My Review:
This game is both good and bad... mostly bad. However, there is only a small team of people working on it compared to other games that have large teams working on individual tasks to complete the whole game.  With that said, I'm sure Rust will be improved over time... maybe.
Without a handful of mods, which make sense and should be in the game by default, playing this game can be a very frustrating.
Unless the Devs step it up... ARK will destroy this game... and is.
Positives:

Playing with friends
True Survival with basic tools... until all the guns were and still are being added.  (Turning into a shooter game)
Custom Base Builds (somewhat... limits near other objects and the landscape)
Updates: Bi-weekly
Negatives:
Solo Survival... not recommened
Random games crashes
Wildlife: very low population, seem to have a jump boost on vertical boulders or cliffs, and two animals give you chicken breast instead of their meat you would expect. (deer and horse)
Not enough resources... ROCKS in particular. (refresh rate is far too low)
Quarry yields are far too low.  Yield needs tripled for this to be worthy to build.
You shouldn't have to repair anything regarding your base, (high stone walls and/or other foundations not attached to base), unless you are attacked and there's damage!

Not enough flat land to build on in the same area.

Foundations should extend farther into the ground so you can build more of them... you get forced not to place them because of the landscape being too hilly!!!!!
Ideas are still in Concept Limbo or placed into the game just to have them removed, (oil rig).
Hope you like rocks.  Whether you are low or high level... ... you will be searching all over for rocks to mine everyday.  Good luck.
Developers are not focused on fixing what's wrong with the game.  They constantly add new items into the game and tweak those, which distracts their attention from the more important tasks... like making the aniamls not go through objects, for example.
Turning into a shooter game... nothing we haven't seen before.
Build something cool... it's going to be destroyed.  Have something worthy... not for long.
Overall, if you can stand the fact that you will be shot, (pvp), and know all your hard work will eventually be stolen from you... then buy and play this game.
The Negatives far out-weigh the positives.  For me to say this is a worthy game, ... ... well it's going to take more than they offer currently.  Buy? ... only if cheap... real cheap.

As someone who generally loathes traditional RPGs, Undertale surprised me. I went in expecting to be bored out of my mind and left having experienced loveable and hilarious characters and an amazing story like none I've seen before.

A spunky RPG with lots of heart.

~ Solid soundtrack
~ Character designs are on-point
~ Characters are unique, and /mostly/ lovable
~ Emotionally gripping story
~ Bullet hell gameplay that is challenging at times, but not enough to exhaust you
~ Changes in the story and dialogue to represent multiple playthroughs
~ Some characters felt particularly annoying or completely unlikeable in terms of personality
~ The art is very hit-or-miss. Character designs are on point, but the pixel art is very wonky
~ Nothing about the layout of the game changes, and no additonal movement options are available. It makes certain things like reruns or backtracking particularly tedious
~ Puzzles aren't really fun
The gameplay sometimes feels slow, but the story keeps you coming back. Multiple ways to play through gives you a lot of insight into the game's universe, and the soundtrack still stands up 2 years after the game's release.

Spoiler free review.
The game was hyped and hyped. So much so, that I had to just check it out. I'm glad to say that it lived up to the hype.
Every source said to go in blind and know nothing about the game. That's what I did, I dodged every single thing people were saying about the game until I played it and finished it for myself, and I had a hell of a time.
As I'm writing this, I've only beaten the game once, and I was shocked to see that my playtime had totaled to just five hours. They packed a lot of emotional depth into those five hours.
It's nice to see a retro-throwback game that's not just focused on the NES and SNES-era of gaming (and, yes, I'm aware as I'm writing this that Earthbound was a huge influence on this game) and it kind of reminded me of the type of games you would see on the Commodore 64 or one of the many other home computers from the 1980's.
There's only two negative things that I thinked slowed this game down, and this isn't a spoiler, but I'll keep it vague just in case, later in the game you get a cell phone that allows texting and social media. Around that time, the game started to annoy me with its constant messaging that started to get less funny and more grating as they went on.
The other thing, and this is a big thing, is the backtracking you're forced to do. This is pretty much only to go back and get items before a boss fight, but I wish the stores were kept a little closer to the boss area, especially in the later areas of the game. It was quite annoying to have to spend five minutes walking back just to buy some healing items before a fight, and another five walking back to the boss. (OK, five minutes is a little hyperbolic on my part)
But other than those two things, the game is fantastic and I would recommend it to everybody.
It's one of the most emotional experiences I've had with a video game. It treated you with a high level of intellect and I praise the game for that, too.
A truly unique experience.

My Child, You thought this was a review, But I was actually going to share my Butterscotch Cinnamon Pie Recipe to the Undernet.
Ingredients:
Crust
1 egg yolk
2 Tbsp very cold water
1 tsp vanilla extract
1 ¼ cups all-purpose flour
1/3 cup sugar
¼ tsp salt
8 Tbsp (1 stick) cold butter cut into small pieces
Filling
¾ cup brown sugar
¼ cup all-purpose flour
2 tsp corn starch
¼ tsp salt
2 cups milk
1 egg yolk, lightly beaten
1 Tbsp butter
2 tsp vanilla extract
Topping
2 cups heavy whipping cream
1/3 cup powdered sugar
2 tsp vanilla extract
1 tsp cinnamon
For the crust:
Mix the egg yolk, water, and vanilla extract together in a small bowl and set it aside.
For these next steps you can do it by hand, in an electric mixer fitted with a flat paddle attachment, or (my favorite way) with a food processor. Add the flour, sugar, and salt into your mixer of choice and then add the butter in pieces and pulse/mix/cut it in until the pieces are no larger than peas and the mixture resembles something like a rough cornmeal. Add in the egg mixture and mix until the dough pulls together.
Place the dough on a floured surface and pat it out with your hands into a disk-shape. Sprinkle a little flour on top of it and then use a rolling pin to roll it out to about 1/8 of an inch thick. Carefully drape it over a tart pan (I put a round of parchment paper in the bottom of mine just in case) and use a sharp knife to trim off the excess dough along the edges. Don’t worry if it tears or has holes - just use the trimmed dough to mend it. A tiny bit of water smoothed along the edges will help to blend them back together. Poke a couple of holes in the bottom with a fork and pop the crust into a 350 degree F oven for 10-15 minutes or until the crust is golden-brown. Remove and allow to cool completely before filling. You can put dried beans or pie weight in the bottom of the crust to keep the bottom from rising if you’re so inclined.
For the filling:
In a medium-sized saucepan over medium heat add the sugar, flour, corn starch, and salt. Use a whisk to combine them and then slowly pour in the milk. Keeps mixing until it is fully combined and thickens, otherwise you might get lumps. This mixture MUST be thick, to the point of resembling a pudding or else it will not set firmly when you start to chill it.
In a small bowl, add a small amount of the hot butterscotch to the egg yolk and mix them together. This will keep the yolk from scrambling when you add it. Whisk the hot egg mixture into the butterscotch and then add the butter and vanilla. Mix until fully combined. Allow the butterscotch to cool before pouring it into the tart shell. If there is any remaining, I highly recommend you keep it to yourself and eat it with a spoon. Sharing is overrated. Refrigerate the pie until the butterscotch sets completely before topping.
For the topping:
Add all ingredients into an electric mixer fitted with the whisk attachment and whisk on high speed until the whipped cream forms stiff peaks. Dollop generously on top of the pie and sprinkle with a little additional cinnamon.

Improving in some areas over the original, Borderlands 2 tries to revel in the ridiculous, but ultimately feels disappointingly similar.
Whilst it's unfair to criticise Borderlands 2 for 'not being innovative enough', it fairly quickly smacks of being very similar to its predecessor. Obviously random loot will pay a part in that and whilst there are different weapons to pick up compared to the original, it's hard to differentiate between two sets of random. There's a much bigger emphasis on story, with a central villain who communicates with you throughout, as well as more attention paid to a vivid cast of increasingly insane characters, but it all feels very much the same. You're still chasing The Vault, you're still collecting weapons, some of which you might keep with you for a bit longer, some you might ditched 10 minutes later and you're still trapsing round environments to complete fairly mundane quests.
This time around it feels like, weirdly, there's just too much effort put in to trying to please the audience. Some weapon varities were removed in the name of balance, but whilst I had an assortment of different types of weapons in BL1, in BL2 I felt I was sticking to the same weapon types that simply had different stats or elemental effects about them. Some of the fun variations seem to be completely missing instead of being balanced and the result is that I never really felt that I had a favourite weapon, they were just there to serve the means of killing enemies and even though that's all you did in the first game, there's something about loot games that makes me connected to certain items (obviously putting them aside when something clearly superior comes along) but there's no real sense of attachment to something.
More of your inventory is subject to randomisation, up from weapon and grenade types, but it all feels very much the same and in fact with certain unique items, it often felt more rewarding to grind out enemies or areas to try and get certain powerful combinations as opposed to making do with what you had. Obviously shield and class modifications don't give so much feedback as to what they do as well, altogether making some loot just down-right boring to the point of upgrading simply because you can rather than wanting to.
It's not just the loot that seems to be at fault either as the characters, dialogue and plot is all dialled up. Whilst BL1 wasn't exactly rooted in reality, the sense of depression oozing out of the environment made all the killing sort of fit in, with the odd few characters you converse with mostly being sane, but traumatized by the environment. In this sequel, everyone seems to be an exaggeration of their former selves and the whole thing just seems over-the-top ridiculous. Spread out and utilised not too often, this is fine, but the seemingly constant bombardment of it can leave character interactions and dialogue just seeming a bit jarring, boring or at worst annoying to suffer through.
Some of the mistakes of the original seep through as well. The opening takes a pointlessly long amount of time given it's a game about shooting things where those things can drop items that let you shoot things better. The user interface, especially when managing inventory, isn't exactly great and whilst I warmed up to it while playing, it felt a bit needlessly awkward. The plot, while trying to be more serious, or at the very least focused, is just as ridiculous and the few attempts at poignant, emotional moments are ruined by the insanity going on around.
My overall problem with the game is that I never really felt a great sense of satisfaction out of what I was doing. Things were better, but they weren't necessarily more fun.

As someone who generally loathes traditional RPGs, Undertale surprised me. I went in expecting to be bored out of my mind and left having experienced loveable and hilarious characters and an amazing story like none I've seen before.

A spunky RPG with lots of heart.

~ Solid soundtrack
~ Character designs are on-point
~ Characters are unique, and /mostly/ lovable
~ Emotionally gripping story
~ Bullet hell gameplay that is challenging at times, but not enough to exhaust you
~ Changes in the story and dialogue to represent multiple playthroughs
~ Some characters felt particularly annoying or completely unlikeable in terms of personality
~ The art is very hit-or-miss. Character designs are on point, but the pixel art is very wonky
~ Nothing about the layout of the game changes, and no additonal movement options are available. It makes certain things like reruns or backtracking particularly tedious
~ Puzzles aren't really fun
The gameplay sometimes feels slow, but the story keeps you coming back. Multiple ways to play through gives you a lot of insight into the game's universe, and the soundtrack still stands up 2 years after the game's release.

Rust is a game that is constantly changing . As a player this makes it highly frustrating as the developers sometimes remove or change the mechanics that already work fine . The single biggest problem with Rust at the moment is that it has become somewhat of a "Battle Royale " with basebuilding. Servers dont hold their population like they used to. (In mid to late 2015, Servers would last a good 2 weeks with very few people quitting).
In my opinion this is down to a somewhat overcomplication of the key elements of rust. One of these elements being the maps. The maps in 2015 were far from perfect but what they did offer was 3 distinct biomes, Desert , Forest and Arctic . The former and latter being a place were the large groups would build their base and the forest biome being a place were smaller groups and solos would fight it out . On top of that there used to be only a few monuments and a few small radtowns on the map. This was ideal because it meant there was many areas in the map that would be secluded , but also guaranteed areas to get some good loot or have some PvP.
The new maps , while full of beautiful massive radtowns and small monuments, are flat , extremely repetitive and crowded. You could easily go to a dungeon and not see anybody and yet not find any good loot either , they are simply too big . ( Also a cause of poor performance). Hopefully in the future they give server owners the option of having the old style of proc gen maps.

Borderlands 2 and I have a love hate relationship. I love it because it does have polished gunplay, tight controls, interesting class design and a diverse talent system that allows you to build your character whichever way you choose. But after all that this game is nothing more than Borderlands with a changed environment and new gags from pop culture sprinkled in.
Don't get me wrong this game is enjoyable I sunk 24 hours of my precious life into this game, but after the new features of the game reveal themselves the game starts to lose its momentum. It boils back down into Diablo like kill and loot all the things, with the constant barrage of new weapons being thrown at you it becomes more of a chore to keep checking to see if that new gun that just dropped is really better than the one you're currently using. A lot of the game is spent comparing numerical values on charts, than it is shooting people giggling about how they got killed and tricking your friends (if you have any who are interested in playing this game with you) into killing themselves.
The game is polished, game play is enjoyable, and the story for the most part seems to be engaging up to a point but some of the NPCs really do grate in your nerves after awhile. I understand it is all part of the tongue n cheek nature of this game series but the amount of quests and the constant quips at trying to be humorous every time you stop in to drop off a mindless "go kill X" quest it loses its charm.
If FPS mixed with Diablo RPG looting is what you really enjoy then by all means pick this game up, though I stressed a lot on the negatives about this game overall this is a game that most should not pass up. I'd just wait for it to be on sale at a decent price first, or simply get the first game.

A major 'cultural shift' (for lack of a better word) has happened since the earlier days of rust. There used to be more interaction and 'adventure' (friendly as well as hostile), then there is now.
More and more (primarily younger) players have come in that treat the game as a competitive FPS, despite the fact that a buggy alpha could never be an accurate representation of skill. Your journey as a castaway on an unknown island will begin, and end with, 'lol n00b, get headshot', 'ban this cheating cancer' and such in the chat. Most discussions on the game have steered entirely to dealing with gun-related cheats, balancing guns, gun QoL changes, etc. etc.
As such I don't feel the game suits me anymore like it did before. I had many fun hours though, and I'm aware that the game isn't there to please me in particular. Nevertheless, if the reason you are interested in buying this game involves interaction beyond shooting each other (be it hostile or friendly interaction), you might be dissapointed.
Will check in every couple of months to see if anything has changed, as the game itself is still enjoyable to me.

Rust used to be fun. The devs killed it by making it a linear progression with a level system, instead of finding the blueprints on the map. You had something to look for and be there was a rewarding feeling once you achieved it. Now out of nowhere this is being replaced with linear progression. No matter if youre a pro or a noob, everyone progress a roughly the same speed by literally doing anything beside being afk. It dulled the game.
The devs have no idea where they are going and changed core aspect of the game, to something completely different that i would never have bought if id knew. They didnt "add more content". they removed a big component of the game in exchange for something boring but easier on newer players.
The cheaters ? rust is rampant with cheaters. Facepunch admit they dont really know how to protect against hackers, so they gave the responsability to a third party EAC. Its not better, hackers can take up to 1 month before being banned, even if half the server are reporting them. Its just not working. It create an unhealthy atmosphere where everyone is paranoid and cant enjoy the game without accusing everyone of hacking. Because you have literally no way to know if someone is casually aimbotting and use ESP.
Facepunch recently gave admin rights to all servers in the game, to a whiny youtuber who abuse his power. In rust if you play a week and then an admin come and mess your thing, destroy you with infinite power, or simply ban you, its frustrating. You would expect that they would try to be good but its the opposite. They give admin rights to youtuber to advertise the game, and those youtubers abuse admin powers to get an advantage over their enemy, on official servers. Ridiculous.
I recommend to not buy until the game its released, otherwise its garanteed disappointment.

A major 'cultural shift' (for lack of a better word) has happened since the earlier days of rust. There used to be more interaction and 'adventure' (friendly as well as hostile), then there is now.
More and more (primarily younger) players have come in that treat the game as a competitive FPS, despite the fact that a buggy alpha could never be an accurate representation of skill. Your journey as a castaway on an unknown island will begin, and end with, 'lol n00b, get headshot', 'ban this cheating cancer' and such in the chat. Most discussions on the game have steered entirely to dealing with gun-related cheats, balancing guns, gun QoL changes, etc. etc.
As such I don't feel the game suits me anymore like it did before. I had many fun hours though, and I'm aware that the game isn't there to please me in particular. Nevertheless, if the reason you are interested in buying this game involves interaction beyond shooting each other (be it hostile or friendly interaction), you might be dissapointed.
Will check in every couple of months to see if anything has changed, as the game itself is still enjoyable to me.

After playing this for many many hours I have come to realize this may be worth your money, but not your time. Not only do these raiders sometimes use hacks to attack your base if you attempt to defend it, you need most of your people online to help. Aside from the gameplay, your pc must have costed about $2,500 in order to run this game and not lag at all in gunfights. Even then a friend of mine has 2 Titan-xs and equally great parts and will sometimes lag in intense gunfights. The game is poorly optomized, it is pretty bad, even when you run it to look like a DS game. Just a note - I left my laptop on a few nights with Undertale open, so shave off about 12 or so hours and that would be closer to my actual play time (Undertale reports ~600 minutes, but that ... also takes into account one of the nights, whoops). This is because I haven't been able to spend all that much time on it, and I'm satisfied with where I'm at right now (one Neutral ending, one True Pacifist).
Now, onto the actual review: where to start? This was so, so hyped up - and fortunately, it's lived up to the hype. Undertale was shorter than I'd expected, but it is ridiculously clever, funny, and sweet. The soundtrack is DEFINITELY one of the best aspects of the game, but to be honest, the characters, the detail, the choices ... it's rewarding and it's brilliant. The implied social commentary in the narrative I'm not so much a fan of, if only because it's too overt to be passed over yet not developed enough to be appreciated, but regardless, Toby Fox is one entertaining writer.
(Populus describes this game as one of those that you marathon whilst excused from school and maybe it's the time constraints I placed myself under but goddamn is that an accurate description. You remember that, right? Wasn't that a wonderful time? Wouldn't you like to go through that again?)
Pick up this game - oh, and, don't let anyone tell you anything (more) about it. You need to play this, but you need to play this as blind as you can be.
And remember: stay DETERMINED.

This game has been in Alpha stage for over 2 years now and has shown little to no progress whatsoever. Remember that article a bunch of websites posted saying DayZ Beta would be out by late 2015 and the full game would be out sometime in 2016? Yeah right hahaha. I'm not gonna lie, DayZ has potential, but that's all it seems to have. It SOUNDS like a promising game, but it's nowhere close to that. This is why Early Access shouldn't even be a thing. Developers should only be able to sell games that are PLAYABLE, not something that is comparable to a post-apocalyptic zombie slideshow. The only thing I can guarantee you about this game is that double clicking it will in fact boot the game up. I can't however guarantee you'll have any fun. However, some rare people manage to put hundreds upon thousands into this game because they are able to put up with the bugs, horrible framerate, desync, etc. But I guarantee that if you're reading this, you're not one of those people. I'd suggest you get Arma II and get the DayZ mod because at least that game is functional. Hell, I'd rather suggest you take a lighter and burn $35 than actually waste your money on this.

Truely mad fun.
The GOOD!
- Like the original Mad Max? (have not seen bikes, they need motor bikes!)
- Do you like it when every character is crazier than you are? (Theraputic!, warning some quests can be hard on the brain or funny bone)
- Like it when you may run out of time before the game runs out of content? (So afraid of missing things but sure I am...)
- Want a game that creates so many stylish ways to die?  (I have laughed, truly laughed at some moments).
- Do you really want to know when you meet someone "special"? (The introductions and "boss screens" are so epic!)
I would dare say I was in awe of some of the poses, epic, like something out of an old anime boss fights.
- Are you into your sound? (Put on earphones and you can tell where they are coming from AND you hear all the truly silly stuff all the characters have to say including the joe guys, especiall... IT BURNS! IT BURNS!).
- There is always a place nearby to get GUNS, AMMO, HEALTH, SHIELDS (yes, personal shields... so happy) and a VEHICLE to rampage around in with UNLIMITED AMMO... oh yes...
- A steady stream of goals, rewards and missions, thank goodness the interface is easy enough to track it all.
- Missions that start off as "same old" until the "special twists" kick in.  I think they use the traditional first person shooter problem solving against the player... oh it goes south in a hurry, the carnage is so fun.
- More freaking guns and grenade types, I swear I die more from "analysis paralysis" because I have too many choices on how to "efficiently" take down a bad guy (or worse yet, a group).
- Many character types to play with specific items to use with what really is a choice of 3 specialization paths within them.
- Handsome Jack, I truely do like him... I truely do want to take him down... I am so torn.
- The variety of body types and every kind of human (ish) coloring and body "features" are so spread all over the place it is like the united nations all got together for a party and got very drunk... offspring resulted... you know....
- The graphics are JUST cartoony enough you do not jump out of your skin when something gets the drop on you (this is a good thing).  Because we are to be super bad vault hunters that scare the scary!!!
- Disturbing moments brought to you by key support characters... surgery, target practice, tea parties <shudder>, insane sniper that randomly shoots (activates but wounds!) bad guys... they SOOOOO rock yet somehow drive you utterly crazy all in one breath.  The character design is an art conducted by truely twisted antisocial people...  I want to be their "friend".
- One complete blessing of the game physics: no death by falling (unless into an impassible area).  It has allowed for truely stylish moments.
The BAD (ish)
- Many locations, with locations within them.  You may hurt your brain trying to remember where they are at.  At least activating a mission does help with the location finding.
- The humor is very politically incorrect... is this good or bad?
- The specialization trees really need to be focused on or you can spread out the points and not get the really powerful skills you need to take on higher level areas.
- The spawning from open doors within buildings is good but give you an itchy feeling when you pass through the same area for a second time (will they come back now?)
- Money, oh my goodness money, never, never enough.  Darn that Jack and his Diamond pony.  You get TONS of option drops you do not need and there are just barely enough vending machines to sell it all without hoofing it for a long time or giving up and throwing it on the ground. The first thing I heard about Undertale was that it is an RPG where you don't have to kill anyone.  I can't tell you how many RPGs I've played where the unstated objective seemed to be to slay all of the wildlife in the countryside. The second thing I heard about Undertale was that it was created almost entirely by one man.  Last but not least, I heard that the game was receiving incredibly positive reviews.  I was still hesitant though, largely due to the fact that the trailer didn't really attract me.  Ultimately, I decided to give it a try anyway.
I have to hand it to Toby Fox, he did a damn good job on Undertale.  It would be an understatement to call him a man of many talents.  The characters are memorable, the music is catchy, the artwork is solid, the writing is humorous, and the combat system is unique.  I will be looking forward to see what sort of work he releases in the future.  What can I say?  The fact that he managed to do all of this alone fills me with determination to work on my own personal projects.
As I mentioned before, the combat system is unique.  It isn't like any other combat system I've ever seen before.  The vast majority of the fights are like distinct bullet dodging mini-games and... quirky for lack of a better word. You can attack, talk to enemies, and spare them.  Your actions in combat affect the game world.  Undertale isn't the type of RPG where you spend hours grinding monsters for exp and loot.  Nor will you spend time trying to improve your sneak and lock picking skills.  If you're looking for that kind of RPG you're going to have a bad time.  I only played through once but there are several different endings.  The game is short (perhaps too short) and it probably wouldn't take too long to do everything.
It is hard to write about this game while avoiding spoilers.  If you end up playing through Undertale, I highly recommend that you do it with as little knowledge about the game as possible.  I'm not sure I would have enjoyed it as much had I known everything about the game.  The humor may wear thin on some individuals.  I couldn't help but think I wasn't the target audience for this game, and that it was probably something I would appreciated more when I was younger.
Undertale really grew on me while playing it, perhaps more so than I initially realized.  Toby Fox managed to instill some sort of magic into the world he created.  I don't think I've felt quite the same way about fictional characters in quite a few years.  It was the sort of magic I remember experiencing while playing some early SNES and PlayStation RPGs.  While this game isn't without its faults, it is easy to see why so many people love it.

"Facepunch Studios boss Garry Newman has some advice for Rust players who have grown bored with the game: Stop playing it. He acknowledged that the sentiment may come across as dismissive, but said in a message on Reddit that it's necessary to break the "ping-pong loop" that's holding the game back from full release.
"I'm noticing a pattern, and we need to address it. It's something we need to get past as a community, not only because it's getting boring but because it has wider implications," he wrote. "We're stuck in ping pong loop. We release an update, you love it for a month, you get bored, blame the system, ♥♥♥♥♥ for a few months, then we release another update—and the same thing happens."
His concern is that the pattern will persist indefinitely, because the real problem isn't that the new systems are better than the old ones, but simply that they're "fresher." But Facepunch obviously can't keep overhauling the game forever, and thus Newman suggests a clean break for those unhappy with Rust. But he also asked that people who do end up quitting, or who think his attitude is unfair, give thought to "whether we have given you enough entertainment over the last three years to justify pocketing your $20" before getting angry."

I got introduced to this game by friends around 6 months ago. At the time, I was retired from PC gaming and didn't own a computer to play on, so I only played at the office after work and during weekends. Shortly, I became familiar with the guards that patrolled the office building late at night. Not long after, because of this game, I reunited with the master race and bought a used PC.
Rust is a game unique in nature. The world is persistent. Your character and constructions will physically remain in the game world when you log off. A well-built shelter with a metal door is required to have any hope of long term survival. The PVP aspect of the game is by today's standards brutal, but also incredibly rewarding. To me it's reminiscent of Ultima Online, grandfather of MMOs; whatever you were carrying remains in your corpse and is lootable by the enemy. Few games today can offer same kind of adrenaline-pumping experience Rust does.
Unfortunately, the changes brought by recent patches have been a massive blow to the core aspects that made the game fun. Because of the XP system, progression in the game has become linear, requiring hours upon hours of tedious MMO style grind. Secondly, somewhat deserved but poorly executed nerfs to primitive weapons such as crossbow and spear have widened the gap between new and established (i.e. well-geared) players. Previously, primitive weapons notorious for their higher skill cap allowed a competent player to emerge victorious in a battle of uneven numbers.
At this time until Facepunch addresses these issues, I am reluctant to recommend Rust for a new player, especially if you plan on playing solo.

Im Speechless. Literally. I am.
This game bends ALL BOUNDRIES of a normal RPG.
This game isnt like a normal luck based where there is a 50/50 chance you will hit your enemy, its all skill based.
Half the time, its nostalgic and lovable. The other time, its exciting and unique.
Now here is where I bring in the reasons why I love this game.
I am going to warn you, there will be spoilers.
First off, The characters. They each have their own personality thats lovable and great, (Even the villains!) And they all seem, Human. (Or monsterous, however toby fox's lingo goes.) Next, the storyline. Its story rich and unique (Which kept reminding me of Neal Shuchterman novels) with so many twists and turns that literally kept my jaw gaping.
Now, the alternate endings. There are three. Neutral, Pacifist, and Genocide. I will go deeper into these later.
Next, the 4TH Wall breaks. This game breaks the fourth wall SO MUCH! At one time, a character took control of my save file, making it so whenever I reopened the game, it would take me to when I DIED. It sounds cruel, but I was able to make it through! Lastly, THE OPTIONS! SO MANY OPTIONS! If I killed one spider, suprise! Their relative comes back and beheads you in front of their snake cult. (Muffet wink wink)
Now, the story. Neutral; The basic gamemode where you can do whatever you want. The ending brings back an unsuspecting character (Flowey The Flower!) and has it be a final boss fight. Flowey then resets your game and tells you that you have to play it over again without killing anyone.
Pacifist; This ending made me SAD. You make so many friends, and the true ending to find that Flowey was your best friend all along. It turns out that it was all a dream and none of it was real. You go up onto the surface with your friends and have your happy ending. There is only one save file, so if you reset, you do it all over again.
Genocide; I never played this gamemode, because I dont want my friends to leave! :(
If you've already read through all of this, its okay. Im sure you will still cry.

I've fought for months to make weapons less random and when it happened, they got more random again because apparently the lead dev wants the game to have a low skill ceiling. Currently most weapons are still too inaccurate, especially the Pistols, SMGs, Semi Automatic Rifle and M249. Most weapons are spammy and deal little damage. Low to mid tier weapons are almost useless against people with high tier game. You barely have any chance to outaim your opponents. The low damage and terrible gunplay turned this game into a strength in numbers game.
Before the game got reworked, every weapon was accurate and dangerous if used correctly. Every weapon had high damage but high recoil to encourage tapping. Now the game is too forgiving and a spamfest.

It's really sad because the previous iteration of the game pretty much nailed the gunplay and balancing. Oh my goodness. I can't even explain how good this game is. I was a little skeptical about it when I saw it released, but every single social media... it was just Undertale, Undertale, UNDERTALE. So, I decided "why not." and I bought the game.
I am very glad I did. The gameplay is great, especially put together with the FIGHT mechanics. I'm also very glad that you are allowed to show MERCY, because like Toby Fox said, most RPGs are just "endless murder-fests" and I agree. The story is an emotional, heartwarming, piece of sunshine (that is if you play the True Pacifist Run). I even enjoyed the neutral run almost as much as I did in the True Pacifist Run. I never actually completed the Genocide Run because it is really sad, and I feel bad for killing literally everything. That is why Undertale is such a great game. Even though it's "just a game", almost every action you perform affects the game in one way or another. You have the power to Reset everything. You can end a happy ending or end a sad ending, but all characters will remember what you did. The game tries to make you understand that your actions have consequences, wether they're good or bad.
Please, if you are skeptical about this game like I was, don't be. I'm 99% sure that you will have a good time playing Undertale. With all the fun characters, great story, and dialogue, it will make you love it.

What to expect from this game:
Really well made plot
Engrossing character development
Self referential commentary on what it means to play a game
Innovative and thematic gameplay
Quirky humor (Not all would enjoy this aspect, but I did)
A superb sound track
This has got to be one of the most beautifully crafted games I've ever seen. A fair number (not a ton, but some) of people rag on the graphics and gameplay being lackluster, but to be honest I think that these elements of the game are not only helpful, but crucial mediums through which the story is told. This game is a game with such depth of plot, such a beautiful creation of a world, where not everything is spoon fed to you but so much is hidden between the lines, and the relationships do not begin and end with the player, but extend throughout the world. A ton of replay value, a ton of emotions, and a stunning sound track all created by one man.
I would rate this game 10/10, and I will definitely be playing it again in the near future. After reading this review, I'd recommend you read nothing else about the game and play it through to really enjoy it.

Early Access for Rust has been around since the dawn of man...
But don't let that little wee statement fool you...
This game (While still being in Early Access) takes the form of Minecraft's development, and works upon it. The developers constantly communicate what they're working on from week to week, bug fixes and changes are constant, so if a type of exploit was to be found, it would take a measly couple of hours just for the team to solve it. Even with its tag of *Early Access* the game manages to have the best re-play value of any game on steam, and has you waiting for the next forced wipe to get into the wild world of Rust once more.
Gameplay isn't bad, and while i'm no professional when it comes to the weapons (I still suck using most guns, due to my absence from this game since legacy) I am thrilled when it comes to the large arsenal of weaponry found in Rust; so many ways of just killing your fellow human being.
Things like Farming, with a pick for rocks, and an axe for trees, is getting ways to make it more appealing to players, so stress doesn't have to be high where before you had to beat the devil out of a resource to get its contents and players could easily gank you when you have finished; Now that has changed with rocks being able to be more quickly harvest-able and wood will soon see the same fate.
My only dislike with the game, is that for the most fun experience, i have to join a solo duo trio server due to the amount of players who want giant clans with like 15 people in them. I'm a solo queing guy, even if i had the best stuff i'd still die to them (cause i reek). So if you the type of person who just plays alone or with a bud, i'd suggest staying away from official servers, until something is done about massive waves of players joined together. But personally the community servers share no difference in gameplay from the offical (aside from regulations, this one in particular being Solo/Duo/Trio servers), but do provide for a more fair gameplay experience.
Personally Rust is a game where the Early Access tag means nothing, as the base game currently has so much to offer to players, with a team that will listen to everyone's bickering and will change what is best for the community. Rust truly deserves your money if your interested in the game, don't let that little Early Access tag spook your decision.

The best part about the game are the devs, they put so much effort into the game that its almost leaves you with a feeling of guilt when you decide to quit the game but there are many reasons to ill list a few:
- The game is always controlled by a group of 5-8 players and as a solo/duo you have almost no chance in looting rad towns.
- The community is intensly toxic, everyone has a KOS mentallity even towards new players who just joined the server.
- The game is very time consuming, you can't just play this game once a week and think you can make progress, this game is almost like a job you have to invest atleast 3-4 hours a day to be able to secure your base and prevent it from decaying.
- It already once saw a major shift from playstyle the now legacy version was near perfect for my taste and i enjoy playing on the legacy servers if i can find a server that is hacker proof. But since they changed it once it would not suprise me if they changed everything again in 1-2 years.
- The game can be a total grindfest if your a solo player, around 45-60 minutes to get materials to start crafting your starter base.
This does not mean the game is not fun to play because it most certainly can be if you have the time and effort to put into the game.

Unfortunately my review will probably be washed down by the large amount of negative reviews this game has received, however I will take a stab at getting my voice out there to the people. First off, however, I want you to look at how many hours I have logged into this game. The amount of time I have spent in DayZ Standalone is close to surpassing any other game I have played on Steam, and for good reason. There is a lot of misconception going around the Steam reviews, and quite frankly many of the negative comments are filled with bigot hate towards the developers and a lack of understanding for how the early access model works in DayZ. Hopefully I can clear some of the confusion and give potential buyers some clarity on the title.
Let's rewind the clocks back to late 2013, a year after DayZ mod was released on Arma II. The survival sandbox genre had just exploded into the videogames scene, and every developer was trying to claim their stake in the land of the survivalist games. At the time, Bohemia Interactive had in their hands the most popular survivalist game on the market. Thousands of people played DayZ mod, and people loved the idea of an open-world survival game in which the elements and players are pitted against you. DayZ mod set the tone for what a survival game should be: challenging, unforgiving, and hard to top. Bohemia wanted to take the title and make it something greater, something much bigger and smoother than what the original mod intended to be. They knew that releasing a full version of the game on that clunky Arma II engine wouldn't cut it, so they had to make major improvements to bring the title into 2016 and beyond.
Instead of releasing the full DayZ Standalone game on the horrible Arma II engine, Bohemia made the decision to completely re-gut the engine and build a new one from scratch. FROM. SCRATCH. There are a few legacy modules that are getting carried over, but for the most part every aspect of the game is new (render, physics, lighting, etc). Anyone who has had any kind of development experience in video-games understands that this is a daunting task, a momentous task, a task that doesn't happen in one month or one year; No, creating a brand new engine takes years to develop, and this is where the root of the "problem" started.
DayZ Standalone went into early access in late 2013, and this is where they made their big mistake. The game simply wasn't ready. With no new engine components even being started on (plus it hit early access only 4 weeks into the development timeline, dear god), many early access players were left in disappointment when new features could not be pushed right away. People cried "fix zombies", but the zombies could not be fixed yet because an entirely new AI system was being created. People cried "fix FPS", but no FPS fix could be put in place because they were busy developing the new renderer. People wanted new vehicles, but vehicles could not be added yet because the physics system was being re-worked. There's no point in providing a "fix" for a mechanic in the game when that mechanic is going to be entirely replaced down the line anyways.
And so people got ♥♥♥♥♥♥, and fed up. "$20 for a Standalone title, and there's no fixes for these bugs?" Even I was at the point of rage, often times quitting DayZ Standalone for months at a time. People started saying that the developers weren't doing anything, that they "took the money and ran". But the real reality was that they were simply hard at work laying out the foundation for the title, unfortunately not being able to fix most bugs and issues at the time because they were so busy writing up new systems for the game to play on.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SO LET'S FAST FORWARD. It's late 2015 now, nearing 2016. DayZ Standalone has been in development for 2 years now. Has the game changed? Are any of the new engine models finished? Are zombies even fixed yet?
You bet your ♥♥♥ they are. If you were to ask me when I think the game should of been released to the public as early access, I would have said right now (version .59) would have been the time to do it. FINALLY, after 2 years of development, Bohemia Interactive is getting around to completing all of the upcoming engine changes and new foundation for the title. Let me make a quick list to get your hype train rolling:
New Renderer is nearly finished, should have "30 - 40 % FPS boost overall"
Zombie AI is brand new and fixed, zombies now have sense of smell and sight, don't clip through walls, are actually a challenge
Four vehicles currently in game: V3S, Sedan, Hatchback, and Bus. Arial vehicles confirmed, as well as bikes and boats
New vehicle physics system taken from GTA V (Bullet SDK). Full vehicle maintenance and parts
All servers persistent. Camps and items are saved after restart. You can create large camps now.
Tents, Barrels, vehicles, protector cases, and backpacks can all be used as base storage now. Stays persistent through server reset
Loot respawn fixed. Loot spawns in areas that make sense now, it is very hard to get access to good weapons and ammo
Sickness and Disease now a major factor of gameplay
Tons of new animals in the game with new Animal AI. They react to sight and sound, as well as naturally roam the map looking for ponds and fields to graze in.
Predator animals confirmed, including wolves and bears
map changes and new northern towns expand the map greatly from mod
Softskills soon to be implemented, aka the more you run the more fit you get. skills develop over time
Every building now enter able with loot
A ton of new weapons and cosmetic items (clothing) added into the game
character wear progession, such as growing beards and getting dirt / blood on yourself, soon to be implemented
Contaminated Zones confirmed and being worked on, the first being a military base up north
And soo so so much more. I could keep the list going forever but it honestly doesn't cover how much they've added into the game since launch.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Conclusion
Anyone who says DayZ Standalone is dead, or that the developers have "taken the money and ran", or that the community is dead, quite frankly is full of ♥♥♥♥. The game is very much alive and so much better than it was when it started. Even though DayZ SA has been slow off the start compared to other survivalist games (H1Z1, Rust, ARK, Unturned, Miscreated, etc), I strongly believe it will come out on top as the best survivalist game when it is finished. No other survival game has this much attention to detail and realism as DayZ. No other survival game has the kind of studio resources and money that Bohemia has to put out a strong title. No other survival game has mastered the hardcore aspect of survival and struggle better than DayZ. Almost every other survival game was rushed out on a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ Unreal engine in an effort to reap money off the survivalist scene and try to outbeat Bohemia to the punch on features and gameplay. Games like Rust and H1Z1 fail to hit the bullseye on what a survival game should be. DayZ Standalone does this right and does it good. I would definitely recommend this game now, as it's about to surpass the ♥♥♥♥ outta all other games on the market. Go out there and start surviving!

Unfortunately my review will probably be washed down by the large amount of negative reviews this game has received, however I will take a stab at getting my voice out there to the people. First off, however, I want you to look at how many hours I have logged into this game. The amount of time I have spent in DayZ Standalone is close to surpassing any other game I have played on Steam, and for good reason. There is a lot of misconception going around the Steam reviews, and quite frankly many of the negative comments are filled with bigot hate towards the developers and a lack of understanding for how the early access model works in DayZ. Hopefully I can clear some of the confusion and give potential buyers some clarity on the title.
Let's rewind the clocks back to late 2013, a year after DayZ mod was released on Arma II. The survival sandbox genre had just exploded into the videogames scene, and every developer was trying to claim their stake in the land of the survivalist games. At the time, Bohemia Interactive had in their hands the most popular survivalist game on the market. Thousands of people played DayZ mod, and people loved the idea of an open-world survival game in which the elements and players are pitted against you. DayZ mod set the tone for what a survival game should be: challenging, unforgiving, and hard to top. Bohemia wanted to take the title and make it something greater, something much bigger and smoother than what the original mod intended to be. They knew that releasing a full version of the game on that clunky Arma II engine wouldn't cut it, so they had to make major improvements to bring the title into 2016 and beyond.
Instead of releasing the full DayZ Standalone game on the horrible Arma II engine, Bohemia made the decision to completely re-gut the engine and build a new one from scratch. FROM. SCRATCH. There are a few legacy modules that are getting carried over, but for the most part every aspect of the game is new (render, physics, lighting, etc). Anyone who has had any kind of development experience in video-games understands that this is a daunting task, a momentous task, a task that doesn't happen in one month or one year; No, creating a brand new engine takes years to develop, and this is where the root of the "problem" started.
DayZ Standalone went into early access in late 2013, and this is where they made their big mistake. The game simply wasn't ready. With no new engine components even being started on (plus it hit early access only 4 weeks into the development timeline, dear god), many early access players were left in disappointment when new features could not be pushed right away. People cried "fix zombies", but the zombies could not be fixed yet because an entirely new AI system was being created. People cried "fix FPS", but no FPS fix could be put in place because they were busy developing the new renderer. People wanted new vehicles, but vehicles could not be added yet because the physics system was being re-worked. There's no point in providing a "fix" for a mechanic in the game when that mechanic is going to be entirely replaced down the line anyways.
And so people got ♥♥♥♥♥♥, and fed up. "$20 for a Standalone title, and there's no fixes for these bugs?" Even I was at the point of rage, often times quitting DayZ Standalone for months at a time. People started saying that the developers weren't doing anything, that they "took the money and ran". But the real reality was that they were simply hard at work laying out the foundation for the title, unfortunately not being able to fix most bugs and issues at the time because they were so busy writing up new systems for the game to play on.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SO LET'S FAST FORWARD. It's late 2015 now, nearing 2016. DayZ Standalone has been in development for 2 years now. Has the game changed? Are any of the new engine models finished? Are zombies even fixed yet?
You bet your ♥♥♥ they are. If you were to ask me when I think the game should of been released to the public as early access, I would have said right now (version .59) would have been the time to do it. FINALLY, after 2 years of development, Bohemia Interactive is getting around to completing all of the upcoming engine changes and new foundation for the title. Let me make a quick list to get your hype train rolling:
New Renderer is nearly finished, should have "30 - 40 % FPS boost overall"
Zombie AI is brand new and fixed, zombies now have sense of smell and sight, don't clip through walls, are actually a challenge
Four vehicles currently in game: V3S, Sedan, Hatchback, and Bus. Arial vehicles confirmed, as well as bikes and boats
New vehicle physics system taken from GTA V (Bullet SDK). Full vehicle maintenance and parts
All servers persistent. Camps and items are saved after restart. You can create large camps now.
Tents, Barrels, vehicles, protector cases, and backpacks can all be used as base storage now. Stays persistent through server reset
Loot respawn fixed. Loot spawns in areas that make sense now, it is very hard to get access to good weapons and ammo
Sickness and Disease now a major factor of gameplay
Tons of new animals in the game with new Animal AI. They react to sight and sound, as well as naturally roam the map looking for ponds and fields to graze in.
Predator animals confirmed, including wolves and bears
map changes and new northern towns expand the map greatly from mod
Softskills soon to be implemented, aka the more you run the more fit you get. skills develop over time
Every building now enter able with loot
A ton of new weapons and cosmetic items (clothing) added into the game
character wear progession, such as growing beards and getting dirt / blood on yourself, soon to be implemented
Contaminated Zones confirmed and being worked on, the first being a military base up north
And soo so so much more. I could keep the list going forever but it honestly doesn't cover how much they've added into the game since launch.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Conclusion
Anyone who says DayZ Standalone is dead, or that the developers have "taken the money and ran", or that the community is dead, quite frankly is full of ♥♥♥♥. The game is very much alive and so much better than it was when it started. Even though DayZ SA has been slow off the start compared to other survivalist games (H1Z1, Rust, ARK, Unturned, Miscreated, etc), I strongly believe it will come out on top as the best survivalist game when it is finished. No other survival game has this much attention to detail and realism as DayZ. No other survival game has the kind of studio resources and money that Bohemia has to put out a strong title. No other survival game has mastered the hardcore aspect of survival and struggle better than DayZ. Almost every other survival game was rushed out on a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ Unreal engine in an effort to reap money off the survivalist scene and try to outbeat Bohemia to the punch on features and gameplay. Games like Rust and H1Z1 fail to hit the bullseye on what a survival game should be. DayZ Standalone does this right and does it good. I would definitely recommend this game now, as it's about to surpass the ♥♥♥♥ outta all other games on the market. Go out there and start surviving!

So this game has taken over my life... It is, BY FAR, the best game I've ever played and I liked it so much I got it on PS3 just so I could play with my brother! The game is amazing, you would be a fool not to buy it.
Every character is extremely well written and the entire game is really funny and the artwork and design of it is very unique and phenomenal and is just very appealing. The shoot and loot aspect is probably the best part because you can guarantee you will find a better gun than the one you just got and thought would last you forever, but it doesn't. (first rule of borderlands: NEVER GET ATTACHED TO A GUN) the blend between RPG and FPS is seamless and flawless, if you like either RPG games or shooting games you'd love BL2, because honestly you don't really have to be good at shooting games because the learning curve to this game is easy enough that you will pick it up within the first few hours or so of play time.
It is actually beneficial to have a friend with the game because, a) it is like 200% more fun, and b) you can find better weapons.
the diversity of characters gives the game an awesome replayability and is easy to put in over 100 hours. That along with the copious DLC's, multiple difficulty modes and raid bosses that have you wanting to get the best weapons possible, will give you enjoyment for days on end!
The story lines are really fun and humorous and can have you laughing and also on the verge of tears because it's just so gripping.
Each character having their own skill trees and special abilities gives it an extra cool aspect going along with the RPG parts of BL2 and again makes it worth while to level up your character to the max and play as every character to get the feel for them, they are all great and it's really hard to choose a favourite...
PROS:
-Amazing story
-Beautiful graphics and artwork
-Hilarious characters/NPC's
-Perfect blend of RPG and FPS
-Incredible replayability
-Super fun looting system with so many guns it literally doesn't matter.
-Cool skill trees and leveling systems
CONS:
-Really addictive and will waste your days away
-I honestly can't think of any cons...
BUY BL2 YOU WON'T REGRET IT!!!!! and when it goes on sale you are literally stealing from them it's so worth it! If you haven't bought it yet get the GOTY edition it's well worth its price!

Undertale is a game loved by many and we really love it. Undertale is a indie RPG game made by a small team and kind of pays homage to games like EarthBound but really the game is just one big love letter to RPGs and a bunch of other games.
- It's filled with a very weird out there but very intriguing story with some lovable characters, catchy music, and classic graphics. We all know that a lot of people love this game Undertale. I scoured the internet for opinions of Undertale fans the world over if you could choose one thing that you didn't like or wanted to change with this otherwise perfect game what it be? There are a lot of puns in the game, lot of funny situations, and surprisingly, its full with double-meaning content, and usually you need to take things literally to get through things, but it's just not always obvious, which is great! It's like putting  up a note on a wall at 5M, waiting for someone to get a ladder to be able to read it, to find a message " I can't believe you made so far for nothing / How's the weather up here? / Yes, you did it! No what? " It's somewhat random, but not the trollface, oh lolololol level of being annoying, but the way that after a few hours you realize that if a character tells you a generic-sounding "Come and drop by my place" then you don't question whether you can go or not, you immediately go to find out what funny stuff the game has to show to you.
- Sounds really weird, but basically exploration and curiosity is rewarded with joy and fun. And about the characters, there are a couple of NPCs who only have a few lines of talk, but they usually still give some information about the area, or have some connection to the story if you pay attention - like how a monster wishes for the school to close because of re-activated ouzzles, and later you can see a new's cast telling schools are closed for the very same reason. So yes, I can totally recommend the game, if you want it you can get the DEMO for it. The link for the DEMO is
.

Honestly not even sure if the developers themselves know the direction they want the game to go.

I've played pretty much every variant of DayZ mod, including the early versions of the original DayZ mod and even the Arma 3 variants (Epoch/Breaking Point). This is the worst variant of them all.
There are some cool concepts in standalone, but it is hounded by a technically inferior engine. It is, simply put, a janky mess.
The thing that DayZ has over other survival games is a far more interactive experience, I mean, that's all that DayZ has going for it. There is no base building or super late game, so hoarding items is not really a thing you can do. It's all about those experiences you create with other players.
I spent thousands of hours playing DayZ mod and its variants, but not this one. This is a pile of junk, avoid it, and either play a mod variant or move along to a different survival game.

I feel i should update my review since the recent addition of the XP System.
Despite the notification on top, I also will stress this is an Early Access review. The game is still being worked on. So this is by no means my final thoughts.
Again, i just cannot recommend this game. While it has made huge strides since the switch to the new engine
Which was actually a pretty big problem i had with it originally. Yet.... it still feels limited.
You can harvest wood! and they've finally made it so you chop trees to do it!
Stone harvesting has been greatly improved, yet still some how lacking. You must find "Nodes" to mine. And if you are on a populated server, its a near impossible task short of logging on when people aren't playing. As they yeild the most lucrative XP for harvestables. Furthermore, another issue i have with this, is you can "steal" peoples XP by getting the last hit on said nodes.
Building has been improved and the only real issue i have right now is with pillars. Which can only be placed in the middle of a floor, which is haphazard to say the least for base continuity. and as such the general strengthening of buildings
because you want to avoid using them. It's really not rewarding building tall, yet some how also nessisary if you want to lock down your territory. Being a person who likes to build in these games, that sucks.
Animals still suck, Bears outrun you no matter what. Animals glitch into and up/over rocks, trees and either into or over the terrain in general. So you will get "Floor bears" and "Glitch Wolves" that are worse than the most perfectly timed jumpscare. With all that said,Hunting has become a little more rewarding, I hope they add better damage for heart and headshots.
Monuments: They have gotten so much better. Even with the XP update. They now have Radiation. The one good side effect of no more Blueprints and BP frags is they are no longer such a hot spot. Which is great as now you are no longer safe in the wilderness. This one small thing has me almost recommending the game.
I still hate to say it, but Rust's popularity still kind of eludes me.
Survival is still not enjoyable. Especially since the XP update.
I really don't like the XP system. Its poorly executed, slows down the game FAR to much. And with the current system of server wipes really doesn't work. As on average servers wipe every 2-4 weeks. So unless you're playing on the equivilent NO BP WIPE servers, you're ♥♥♥♥ed and stuck in a constant cycle of perpetual grinding.
It was a nice idea, but right now, it just doesn't fit the game. That said, it could work in future.
A solid group of friends. Because thanks to the XP system, solo play is pretty much gone.
A good server that doesn't wipe XP to regularly. Map wipes are cool but yeah.
A♥♥♥♥♥♥tonne of time. To achieve next to nothing. This has become more true sicne the XP update.
End game hasn't changed much. Except thanks to afforementioned XP system it has become
harder to get to it. Because any advanced player worth their salt
will grind you back to dust before you get there and hence, prevent progression. Despite having the level, you'll loose your stuff. PvP is probably the
features of this game.
Fact is, still nothing better to do in the end game than harass people, and to be honest. This is where this game shines. The end game is great if you can achieve it. But up until then, its a huge grind.
I still consider this game an "arcade" game. Along the vein of CoD. Moreso than before with the addition of the XP system. It's really cheapened the entire experience. Not to mention, 3/4 of the player base are sass talking 14yo neglected basement dwellers. So expect an authentic XBOX experience. All the routes of Undertale were all satisying adventures in themselves and it's perfect because everything simply...connects.
