It’s alpha. The game runs, but it doesn’t 'work' imo. I don’t see it blossoming into anything greater than what it currently is. It’s not a satisfying experience for the run+gun type.
On a high end pc this old looking game will nearly scrape 60fps in open areas if you're lucky, but as soon as you see grass and trees, expect frequent drops below 10 fps.
The game runs like a dog, and looks like it too. the movement is very clunky so any gun battles are slow and frustrating while you wait for your character to respond, draw his weapon, zoom in and struggle to aim (you're always breathless from running so your crosshair will be floating everywhere, you're likely to only have a handful of bullets too)
There is no in game map and places are not well sign posted and when they are, the Russian text is impossible for a non-native person to read. Expect to be alt+tabbing a lot to locate yourself on an online map (why is that a thing? if it needs to exist online, put it in the damn game.)
If you are playing with friends, set aside multiple hours and try to have a lot of patience. If you spawn too far apart, you'll be looking for tall buildings to jump off, just so you can roll the dice and get a closer spawn. - Why can’t you spawn on your friends or a desired city? Who has the time to run for 40+ minutes just to meet up and get killed minutes later.. devs - take a hint from battlefield, people have lives to live as well, cut the crap.
The people in game seem to generally sit in a few categories:
1 - bambis with no gear, they are not a threat unless they want you to kill them so they can respawn elsewhere
2 - People with gear who are friendly - they don’t want to die.
3 - people with gear who are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s, they wait for their prey and when they kill a bambi who was no threat, they flood them with unnecessary abuse over the mic. You get to listen to this for 30 seconds while you respawn. Beautiful, but thats probably the mindset of the people willing to play it.
It’s very unintuitive, there are no instructions on what to do or how to do it. Every interaction is a slow animation which is hard to cancel and leaves you vulnerable to attack
Visibility is poor, when you finally find your friend you can lose them very quickly without communication. Simply walking through a bush I’ve lost eye sight and got lost many times. Other than the random clothes you pick up, there’s nothing to distinguish you from any other player on the server. It could be your buddy, or it could be an enemy. The ability to at least highlight allies would be nice.
You have to stand right in front of someone and press a key to see their name, not something you can do every time you want to know if that person is a friend or not. By the way, this feature has never even worked for me.
Night time is another issue, you cannot see anything unless you make a torch. It seems people prefer to turn Gamma up as a work around to see in the dark..
There are a lot of random ability’s in the game, which seem to serve little purpose. EG. The vehicles you can work your♥♥♥♥♥off to repair, they are weak and NOBODY uses them. Putting a banana on a stick, farming, putting meat on the fire etc. none of this is worth the effort and serves no purpose.
There’s probably more I haven’t mentioned. This game has managed to make me rant enough to write this review.
I believe it’s like Marmite: you love it or you hate it.
If real life isn’t hard enough, then maybe dayz is for you.

This is a review of contradictions, let me skip to the end:
Do I recommend Rust? YES! The game itself is my favourite thing to play at the moment, even though I spend most of my time trying to avoid any kind of player interaction. I love Facepunch's approach, often the ambitious patches ♥♥♥♥ everything up and there will be a flurry of activity to try and restore order. Garry and co should be commended for their hardworking and continuously open and honest approach, something I'm not used to seeing from many devs. I also personally like the new XP system which has removed the lottery of hunting for blueprints, imbalanced as it is against solo players.
By far and away the worst thing about the game (see "soul destroying") is its community, particularly on the official servers. A lot is said about the toxic nature of Rust players, in fact it's probably the first thing that springs to mind when people mention the game. To quote a certain popular, now sadly departed, science fiction smuggler: "It's true. All of it." The Rust community is hands down the most unpleasant I have ever had the misfortune to experience in ~14 years of online gaming. Suffice to say the common standards of behaviour and language are abhorrent.
Yet somehow, despite that, Rust is an exceptionally good game and is well worth your time. Compared to other Early Access games (say ARK) it runs very well and looks great. The sense of atmosphere is immense and from someone now mostly desensitised to flashy visuals I still often have to stop and look at how amazing the scenery is on a particularly beautiful evening as the sun is beginning to set. Not for too long though because that bloke who just came over the hill is going to shoot me in the side of the face, steal everything I collected in the last hour and cut me up for dinner while repeatedly referring to my Mother's bottom.
That said, get this game. Just whatever you do, don't get attached to anything in it.

It’s alpha. The game runs, but it doesn’t 'work' imo. I don’t see it blossoming into anything greater than what it currently is. It’s not a satisfying experience for the run+gun type.
On a high end pc this old looking game will nearly scrape 60fps in open areas if you're lucky, but as soon as you see grass and trees, expect frequent drops below 10 fps.
The game runs like a dog, and looks like it too. the movement is very clunky so any gun battles are slow and frustrating while you wait for your character to respond, draw his weapon, zoom in and struggle to aim (you're always breathless from running so your crosshair will be floating everywhere, you're likely to only have a handful of bullets too)
There is no in game map and places are not well sign posted and when they are, the Russian text is impossible for a non-native person to read. Expect to be alt+tabbing a lot to locate yourself on an online map (why is that a thing? if it needs to exist online, put it in the damn game.)
If you are playing with friends, set aside multiple hours and try to have a lot of patience. If you spawn too far apart, you'll be looking for tall buildings to jump off, just so you can roll the dice and get a closer spawn. - Why can’t you spawn on your friends or a desired city? Who has the time to run for 40+ minutes just to meet up and get killed minutes later.. devs - take a hint from battlefield, people have lives to live as well, cut the crap.
The people in game seem to generally sit in a few categories:
1 - bambis with no gear, they are not a threat unless they want you to kill them so they can respawn elsewhere
2 - People with gear who are friendly - they don’t want to die.
3 - people with gear who are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s, they wait for their prey and when they kill a bambi who was no threat, they flood them with unnecessary abuse over the mic. You get to listen to this for 30 seconds while you respawn. Beautiful, but thats probably the mindset of the people willing to play it.
It’s very unintuitive, there are no instructions on what to do or how to do it. Every interaction is a slow animation which is hard to cancel and leaves you vulnerable to attack
Visibility is poor, when you finally find your friend you can lose them very quickly without communication. Simply walking through a bush I’ve lost eye sight and got lost many times. Other than the random clothes you pick up, there’s nothing to distinguish you from any other player on the server. It could be your buddy, or it could be an enemy. The ability to at least highlight allies would be nice.
You have to stand right in front of someone and press a key to see their name, not something you can do every time you want to know if that person is a friend or not. By the way, this feature has never even worked for me.
Night time is another issue, you cannot see anything unless you make a torch. It seems people prefer to turn Gamma up as a work around to see in the dark..
There are a lot of random ability’s in the game, which seem to serve little purpose. EG. The vehicles you can work your♥♥♥♥♥off to repair, they are weak and NOBODY uses them. Putting a banana on a stick, farming, putting meat on the fire etc. none of this is worth the effort and serves no purpose.
There’s probably more I haven’t mentioned. This game has managed to make me rant enough to write this review.

At the point that I am writing this review, I have logged about 89.2 hours. I can tell that it will increase, because I think that I am able to call this game MY FAVORITE game on steam. This game is a rollercoaster. No game in history has made my heart beat faster than this one, and I feel that it brings out some interesting natural human reactions to fear/anxiety. The mix of interesting mannerisms and player interaction is what brings this game to life. Now, I want to bring up the overwhelming amount of reviews that bring up the amount of time that this game has been in early access. I think that a lot of players think that when they buy this game, they are getting a finished product. This is 100% not the case; that is what early access is.
"Yeah, but its been SO long since its first realease!"
If you are not willing to actively SUPPORT and FOLLOW the development of Rust, then you shouldent purchase this game. early access alpha is not just a way to play a game before you are "supposed" to, it is a platform for the community to get in on a piece of the active development. Follow the dev team's Twitter, read the status reports, and enjoy the process of development for the best possible experience with Rust.

Lastly, the game has great replayability. There are different routes you can take. A lot of them, actually.
Personally, I can se no reason anyone would have not to like this.
Try it, as cheap as it is there are only few better investments. Food or rent, maybe.

When people ask me about Rust, I'm never really sure where to start. Sure, it's a survival shooter and base builder sim, and a damn good one at that, but it's so much more than that thanks to emergent gameplay and the variety of mods. This comes on top of the fact that Rust's development is so continuous and transparent (devblogs, trello, dev plans, reddit interaction, source control commits public on twitter, and so much more) which is always great in early-access games. Don't be fooled by that label, either: Rust is a fully playable and fairly polished experience with an immense community, not some broken half-built side-project.
For those of you who haven't actually seen the gameplay, I recommend digging up some YouTube videos from the last month or so. The game changes so quickly that anything before then is likely to be out of date in terms of game mechanics, particularly with the recent XP system.
If you're not so big into video reviews, I'll give you a short description of gameplay. You start naked (and I mean naked) with nothing more than a rock and a torch. You run around, probably get chased by other nakeds with rocks, and try not to die. The world is huge, you have no map or compass, no GPS, and only landmarks and the geography to guide yourself by. You bash your rock against some trees to get wood. You see some lumps of stone, you bash those to get stone. You pick up hemp plants for cloth, mushrooms for food, and if you're lucky you might find a pig that you can chase down and butcher for meat. You build a camp fire, you cook the meat, you eat it, your food and water bars jump up a little. It's getting dark and someone with a bow sees your campfire... you're forced to make a hasty getaway down a hill and hide in a bush until the arrows stop flying past. Eventually you brave it out, but it's now pitch black and you're forced with a dilemma: light your torch to see your way around, but risk being spotted and hunted down, or fumble around in the dark and hope you don't wander off a cliff or into the mouth of a bear. You manage to find a small archway to hide under until daybreak. You've been bonking things with your rock for a bit and you've gained enough XP to level up! You can now spend some of that XP on unlocking better tools, and some clothes. You make a hatchet, some cloth pants, and go back to farming some materials. You get enough to build a small base. You craft yourself some paper, then a building plan, and a hammer. You build a small two-by-two base with foundations, then walls and a doorway, and finally a roof. You craft a wooden door, then a lock, and place them. Ah, secure. Down goes a sleeping bag as a respawn point, in case the worst should happen. You craft and place a small wooden box to store some spare loot - you don't want to get caught out with a pile of ore and stone on you if you get shot at! Now that's all done you can feel safe. Right?
Footsteps and rustling outside. Then another set. It goes quiet, then you hear some jumping, then the sound of wooden structures being erected. Silence for a second, followed by footsteps... from above? They're on the roof! Thunk. An arrow? Thunk! Another! Then more, two, three at a time. You're being raided. Not long before they break through your roof. You craft a wooden spear, frantically watching the craft timer tick down, seconds seeming like minutes. Finally, it completes, and you equip it. You're nervous. You crouch-walk up to the door, spear in hand, in the throw position. You open the door- and get blasted in the face by a pipe shotgun. The respawn screen appears. You click your bag to respawn, but before you even make it back in game you've had a hatchet stuck through your head and your sleeping bag has been cut into pieces. Your loot is gone. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s even took the key and stole your front door.
You respawn, back at the beach. You carry on, though you've still got your XP and level. You farm your way back up, and this time when you build your base you add a second door as an airlock, to make sure they only get the loot on your body if the front door is compromised when you die. You learn about tool cupboards and place one down to prevent people building near your base. You even manage to farm a load of stone and upgrade your base to prevent arrow-raiding, then get a furnace going to produce metal fragments and sulphur, and get yourself a nice metal door and code lock (those keys are so annoying to manage!). You've got a crossbow, a bow, clothes, a bit of armor, and even a pipe shotgun with a few shells. Things are looking good. But wait... footsteps outside again. And what's that beeping sound? Before you know it an explosion rips a hole in your wall and you're blasting the interlopers with your pipe shotty and skewering them with arrows. But it is too much, and you fall. Your bag is destroyed, and your loot is being pilfered, but this time you built a little 1x1 shack up the road with a bag and a small box of supplies. You leap back into the game, arm up with a few stone spears and a bow, and jump the raiders from behind. You get some kills in, but the commotion has drawn the attention of a roving clan and you (along with the raiders) get mown down by AK-47 fire.
You respawn, back at the beach, this time on the other side of the map. You're running through a small forest while farming, and spot another player. They see you. Your instinct is to run, but you have nothing to lose, so you jump up and down repeatedly as part of the internationally understood friendly greeting. They crouch for a moment, unsure of you, but then return the gesture. You have a brief chat, your voices broadcast locally to the surrounding area. A crossbow shot flies between you, and you both scarper into a nearby maze of rocks. You quickly erect a small shack and both take shelter. The enemy appears to have lost you for now, so you gingerly explore the surroundings for any sign of them. Nothing around. Your friend suggests teaming up to make a base. A wise move - with twice the farming rate you could have a nice big base with honeycombed walls, multiple floors, lots of doors, and double the active defense. Before long this dream is becoming a reality, and you're both high enough level to take on passing aggressors and small raid parties. You decorate your house with paintings, you build a tower with a sniper's nest, and overhanging positions to shoot down from. Your base is fortified with metal and stone, and you even save up enough sulphur and animal fat to make your own raiding supplies. Your friend brings another online, so you're now a group of three. You decide to go out on a raid.
You're on your way to the airfield when you spot a small two-by-two wooden base. Ordinarily you'd ignore it, but as you sprint past you notice you're not building blocked. A foolish move! You here a couple of steps inside... oh, someone's online. This could make for some fun. Your friends build a foundation and staircase up the side, and you all hop onto the roof. One keeps watch of the door while the others fire arrows into the flimsy wooden surface. A moment later, the door opens. The poor inhabitant doesn't stand a chance against the shotgun blast to his face. The loot inside is yours. You take a moment to reflect on how, not so long ago, that would've been you.

Borderlands is primarily a single-player game where you wake in a snow drift and gradually fall deeper and deeper into a complicated plot. Fortunately there are lots of side missions, most of them short, most of them pretty easy, and you can save and exit the game at any point. There's plenty of humour too, and some very memorable NPC characters. One of them is uncannily like a certain friend of mine, and their antics had me laughing out loud.
The neat twist is that when you're playing a game, up to three of your Steam friends can join in by clicking 'Join Game' on your profile page. No random strangers, no public internet servers, just people you know.
In Borderlands your character gains levels with experience, which could lead to a mismatch between friends. Fortunately it's easy to start a new character, and just as easy to switch between them. It was fun to start the game over with a friend on level one, while my character was level 21. Fun for me, not so much for the bad guys ...

The mix of interesting mannerisms and player interaction is what brings this game to life. Now, I want to bring up the overwhelming amount of reviews that bring up the amount of time that this game has been in early access. I think that a lot of players think that when they buy this game, they are getting a finished product. This is 100% not the case; that is what early access is.
"Yeah, but its been SO long since its first realease!"
If you are not willing to actively SUPPORT and FOLLOW the development of Rust, then you shouldent purchase this game. early access alpha is not just a way to play a game before you are "supposed" to, it is a platform for the community to get in on a piece of the active development. Follow the dev team's Twitter, read the status reports, and enjoy the process of development for the best possible experience with Rust.

Borderlands 2. Those who like it love it, those who hate it always will. Nonetheless, I'm one of those who loves it. I myself have played well over 300 hours of this game across different platforms, and have at least 9 separate characters. The game-play is fluid, easy to jump into, and immensely fun. The amount of enemies spanning from humans, to robots, to crazy♥♥♥♥♥creatures is immense, and the amount only increases with the second and third play-throughs. And obviously, Borderlands 2's procedural weapon system, with the 12 bazillion guns, is a lot of fun. You never know what you're gonna get. And the DLC's amazingly add even more of these great things into the game, along with more of the hilarious humor that you quickly come to love. Overall, this game is easily in my top three of all time favourites, and might just be up there as #1. I'd recommend it to anybody who likes grinding for levels and loot, and somebody who has a sense of humor.

Borderlands is primarily a single-player game where you wake in a snow drift and gradually fall deeper and deeper into a complicated plot. Fortunately there are lots of side missions, most of them short, most of them pretty easy, and you can save and exit the game at any point. There's plenty of humour too, and some very memorable NPC characters. One of them is uncannily like a certain friend of mine, and their antics had me laughing out loud.
The neat twist is that when you're playing a game, up to three of your Steam friends can join in by clicking 'Join Game' on your profile page. No random strangers, no public internet servers, just people you know.
In Borderlands your character gains levels with experience, which could lead to a mismatch between friends. Fortunately it's easy to start a new character, and just as easy to switch between them. It was fun to start the game over with a friend on level one, while my character was level 21. Fun for me, not so much for the bad guys ...

I've been hooked onto Rust as soon as I started playing it, today marks my attempt to break away however. Anyways, the Rust mindset has been seeping into my brain like a parasite. Everytime I see a bald person/cancer patient I shoot them in the head, quick and clean kill. Yeah I know this is frowned upon by the community but when I get home I can start playing Rust as an escape from that reality.

Rust is a fun game ruined by a horrible community.
Imagine spawning in, freshly naked with only a rock as your weapon/tool.
Imagine farming some wood to start crafting when all of a sudden, you're dead.
Why? Because fun is not allowed.
99% of this game is dying in the first 10 minutes because most people have nothing to really do other than hunt fresh spawns by the beaches.
It's less common in low pop. servers as there are less people to actively trying to kill you. I believe the reason why this issue is so prelavent is due to having absolutely 0 PvE elements. This issue can occur in Ark as well, but Ark gives you reasons to work together. This game, does not. The progression system is SUPPOSED to help with that, but a lot of servers already have preformed clans. New players are basically resource hogs for more veteran players. You aren't worth keeping alive and munitions aren't hard to come by end game.
It CAN be fun if you get a group of friends together, but as a solo player, you're pretty much SOL unless you manage to come across a friendly player, which seems to be pretty rare.
Losing all that you literally built up, in .5 seconds because someone else is bored, makes this game far more frustrating than fun.
On top of that, the progression system, similar to Ark, makes it even more difficult for a solo player to get anywhere. The leveling system is pretty bad at the moment, far worse than Ark from my experience.
The game itself is about a 7/10
Performance issues and the progression system really hinder the game, but outside of that it's a really nicely crafted survival game with a neat take on the genre.
However, the playerbase makes it a 3/10. Trying to get some sort of progression, is usually halted 5 minutes after you spawn. I always see people say it's server dependant yadda yadda, but it shouldn't be. The game needs an incentive to NOT kill new players. I wouldn't mind the KoS if it were on fair grounds, but have no way to defend yourself while being instantly killed by someone is not fun. And that's a majority of your time spent on this game unless you happen to find a freshly wiped server. And even then, as a solo player, or even duo, you'll still get out progressed fairly quickly by already formed clans.
tl;dr Do not buy unless you have 4 or more friends to play with and expect a LOT of frustration early on.

How this got game of the year I'll never know.
Not that it's a bad game by any stretch, it's just that it's not doing anything new.  Through the first play-through of the game I quite liked it a lot, but getting to new-game plus (true vault hunter mode) I noticed that getting better weapons is just not happening.  These are the minor qualms in the design, and the major ones will follow.
Enemy design and AI: It gets old very quickly fighting the same set of raiders over and over.  In the late game enemies basically become giant bags of HP that will take every single bullet you have to take down solo without getting any smarter.  boss design is good, but the game does become a grind too quickly.
Multiplayer: This is about the best thing Borderlands has going for it, and it still works well in this game.  This is the reason I recommend this game.
Weapons: Here's the biggest problem I've had with the game.  Spending hours upon hours playing, never seeing an orange weapon, and having multiplayer characters basically waiting till you kill the enemies to swoop in and take the best weapons does get quite old after a while.  This basically means that long-range sniper characters will have the hardest time in multiplayer but tend to play one of the most important roles.
DLC: Is it just me, or are more and more game companies shipping unfinished products with the intention of making games even more expensive than they were back when cartridges actually cost something to produce?
Engine Design/Performance: For what's going on in the game it surprises me that one some hardware this game gets frame-drops like crazy when it's really not doing much more than the original game did.  Otherwise, the graphical style and execution is as well done as anything that talks to the graphics card using DirectX or OpenGL should.
Bottom Line: Good game, a few problems here and there that get under my skin, but as a developer myself I tend to be quite a bit more critical than most.  The best part of this game is the socialization with other players, and as that role it works very well.

No matter how many times I get killed, raided, betrayed, harassed and ragequit, I still find myself comming back to this game. There are so many ways to play this game:
*Be a builder- design your base in Fortify, build it ingame, and put it to the test against real players to see what needs to be improved in either strength, complexity or mobility. Or build something to show off your architectural skills, something that shines above all the giant inpenetrable cube vaults.
*Be a lone hunter- lurk around trees, bushes or monuments behind unsuspecting prey, and kill them for either loot or just pure self satisfaction. But remember to watch your own back as well...
*Be an explorer- scavenge monuments, and lay your eyes on player built marvels as you avoid direct contact with other players, and appreciate the vast world that is Rust!
*Be a pirate- get some buddies and gang up on lone wanderers, harass bases, and troll asshats. Wether it's for revenge, pure bloodlust or just ♥♥♥♥♥ and giggles, there's always strength in numbers.
*Be a collector- spend time gathering rare resources, weapons, and equipment- raising the risk by defending something worth defending always gets your blood rurshing when someone attempts to take it away.
*Be a ruler- create a clan and expand your territory to show everyone nearby who's the boss. Though beware of making too many enemies, as even a king can't fight the entirety of his own people, not to mention betrayals that lurk around every corner.
*Be an altruist- rather than launching a bullet into the fresh, naked newcommers, instead offer a helping hand why don't ya- give them advice, protection, starting loot or just a friendly chatter. Even if just one out of ten remembers your kindness, then ten out of hundred might become your allies in a time of need.
Or be all of these! You can be whoever you choose to be, and you can be sure that someone will always try to get in your way to make sure you don't succeed- ain't that a bucket of salt and peppers, eh lad? Nothin' like a good challenge to spice up an otherwise mundane ball!
Happy Rusting my fellow canibals!

DayZ is simply brilliant, it always has been.  Ever since the dayz, if you'll pardon the pun, of ARMA II.  Bringing survival to the everyday man, with its massive world, with laregely varying locations.  There is no script, there is no story, there is only you and whoever you choose to bring along on a mighty adventure.
This game isn't for the faint of heart, those who will drop something at the drop of a hat will not be satisfied with this game.  Those, however, who are persistent, competitive and most of all ruthless, will love this game.
Although the game has many, many positives, there are currently a few aspects that let the game down.  Ladders are at the moment my biggest enemy, killing fully geard characters dar to often for it to be looked over.  The audio engine, whilst it works it is not perfect, the 3D audio is let's just say not great, if you hear a sound that continues, you look around, that sound will stay at the same spot and not rotate along with your character.  Which forces you to be on your feet for the entire time you are playing.  If you slack off and don't pay attention you will be killed, you will be captured, and the Bible will be read to you.
To wrap this up, buy this game if you want to, if you think you can handle it, handle the losses and the victories, you are not only fighting zombies, there are hardly any, Thank Darwin, they are merely a nuisance.  Your main foe will be the environment first, which includes survival aspects like sickness, people (other players) second they are sneaky little buggers, and of course third Zombies.
The game is currently great fun, with some mates and will only get better.

First off I'd like to say that there are a few things that are not perfect about this game and that none of that matters because this game is built solely for a fun time to be had, and it achieves that in every way.
The main complaint that will come aroung is that most quests are simply "Go find this regular enemy and kill him," or, "Find these items that fall from killing all these bad guys." In other words, much of the questing is simply fetch quests and they have the potential to feel a bit repetitive. This is absolutely true and it can feel a little grueling wading through hours of the same fetch quests for the third time simply to complete all three playthroughs of a single character.
However, as I said before, this would absolutely not stop me from recommending this game to every single person as it incorporates a number of things that put it far above the competition in plenty of ways and in turn becomes one of the most enjoyable games that I have ever played.  First, and to me most importantly, it does something that used to be the norm and has long since become something that most games these days forget about, cooperative gameplay, and in particular, split-screen coop (I realize split-screen is not initially supported on the PC but setting it up takes a matter of a 2 minutes and a google search.)
Another thing that puts this game on top for me is the absolutely gorgeous art style. In my opinion trying to create realism is a commendable goal but sets up one's game for less than three years of relevance as graphics power improves so much with each passing year. This cel-chaded style on the other hand, will look wonderful for years to come. In fact, going back and playing the first Borderlands is still quite fun as it doesn't look heavily outdated like most FPS games from more than a year or two ago.  One more thing to mention in regards to the art style is just how many different guns there are and the pure excitement of finding a new gun of high rarity. It is a truly exciting experience picking up a new gun and just bringing it into battle to find out what makes it truly unique, whether it be a gun that is completely inaccurate but with ricocheting bullets to create a virtual wall of bullets or one that upon reloading gets thrown into the air and chases down the enemies while shooting them.
And one more thing that truly separates it is how it refuses to take it self seriously for even a moment. Time after time, it makes an absolute fool of itself in the most wonderful way possible and through this creates completely unrealistic characters and makes you fall in love with every single one of them. Whether it be the endlessly annoying but truly hilarious CL4P-TP or the main characters themselves, such as the assassin that refuses to speak anything but Haiku, the characters are truly unique and never get old.
In the end, while it has one or two shortfalls in comparison to games built around story or a specific gameplay element, it never fails to be one of the most fun experiences out there, and will never fail to entertain, especially if one plays it with a friend.

In all seriousness, Borderlands 2 is a great step forward from the first game. The menus are cleaner and more crisp, the enemies are more diverse, and the jokes are funnier. In fact, one of the best things about the Borderlands franchise is it's trademark sense of humor. Not to mention the improvement to the looting system. Items will be more unique, swapping out weapons for better ones is easier, and there are so much rare guns to be gotten. There is also the huge amount of quests to be completed, some more serious and difficult than others.
Boss fights are almost always engaging, keeping you interested and urging you to find a useful strategy to beating them. As I said, there a lots of different types of enemies, such as armored enemies, tentacle enemies, invisible enemies and more. The "price for content" aspect is terrific, as there a lot to do and see in this game.
The plot is also one of the strong points, with one of my favourite villains. Combine these with the campaign add-ons, and you've got a well-structured, enjoyable story.
Borderlands 2 will give you many hours of enjoyment, and is highly recommended.

Yes, it's in Alpha and a bit buggy. Yes, it takes quite a long time to get full military gear compared to Arma 2/3 mods. And yes, there are almost no vehicles. But all server-hopping bandits and horrible glitches aside, the experience is great. First of all, you have to plan encounters with other players, because since gearing up is so hard, in this game you actually don't want your character to die. Second, the amount of detail in this game is pretty amazing. By that I don't mean graphics and physics (which are also great), but gameplay.
For example, if you accidentally drink/get force fed some raw meat, you might get sick. Your body temperature will rise and you will puke. You will need to keep yourself hydrated and find charcoal tabs to heal the disease. If you are getting soaked because of the rain or because of falling into water, your temperature will lower and you will need to find dry clothes or use heat packs, because if you don't, you will die of hypothermia. Or, if your pistol is in a chest holster and you get shot in the chest, your pistol will get damaged and be inaccurate and have a change of misfiring. You will need to find a repairing kit in order to properly use it again. And, if you find a car, chances are its battery is empty and you will need to find a new one in order to drive it.
It's these little things that make the game so realistic and more and more stuff is being added in updates every month or so, and the game-breaking glitches are also mostly a thing of the past.
I do highly recommend playing this game with a (group of) friend(s), though, because IMO it's more fun than being a lone wolf (which could get boring pretty fast).

In this review I'll try to be concise but deepening the major aspects of the game. (°ロ°)☝
This game has a Difficulty Curve that is a lot steep.
Everytime you start a new game (I'll talk about this later, in the gameplay section), the enemies become A LOT stronger. But until you enter OP, it's pretty easy. Once you reach level 72 and try to reach lvl80 OP80), this game becomes impossible.
This game has a LOT of DLC and every single one is nice (except for the aesthetics ones).
The regular ones are beautiful and add an incredible amount of missions and new enemies to slay;
The levelers expands the level pool from 60 to 72 and OP8;
The festive usually came out for the holidays and contained a small main mission, some secondary missions and a raid boss.
I suggest to buy the GOTY.
Every weapon is made of 5 parts (Barrel, Body, Grip, Sight, Stock), each one of these can be made by a single manufacturer (for a total of 9), making the gun-pool virtually infinite. Actually the viable ones are only a few.
The cell shading, combined with how the textures are painted is AMAZING. It makes the closest objects look smoother and nicer, and enhance the beautiful locations creating a “cut” effect between the background and the actual playable game.
Another aspect of this game that is fascinating is how well the cast is characterized, painted and located in the game.
The storyline is sweet, nothing too deep nor shallow, it creates a few hours of gameplay without boring the player and making room for a few additional runs.
This game actually starts once you've beaten it 3 times, entering the UVHM: this will for sure provide a very fun (even if frustrating) challenge.
Probably this game has the best community ever.
The 90% of people that  you will meet in-game is nice and cool and has no problems with explaining you some secrets or unusual ways to reach your objective.
Gearbox also keeps track of the community and releases almost everyday Shift codes, which can be used to unlock various in-game content such as weapons, costumes and other vanity items. In addiction they organise events and entertain the fans even out of the game.
I Love you Gearbox.

Borderlands 2 achieved what I thought would be hard to pull off: It was much better than the first one
When Borderlands 1 came out, it was, without doubt one of the best shooters of the year. Tho it still felt cold at times, yet the funny moments made you look over it. Now, Borderlands 2 gave some warmth to it, the characters felt more alive (mainly to the fact that you are by now used to them as some are already from the last game, like the playable characters who are now important NPCs). In the first game, you had to find the vault key, stop Atlas, etc... In the second one, evil has a face, a handsome face in the form of Handsome Jack.
But to the game elements itself. There are still bazzilions of guns, but there are much more diverse depending on the corporation that made them. The cartoonish graphics are back, and better than ever. The sounds are quite good. The voice acting is better mainly to the fact that there are more lines. Gun sounds again are neat.
The story, like said, has a better grip on you. The return of the playable characters (Roland, Brick, Mordecai and Lilith), good ol' Claptrap, Scooter, Moxxi, Marcus,.... as well as some new, like, the propably craziest thirteen-year-old girl you will ever see in a video game, Tiny Tina.
Anyone who played the original will know of the special abilities of the playable classes and the vehicular combat, but I shall repeat that. You get 4 classes (soldier, siren, gunzerker and assassin) without DLCs. Each has an RPG kind of leveling and unlocking skills. You can edit their looks in special stations for customatization. The combat is great and doesn't stop on running and gunning, but there is also driving and gunning. Vehicles are back. Not just a fast way to travell the map, but also a nice tool to crush your enemies.
Aside the long-enough campaign, the co-op online mutliplayer is again one of the best in gaming in general, with up to 4 people joining together to fight the evils on Pandora and stop Jack (note: for each player that enteres the game, the game becomes slightly harder). After the regular SP, you get the option for a harder mode, going back to the starting point, just now, enemies will be on higher levels. Much later you get even more powerful bosses, which I recomend, if you ain't some crazy asian pro-gamer, to fight in a group of 4.
You know the people saying how good Borderlands 2 is? Yes? They are freaking right, so go buy it

Rust: Hobbes Was Right
Have you ever wondered if Thomas Hobbes' philosophies still hold merit in the modern day and age?
Do you long to see what life would be like without the firm hand of the state?
Do you fancy yourself a good person?  An enlightened and upstanding human being that cares for their fellows?
Then wait no longer for I give you Rust!  The post apocolyptic misery simulator that shows us just how much we need society to keep our animal instincts in line.
Your day begins as follows - You walk up naked and alone and in between 9 -30 minutes you'll be dead having accomplished nothing at all.  In all likelihood you'll have been killed by the animals that walkaround on two legs(this is a grave insult to animals since they are nowhere near as barbaric as people).  You'll then respawn to repeat the process!  This game has recieved Satan's approval as a subsitute for hell.
Worse still is that the game teaches us something - that we should distrust the people around us and kill them for no better reason than they could kill us.  Yes, this is proof positive that we truly flawed and pathetic creatures for even in a game do we revert back to animal natures.
Thank you Rust for teaching me how much I truly do value the bootheel of the state on my throat for it keeps me safe from all the other monsters that live around me and who would kill me if the constraints of society were lifted from them.
If you too want to experience this existential awakening and be butchered(virtually) by your fellow human beings then buy this game now!
Misery awaits you too!

After playing through Undertale 3 times, experiencing all 3 endings of this amazingly crafted game, I must say, the game has been really impressive. Although it doesn't have crazy graphics like Call of Duty or Battlefield, all that should matter is the story and purpose of the game, as well as character development, plot, and many other elements of the game.
The Neutral run opened my eyes to wanting to do a Pacifist run, reflecting back on what I did in the run, killing Toriel. It all inspired me to keep going, reset and fix the mistakes I did. The final boss, Asriel Dreemur, was just great. Knowing his childhood, becoming best friends with the First Human (AKA Chara), and then losing Chara is just heart touching. Knowing his suffering, losing his best friend, living a miserable life as a flower with the mindset of "kill or be killed" and the inability to love or feel anything, gah. The battle itself was great, giving a little backstory of Asriel's past life, having a person to call a friend, losing them. Here he is trying to get them back and assuming the protagonist (Frisk) is their best friend. Saving your friends, and saving Asriel. It's all just amazing and beautifully made. Having the option to comfort Asriel just brings tears to my eyes thinking of it. Knowing all he's gone through, he truly deserves some comfort and love. It was sad knowing he wasn't able to go on with his happy life with the worry of turning back into a flower again.. I feel bad for the poor kid.
The Genocide run.. is a completely different story. It did bring out some additional story and tough bosses and tough decisions. Should I keep going on my path and kill everyone I've befriended in my last run, or turn around before it's too late...? It's basically a grindfest but I was interested in the new characters because of my actions.. Undyne the Undying, Mettaton NEO, the different dialogues, way too much for me to think of at the moment. The battle with Sans was by far one of my favorites, since it puts you right into the battle and requires you to be quick with dodging attacks. In the end, it's worth it though. Kind of creepy knowing Chara was watching you and "guiding" you the entire run, though.
Personally, my favorite run was the Pacifist since that was the run that touched my heart the most, seeing all of the (main) characters together, living a happy life outside of the pitiful and dreadful Underground, and just the thought behind it. Live life while you can. The special thanks was really interesting as well.
Honestly, Undertale HAS to be the best game I've played EVER, I give it a 10/10. If you haven't bought it yet, what are you waiting for? If you want amazing characters, personalities, different stories, endings (depending on your run you do), soundtrack, and many other things, all in one great game, I believe it is worth the $10.

Don't make the mistake I did - buy the soundtrack bundle! The music is amazing and I'm gonna buy the soundtrack (seperately) after writing this. It's a great game and I'd reccommend it to anyone who loves a story based game!

In this review I'll try to be concise but deepening the major aspects of the game. (°ロ°)☝
This game has a Difficulty Curve that is a lot steep.
Everytime you start a new game (I'll talk about this later, in the gameplay section), the enemies become A LOT stronger. But until you enter OP, it's pretty easy. Once you reach level 72 and try to reach lvl80 OP80), this game becomes impossible.
This game has a LOT of DLC and every single one is nice (except for the aesthetics ones).
The regular ones are beautiful and add an incredible amount of missions and new enemies to slay;
The levelers expands the level pool from 60 to 72 and OP8;
The festive usually came out for the holidays and contained a small main mission, some secondary missions and a raid boss.
I suggest to buy the GOTY.
Every weapon is made of 5 parts (Barrel, Body, Grip, Sight, Stock), each one of these can be made by a single manufacturer (for a total of 9), making the gun-pool virtually infinite. Actually the viable ones are only a few.
The cell shading, combined with how the textures are painted is AMAZING. It makes the closest objects look smoother and nicer, and enhance the beautiful locations creating a “cut” effect between the background and the actual playable game.
Another aspect of this game that is fascinating is how well the cast is characterized, painted and located in the game.
The storyline is sweet, nothing too deep nor shallow, it creates a few hours of gameplay without boring the player and making room for a few additional runs.
This game actually starts once you've beaten it 3 times, entering the UVHM: this will for sure provide a very fun (even if frustrating) challenge.
Probably this game has the best community ever.
The 90% of people that  you will meet in-game is nice and cool and has no problems with explaining you some secrets or unusual ways to reach your objective.
Gearbox also keeps track of the community and releases almost everyday Shift codes, which can be used to unlock various in-game content such as weapons, costumes and other vanity items. In addiction they organise events and entertain the fans even out of the game.
I Love you Gearbox.

Borderlands 2 achieved what I thought would be hard to pull off: It was much better than the first one
When Borderlands 1 came out, it was, without doubt one of the best shooters of the year. Tho it still felt cold at times, yet the funny moments made you look over it. Now, Borderlands 2 gave some warmth to it, the characters felt more alive (mainly to the fact that you are by now used to them as some are already from the last game, like the playable characters who are now important NPCs). In the first game, you had to find the vault key, stop Atlas, etc... In the second one, evil has a face, a handsome face in the form of Handsome Jack.
But to the game elements itself. There are still bazzilions of guns, but there are much more diverse depending on the corporation that made them. The cartoonish graphics are back, and better than ever. The sounds are quite good. The voice acting is better mainly to the fact that there are more lines. Gun sounds again are neat.
The story, like said, has a better grip on you. The return of the playable characters (Roland, Brick, Mordecai and Lilith), good ol' Claptrap, Scooter, Moxxi, Marcus,.... as well as some new, like, the propably craziest thirteen-year-old girl you will ever see in a video game, Tiny Tina.
Anyone who played the original will know of the special abilities of the playable classes and the vehicular combat, but I shall repeat that. You get 4 classes (soldier, siren, gunzerker and assassin) without DLCs. Each has an RPG kind of leveling and unlocking skills. You can edit their looks in special stations for customatization. The combat is great and doesn't stop on running and gunning, but there is also driving and gunning. Vehicles are back. Not just a fast way to travell the map, but also a nice tool to crush your enemies.
Aside the long-enough campaign, the co-op online mutliplayer is again one of the best in gaming in general, with up to 4 people joining together to fight the evils on Pandora and stop Jack (note: for each player that enteres the game, the game becomes slightly harder). After the regular SP, you get the option for a harder mode, going back to the starting point, just now, enemies will be on higher levels. Much later you get even more powerful bosses, which I recomend, if you ain't some crazy asian pro-gamer, to fight in a group of 4.
You know the people saying how good Borderlands 2 is? Yes? They are freaking right, so go buy it

Undertale: The game that took the internet by storm, and isn't for everyone.
Reasons:
-Fantastic Music
-Applies unique qualities to familiar formats for RPGs (such as the battle system)
-Simple and effective writing (simple is not a bad label, it is a descriptive label) It achieves its goal and delivers what it intends to at a fitting pace for how the game is presented.
-Uses graphical simplicity in an efficient way beyond the "eurphoric retro feel"
-Supports out-of-the-box thinking with the genre (or games as a whole) and how to convey a story
* Examples: All choices of playstyle aim to deliver a finish that inspires reflection and may cause alternate path walking. (Many games can be satisfactory with only going through one path.) Special example; creator understands curiosity, delivers additional content in mysterious ways for the curious such as in coding. Missing this has no impact on the game though.
Issues:
-Simplicity is off-putting for many (this is a preference meaning it cannot be wrong to find the game unenjoyable)
-Story is both deep and simple. Once you learn -everything- and can analyze it from an "overall" view the story can be summarized in merely a few key points. (does not make it poorly delivered)
-Gameplay becomes repetitive (boss fights are exempt from this due to additional mechanics)
-Short playtime
-Little to no replay value (In this context, replay describes AFTER learning all endings and differences)
-Dialogue is extensive (can be good, bad if the dialogue form in comedy is not to player's taste)
Overview
A simple game with a not so simple objective that successfully fiddles with the formula for the genre. It delivers this objective effectively. Do not try the game with high or low expectations as endless others claim it to be. It is good for the right consumer, bad for the other consumers. Judge whether it is for you or not by seeing what it gives you, not by what others say it will or won't give you.
Best played with no knowledge of the game, spoilers from early or late in the game will affect experience SEVERELY.
Personal rating: 10/10
True Rating: 8/10

Okay so this is my first review.
*EARLY ACCESS CRY BABIES*
I cant stress enough: This game is in EARLY ACCESS. Many of the reviews as of today are complaints. They talk about how the game is ruined becasue of a new feature. Or how the developers wipe the servers every so often and so on. What they dont relize is that this is... EARLY ACCESS. The game is currently being developed! It is not the finished project. They wine and complain about this stuff and♥♥♥♥♥♥on the devs for developing. That like a teacher yelling at you for doing your homework right and on time. Shesh these reviews are from people who got the game to play a finished project. They probably dont even submit bug reports or feedback.
**ABOUT THE GAME**
So the game is a survival game. who would have guessed. You wake up in a world with a rock and torch. You wander off and collect essintial materials(stone and wood). You craft things with a very nice and easy on the eyes menu. You equip weapons you craft or find. Many of the best places to find good items are the "monuments." These can be easily identified by there massive scale. They are most likely the remanance of an old world. You can craft "Building Plans" wich alow you to build a house/base. You progress by leveling up and learning new recipies(as of the latest update.) You will find yourself meeting other survivors. They may be nice or they may want to kill you. Creating a pvp aspect. The game is very much a phycological stimulator. Trying to decide if you should kill or help the man you just met. Thinking of the best way to get away from an encounter. Or teaming up and suviving together. This is the basic style of gameplay.
***MY OPINION***
So I've played rust for a little bit. I dont have 2000 hours on it like some "people". However I have seen enough to know what to do and how to play. One thing that is a big problem is the community. They are toxic. They kill any and everyone if they can. Its a KOS game really. Now there is a way to escape this toxicity. What I have been doing is playing on PVE servers. There are very few of them but they seem to be getting popular. You can escape the senseless killing and team up with other players, build a house start a farm, make an obstical course. What ever you want. However in PVE you can still be killed by animals or the helicoptor. What I love about the game is playing with friends is really fun. But playing solo is just as fun. You can meet people at a monument and barder a pickax for some cloth or whatever. I really like this game. Its enjoyable and its constantly being updated and the devs are active.
****FINAL NOTE****
EARLY ACCESS = CHANGE = RESTARTS = STARTING OVER NEW!! Be aware of this when buying any EARLY ACCESS game. It gets very hard for developers when they dont get game feedback. Give them feedback! dont complain about changes! find a bug? report it then. The only bad thing this game has is people ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ on new content the developers add. Go play a finished game if you want to♥♥♥♥♥♥on something. Dont give a game that ISNT FINISHED criticism for a feature that they are testing. This game is a test not a final product.
IF YOU THINK IT LOOKS GOOD AND WANT TO TEST IT OUT THEN GET IT. IF YOU WANT A FINISHED GAME GO SOMEWHERE ELSE.

I have played nearly 1000 hours on this game. DayZ has it's shortcomings, mainly some glitches and optimization issues. I am, however, confident that if the developers do get this game finished and released, within the next year or so, it could be one of the best games ever made. With all the potential that I believe it has, it would be sad if that didn't come to fruition.

DayZ is currently in an Early Access state, meaning the game isn't finished yet. Truthfully, when you play the game, you will see why. It's clear to anyone this game is unfinished. It has a lot of bugs, and glitches, and things will happen that will make you want to rip your hair out of your head, but that doesn't inherently make a game lesser.
DayZ has a niche crew. If you like surviving, being on the run, and looting towns whilst feeling constant pressure that at any moment you could die is actually very fun. On the other hand, losing items, dying, and having to restart due to bugs isn't very fun.
The idea of DayZ is very cool and interesting, but the exceucution is subpar. In the end, if you like exploring and cooperating with your buddies, and have a tolerance for bad things that will (eventually) happen, you might just get a kick out of DayZ.

(I'm going to be skinned alive for this but I don't care.) Undertale is a RPG that came out a few months ago, and was praised by so many people. Now, at first I thought the game was somewhat fun, but now it just seems boring. "Why?" you may ask, and I will tell you. The reason I got bored with the game is how you always encounter enemies in the wild, without any signs. Another complaint is the difficulty, the pacifist run is extremely easy to beat, and the genocide is a major grindfest that takes a long time, and only has a few (I'm not mean enough to spoil exactly how many.) challenging battles. My final complaint is the one that made me despise this game. THE FANBASE. You might say "well just ignore it you idiot" but... its everywhere. Its in Splatoon. Its in TF2. Its in every little unrelated youtube video. Its nearly impossible to avoid, especially when someone goes "I won't spoil the game for you" yet spoils the game in the next sentence. Overall, Undertale is a game that doesn't have much replay value, has a bad fanbase(but its tame compared to what I've seen before.), but it was fun at first, has a creative dodging system, and does have some pretty good music (my favorite part about the game.). In my opinion though (you can't tell me what I can and can't like, but you could tell me possibly what could redeem some of the negatives i mentioned, I am up for that.) the game got very boring for me after a while. (I did play the game for a while, so I didn't play the game for 5 mins and write a negative review.)

This game is extremely addicting-With every death, there's the feeling that you've learned something new that might keep you alive just a little bit longer. A few tips include:
1: Find at least one other person to be your friend. Survival alone gets stressful and depressing, if you can even pull it off.
2: Establish a house as quickly as possible. It doesn't have to be super fancy, you can improve it later. But the worst feeling is returning to your character to find he's been eaten by a wolf in his sleep.
3: If you hear gunshots, run. The hunting of naked characters has been turned into an art form and you have only a rock.
Overall, 90% of the people you meet in game are some of the moste distrustful, angry, opportunistic people you'll ever meet. Treasure those few kind souls you find, and don't get discouraged.

To be fair, you have to have a very high IQ to understand Undertale. The humour is extremely subtle, and without a solid grasp of theoretical physics most of the jokes will go over a typical viewer’s head. There’s also Sans`s nihilistic outlook, which is deftly woven into his characterisation- his personal philosophy draws heavily from Cancer Fandom literature, for instance. The fans understand this stuff; they have the intellectual capacity to truly appreciate the depths of these  jokes, to realise that they’re not just funny- they say something deep about LIVE. As a consequence people who dislike Undertale truly ARE idiots- of course they wouldn’t appreciate, for instance, the humour in Rick’s existential catchphrase “DO YOU WANNA HAVE A BAD TIME?,” which itself is a cryptic reference to Turgenev’s Russian epic Fathers and Sons. I’m smirking right now just imagining one of those addlepated simpletons scratching their heads in confusion as Toby Fox’s genius wit unfolds itself on their computer screens. What fools.. how I pity them.

I tried to enjoy this game. I really did.
But, it's just too much of an aquired taste.
Though some aspects of this game (most prominently the soundtrack) are amazing, it falls so short in other aspects that it's not worth buying.
But because I'm not going to waste 20 minutes of my time bagging on a game I don't like I'll just list what I find wrong with the game below:
1.  Though this has little to do with the game itself, most of the community is trash and you would be doing yourself a favor to not associate with them before it's too late and you get sucked into the trash can as well.
2. The game relies on a feauture called "Reset" to help it's lore make sense. However, the problem with resetting your save is that it means you have to play all parts of the game, all over again, every. single. time. Didn't want to deal with dialogue you spam through because you have already seen it? too bad. Didn't want to walk through an entire section again and do horribly made puzzles? too bad. Didn't want to walk around a single room for ten minutes looking for enemies with a continuously lowering spawn chance just to get the genocide ending? too. bad.
3. Though many of the characters may seem original, after further inspection you may realize they are less unique than you think. Papyrus is the socially awkward guy who always tried to be nice and helpful but continuously fails and has little to no real friends. Undyne is the super anime heroine who hates a specific set of people for reasons no one gives a damn about. Alphys is the stereotypical clumsy character who has some VERY dark secrets. And sans is the guy who seems nice and normal but is actually watching over the protaganist the whole time like a god and contains massive hidden power. Ring any bells?
4. Most of the game's humor (but luckily not all of it) relies on memes and references which in a few years I guarantee you nobody still playing this game will understand.
And you may find yourself with your own problems while playing the game. So don't succum to peer pressure, and simply don't buy the game before you waste your money.

I was late to playing this game, but fortunately nothing too big was spoiled for me. At first I thought it was just a meme game because of how overly silly it seemed, but it turns out this game doesn't over-do it, and the "meme status" of certain characters is only a result of how popular they have become. It's kind of a random kind of humor, without being "penguin of doom" levels of cringe. It's just perfect.
The game breaks all of your expectations. It will screw with your mind over and over again - just when you think you've figured it out, the game (gently) slaps you in the face and tells you "no". I can't go into too much detail about the story without spoiling it. What I will say is that the story and lore is extremely interesting, and some details are still shrouded by mystery, with loads of fan theories online about them. The game has different endings based on your choices during your playthrough. The characters will adapt and treat you differently depending on what kind of a person your character is.
The gameplay itself consists of rpg style battle screens, with the exception that you fight the enemies with a danmaku styled minigame (think Touhou) in a little box. The rules of the bullet hell minigame varies by enemy type, and even the enemy projectiles are unique to each type. For example, a crying enemy's bullets could be its tears falling into the bullet-hell box. It's not nearly as hard as full on bullet hell shooters though, so even people who aren't fan of that specific genre can easily complete the battles. There are also a couple of items you can get to make some of the fights easier, if you need to.
I really can't think of anything negative to say about this game. The soundtrack is amazing as is proven by the countless remixes you can find on Youtube and Soundcloud, the art of the enemies, the way the game keep surprising you, it's all amazing. To me it's incredible how Toby Fox could do this all by mostly just himself (he did have some other people designing the characters and making the art for them IIRC). Usually with one man projects it seems you get games where only one aspect of the game shines, and the others are lacking - but Undertale is a masterpiece on all fronts.
It's funny, it's cute, it's exciting, it's intriguing, AND it's affordable. If somehow you still haven't played it, you need to, ASAP.

Then came Undertale. Originally I was skeptical, thinking this would be another Fnaf but this oddly enough wasn't! The graphics were terrible and I loved it! Too many games nowadays try to make the gameplay realistic so to see some old 8-bit graphics that actually belonged in the game was a breath of fresh air.
Then came the storyline. The thing I love the most about Undertale is the lore, sure the music is awesome and gameplay is pretty cool but the lore made the entire experience magical for me. The fact that the different routes referenced one another and the fact that other endings even EXISTED immediately got me hyped to play this game. The game is challenging, fun and the entire experience is worth having.
Sure the comedy may be crappy but it's why it is funny! This world tries too hard to purposely be funny and with how everything plays out in Undertale, I wouldn't have it any other way.
My main complaint resides in the Genocide Route with Chara. While I love how Chara is introduced and you gradually learn the storyline of Chara and Asriel, I just wish that Toby Fox advanced their storyline and gave both Chara and the Protagonist specified genders but even though this is what I hate about Undertale, I also love it at the same time. I love how Fox had at least one or more characters under the air of mystery but I have to wonder if Chara and their storyline is a plothole or just a trail of mystery...

I recommend, and will continue to recommend, this game to everyone. As well as theorize and draw Undertale.

As the owner of 2 servers and the admin of 3 others, who has spent nearly 900 hours ingame (as of the posting of this review) I highly recommend Rust to my fellow players.  Below I've listed the best features of the game, as well as things which need to be worked on and improved by the devs.
Best things about Rust:
-Extremely active devs who release updates every week and interact with their fan base.  The game gets better every week as the devs release new content.
-Well balanced, brutal fight for survival against your fellow players.
-Bears are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s.
-2 great events in vanilla, the air drop and the heli, which encourage both cooperation and pvp.
-Amazing modding community with thousands of amazing servers for those who want a little extra out of their game.
-Beautiful landscapes.
-Well designed building system.  Improvements need to be made but in it's current state players can still spend hours designing new and improved bases.
-Dat Boltie
Things which need to be improved:
-Animals can walk through monument walls.
-Animals can run up sheer cliffs at amazing speeds.
-Lots of glitches which need to be patched.  This is to be expected in Alpha games and everything game-breaking has fixes, but we shouldn't need to be spending time fixing♥♥♥♥♥♥right after buying the game.
-Performance enhancements which don't completely nerf graphics would be nice.
-Devs should consider hiring a couple more people to help accelerate development.  Just a personal opinion.
-Quarries are currently useless.  Their output needs to be at least 5-10x current to be worth the fuel used.
-Body assignment is cool, but it would be nice if bodies randomly changed every couple of weeks of something.  Switch things up a bit.
-Bicycles, boats, hint hint.
-Can we please get more options for building.  Current system is great but could be improved.
-Prone position would be cool.
I'm going to stop, because there are tons of things the devs could add which would be nice, but would not majorly impact the quality of the game.  So far the game is amazing and I know we'll see lots of great things from the devs in the future.  As of this time I would rate rust 9.5/10.

Undertale is a charming, retro RPG game that takes players back to the early years of gaming when everything was black and white, pixelated, and unimpressive in terms of graphics. While the details of colour and style may not appeal to players initially, the fantastic plot, character depth and ideas explored in the game do alot more than just make up for it. I can guarantee you that you will become deeply attached to the characters in this game, and the concept of DETERMINATION becomes a very important aspect of the game's overall plot structure. As of yet I have not yet seen any bugs or unfair gameplay balance in the game.
Another thing that makes this game so outrageously awesome is the fact that just when you think you have completed the game, you get thrown a new route to play through, which provides more content to make you fall in love all over again. These routes are based upon how aggressive you are towards enemies in the game, which is another important concept in that Undertale is a game where you don't have to kill anyone. One of these routes, the Genocide Route, forces you to achieve the goal of killing everyone and everything, and destroy the monster world. I find it interesting how the game does their best to punish you with frustratingly difficult battles due to your failure to listen to the motto of the game.
All in all, there is tons of content to explore in this game. What is interesting is special things in the gameplay change when you do certain actions or replay through the whole game again. It is definitely worth the money if you want to explore this game to the greatest extent. However, if you are only interested in the main story and that's it, you may as well just find a youtube series and watch that.

Yes I recommend it. Confused? Let me explain. I played the heck out of BL2. I played BL1 to death before I even had a Steam account or even cared for FPS games. I love the art, characters, dialogue, banter, jokes...I mean I love it all. I did....until UVHM came along and ruined the game totally. Ultimate Vault Hunter Mode...at the time I quit playing, was the top difficulty setting to play on and to do this youd play through normal all the way through again and again until you hit the difficult playthrough UHVM.
Whats wrong with playing through a few hundred missions a few times? Nothing as long as the gameplay allows you to feel a sense of power. As you progress the weapons scale with you and enemy life bars scale a bit faster until the last playthrough where it takes more ammo than you have on your person to  take down a simple mob and bosses are reduced to a high pressure grind fest.
In BL1 you feel that sense of power. You feel strong when you attack a group of bad guys. You feel like the comic book, John Woo styled hero, just blazing away at the baddies. There was a sense of danger and a sense of heroism as you battled on through hordes of monsters and midgets. In BL2 when you get to the fabled UVHM, which is forced upon you as you purchase a DLC, you dont feel heroic. You feel like a victim. Pushed into a corner as you constantly die. Enemies resisting your attacks on an elemental AND physical level. The game forces a particular style of play. Slagging!
Allow me to introduce to you the element known as Slag. Its the element pretty much ignored for lack of importance on the first few playthroughs. Slag increases damage. Thats it. Its a mechanic that you use to basically manage damage on powerful enemies. It also wears off every few seconds so you have to re Slag an enemy every few seconds. Couple this with a horde of overpowered "bad asses" and you get a dysfunctional damage management game instead of a shooting party.
This is every encounter during the last mode of play. Enemy appears. You get tagged with a shot. Shields down. Slag shots. Enemy slagged. Switch to gun of choice. Blast a few rounds. Enemy becomes resiliant. Switch back. Hit "Special" and hope it regens health because most likely youre low on health at this point. Slag...bam bam bam...switch...Slag...bam bam dead. One baddie down. Rinse and repeat for another 12 thousand enemies of increasing difficulty to go.
Couple that with a few other issues like lack of gun variety, lacluster "cover", worthless skills as a point sink, and TONS of crap items flying out of every badguy you can hit. I still recommend this game for ONE thing. Dont get the all the DLC if you DO buy this game. Get this game and really play the heck out of the story the first time and on the second playthrough go through the DLC as released in order. Its worth every penny to one time it. After that however....I just got sick of it after a while. The fighting at higher levels is just a huge unbalanced slaughter.
Awesome game, recommended. It has the fun, and the fantasy.

If you really cannot wait to play a good survival game, then yeah buy DayZ. But as a fan promised something much more in 2+ years, this has been a massive disappointment.

DayZ has to be, truly, a disappointment for the ages.
Coming off the original mod for Arma 2, expectations for the standalone game were astronomical.  Naturally, it would be unreasonable and naive to assume that it could live up wholly to such expectation, but what no one expected was such a colossal failure and squandering of potential.
Two years after its release, not only is DayZ still in early access with no end in sight, but serious bugs that have lingered since day one are still yet to be fixed, there are massive stability issues at a foundational level, and, currently, there are quite literally no zombies in the game.  Like, none.  At all.  To call this situation a shambles would be an understatement.
I think the boat has long since sailed for DayZ, especially in the face of other games like Rust, ARK: Survival Evolved and 7 Days to Die. Its popularity peaked years ago, and with the standalone in a state of perpetual stagnation, helmed by an inexperienced set of developers, the lofty ambitions originally set for it are never likely to be realised.
The only unique thing DayZ still has going for it is the intensity of encounters with other players. No other game has managed to capture the feelings of panic and uncertainty you get when you come across another survivor, and that the next decision you make will mean you either live or you die.
It's a terrible waste, really.

Undertale is a charming, retro RPG game that takes players back to the early years of gaming when everything was black and white, pixelated, and unimpressive in terms of graphics. While the details of colour and style may not appeal to players initially, the fantastic plot, character depth and ideas explored in the game do alot more than just make up for it. I can guarantee you that you will become deeply attached to the characters in this game, and the concept of DETERMINATION becomes a very important aspect of the game's overall plot structure. As of yet I have not yet seen any bugs or unfair gameplay balance in the game.
Another thing that makes this game so outrageously awesome is the fact that just when you think you have completed the game, you get thrown a new route to play through, which provides more content to make you fall in love all over again. These routes are based upon how aggressive you are towards enemies in the game, which is another important concept in that Undertale is a game where you don't have to kill anyone. One of these routes, the Genocide Route, forces you to achieve the goal of killing everyone and everything, and destroy the monster world. I find it interesting how the game does their best to punish you with frustratingly difficult battles due to your failure to listen to the motto of the game.
All in all, there is tons of content to explore in this game. What is interesting is special things in the gameplay change when you do certain actions or replay through the whole game again. It is definitely worth the money if you want to explore this game to the greatest extent. However, if you are only interested in the main story and that's it, you may as well just find a youtube series and watch that.

As the owner of 2 servers and the admin of 3 others, who has spent nearly 900 hours ingame (as of the posting of this review) I highly recommend Rust to my fellow players.  Below I've listed the best features of the game, as well as things which need to be worked on and improved by the devs.
Best things about Rust:
-Extremely active devs who release updates every week and interact with their fan base.  The game gets better every week as the devs release new content.
-Well balanced, brutal fight for survival against your fellow players.
-Bears are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s.
-2 great events in vanilla, the air drop and the heli, which encourage both cooperation and pvp.
-Amazing modding community with thousands of amazing servers for those who want a little extra out of their game.
-Beautiful landscapes.
-Well designed building system.  Improvements need to be made but in it's current state players can still spend hours designing new and improved bases.
-Dat Boltie
Things which need to be improved:
-Animals can walk through monument walls.
-Animals can run up sheer cliffs at amazing speeds.
-Lots of glitches which need to be patched.  This is to be expected in Alpha games and everything game-breaking has fixes, but we shouldn't need to be spending time fixing♥♥♥♥♥♥right after buying the game.
-Performance enhancements which don't completely nerf graphics would be nice.
-Devs should consider hiring a couple more people to help accelerate development.  Just a personal opinion.
-Quarries are currently useless.  Their output needs to be at least 5-10x current to be worth the fuel used.
-Body assignment is cool, but it would be nice if bodies randomly changed every couple of weeks of something.  Switch things up a bit.
-Bicycles, boats, hint hint.
-Can we please get more options for building.  Current system is great but could be improved.
-Prone position would be cool.
I'm going to stop, because there are tons of things the devs could add which would be nice, but would not majorly impact the quality of the game.  So far the game is amazing and I know we'll see lots of great things from the devs in the future.  As of this time I would rate rust 9.5/10.
