(TL;DR at the very end)
It's like DayZ, stranded out in♥♥♥♥♥♥dick nowhere with basically no supplies and you have to stumble around looking for your friends. Difference is that DayZ was on a fixed map and not randomly generated. So in DayZ your friend group could just meet up at a major landmark, in this game you just jerk yourself and walk around hoping you find your friends.
------------------------------------------------
YOU HAVE NO CONTROL OVER YOUR CHARACTERS APPEARANCE
You cannot change the way your character looks in any way, when you start up a game you are assigned a random race gender and face which then gets tied to your steam id. Garry Newman (The Lead developer on this game for any who were unaware) said, "We don’t believe that letting you choose your race and gender would improve the game."
As someone who spends 40+ minutes in games like Saints Row, Bethesda games, or GTA online just in the character creation menu, a lack of character customization breaks a game for me. So being able to customize my character WOULD improve the game experience for me. It gives me an actual attachment to my in game character. Even a gimped customization tool would still be better than what this game gives you.
Another Newman Quote
"We get an even spread of races and genders that make players more identifiable – while at the same time making the social aspects of the game much more interesting."
I'd like to know how making people black makes social aspects of the game more interesting. No seriously, I want to know. I'm not joking, someone tell me how forcing people to be something improves the social aspects of the game.
TL;DR
No character customization (also can't "reroll" your random chracter, it's tied to your steam ID), you'll probably get thrown in as something you don't like. Or you'll get lucky like me and get atleast close to what you wanted.
----------------------------------------------------------
I'm done ranting about character customization.
I just feel like it's a lesser version of DayZ, sure there's building and hunting, but in the 2 hours I played, it just felt like scrambling around looking for my friends and trying to not starve to death. An experience I received during my time in DayZ. The game doesn't seem oriented around playing with your friends, Sure you're all tossed in the same general area, but the early game task of running around looking for your friends seems annoying after your third or fourth death.  Games like minecraft or don't starve together Show examples of a much more "Friend Group" oriented experience (all players are thrust down together and can instantly begin cooperating to survive)
I can't say anything about the combat system, I died too frequently trying to find my friends to get any real weapons.
It doesn't seem very well optimized. Newman wants you to have a GTX 980 to run this on the highest settings. He's also kind enough to not suggest a minimum card requirement. I have a GTX 640 and hovered around 40 or 50 fps on "Fast" settings. Most of my friends have higher quality cards, but for me this game wasn't as easy to run as some titles that offer a similar experience (DayZ mostly).
-------
There's better games out there for twenty bucks.
If you're looking for a game that's as "goofy" as naked people running around trying to survive, then try Garry's Mod you can pick it up for ten dollars (Also goes on sale for $2.50 or $5.00 very often)
If you're looking for a game about running around trying to survive try DayZ. It's a little more expensive than rust but it's a better game in my opinion (Don't misinterpret me, I dislike both games. DayZ is just the lesser of two evils)

Let me start by explaining, I love this game. I want to spend my time playing this game. For lack of a better explanation, this is the game I had always been waiting for...but I cannot reccomend it, even after the amount of time I have spent playing (and enjoying it). After years in development, I am finally willing to cross over to the darkside and join the naysayers. DayZ is a development nightmare, and will forever be a telltale warning to buying any early access game. There was time, when I reccomended this game to everyone I knew, heck I even bought it for 3 or 4 of my friends so they could enjoy it with me. That was then...when the games potential wasn't blurred by what it was slowly becoming (or, in this case, what it slowly isn't becoming)
The game still hasn't even come close to matching the features of the mod. It is built on an outdated, buggy, and poorly optimized engine. The devs have slowly added more functional and cosmetic content over time, but every update seems to  shift the game into more and more of an unplayable state. This game functioned better when it first came out, then after all of its consecutive updates that reduce frame rates, increase desync, and break many of the aspects that make it so fun.
In theory, this game is everything a gamer could ever want. Harsh, post apocalyptic survival in a rural, zombie infested foreign land. A place where the players make the rules and almost anything can happen. Imagine spending hours, fighting the odds, finding food, clothing, eventually weapons, and building up a survival strategy against all odds, and then, you see it, your first encounter with another player. Do you shoot them on sight? Do you try to talk to them? Will they help you? Maybe they will just shoot you and take your hard earned gear leaving you for dead, the decision is yours to make and the risks and rewards flow both ways. That being said, this game simply prevents players from experiencing the magic it does so well, with its myriad of bugs, desync, and poor optimizations, rendering it nearly unplayable.
I have finally uninstalled this game (likely permanently unless the development takes a serious turn for the better) and placed it into my "junk pile" game category. I fear this game has become an embodiment of "take the money and run" philosphy, and because of that, I cannot reccomend anyone purchase this game.

I'm writing this review not because I have anything against this game, it's good in it's own right, but because I want to save you guys from wasting your money. On sale, this game costs $30 U.S.D. However they still charge $35 USD and give either no or minimal discount during sales to encourage new players and many players who are tired of waiting for major progress or a finished product have moved on.
My final recommendation is to take your $30+ dollars and buy ArmA 3 when its on sale if you are looking for a survival zombie game. Borderlands 2 is a game worth hundreds of hours of gameplay, no matter if you play solo or co-op, with or without DLCs. The story and interface is WAY better than in the first game, characters are hilarious, dozens of easter eggs and memes hidden in texts and images left and right, insanely addicting ARPG gameplay and a lot of quests to complete (around 30~40 hours for almost everything, except for the hardest quest that really requires 3~4 co-op players and lvl40+).
The achievements aren't easy, but aren't hard either if you like exploring and enjoying every bit of detail in this gorgeous game. It's also a great game to meet new friends and have fun on public matches (even though there aren't many people playing nowadays, strangely). If you want to buy the GOTY version of the game (which I got lucky enough to pay 10 bucks for it on the Winter Sale), it's even funnier and more rewarding than the main campaign experience.
Overall, if you don't mind investing a little money on a quality and non-overhyped game, buy the GOTY version right away (normally 50% off) since it's the complete experience you will have in this game. If you just want to try it out to see with your own eyes how it works, the normal version often goes 75% off a lot on Steam... just need to keep an eye out for it in those times, it's worth every cent!

This game is not in any way shape or form even remotely for hardcore gamers or for people that are just not comfortable with relating to or expressing empathy or their emotions to a video game. It's an adventure that wants to invest you in it's tale rather than it's gameplay that flips typical RPG elements that everyone should be used to by now on it's head. The game is very sensitive to talk about so ill try to be as informative about what to expect if youre interested in it without divulging anything about the game.
You get to assume the role of either a hero that saves everyone, a neutral entity that only cares for themself, or a villain that eradicates everything--with each decision having a reward or consequence that not only affects you, but the world and its inhabitants. Adhering to any of these 3 tropes reveals a lot of depth to the world and it's characters you will decide the fate of.
It's sweet tender and humerous, and assuming you are the kind of person that reacts to that sort of thing, you will enjoy the sensitivity and humor it has to offer. There have been people that have told me ( :V ) that the fandom of the game ruined their interest in playing it to which i have yo say is no excuse to not enjoy something you like when you can ignore things you dont like about it. You're only spiting yourself and not anyone else but.
So i reccomend this game to the people that like a story and an adventure that tries not to be one dimensional and straight forward in how you play it, while trying to pluck emotions and laughter from you. I do not reccomend this game to people that simply feel they fit best in the COD, Gears, Final fantasys and all that hardcore fast paced♥♥♥♥♥♥that tries to invest you in their gameplay first and everything else second, and doesn't try to berate you into investing an attachment to it's characters when thats just not what they play games for.

This review was originally written for the Xbox 360 version of the game and may not entirely reflect the PC version. The full, unedited version of this review may be viewed
Pandora: a “border world” home to bandits, liars, murderers, psychopaths, entrepreneurs, vicious monsters of all sizes, but most importantly home to vault hunters. In Borderlands 2 we're given the role of one of four playable gun-toting mercenaries, assassins, mystical sirens, or steroid-junkies that all share one thing in common: their love for challenge. Each one has been brought to Pandora by different circumstances, but they were all drawn by the promise of an alien vault full to the brim of who-knows-what. The mystique, the danger, the hunt... it was enough for our heroes.
Sound familiar? I am talking about Borderlands 2, though you may have confused this synopsis with the original installment. Indeed there are many similarities at face value, but Borderlands 2 lives up to its name as a proper sequel, making the original Borderlands look nothing short of a beta test. The review will try to be as friendly as possible to both returning players and players who have never touched the series. The review is broken up into segments with concise summaries immediately following each.
Pros:
-Improved, rich user interface
-More customizing, more gun/etc. models
-Diverse locales to progress through
Cons:
-Hectic activity can significantly reduce frame rate momentarily
Pros:
-Subtle but masterful background music appropriately reflects the pace of action
-Explosions, bullets, and everything in between satisfyingly match the chaos you're sure to incite
-Voice work is solid and expansive, and is how the majority of the plot is conveyed
Cons:
-Dialogue may often be cut out by another NPC, causing you to miss anything from a joke to a plot point
-Dialogue, even crucially important dialogue, for the most part, cannot be reheard
Pros:
-Much improved emphasis on plot gives players meaning
-Surprises keep the player guessing until the very end
-Wider cast of voiced non-playable characters contribute to the plot
-Humour tries to keep the tone of the game lighthearted*
Cons:
-Lack of backstory may leave new players in the dust for a few hours
-Some story is only learned
by collecting
items

*Pro or con depending on if you find the humour actually funny, or just distracting. There are a lot of conflicting opinions about this, and you're just going to have to decide for yourself.
Pros:
-All equipment is randomly generated based on level, resulting in higher possibilities
-Larger variety of equipment than predecessor
-Four playable characters can excel with all weapon types while still remaining entirely unique from each other
-Larger variety of enemies than predecessor
-Side missions mix up their objectives to keep it fresh
-Bank and cross-character storage
-Drop-in/drop-out coop made even easier
-Take couch coop online
Cons:
-Returning players
get bored with the essentially unchanged core formula
-Returning players may be disheartened by the smaller inventory size
Pros:
-Multiple character playthroughs and reaching maximum level can net you hundreds of hours
-Multiple DLC expansions
Cons:
-One play will net around 20 hours
In conclusion, players must remember that Borderlands 2 does not try to be a shooter, or an RPG. It is a hybrid genre that embraces both equally, providing both wild over-the-top action and RPG elements such as leveled gear, skill trees, and character classes. The game can be fully enjoyed alone, with a friend using couch co-op, or online with up to four other players in cooperative play publicly or with friends. The concept of randomly generated equipment can be so hit-or-miss with some players that if you're even feeling a little unsure about it you may want to borrow the game or rent it for a quick personal experience. BL1? It makes me happy. BL2? HOLY [Five lines of explicit praise omitted.] MAN THIS GAME IS GOOD. Everything I like and love from the first is enhanced to the max, mixed together, and blown out of proportion for maximum [woot]. See, I still love the loot system from BL1, but you could go through half a playthrough with the same set of weapons and fare fairly well. The emphasis on switching up new weapons wasn't that big, since the way damage per level increased in a linear fashion. A pearl "Bessie" (look it up) I got from Craw did something upwards of 1000 damage. A level 35 blue rarity sniper in BL2 I have does 4200 damage. With damage changing this much in-between levels in the game (non-linear, oh yeah, MATH IS ACTUALLY USEFUL), you HAVE to switch weapons up or you get mauled later in game. However, this is a good thing since it helps keep gameplay fresh to the player. Heh, like this game isn't fresh enough. Graphics were updated from the first by a ton, and I'm not one to care about graphics, but DAAYYUUUMM this game is pretty. Replacing the trash heaps and desert from the first, tundra, highland, blight, and... desert make a stunning backdrop to the carnage you will wrought (yeah, ENGLISH TOO) upon the poor AI of Pandora. Classes and their skill trees have their similarities to their forebears, but everything has a sleeker feel, like it's more "sci-fiey." (it's a word now) Skill trees also have much more skills available giving more freedom on how to decimate/obliterate/annihilate all in the way. Only problem is the well-known "ButIwannausethemall" syndrome, where subjects' brains implode due to the conflict on which skills to pick. Well, I really should be wrapping up now, so, on to...
THE STORY
HOLY BALLS. THE STORY. it's good.
Unlike BL1 (btw, this game is a sequel, so you should already expect this "Unlike BL1" thing I keep throwing around by now) this game has a story that 1) is good, 2) <---. 3) MOVING ON.
Unlike BL1 (heh) this game doesn't feel lonely after a while. In fact, sometimes you'll be all "AAHHH, SO MUCH DIALOUGES!" Characters are colorful, funny, and in your face with what they have to say. Writing's good, voice-acting is awesome (when did Mordecai become Truxican?), and Gearbox still has a badass sense of humor, all leading to more WIN-per-dollar. Or euro. Whatever.
HEY. Just cause I said this game doesn't get lonely like BL1 could doesn't mean it's better blasting away enemies alone. Friends are for blasting away baddies away with. Everybody knows that. (I find best friend is the best ammo for snipers.) Matchmaking is streamlined, meaning you don't have to create a Gameshark account like you did for BL1 (didn't like Gameshark all that much) and connection seems more reliable too. The wonder of technology. Yay.
DLC: Well, I didn't like the first three as much as I liked BL1s DLCs, but they're still worth the cash (maybe not Torgue...funny, but....) Haven't had the chance to play Tina's DLC yet, but I hear it's to die for. (Don't take that literally.) Oh yeah, not to forget the extra characters, but they're both worth it IMO. They both seem to be geared for expert players, looking at some of their mechanics, but anybody can still have fun with them, n00b or n0t.
Wow... I can talk way too much, can't I?
Negatives: Really? OK.
Honestly, the story isn't really good, so if you're expecting a brain♥♥♥♥, sorry. This game is irreverent fun and it knows it. But the story beats "Find Vault. Get sweet Lewts." by a long shot. It isn't the plot points that really drew me in, it was the characters. H. Jack is no Vaas, he's your stereotypical asshat that you love to hate. I'd give him a raise cause he did a good job, but his♥♥♥♥♥is grass now.
Countering alla the people who say the game is repetitive. It's a shooter. Your only way to deal with a problem is the careful/Zer0 or haphazard/Salvadore placement of bullets in the bad guys. So if you find shooters boring, fun (not really) fact. You. Will. Find. Borderlands 2. Boring. (Seriously)
And finally, that thing I mentioned about how you have to change weapons up because of damage increases? Yeah, that affects the damage you take too. Expect the game to get hard (stupid hard) on later playthroughs. Blame Gearbox all you want, they're not going to change it. I blame Gearbox. However, I doesn't "ruin" the game. People like to ♥♥♥♥♥ cause they can and it's the Internet. I do too.
tl;dr- Buy the game. It's good. Correction: It's Good. Direct upgrade in every way from BL1. DLC are good, I don't think 1-3 are all that much compared to BL1s DLCs (especially Torgues, sorry), but I hear Tiny Tina's is awesome. If you want a summary of my feelings toward this game as a sequel, check out Egoraptor's "Sequelitis" for Megaman X on YouTube.

A friend of mine gave this game to me along with him and 2 other people, and I've had it for a few years now. I've seen this game go in different directions and some were a lot worse than others. But as much as I enjoy playing this game, I simply cannot reccomend it in it's current state, and heres why:
Now don't get me wrong, I understand Facepunch Studios isn't a big company, but it doesn't seem like the game has gotten much better since i've bought it 3 years ago. While Facepunch continues to add more content/features into the game, they put less work into fixing bugs, and other big issues. Now I have a 1070 so things like performance don't affect me too much. But a lot of my friends can't even go into a server without their game crashing. Some can't even open the game up because of EAC. Not to mention the hundreds of bugs with things like the weapons, playermodels, hitboxes, animal AI, and graphics.
The devs currently update the game every week on Thursdays, but not a lot can get done in one week. Also, if you read the dev blogs on their website, they mostly talk about things they will be adding. This in itself isn't a bad thing, but I'd rather play an EA game that focuses on fixing their game instead of adding in new content. Facepunch needs to understand that before you add something new, you need to fix what you already have. Because the more stuff you add, the more stuff you have to fix.
Just so we're clear, I have no problem with grinding out a game. But this game doesn't feel like it's worth the grind. I could spend an entire day building myself up, have a small house, and then i could leave to go eat dinner and come back finding out I died. Then I have to repeat the process all over again. The whole process is way too time consuming and I can't afford to invest a lot of my time into it.
A lot of this has to do with the game mechanics. It takes too long to build yourself up and those who have the time to do it are the only ones who will be able to keep it up. It takes so long in fact that I'm willing to bet that at least 75% of my hours on this game are me crafting and building alone. A game shouldn't have this much of a grind, especially if people have full time jobs or go to college/univeristy.
Now despite all that I've said in this review, I'm still playing the game to this day. I'm doing my best to keep up-to-date with the games state, and what the devs are curently working on. Rust is one of the first Early Access games that i have had hope for, and i hope some day it will get better. Hopefully in the future i will give this game a better review. But for right now, it's not worth it.

Borderlands 2 is a game worth hundreds of hours of gameplay, no matter if you play solo or co-op, with or without DLCs. The story and interface is WAY better than in the first game, characters are hilarious, dozens of easter eggs and memes hidden in texts and images left and right, insanely addicting ARPG gameplay and a lot of quests to complete (around 30~40 hours for almost everything, except for the hardest quest that really requires 3~4 co-op players and lvl40+).
The achievements aren't easy, but aren't hard either if you like exploring and enjoying every bit of detail in this gorgeous game. It's also a great game to meet new friends and have fun on public matches (even though there aren't many people playing nowadays, strangely). If you want to buy the GOTY version of the game (which I got lucky enough to pay 10 bucks for it on the Winter Sale), it's even funnier and more rewarding than the main campaign experience.
Overall, if you don't mind investing a little money on a quality and non-overhyped game, buy the GOTY version right away (normally 50% off) since it's the complete experience you will have in this game. If you just want to try it out to see with your own eyes how it works, the normal version often goes 75% off a lot on Steam... just need to keep an eye out for it in those times, it's worth every cent!

This review was originally written for the Xbox 360 version of the game and may not entirely reflect the PC version. The full, unedited version of this review may be viewed
Pandora: a “border world” home to bandits, liars, murderers, psychopaths, entrepreneurs, vicious monsters of all sizes, but most importantly home to vault hunters. In Borderlands 2 we're given the role of one of four playable gun-toting mercenaries, assassins, mystical sirens, or steroid-junkies that all share one thing in common: their love for challenge. Each one has been brought to Pandora by different circumstances, but they were all drawn by the promise of an alien vault full to the brim of who-knows-what. The mystique, the danger, the hunt... it was enough for our heroes.
Sound familiar? I am talking about Borderlands 2, though you may have confused this synopsis with the original installment. Indeed there are many similarities at face value, but Borderlands 2 lives up to its name as a proper sequel, making the original Borderlands look nothing short of a beta test. The review will try to be as friendly as possible to both returning players and players who have never touched the series. The review is broken up into segments with concise summaries immediately following each.
Pros:
-Improved, rich user interface
-More customizing, more gun/etc. models
-Diverse locales to progress through
Cons:
-Hectic activity can significantly reduce frame rate momentarily
Pros:
-Subtle but masterful background music appropriately reflects the pace of action
-Explosions, bullets, and everything in between satisfyingly match the chaos you're sure to incite
-Voice work is solid and expansive, and is how the majority of the plot is conveyed
Cons:
-Dialogue may often be cut out by another NPC, causing you to miss anything from a joke to a plot point
-Dialogue, even crucially important dialogue, for the most part, cannot be reheard
Pros:
-Much improved emphasis on plot gives players meaning
-Surprises keep the player guessing until the very end
-Wider cast of voiced non-playable characters contribute to the plot
-Humour tries to keep the tone of the game lighthearted*
Cons:
-Lack of backstory may leave new players in the dust for a few hours
-Some story is only learned
by collecting
items

*Pro or con depending on if you find the humour actually funny, or just distracting. There are a lot of conflicting opinions about this, and you're just going to have to decide for yourself.
Pros:
-All equipment is randomly generated based on level, resulting in higher possibilities
-Larger variety of equipment than predecessor
-Four playable characters can excel with all weapon types while still remaining entirely unique from each other
-Larger variety of enemies than predecessor
-Side missions mix up their objectives to keep it fresh
-Bank and cross-character storage
-Drop-in/drop-out coop made even easier
-Take couch coop online
Cons:
-Returning players
get bored with the essentially unchanged core formula
-Returning players may be disheartened by the smaller inventory size
Pros:
-Multiple character playthroughs and reaching maximum level can net you hundreds of hours
-Multiple DLC expansions
Cons:
-One play will net around 20 hours
In conclusion, players must remember that Borderlands 2 does not try to be a shooter, or an RPG. It is a hybrid genre that embraces both equally, providing both wild over-the-top action and RPG elements such as leveled gear, skill trees, and character classes. The game can be fully enjoyed alone, with a friend using couch co-op, or online with up to four other players in cooperative play publicly or with friends. The concept of randomly generated equipment can be so hit-or-miss with some players that if you're even feeling a little unsure about it you may want to borrow the game or rent it for a quick personal experience. This is one of the few early access games that will see daylight. Ever since it hit early access, it has continuously been worked on by the beautiful dev's of Facepunch Studios.
This game started as a zombie survival game with radiation. Now, zombies are out of the game and won't make a return, radiation is only a mechanic in BR, and they have recently added a xp system. The game has improved and will continue to do so.
This game is a survival game where you face off animals and other players. It has a building system where you can create strong bases to hold your equipment and for a place of safety, it has base raiding, a recently introduced xp system, and it is the best survival game on steam as of now.
The xp system was added a few days ago and has its problems. However, it is being worked on and they are continuing to add things to the game and balance things. Graphically, this game is amazing but it is also taxing to run on even high-end hardware. As a solo player, this game can be quite infuriating at times since people will make large clans, but in time you can gather xp and craft weapons and armor to get payback on the folks who kept killing you. This game has a big sense of progression. You start off with a rock, and as you level up, you end up with full sets of armor and a highly varied range of weapons. This game will give you some of the best gaming and social experiences you will ever have.
TL;DR: It's highly worth it. You will get a lot of hours out of this game and the dev's consistently add new content to this game and listen to their fans. Please, give it a shot. Convince your friends to get the game and play it together. It will be worth it.

A friend of mine gave this game to me along with him and 2 other people, and I've had it for a few years now. I've seen this game go in different directions and some were a lot worse than others. But as much as I enjoy playing this game, I simply cannot reccomend it in it's current state, and heres why:
Now don't get me wrong, I understand Facepunch Studios isn't a big company, but it doesn't seem like the game has gotten much better since i've bought it 3 years ago. While Facepunch continues to add more content/features into the game, they put less work into fixing bugs, and other big issues. Now I have a 1070 so things like performance don't affect me too much. But a lot of my friends can't even go into a server without their game crashing. Some can't even open the game up because of EAC. Not to mention the hundreds of bugs with things like the weapons, playermodels, hitboxes, animal AI, and graphics.
The devs currently update the game every week on Thursdays, but not a lot can get done in one week. Also, if you read the dev blogs on their website, they mostly talk about things they will be adding. This in itself isn't a bad thing, but I'd rather play an EA game that focuses on fixing their game instead of adding in new content. Facepunch needs to understand that before you add something new, you need to fix what you already have. Because the more stuff you add, the more stuff you have to fix.
Just so we're clear, I have no problem with grinding out a game. But this game doesn't feel like it's worth the grind. I could spend an entire day building myself up, have a small house, and then i could leave to go eat dinner and come back finding out I died. Then I have to repeat the process all over again. The whole process is way too time consuming and I can't afford to invest a lot of my time into it.
A lot of this has to do with the game mechanics. It takes too long to build yourself up and those who have the time to do it are the only ones who will be able to keep it up. It takes so long in fact that I'm willing to bet that at least 75% of my hours on this game are me crafting and building alone. A game shouldn't have this much of a grind, especially if people have full time jobs or go to college/univeristy.
Now despite all that I've said in this review, I'm still playing the game to this day. I'm doing my best to keep up-to-date with the games state, and what the devs are curently working on. Rust is one of the first Early Access games that i have had hope for, and i hope some day it will get better. Hopefully in the future i will give this game a better review. But for right now, it's not worth it.

This is one of the few early access games that will see daylight. Ever since it hit early access, it has continuously been worked on by the beautiful dev's of Facepunch Studios.
This game started as a zombie survival game with radiation. Now, zombies are out of the game and won't make a return, radiation is only a mechanic in BR, and they have recently added a xp system. The game has improved and will continue to do so.
This game is a survival game where you face off animals and other players. It has a building system where you can create strong bases to hold your equipment and for a place of safety, it has base raiding, a recently introduced xp system, and it is the best survival game on steam as of now.
The xp system was added a few days ago and has its problems. However, it is being worked on and they are continuing to add things to the game and balance things. Graphically, this game is amazing but it is also taxing to run on even high-end hardware. As a solo player, this game can be quite infuriating at times since people will make large clans, but in time you can gather xp and craft weapons and armor to get payback on the folks who kept killing you. This game has a big sense of progression. You start off with a rock, and as you level up, you end up with full sets of armor and a highly varied range of weapons. This game will give you some of the best gaming and social experiences you will ever have.
TL;DR: It's highly worth it. You will get a lot of hours out of this game and the dev's consistently add new content to this game and listen to their fans. Please, give it a shot. Convince your friends to get the game and play it together. It will be worth it.

This game is destined, if not already, to go down as one of the greatest FPS games of all time. The story is amazing and Handsome Jack is quite possibly one of the greatest antagonists to surface in recent years. Memorable characters and lush Pandoran environments abound. Plenty of challenges to be found with the ever increasing new game+ modes of True and the downloadable Ultimate Vault Hunter modes. Like the first BL before it, there are plenty of DLC goodies to be had, including the award winning "Tiny Tina's Assault on Dragon Fortress" DLC. The game is well over a year old but continues to pump out some great content in new DLC's. I realize, however, that you might very well end up paying as much for the DLC's as you do for the core game itself, which is a somewhat annoyingly common factor in games these days. BL2 could also greatly benefit from a multiplayer PvP mode and a character creation mode as well to keep the ever aging game relevant before the inevitable release of BL3 someday. Still, BL2 is a powerhouse of a RPS that continues to go strong and would make a great addition to anyones library of games.

I'm torn because I enjoy playing Rust, or at least I used to, and at nearly 1300 hours, I've already got my moneys worth out of the game.  That being said, the game seems to promote and reward no-lifers and massive clans, with very little room for anyone below  that.  The community is dowright toxic, it's nothing but racial slurs, homophobic slurs,♥♥♥♥♥♥jokes and little kids planting 30 bags around your base and just running up and crying at you because they're bad at the game.  Then there are the hackers, and they are everywhere.  They do ban waves around when they plan to have the game on sale to encourage people to buy new accounts and feed Gary's ego.
The game was already bad about punishing people who can't play the game all day every day.  With the recent implementation of the experience system they further punish anyone with a life outside of Rust because you can't even get lucky with random blueprint drops, you have to grind for days at a time to get anything.  Things that used to be known by default, like pants (lvl 13), Longsleeve shirts and Hoodies (lvl 16) can literally take days to obtain, I unlocked the latter after four days of playing every day from the time I got off work until the time I went to bed.  If I had been on a server that actively banned hackers when they were obvious about it, then I may have done so a little quicker, but it's hard to do anything with the rampant abuse of ESP hacks and people toggling aimbot when they start to lose.  (A side note:  I'm not claiming everyone  hacks, or that every time I die it was to a hacker, but they are very rampant in this game.)
In the current state of the game, if you're not part of a big clan, you're likely to get stomped on.   If you happen to kill them when you're online, they will just wait until you are offline, blow into everything you have and kill you while you sleep, then put signs on your walls with whatever slurs they're tiny little brains can spell.  The only defense is to build massive, confusing bases and hope that they run out of explosives before you run out of walls/doors.  You may also build a bunch of small bases, and then it's just a roll of the dice as to whether any of them survive.
If you want to spend all of your free time grinding and playing with large groups, I recommend you go find a traditional MMO.  At least there, your progress will feel somewhat rewarding.  If you want to just kill people consantly and♥♥♥♥♥♥talk people, go play an FPS that isn't glithcy and everychanging in Alpha.   Rust is trying to be a bit of everything, but it's failing because it's not focused on making any of those things any good.  Base building is fun, but ultimately pointless.  PvP is intense, but you're just as likely to die from a glitch or hacker as you are a skill player or a bear spawning on top of you.  The leveling system is just a grindy joke, I wanted to love it, but it was done in such a♥♥♥♥♥♥poor manner that it's not even slightly enjoyable.  Rust is a game for people who want to harass and grief other players, because if you lose in Rust, you lose potentially days worth of work.

Rust is one of the best survival games ive ever played. You can go lone wolf, small group or make a large clan, all choices having there pros and cons. There is a bit of a learning curve to begin with and you dont really get good with all the weapons until youve got alot of experience with them as you must compensate for bullet drop, bullet speed and moving targets. Bases must be built strategicly as exploits will generally always be found by experienced raiders. Procedurally generated worlds means no map is ever the same and thats a great thing. The graphics are beautiful and the UI is simple.
Now as for the community...
If youve read other peoples reviews you will see most people call it toxic but to be honest toxic is an inaccurate word that people just use and stereotype with. As this is a SURVIVAL game the harsh reality is its a dog eat dog world in this game. One of the best ways to advance is to feed off the weak and to avoid the strong(until your strong). What it comes down to at the end of the day is trust. Most people dont know eachother and do not trust eachother therefore you do not take risks by been friendly to anyone, even people who do not appear to be a threat (such as nakids). As you can die at any moment and lose all your stuff, trust is something that simply doesnt really exist in this game unless your playing with people you have real relationships with and to be honest thats how it would be in a post apocolyptic world which is what this game is meant to be.
This game does get you invested in terms of time and emotion. Nothing sucks more then getting rolled after a big farm or logging in to find your base raided and hours of work gone but that IS part of the game and you get over it the more it happens and you also get smarter about building and with the tactics you use while out in the world such as farming and avoiding conflict and not engaging groups bigger and more kitted then you.
Now as for the XP system which was just released...
There were many claims that this XP system was going to be a real game changer but in terms of the community it has really changed nothing at all. The only real changes is it delays the ability to raid for EVERYONE not just big clans. You are safe for the first day of the wipe but anything after that and its game on. It is significantly hard to progress as solo players and it CAN give big clans an edge if they are coordinated enough, both of which i do not agree with. The XP system does very little to create a less hostile community regardless of the few tools you might get from people. There is still 0 incentive not to kill and loot people.
I predict you will only see more and more large clans as this game continues as thats the only way you can really survive long term. Safety in numbers. You will see more "alliances" between big groups and you will just find graveyards of solo/small group bases around the maps as eventually most clans get physically too big to raid eachother so they just roam in zerg squads killing and raiding the smallest and weakest of the groups.
Dont get me wrong there is fun in every aspect of this game but it can be as harsh and brutal as it is fun. I persoanlly would like it if the devs created more incentive to create a less hostile community and incorporated some RPG aspects but i doubt it going to happen. I would also recommend keeping blueprints(not frags) in the game, just make them rare to find.
This game reveals true human nature in a post apocolyptic dog eat dog world. The brutality, harshness and sadism is plentiful and kindness, compassion and trust is rare. You will find every personality type in this game ranging from the typical unforgiving rude ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s to the rabid packs of 12v's to the mature friendly groups of gamers.
If you have a real life outside of this game and like what i have talked about then this game is definatly for you. However if your a kid and have no life outside of this game, it has the potential to turn you into a truely sad and dispicable person.

The devs currently update the game every week on Thursdays, but not a lot can get done in one week. Also, if you read the dev blogs on their website, they mostly talk about things they will be adding. This in itself isn't a bad thing, but I'd rather play an EA game that focuses on fixing their game instead of adding in new content. Facepunch needs to understand that before you add something new, you need to fix what you already have. Because the more stuff you add, the more stuff you have to fix.
Just so we're clear, I have no problem with grinding out a game. But this game doesn't feel like it's worth the grind. I could spend an entire day building myself up, have a small house, and then i could leave to go eat dinner and come back finding out I died. Then I have to repeat the process all over again. The whole process is way too time consuming and I can't afford to invest a lot of my time into it.
A lot of this has to do with the game mechanics. It takes too long to build yourself up and those who have the time to do it are the only ones who will be able to keep it up. It takes so long in fact that I'm willing to bet that at least 75% of my hours on this game are me crafting and building alone. A game shouldn't have this much of a grind, especially if people have full time jobs or go to college/univeristy.
Now despite all that I've said in this review, I'm still playing the game to this day. I'm doing my best to keep up-to-date with the games state, and what the devs are curently working on. Rust is one of the first Early Access games that i have had hope for, and i hope some day it will get better. Hopefully in the future i will give this game a better review. But for right now, it's not worth it.

Skip to the last paragraph for the reason why I've upped this game.
This game is hardcore, which means you can lose everything at a moments notice. The XP system allows you to retain at least knowledge on how to build in game items, but the resources you lose are often accrued over hours of grinding. Point made simple: every minute you spend on this game transitions into minutes wasted as soon as some player breaks into your base.
Don't buy this game unless you're ready to work for resources and progress that will inevitably be stolen, or lost when the server wipes. The vast majority of the game is grinding for resources, which benefits people who work in teams. This disadvantages the solo player, or a player who has no real world friends in game -- teams of real world friends can grind faster than a single man can, and can, consequently, massively stack their characters over single players.
Offline raiding is possible in the game, which especially upsets some players. The ability for nocturnal or different timezoned players to break into your base whilst your player sleeps on the ground disables you to defend you base. The whole cycle is as thus: work for hours building a base, log off and go to sleep, log back in and wake up to the death screen, then respawn with nothing -- not even a base to return to.
There's a certain beauty in working knowing your work will be lost. It's a beauty that teaches you to accept loss, and almost expect loss. I don't like this game because of its hardcore nature. Not because it's not playable, or because there are too many bugs. It's a fairly well polished, graphically acceptable, playable game. I don't like this game because someone can spend hours working for progress, and lose all that progress to some random player. It's not something one can protect against -- you will always lose everything. That's why it's called a hardcore game, and that's why I don't like the game. It could totally be for you if you like the game and ideas I just described.

Ok, so since this game is that sorta game where it ccan be enjoyed much more the less you know, ima tell you a few things first. I recommend you get this game. Some people may not enjoy it. It's really up to your tastes. Many find it boring, or the fanbase ruins ir for them. But lemme give my full review;
[NO SPOILERS]
This game is an (admittably short) RPG, that is very story heavy, and also tries to make especially good characters. The basic innovative thing is that NOBODY needs to die. It's really flipping off the well known rule that in an RPG, in a random encounter you hit the enemy with a baseball bat, they deal some damage to you, and you contimue beating the crap out of them, etc.. But in Undertale, you learn that... your actions have consequences. Every random encounter is meant to feel like a puzzle so you don't have to kill anyone, because unless you wuss out and try to flee and get no reward, you'll want to figure out how to get an enemy to spare you, by doing certain things. This game's story, also... it's excellent. The characters stand out and have a memorable and realistic personality, with tone shifting from funny, to emotional, to horrorful... but it also matters how you play the game. Remember. It may not seem like it; but everything you do, it has an effect on the story. Who you kill. Who you spare. Who you befriend. The battle system also is bullet hell type; which is new in RPG's because instead of relying on luck and levels to how much damage you get a turn, you must more rely on skill, and memory. Also the game makes you feel bad if you kill everybody. The game must be replkayed at least twice to get a good time; three if you have no soul... Because even after a playthrough, the things you did in a previous playthrough can have an effect on the other.
I warn you. Do not play this game if
*You cannot handle the fourth wall being broken, like, obsessively
*You cannot handle puns
*You cannot handle desicions
*You are a perfectionist, and relatable characters make you feel bad...

Ah... This game, benn hesitating to write a true review for Rust, because of how unstable the community can be compared to how fluent and amazing the gameplay can be... So here it is.
Rust, where the description of the game that the devs wrote up only explains what the game could be and what it severely lacks of. Rust has always been the go to game for stable PvP fights, because DayZ has that "I hope I don't lag out while shooting this guy from 400 meters away" feel, many people left the game to transfer to Rust, but since the game developers have been reiterating the gathering and crafting system into a blueprint system, then a component system, it makes it difficult for a solo player, which yes I get that numbers make the experience easier therefore better, but nothing can stop offline raids, which is the nail in the coffin whenever my friends and I play rust in the big servers, no clans want to raid you when you have defenses, which really hits us all hard, unfortunately with the way the community's mentality formed around "kill or be killed" and "scumbag mentality wins over playing the game the way it is intended to be played" no one will ever think to raid you online, our clan is of 5 people, all who get on relatively same time, so we can enjoy roaming meeting people, and shooting those guys who shoot at us. But we never get farther than the first three days before we get offlined. Now this is not to bash on the devs. They are great at updating this game, and their future plans for Rust makes it such a promising game, more so than any other game I can think of. But it's where the community forms, from its public mentality that makes this game unplayable. If people like cruel and punishing gameplay then yes I strongly recommend this game to anyone, to me however, I like having a defense against offline raids, tameable creatures, or more ai controlled defenses, like electric fences or robotic mechanisms! This is where I would like to see this game at, until then I will stick to a server where the community would rather be that bit more friendlier and not shoot that guy who only has a Tshirt on, or would og as far as to greeting you without guns to your face, or at least not offline raid me the moment I go to bed. :D

This game is destined, if not already, to go down as one of the greatest FPS games of all time. The story is amazing and Handsome Jack is quite possibly one of the greatest antagonists to surface in recent years. The gameplay of BL2 is lightyears ahead of the original BL which, itself, was a revolutionary game in the FPS genre, having been one of the frontrunners of the now established RPS (role-playing shooter) genre alongside Mass Effect. Memorable characters and lush Pandoran environments abound. Plenty of challenges to be found with the ever increasing new game+ modes of True and the downloadable Ultimate Vault Hunter modes. Like the first BL before it, there are plenty of DLC goodies to be had, including the award winning "Tiny Tina's Assault on Dragon Fortress" DLC. The game is well over a year old but continues to pump out some great content in new DLC's. I realize, however, that you might very well end up paying as much for the DLC's as you do for the core game itself, which is a somewhat annoyingly common factor in games these days. BL2 could also greatly benefit from a multiplayer PvP mode and a character creation mode as well to keep the ever aging game relevant before the inevitable release of BL3 someday. Still, BL2 is a powerhouse of a RPS that continues to go strong and would make a great addition to anyones library of games.

To the untrained eye, Undertale may come across as just a typical RPG not worth your time. However, I assure you this isn't some random game. Undertale gives you the option to spare your enemies and not just kill them in the regular RPG sense. This allows manueverability in the type of game style desired. Three types to be precise. There's neutral route, pacifist route, and genocide route. All of these routes are fairly self-explanatory, however neutral is a mix between killing and sparing, and pacifist is doing everything in your power not to kill anyone while genocide is the complete opposite. The story is very deep, almost like a novel. This deep story allows for emotion and compassion towards characters, and the soundtrack definitely helps to further this tie. I highly recommend this game because of the unique RPG style, amazing soundtrack, and sense of depth given by story. Subjectively, Undertale is one of the greatest games you will ever play.

Skip to the last paragraph for the reason why I've upped this game.
This game is hardcore, which means you can lose everything at a moments notice. The XP system allows you to retain at least knowledge on how to build in game items, but the resources you lose are often accrued over hours of grinding. Point made simple: every minute you spend on this game transitions into minutes wasted as soon as some player breaks into your base.
Don't buy this game unless you're ready to work for resources and progress that will inevitably be stolen, or lost when the server wipes. The vast majority of the game is grinding for resources, which benefits people who work in teams. This disadvantages the solo player, or a player who has no real world friends in game -- teams of real world friends can grind faster than a single man can, and can, consequently, massively stack their characters over single players.
Offline raiding is possible in the game, which especially upsets some players. The ability for nocturnal or different timezoned players to break into your base whilst your player sleeps on the ground disables you to defend you base. The whole cycle is as thus: work for hours building a base, log off and go to sleep, log back in and wake up to the death screen, then respawn with nothing -- not even a base to return to.
There's a certain beauty in working knowing your work will be lost. It's a beauty that teaches you to accept loss, and almost expect loss. I don't like this game because of its hardcore nature. Not because it's not playable, or because there are too many bugs. It's a fairly well polished, graphically acceptable, playable game. I don't like this game because someone can spend hours working for progress, and lose all that progress to some random player. It's not something one can protect against -- you will always lose everything. That's why it's called a hardcore game, and that's why I don't like the game. It could totally be for you if you like the game and ideas I just described.

So.. Undertale.
The basic synopsis of this game without giving anything away is that you fall down a hole to where monsteres reside, and you have to escape.
But the game is so much more than that.
Undertale is an emotional joyride where you decide your fate, the fate of others and the world around you. At first, the game seems like a fun, silly new form of RPG which has nice characters, a fun story and gives you the choice with what to do with that, which is a great game alone, but then it becomes even better as you make your way to endgame. If you're looking for an emotional story over something more often seen in new releases, this game is definitely for you.
As said before, your choices effect the story. A lot. And before you go and relate this to something else such as "Life is Strange", which sure, allows your choice on what you do to affect small narratives, however none (other than one I can think of the top of my head) makes a significant difference. Looking back at Undertale, I can't think of one choice that wasn't funny to make, didn't affected the story line in a far more drastic way than you'd think or wasn't there for no reason at all.
The combat system is fairly unique, too. People may refer to this as an RPG, though the combat system seems minor compared to everyone else. Even if it isn't that important compared to the story or the choices you make, it can be fun or even challenging at times. In battle, you can do either 3 things, be merciful and spare or flee from them, maybe having to act a certain way for sparing to be possible, or fighting them. The choices you make in these battles are perhaps the most important when getting to the different types or endings, (and I say types as there are multiple endings in these different 'types' of endings), as 2 of them require only one type of way to get out of a battle.
The soundtrack for this game is, if I may say so myself, near perfect. Nearly every song spare one or two in my opinion is still catchy to listen to, even outside of the game, and if it isn't it fits beautifully with where it's set. The music alone gives a lot of emotions throughout the game - not much soundtracks which I've heard can create ambience, happiness, fear, laughter and determination as well as Undertale did.
Some people may be put of by the graphics, but honestly, they don't really matter. Looking at the starting pictures, it doesn't look that great as a game but it makes use of what graphics it uses, dare I say, as well as the likes of Earthbound or Mother 3. Undertale is a game which, if it had better graphics or more detail, it could even be worse as a game - though if you still doubt me I recommend playing the demo (located at
.
Honestly, theres a reason this game has so little unrecommendations compared to its positive reviews. Although I've been overwhelmingly positive on how much I love this game, it does have some downfalls. Some people find certain characters annoying, as they tend to speak a lot (which makes playing the game over again a tad annoying once you've already known what they're going to say). I would go into more detail on some tidbits (and one major part which I found great, but when going back for more just seemed depressing) but I think most problems do fit well into the game and might even make the game worse without them.
The fandom is great and terrible in its own ways. The community loves the game, but to a point where some fans think it is the 'greatest game of all time to ever exist and that no game will ever live up to its standards therefore there is no point in playing other games at all, what're you doing with your life'. Although I think the game is definitely in my top 3 which I've ever played, there are a lot of games out there which are as good or even better than Undertale in my opinion. Other than this, the fandom actually has a lot to offer in terms of art (etc) which really helps fill the gap you get once it's over. I would suggest steering clear of the fandom until you beat the game, as the majority of the community could end up spoiling parts of the game unintentionally.
In conclusion, Undertale is a fun, classy, unique game mixed with a beautiful story, original characters and choices which matter to form the perfect game which it is. I recommend this game for anyone 12 and over, as it is more recommended for 'mature' audiences and perhaps a bit younger. I would rate this game a 10/10 - you really need to play this game. Don't even watch it on someones youtube channel, just buy it and play it. It's better to go in blind, the experience is something you won't be able to describe.

The fanbase of this game doesn't make it a bad game any more than the fanbase of Portal or Skyrim beating "the cake is a lie" and "arrow in the knee" jokes into the ground made those bad games. I will be completely real with you, the reader.
With over five hundred hours of Rust under my belt, I have some grounds to speak upon this wonderful, horrible game.
Most guides will be biased. In the sense that some people are just straight up fanboying over it, and others are completely enraged because they got raided/KOS'd/hacked/etc. I, however, have been through all the twelve steps in this program, and I can tell you what Rust will be for you.
You will begin playing, and you'll feel a sense of wonder. This world just became your oyster, and you're eager to begin in your journey of rusty goodness. If you had the good judgement (sarcasm is difficult to convey here) of joining a 200+ player server, your sense of wonder will last around 30 seconds to 1 minute, because now you've got to worry about the naked guy hitting you with a rock.
However, that sense of wonder can be extended if you join a low pop server. To about 20 minutes. You'll be happily farming wood and stone, killing animals, getting that XP that's oh-so-necessary nowadays (I'll get to that in a minute). And then a random, geared guy will happily take your farm, because you couldn't throw your spear through his head before he mowed you down with a proper firearm. Or, who knows, maybe you did manage to kill him, and now you're the one with the gear. Victory definitely never tasted as immesurably sweet as it does in this game. And defeat was never as bitter.
Lets say you managed to farm up a bit for your first starter base. Something simple, like a 1x2. You've gotten yourself a wooden door, a chest to keep all your looted and farmed goodies, and a lock to keep it all safe. Now you're going out farming again.
You step out the door, and some guy kills you. Not instantly, mind you, but death and Rust are synonims. If you play this game, you will die. There's no way around that. You respawn inside your base. But the only key to your base is now in your rotting corpse. Hello darkness, my old friend.
There are ways around this (THANK GOD FOR SMALL STASHES) but until you farm enough for a keylock, a proper door, a furnace, the fuel to craft the furnace, and the metal to make the keylock and the proper door, you're gonna come back to the game just as you started it: on a beach.
I could go on for days on end, talking about how you'll die, or how people will KOS you, or how the naked that said "Friendly" just ended up shooting you in the face with the pipe shotgun he was keeping hidden in is buttcheeks.
I could go on for days on end, how the community is made up of 90% scum on adderall that shoots at anything that isn't stationary, or griefs your base, etc.
Albeit, the most fun I've ever had in a videogame was when I was "attacked" by a group of 20 nakeds that demanded that I gave them all my hemp seeds or they were gonna tear my base apart. I joined them, people were playing songs, we littered the landscape with campfires, we hatcheted down doors of people that told us to ♥♥♥♥ off. It was pure bliss.
If you're a solo player or in a very small group, you'll definitely struggle. Playing solo is Rust in Hard mode. I often compare solo Rust to Dark Souls, but worse. Because in Dark Souls, you get cucked while you play, in Rust, you can get cucked at any given time of the day, and since you're the only one that's gonna defend your base, farm for defenses and fight out on the plains, savannahs or tundras, you're in for a rough (but still rewarding) defense.
This is a game where the amazing graphics and mechanics make you want to play it constantly, but where the community will make you lose hope on humanity.
And this is why I'm recommending it. Because the game is definitely one of my all time favorites. It's not the game's fault that the community is littered with (and mainly composed by) sociopathic sadists. Bearing this in mind, if you're a paranoid person, if you can't handle losing, if you're not mature enough to handle a victory, if you're prone to flaming and mistrust others, please, don't buy Rust, and get the ♥♥♥♥ out. We're full already.

So.. Undertale.
The basic synopsis of this game without giving anything away is that you fall down a hole to where monsteres reside, and you have to escape.
But the game is so much more than that.
Undertale is an emotional joyride where you decide your fate, the fate of others and the world around you. At first, the game seems like a fun, silly new form of RPG which has nice characters, a fun story and gives you the choice with what to do with that, which is a great game alone, but then it becomes even better as you make your way to endgame. If you're looking for an emotional story over something more often seen in new releases, this game is definitely for you.
As said before, your choices effect the story. A lot. And before you go and relate this to something else such as "Life is Strange", which sure, allows your choice on what you do to affect small narratives, however none (other than one I can think of the top of my head) makes a significant difference. Looking back at Undertale, I can't think of one choice that wasn't funny to make, didn't affected the story line in a far more drastic way than you'd think or wasn't there for no reason at all.
The combat system is fairly unique, too. People may refer to this as an RPG, though the combat system seems minor compared to everyone else. Even if it isn't that important compared to the story or the choices you make, it can be fun or even challenging at times. In battle, you can do either 3 things, be merciful and spare or flee from them, maybe having to act a certain way for sparing to be possible, or fighting them. The choices you make in these battles are perhaps the most important when getting to the different types or endings, (and I say types as there are multiple endings in these different 'types' of endings), as 2 of them require only one type of way to get out of a battle.
The soundtrack for this game is, if I may say so myself, near perfect. Nearly every song spare one or two in my opinion is still catchy to listen to, even outside of the game, and if it isn't it fits beautifully with where it's set. The music alone gives a lot of emotions throughout the game - not much soundtracks which I've heard can create ambience, happiness, fear, laughter and determination as well as Undertale did.
Some people may be put of by the graphics, but honestly, they don't really matter. Looking at the starting pictures, it doesn't look that great as a game but it makes use of what graphics it uses, dare I say, as well as the likes of Earthbound or Mother 3. Undertale is a game which, if it had better graphics or more detail, it could even be worse as a game - though if you still doubt me I recommend playing the demo (located at
.
Honestly, theres a reason this game has so little unrecommendations compared to its positive reviews. Although I've been overwhelmingly positive on how much I love this game, it does have some downfalls. Some people find certain characters annoying, as they tend to speak a lot (which makes playing the game over again a tad annoying once you've already known what they're going to say). I would go into more detail on some tidbits (and one major part which I found great, but when going back for more just seemed depressing) but I think most problems do fit well into the game and might even make the game worse without them.
The fandom is great and terrible in its own ways. The community loves the game, but to a point where some fans think it is the 'greatest game of all time to ever exist and that no game will ever live up to its standards therefore there is no point in playing other games at all, what're you doing with your life'. Although I think the game is definitely in my top 3 which I've ever played, there are a lot of games out there which are as good or even better than Undertale in my opinion. Other than this, the fandom actually has a lot to offer in terms of art (etc) which really helps fill the gap you get once it's over. I would suggest steering clear of the fandom until you beat the game, as the majority of the community could end up spoiling parts of the game unintentionally.
In conclusion, Undertale is a fun, classy, unique game mixed with a beautiful story, original characters and choices which matter to form the perfect game which it is. I recommend this game for anyone 12 and over, as it is more recommended for 'mature' audiences and perhaps a bit younger. I would rate this game a 10/10 - you really need to play this game. The game itself has HUGE potential and already has some decent mechanics. There are serious problems in its current state though (still ALPHA). Here are some of them:
1) Network code is awful, considering the fact that you don't live in the server room, you will have 0-100 ping which is quite normal for online games. Regardless, when it comes to fights you will see constant lag jumps in other players' movement. The combat system is about positioning. If you can't see their movement, you can't do anything to help yourself.
2) Performance. The same server can give my GTX 960 30-100 fps depending on the population. The problem is that you don't need to see players running 20km away behind a mountain so the amount of players shouldn't affect it this dramatically. Tons of bodies and deaths per second as the result of its toxic
3) Community. Some players (after some time playing) get better equipment + they can form groups and huge clans. Seems fine and fun but there is zero penalty for killing fresh spawns whics is exactly what most of them do. The new XP system didn't really change a lot, it made the gathering part kinda more fun, but you'll be killed by an instant headshot with a crossbow on sight and lose all the stuff you've been gathering for last 2 hours and your house and the cycle repeats. There is no reason to keep another player (a potential threat) alive so noone will ever do it.
The game can become SUPER, EPIC, GREAT (drop new amazing words here) but for now it has its flaws that kinda ruin the experience for me. Add the game to your wishlist or just keep track of it but DO NOT BUY IT NOW (or just buy it for a low price and do not play it yet).

UPDATE!
With a new component system, my opinion has changed.Game finally got back the miracle of randomness in what you may find and got rid of XP progression.Progression that has put everyone`s learning and progress into same order, which in my opinion does not really suit survival based game.
Component system ensures that each time you join new server, you have a balanced field to catch up with people who may have played there longer than you did.All items can be found anywhere in the map, so the old trend of large groups camping certain areas and preventing solos to get useful things is no longer a problem.
In the same time, your progress transfer between servers is not an issue anymore; there is simply no progress in the game at this point.Its all about farming.
Component encourages more PVP, as everyone is forced to go outside and look for certain components required to craft certain high end items.So you will no longer see people camping inside their bases, solely using quarries to pump out resources of turrets to kill an animal that clipped through their wall and farm its food.
This game is ridiculously addictive and funny. Play at your own risk (of your time).

Is it the Story?
Is it the Gameplay?

I have seen many people turn there head at this game because of the retro(ish) graphics while others praising it for being beautifully designed, so it's either was on the graphics. For the characters, I have heard either way on those as well. While (again) some say the characters are well designed, thought through and help move the story along at a good pace while (again) others say that they are dull, with nothing more than cheesy jokes that don't have much thought put into them as well as having little to no relevance to the story at all. But after all is said it ends up going to the player if this is a good game or not. For those who love to sit down, explore and discover secrets as well as history behind each character than this is the game for you but, if your more into fast paste button mashers that do not really have an emphasis on the story what so ever you really are going to hate this game. Rust is extremely unforgiving pvp survivor game! Maybe it is the best battle royale game in the market to date. The best feature is the beautiful and naturally procedurally generated map. No server will have same maps ever.
However, this is not a game for everyone. If you get killed by raiders, bandits or innocent and unarmed naked savages, you will become very upset. They will steal anything you are holding whether you are a friendly or newbie. All the time you spent will be gone at anytime. So in opposite, killing them will be most rewarding and satisfying experience you will ever feel.
Many people say the community is toxic! That is very true, but there are reasons. Basically NO ONE trust each other in Rust. And servers are infested with cheaters and hackers. If they bully you for dying even though you were unarmed naked, suck it up and move on.
Do not expect to have peace whether you are farming, building. There is no peace, you will be in constant struggles against your friends and foes, especially naked ones.
New XP system is great but because everyone receive same recipe to unlock, everyone can raid as soon as they level. IMO it's too chaotic. Everyone is destined to kill and raid anyone. Shared xp is great but as soon as you hit max level, you won't benefit from being raided. Starting over after being raided is like you just lost every effort you have put into something great. That is the true pain you can actually feel... Most people quit after this. Even if you have a backup plans, it's just long way to recover. To me, map is bit too compact. If there was PVE zone where you can trade with people and pvp zone where everything is chaotic, it could fare better for both worlds, casuals and hardcore pvpers. IMO most people are defenseless. People who already unlocked efficient weapons will kill and raid everything, it should feel extremely unfair to you but welcome to Rust...
When you play this game and see a bandit or a raider harrassing you, you would likely buy a plane ticket no matter how much it costs, travel to where he lives, track him down, and murder that person in cold blood. You will know the exact feeling what I'm talking about...

if you didn't like my review then heres a recipe for some kickass brownies
Cut 185g unsalted butter into smallish cubes and tip into a medium bowl. Break 185g best dark chocolate into small pieces and drop into the bowl. Fill a small saucepan about a quarter full with hot water, then sit the bowl on top so it rests on the rim of the pan, not touching the water. Put over a low heat until the butter and chocolate have melted, stirring occasionally to mix them. Now remove the bowl from the pan. Alternatively, cover the bowl loosely with cling film and put in the microwave for 2 minutes on High. Leave the melted mixture to cool to room temperature.
While you wait for the chocolate to cool, position a shelf in the middle of your oven and turn the oven on to fan 160C/conventional 180C/gas 4 (most ovens take 10-15 minutes to heat up). Using a shallow 20cm square tin, cut out a square of non-stick baking parchment to line the base. Now tip 85g plain flour and 40g cocoa powder into a sieve held over a medium bowl, and tap and shake the sieve so they run through together and you get rid of any lumps.
With a large sharp knife, chop 50g white chocolate and 50g milk chocolate into chunks on a board. The slabs of chocolate will be quite hard, so the safest way to do this is to hold the knife over the chocolate and press the tip down on the board, then bring the rest of the blade down across the chocolate. Keep on doing this, moving the knife across the chocolate to chop it into pieces, then turn the board round 90 degrees and again work across the chocolate so you end up with rough squares.
Break 3 large eggs into a large bowl and tip in 275g golden caster sugar. With an electric mixer on maximum speed, whisk the eggs and sugar until they look thick and creamy, like a milk shake. This can take 3-8 minutes, depending on how powerful your mixer is, so don’t lose heart. You’ll know it’s ready when the mixture becomes really pale and about double its original volume. Another check is to turn off the mixer, lift out the beaters and wiggle them from side to side. If the mixture that runs off the beaters leaves a trail on the surface of the mixture in the bowl for a second or two, you’re there.
Pour the cooled chocolate mixture over the eggy mousse, then gently fold together with a rubber spatula. Plunge the spatula in at one side, take it underneath and bring it up the opposite side and in again at the middle. Continue going under and over in a figure of eight, moving the bowl round after each folding so you can get at it from all sides, until the two mixtures are one and the colour is a mottled dark brown. The idea is to marry them without knocking out the air, so be as gentle and slow as you like – you don’t want to undo all the work you did in step 4.
Hold the sieve over the bowl of eggy chocolate mixture and resift the cocoa and flour mixture, shaking the sieve from side to side, to cover the top evenly. Gently fold in this powder using the same figure of eight action as before. The mixture will look dry and dusty at first, and a bit unpromising, but if you keep going very gently and patiently, it will end up looking gungy and fudgy. Stop just before you feel you should, as you don’t want to overdo this mixing. Finally, stir in the white and milk chocolate chunks until they’re dotted throughout. Now your mixing is done and the oven can take over.
Pour the mixture into the prepared tin, scraping every bit out of the bowl with the spatula. Gently ease the mixture into the corners of the tin and paddle the spatula from side to side across the top to level it. Put in the oven and set your timer for 25 minutes. When the buzzer goes, open the oven, pull the shelf out a bit and gently shake the tin. If the brownie wobbles in the middle, it’s not quite done, so slide it back in and bake for another 5 minutes until the top has a shiny, papery crust and the sides are just beginning to come away from the tin. Take out of the oven.
Leave the whole thing in the tin until completely cold, then, if you’re using the brownie tin, lift up the protruding rim slightly and slide the uncut brownie out on its base. If you’re using a normal tin, lift out the brownie with the foil. Cut into quarters, then cut each quarter into four squares and finally into triangles. These brownies are so addictive you’ll want to make a second batch before the first is finished, but if you want to make some to hide away for a special occasion, it’s useful to know that they’ll keep in an airtight container for a good two weeks and in the freezer for up to a month.
