TL;DR: Technical issues aside, my biggest problem with the game is best explained with a cake metaphor: The title implies that zombie-killing is the cake, with player interaction and survivalism as the icing. In reality, the player interaction and survivalism is the half-baked cake, and the zombies are the icing, which is made from literal sh*t. Steer clear, people.
An MMO zombie game sounds like every zombie-killing gamer's wet dream. This can't be too bad, right?
...
...right?
I'm sorry, but this take on the concept is just terrible, even for Early Access. Since its initial release forever ago, there has been no real fixes for some of the biggest problems in the game that affect the core gameplay and overall performance. The dev team's idea of updating this game seems to be occasionally fixing random bugs and dumping random heaps of unpolished content into the game. I'm sorry, but adding content should be VERY low on the priority list when there is already a grotesque fustercluck of problems with performance and the core gameplay that DESPERATELY need fixing. Can't exactly enjoy all that shiny new content if you can't see it through all the problems with the friggin' core gameplay.
But the horrendously inefficient development process and other usual Early Access issues aside, this game suffers from the same problem as the Walking Dead. Namely, the fact that there is a much bigger focus on interaction between characters and boring survivalist mumbojumbo than the actual zombie killing. Seriously, engaging in zombie-related entertainment for character interaction and survivalism is like going to McDonalds for salad. Heck, this game is straight-up called "Day-Z" (implying that the zombies are the primary focus of the game) and it just doesn't deal in zombies a whole lot. So it's more like going to a fast-food joint called "Delicious Hamburgers" or something of that nature, only to discover that they primarily serve salad and their hamburgers are actually terrible.
This lack of focus on the actual zombies is further exacerbated by the completely broken combat system, whether you are dealing with other player characters or zombies. I don't know if it has something to do with networking problems or inefficient/crappy coding of the game itself, but I don't think I can find the words to describe how atrociously clunky and broken the combat (and the entire game as a whole, I should add) feels.
The terrible zombie combat is made EVEN WORSE by the fact that there is poor feedback in combat. I suppose I could understand poor feedback in a PvP situation as a means of discouraging players from going straight to killing each other, but the zombie killing in this game is a straight-up chore. I think just about everyone can attest to the fact that one of the biggest appeals of zombie-related entertainment is the blood and gore. Left 4 Dead 1 is a perfect example of the BARE MINIMUM when it comes to zombie gore in video games. Day-Z doesn't even live up to THAT. All you get is a crappy blood-spray animation and the zombie kinda just falls over. Not fun in any way, shape, or form.
In the end, what we have is an unpolished mess with mediocre visuals, poor performance, horrible UI, clunky combat, and terrible zombie gore. And it's in the hands of a dev team that hasn't a f*cking clue what they are doing.

I have logged close to 600 hours in this game at this point. Here are some of the pros and cons:
Pros:
- Beatiful, open world maps and interesting monuments to explore. Player generated structures are fascinating and each wipe cycle brings a new map and a new round of buildings created by players.
- Scratches a survival itch that other games haven't been able to for me.Hearing the footsteps of other players, especially when you are vulnerable, is terrifying. No zombies needed in this game, other people are the scariest threat of all. There is nothing like the feeling of leaving the protection of your base to venture into the great unknown, and nothing like that of closing that door behind you when you return to safety. (Unless, of course, you are in your base and hear the dreaded BEEP BEEP BEEP of a timed explosive charge stuck an outside wall...)
- The pvp is VERY challenging. If you engage with other players you have the opportunity to form alliances, neighborhood comradery or enemies. Plenty of opportunity to make enemies with the community this game has. Player to player interactions are my favorite part of this game. Make sure you have a mic and be prepared to die. A lot.
- Building a secure base that is difficult to raid is appropriately challenging. The more you build the better you will become at raiding other bases and predicting design elements that compromise security or make a base stronger.
- Very active development team. The changes that have been made to the game since November 2015 when I started playing have greatly improved gameplay. It has been a priviledge to play this game during its development and watch it grow.
Cons:
- The community is absolutely brutal. KOS mentality abounds and it will take lots of effort to get a base built on most higher population servers. Gameplay favors groups. If you have a friendly personality and are willing to put yourself out there, you can absolutely make friends in-game to team up with. Many people are very relieved to meet a friendly person that wants to join forces. This being said, large clans will always dominate servers.
- Some of the guns need some tweaking in terms of cost and performance, but it does seem as though the developers are working on this.
- VERY grindy. I love gathering resources in games, but even I feel a little too much gameplay is dedicated to smacking trees or stone nodes. This tends to promote more KOS mentality, it's easier for fully geared groups to massacre unarmed resource farmers than it is to farm the resources yourself.
Overall: I bought this game while it was on sale, this is the most fun I've had for $9.99 in my life. While other players are the cause for much grief (literal and figurative) in this game, they are also what makes gampley so interesting, complex, and addicting. I keep coming back for more because of the unpredictability of Rust.

I bought the game anyway and jumped right in. I quickly got the hang of the controls but with no "tutorial" it would be difficult for first time PC gamers. The gameplay was not the best but it was pre alpha, and for a pre alpha i would give the game a 5/10 in 2014 when i bought the game. However, that was in 2014 as I stated. Fast forward one year, and not only has dayz standalone had many updates, they have planned to put dayz standalone on consoles in the upcomming future. In 2015 I have seen choppy landscapes turn into beautiful areas with vast amounts of color and detail. I have seen gameplay run a lot smother. The developers have come along way from where they began, and they are not stopping there. There has been talk of adding the little bird in the next update and talk of blood thirsty wolves to add to the mix of zombies, hunger, and punk bandits. I only have 97.9 hours on dayz standalone but with these upcomming updates those hours will multiply by 10. I am ready to see what the developers have planned for 2016 AND AS OF 2015, I GIVE DAYZ STANDALONE A 8.5/10. Okay, so here's your typical RPG battle:
>Attack
>Sit still and get attacked
>Heal
>Sit still and get attacked
>Listen to some generic dialogue you've heard 100+ times before
>Attack
>Kill enemy
>The end
Here's a typical Undertale battle:
>Ask oppenent how they're doing
>Get attacked
>Take no damage because you can dodge attacks manually
>Give the enemy a sandwich to cheer them up
>Have a heartfelt conversation you've never heard before
>Make friends with opponent
>The end
Undertale delivers a unique RPG experience that allows players to break the usual monotony of turn-based combat by giving them a myriad of options in combat. You can win battles without ever raising a weapon or taking a single hit. Boss fights are fun and challenging, and are accomanied by some of the best retro-style game music I've heard in years. Combat is never repetitive, and each enemy offers entertaining dialogue and unique attacks to accompany their battles.
Undertale is also the first game in years that I've actually wanted to replay. The effects your choices have on the story are subtle, but they do matter enough to make giving the game a second run worth it. There are also a few secrets you'll be able to access on a second playthrough that weren't present the first time.
It might not look like much, but underneath its simple style is a brilliantly designed game that offers a refreshing departure from the current generic-FPS-saturated state of the gaming world.

This game is actually amazing. The multiple endings all fill you in on more of the story, which is incredible in and of itself. They way the story is told is a way that can only be done through video games. Another amazing thing about Undertale is the world. Each NPC and character each have their own personality, something rarely seen nowadays. This makes the Underground feel as if it's habited by actual people(monsters?). The battle system is very fresh and really changes up the standard RPG formula. As someone who likes games that engage the player almost all the time, such as fighting games or rhythm games, I can say that I never felt bored while playing. Typical RPGs make battles a chore where you're just navigating though menus. In Undertale, the battles are always engaging, plus they have an excellent difficulty curve. Everything about this game just oozes personality and character and it's evident that Undertale was made with a specific goal in mind, to have a game that not just makes the player feel as if they are witnessing a great world, but makes the player feel as if they are a part of the great world. The entire game will make you laugh and a certain ending will make you cry 99 times out of 100. Undertale is a masterpeice and is tied for my favourite game of all time. 10/10
P.S. The music is composed of 100% bangers. Literally the best soundtrack I have ever heard in my life.
P.P.S. Oh yeah, Forgot to mention the fanbase is a little, uhh, how do I put this, hmm, rabid. Let's go with rabid. That doesn't take away from the game though.

Don't play rust. Rust is a game made for people over the age of 18, and is dominated by people under the age of 18, who have no job, and all the free time in the world. I've put a boatload of effort into rust, and this is essentially what you can expect:
-Over half the content in this game is worthless on 99% of servers if you aren't playing 3+ people.
-If you have a job you're just wasting money buying Rust. If you (and/or your group) don't have at least 2-3 people who can play actively during the day, there is no way you can keep your♥♥♥♥♥♥safe, irrelevant to how big you build your base.
-Long♥♥♥♥♥periods of AFK crafting items, and working your♥♥♥♥♥off just to gather resources, which you'll probably die before you can secure unless you play in a low pop server, or past like midnight. In the 830 "hours" I've put into rust,  less than 20 hours has been spent doing anything actually fun and exciting. Most of it has simply been gathering materials and building a base to keep said materials to try and prepare to do something fun. But any time you have a large stockpile of equipment, you're going to get raided. I guarantee it.
-100% of what you do in Rust is high risk, but unless you're running with a huge squad is incrdibly low reward.
-A bunch of people accusing you (Or a member of your group) of hacking. Honestly, in my experience, they are probably right too. It's pretty common for people to wait til late night to use things like ESP (the ability to see all items, enemy players, and what their names are from basically any area) to find and steal all your♥♥♥♥♥♥ As well people take the lengths to purchase hacks, make alternative accounts to run them safely (and on almost all servers it won't get their main accounts banned) who go around and scout bases to see whats inside so that they can raid you.
-on official servers, most everything is over crowded, and everything is still dominated by a large few. On modded servers, everyone has the same size bases usually, and its still dominated by a large few, but everyone just sits in their base and shoots at you with bolt action rifles.
It's really unfortunate, because honestly the game visuals are phenominal. Ambient sounds, environment, and everything is fantastic. The Dev's are really awesome, and they work hard, and are one of the best dev teams at updating both their game, and the player base. the problem is it's just a full time job more than a game. If you can't (Or don't have at least 2-3 friends) who can actively play 4-8 hours a day, you'll probably never get anything done. Oh and the community is essentially toxic ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s for 99% of the time, which to a degree is pretty fun when you're in a server with no large clans/groups. Unfortunately you would be better off trying to find a dolphin who speaks English. It just takes way too much effort to play.
For example: The most efficient way to raid a large base is usually with rockets. It takes 4 rockets to destroy 1 wall. Unless you hit perfect corners, in which case you can destroy up to 4 walls with 4 rockets. That cost 40 explosives. To get 40 explosives you need about 2,000 gun powder. 2,000 gun powder requires 4,000 sulfur and 6,000 charcoal. The cost of 6,000 charcoal is roughly 8,000 burned logs, or about 12 trees chopped down. You get like 450 or so sulfur per rock that you mine. So about 10 rocks worth. Plus probably a couple hours worth of waiting, for the smelting. Now you can increase efficiency by using large furnaces, or huge quantities of small ones. All of which costs a lot of time and resources to safely protect/secure, and use. Which is more effort. You do have other options such as taking down the helicoptor that appears roughly once every hour, and has random loot. The issue again, impossible to do alone (Shooting it down is easy, but getting the loot without distracting half a maps worth of people gearing up to try and take it from you is different though) you can also try to loot randomly at monuments, but the drop rates for raid equipment is incredibly low, and entirely luck based not only in finding the barrels/crate spawns, but also in what you get out of them.
So if you don't have friends (and most of you ♥♥♥♥s don't) and you have a job. Not the game for you.

The rawness of Rust really astounds me every time I log in; I've found tribes of naked people; gangs of hoodlums; and community's designed for survival. Much like other Survival games, you'll question why you put so much time into your base just to see it raided one day - your shelter destroyed and valuables stolen. You'll lament at the fact you got murdered because you stepped outside to collect wood and stones. And you'll find yourself obsessively preying on harmless noobs when their naked body runs past you. Only to find they were carrying a rock and a torch.
But you'll love every second of it.
The enjoyment comes from being unattached to your belongings and contributing to the predator/prey game dyanmic. Whether it be working towards a sense of security for you or an alliance with other players or unleashing mayham for unsuspecting players, you'll feel a sense of satisfaction from completing your tasks. I could sit here and type a review, saying "Great game! Story's good, gameplay is great, etc", but instead, to really give you a feel and perspective to  Undertale, I thought I would share MY PERSONAL EXPERIENCE with the game.
I'll be honest, when Undertale first came out, I instantly HATED IT. It was becoming the new "FNaF". It was everywhere on the internet, and like FNaF, the fanbase was turning bad. So, I went around hating the fanbase and the game without any knowlege of the game itself.
So, after talking to some of my friends, and theem telling me how good the game was, Steam was having the lunar sale and I thought, "Well its  on sale so..." and than I planned to play the whole game in one day, but eventually ran out of time with new classes and stuff in school.
As of writing this review, I have MORE than 6.7 hours on undertale. If anything I should have 18 since I played the game in offline mode, since I was on vaction and didn't have internet.
When I finally decided to play the game, I wanted to do Genocide first, regardless what the fanbase said. However, I didn't know the rules to the Genocide route, and ended up going with the Neutral route. When the  ending finally came. when Asgore was killed, Flowey's little "scene" at the end scared the living sh*t out of me, and the whole boss fight after was difficult but touching at the same time. Eventually, after I beat flowey:
I chose to kill him.
You know how people in the fanbase say "Even your choices in a previous game effect future games?"
I can't begin to tell you how true that it.
After getting my neutral ending, I quickly restarted my game and decided to do the Pacifest route, and I ended up doing amazing and almost rushing it, since I already had done all the puzzles and fights. Now, during Asgores fight, I ended up fighting as usual, and drained his health to the point of choosing to kill or spare. Now, I'll tell you this:
I DIDN'T GET THE PACIFEST ENDING.
My neutral game before hand, when I killed flowey, AFFECTED THE ENDING. Flowey KILLED ASGORE, EVEN WHEN I SPARED HIM. And than proceeded to tell me that he can foil any happy ending in Undertale due to save files or some crap like that.
Was I angry? A little. But, also, I was amazed at how much effort was put into this game, and how, like they say "EVERY Decision Matterss".
Another feature in the "Undertale Experience" was the characters. The characters are NOT forgettable. The attach to you in a way. I actually felt like I was "Knew" the some of the Characters, like Papyrus and Sans.
But one thing the charcters in this game did to me, was really creepy to me at first. Let me explain:
After beating the Neutral Run, and the foiled Pacifest, I decided to attempt Genocide, after using the Data on my phone to research it. When I reached Toriels fight, and I killed her.....
What she said felt like, she wasn't saying it to Frisk, but if felt like she was saying it to ME as a person. Same with Sans when he said his line about "having a badtime". I FELT LIKE HE WAS TALKING TO ME. Therfore, a little creeped out I reset the Genocide route and haven't touched Undertale since yesterday.
See, that was the power of this game. Undertale made me happy, sad, angry, creeped out. It made me feel and connect.
I would reccomend Undertale to ANYONE who wants a Unique game experience. And if you don't like it, thats fine.We all have opinions. But, I'd just give it a try.
And as my friend said about this same game:
"10 bucks os super cheap for a game of this strature. It will exeed ALL your expectations"

"Unfortunately my review will probably be washed down by the large amount of negative reviews this game has received, however I will take a stab at getting my voice out there to the people. First off, however, I want you to look at how many hours I have logged into this game. The amount of time I have spent in DayZ Standalone far surpasses any other game I have played on Steam, and for good reason. There is a lot of misconception going around the Steam reviews, and quite frankly many of the negative comments are filled with bigot hate towards the developers and a lack of understanding for how the early access model works in DayZ. Hopefully I can clear some of the confusion and give potential buyers some clarity on the title.
Let's rewind the clocks back to late 2013, a year after DayZ mod was released on Arma II. The survival sandbox genre had just exploded into the videogames scene, and every developer was trying to claim their stake in the land of the survivalist games. At the time, Bohemia Interactive had in their hands the most popular survivalist game on the market. Thousands of people played DayZ mod, and people loved the idea of an open-world survival game in which the elements and players are pitted against you. DayZ mod set the tone for what a survival game should be: challenging, unforgiving, and hard to top. Bohemia wanted to take the title and make it something greater, something much bigger and smoother than what the original mod intended to be. They knew that releasing a full version of the game on that clunky Arma II engine wouldn't cut it, so they had to make major improvements to bring the title into 2016 and beyond.
Instead of releasing the full DayZ Standalone game on the horrible Arma II engine, Bohemia made the decision to completely re-gut the engine and build a new one from scratch. FROM. SCRATCH. There are a few legacy modules that are getting carried over, but for the most part every aspect of the game is new (render, physics, lighting, etc). Anyone who has had any kind of development experience in video-games understands that this is a daunting task, a momentous task, a task that doesn't happen in one month or one year; No, creating a brand new engine takes years to develop, and this is where the root of the "problem" started.
DayZ Standalone went into early access in late 2013, and this is where they made their big mistake. The game simply wasn't ready. With no new engine components even being started on (plus it hit early access only 4 weeks into the development timeline, dear god), many early access players were left in disappointment when new features could not be pushed right away. People cried "fix zombies", but the zombies could not be fixed yet because an entirely new AI system was being created. People cried "fix FPS", but no FPS fix could be put in place because they were busy developing the new renderer. People wanted new vehicles, but vehicles could not be added yet because the physics system was being re-worked. There's no point in providing a "fix" for a mechanic in the game when that mechanic is going to be entirely replaced down the line anyways.
And so people got ♥♥♥♥♥♥, and fed up. "$20 for a Standalone title, and there's no fixes for these bugs?" Even I was at the point of rage, often times quitting DayZ Standalone for months at a time. People started saying that the developers weren't doing anything, that they "took the money and ran". But the real reality was that they were simply hard at work laying out the foundation for the title, unfortunately not being able to fix most bugs and issues at the time because they were so busy writing up new systems for the game to play on.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SO LET'S FAST FORWARD. It's late 2015 now, nearing 2016. DayZ Standalone has been in development for 2 years now. Has the game changed? Are any of the new engine models finished? Are zombies even fixed yet?
You bet your ♥♥♥ they are. If you were to ask me when I think the game should of been released to the public as early access, I would have said right now (version .59) would have been the time to do it. FINALLY, after 2 years of development, Bohemia Interactive is getting around to completing all of the upcoming engine changes and new foundation for the title. Let me make a quick list to get your hype train rolling:
New Renderer is nearly finished, should have "30 - 40 % FPS boost overall"
Zombie AI is brand new and fixed, zombies now have sense of smell and sight, don't clip through walls, are actually a challenge
Four vehicles currently in game: V3S, Sedan, Hatchback, and Bus. Arial vehicles confirmed, as well as bikes and boats
New vehicle physics system taken from GTA V (Bullet SDK). Full vehicle maintenance and parts
All servers persistent. Camps and items are saved after restart. You can create large camps now.
Tents, Barrels, vehicles, protector cases, and backpacks can all be used as base storage now. Stays persistent through server reset
Loot respawn fixed. Loot spawns in areas that make sense now, it is very hard to get access to good weapons and ammo
Sickness and Disease now a major factor of gameplay
Tons of new animals in the game with new Animal AI. They react to sight and sound, as well as naturally roam the map looking for ponds and fields to graze in.
Predator animals confirmed, including wolves and bears
map changes and new northern towns expand the map greatly from mod
Softskills soon to be implemented, aka the more you run the more fit you get. skills develop over time
Every building now enter able with loot
A ton of new weapons and cosmetic items (clothing) added into the game
character wear progession, such as growing beards and getting dirt / blood on yourself, soon to be implemented
Contaminated Zones confirmed and being worked on, the first being a military base up north
And soo so so much more. I could keep the list going forever but it honestly doesn't cover how much they've added into the game since launch.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Conclusion
Anyone who says DayZ Standalone is dead, or that the developers have "taken the money and ran", or that the community is dead, quite frankly is full of ♥♥♥♥. The game is very much alive and so much better than it was when it started. Even though DayZ SA has been slow off the start compared to other survivalist games (H1Z1, Rust, ARK, Unturned, Miscreated, etc), I strongly believe it will come out on top as the best survivalist game when it is finished. "Unfortunately my review will probably be washed down by the large amount of negative reviews this game has received, however I will take a stab at getting my voice out there to the people. First off, however, I want you to look at how many hours I have logged into this game. The amount of time I have spent in DayZ Standalone far surpasses any other game I have played on Steam, and for good reason. There is a lot of misconception going around the Steam reviews, and quite frankly many of the negative comments are filled with bigot hate towards the developers and a lack of understanding for how the early access model works in DayZ. Hopefully I can clear some of the confusion and give potential buyers some clarity on the title.
Let's rewind the clocks back to late 2013, a year after DayZ mod was released on Arma II. The survival sandbox genre had just exploded into the videogames scene, and every developer was trying to claim their stake in the land of the survivalist games. At the time, Bohemia Interactive had in their hands the most popular survivalist game on the market. Thousands of people played DayZ mod, and people loved the idea of an open-world survival game in which the elements and players are pitted against you. DayZ mod set the tone for what a survival game should be: challenging, unforgiving, and hard to top. Bohemia wanted to take the title and make it something greater, something much bigger and smoother than what the original mod intended to be. They knew that releasing a full version of the game on that clunky Arma II engine wouldn't cut it, so they had to make major improvements to bring the title into 2016 and beyond.
Instead of releasing the full DayZ Standalone game on the horrible Arma II engine, Bohemia made the decision to completely re-gut the engine and build a new one from scratch. FROM. SCRATCH. There are a few legacy modules that are getting carried over, but for the most part every aspect of the game is new (render, physics, lighting, etc). Anyone who has had any kind of development experience in video-games understands that this is a daunting task, a momentous task, a task that doesn't happen in one month or one year; No, creating a brand new engine takes years to develop, and this is where the root of the "problem" started.
DayZ Standalone went into early access in late 2013, and this is where they made their big mistake. The game simply wasn't ready. With no new engine components even being started on (plus it hit early access only 4 weeks into the development timeline, dear god), many early access players were left in disappointment when new features could not be pushed right away. People cried "fix zombies", but the zombies could not be fixed yet because an entirely new AI system was being created. People cried "fix FPS", but no FPS fix could be put in place because they were busy developing the new renderer. People wanted new vehicles, but vehicles could not be added yet because the physics system was being re-worked. There's no point in providing a "fix" for a mechanic in the game when that mechanic is going to be entirely replaced down the line anyways.
And so people got ♥♥♥♥♥♥, and fed up. "$20 for a Standalone title, and there's no fixes for these bugs?" Even I was at the point of rage, often times quitting DayZ Standalone for months at a time. People started saying that the developers weren't doing anything, that they "took the money and ran". But the real reality was that they were simply hard at work laying out the foundation for the title, unfortunately not being able to fix most bugs and issues at the time because they were so busy writing up new systems for the game to play on.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SO LET'S FAST FORWARD. It's late 2015 now, nearing 2016. DayZ Standalone has been in development for 2 years now. Has the game changed? Are any of the new engine models finished? Are zombies even fixed yet?
You bet your ♥♥♥ they are. If you were to ask me when I think the game should of been released to the public as early access, I would have said right now (version .59) would have been the time to do it. FINALLY, after 2 years of development, Bohemia Interactive is getting around to completing all of the upcoming engine changes and new foundation for the title. Let me make a quick list to get your hype train rolling:
New Renderer is nearly finished, should have "30 - 40 % FPS boost overall"
Zombie AI is brand new and fixed, zombies now have sense of smell and sight, don't clip through walls, are actually a challenge
Four vehicles currently in game: V3S, Sedan, Hatchback, and Bus. Arial vehicles confirmed, as well as bikes and boats
New vehicle physics system taken from GTA V (Bullet SDK). Full vehicle maintenance and parts
All servers persistent. Camps and items are saved after restart. You can create large camps now.
Tents, Barrels, vehicles, protector cases, and backpacks can all be used as base storage now. Stays persistent through server reset
Loot respawn fixed. Loot spawns in areas that make sense now, it is very hard to get access to good weapons and ammo
Sickness and Disease now a major factor of gameplay
Tons of new animals in the game with new Animal AI. They react to sight and sound, as well as naturally roam the map looking for ponds and fields to graze in.
Predator animals confirmed, including wolves and bears
map changes and new northern towns expand the map greatly from mod
Softskills soon to be implemented, aka the more you run the more fit you get. skills develop over time
Every building now enter able with loot
A ton of new weapons and cosmetic items (clothing) added into the game
character wear progession, such as growing beards and getting dirt / blood on yourself, soon to be implemented
Contaminated Zones confirmed and being worked on, the first being a military base up north
And soo so so much more. I could keep the list going forever but it honestly doesn't cover how much they've added into the game since launch.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Conclusion
Anyone who says DayZ Standalone is dead, or that the developers have "taken the money and ran", or that the community is dead, quite frankly is full of ♥♥♥♥. The game is very much alive and so much better than it was when it started. Even though DayZ SA has been slow off the start compared to other survivalist games (H1Z1, Rust, ARK, Unturned, Miscreated, etc), I strongly believe it will come out on top as the best survivalist game when it is finished. No other survival game has this much attention to detail and realism as DayZ. No other survival game has the kind of studio resources and money that Bohemia has to put out a strong title. No other survival game has mastered the hardcore aspect of survival and struggle better than DayZ. Almost every other survival game was rushed out on a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ Unreal engine in an effort to reap money off the survivalist scene and try to outbeat Bohemia to the punch on features and gameplay. Games like Rust and H1Z1 fail to hit the bullseye on what a survival game should be. DayZ Standalone does this right and does it good. I would definitely recommend this game now, as it's about to surpass the ♥♥♥♥ outta all other games on the market. Go out there and start surviving!"

This is my first ever review and if it helps at least one person, it would have been worth the time to write it. This is a game of heavy cons and very little pros. Playing this game is like walking through the desert in the nude during a sandstorm and getting extremely happy when half a drop of rain drops on your butt cheek. It is beyond brutal.
I started playing this game early last year and i fell in love with not the game, but my own ego. This is a game that breeds this sort of ego driven gameplay "I am better than X, my group is better than yours". If you want to spend countless hours talking in all chat convicing other players you are a god amongst them, this will be a game you will also sink well over 1,000 hours into. If you on the other hand are a humble player looking to build a base and maybe make friends with your neighbor.. THIS IS NOT THE GAME FOR YOU.
The community is beyond cancer and revels in the fact it is so crappy. You will get killed by any and all players regardless if you are a threat to their survival or not. If you even try to tell them you are friendly or you are unarmed they will shout "kill yourself" in their mics while slaughtering. But you can't really blame a community that is driven by content creators debuting the PvP of this game, it is a highlight - and the only redeeming factor outside of it's amazing AFK crafting simulator you will dedicate at least 80% of your time to if you aren't in a group with a dedicated crafter.
If you want to play this game efficiently do the following:
1. Say goodbye to your loved ones, and your dog
2. Watch every video on the subreddit as fast as possible to learn any new exploit to raid people with
3. Talk really big in chat, this will make the game more interesting as players will want to raid you
4. Remember that this is Rust, and anything you do gets deleted in 1 week, 2 weeks, 4 weeks, whenever the admin drops his coffee and decides the server needs to be culled
5. Prepare yourself for endless hours of frustra-Fun. I mean fun.
This is a game with a very very niche playerbase, and it isn't for everyone.

WARNING! THIS REVIEW WILL  CONTAIN SPOLIERS! ALSO IT WILL BE REALLY LONG!
I could sit here and type a review, saying "Great game! Story's good, gameplay is great, etc", but instead, to really give you a feel and perspective to  Undertale, I thought I would share MY PERSONAL EXPERIENCE with the game.
I'll be honest, when Undertale first came out, I instantly HATED IT. It was becoming the new "FNaF". It was everywhere on the internet, and like FNaF, the fanbase was turning bad. So, I went around hating the fanbase and the game without any knowlege of the game itself.
So, after talking to some of my friends, and theem telling me how good the game was, Steam was having the lunar sale and I thought, "Well its  on sale so..." and than I planned to play the whole game in one day, but eventually ran out of time with new classes and stuff in school.
As of writing this review, I have MORE than 6.7 hours on undertale. If anything I should have 18 since I played the game in offline mode, since I was on vaction and didn't have internet.
When I finally decided to play the game, I wanted to do Genocide first, regardless what the fanbase said. However, I didn't know the rules to the Genocide route, and ended up going with the Neutral route. When the  ending finally came. when Asgore was killed, Flowey's little "scene" at the end scared the living sh*t out of me, and the whole boss fight after was difficult but touching at the same time. Eventually, after I beat flowey:
I chose to kill him.
You know how people in the fanbase say "Even your choices in a previous game effect future games?"
I can't begin to tell you how true that it.
After getting my neutral ending, I quickly restarted my game and decided to do the Pacifest route, and I ended up doing amazing and almost rushing it, since I already had done all the puzzles and fights. Now, during Asgores fight, I ended up fighting as usual, and drained his health to the point of choosing to kill or spare. Now, I'll tell you this:
I DIDN'T GET THE PACIFEST ENDING.
My neutral game before hand, when I killed flowey, AFFECTED THE ENDING. Flowey KILLED ASGORE, EVEN WHEN I SPARED HIM. And than proceeded to tell me that he can foil any happy ending in Undertale due to save files or some crap like that.
Was I angry? A little. But, also, I was amazed at how much effort was put into this game, and how, like they say "EVERY Decision Matterss".
Another feature in the "Undertale Experience" was the characters. The characters are NOT forgettable. The attach to you in a way. I actually felt like I was "Knew" the some of the Characters, like Papyrus and Sans.
But one thing the charcters in this game did to me, was really creepy to me at first. Let me explain:
After beating the Neutral Run, and the foiled Pacifest, I decided to attempt Genocide, after using the Data on my phone to research it. When I reached Toriels fight, and I killed her.....
What she said felt like, she wasn't saying it to Frisk, but if felt like she was saying it to ME as a person. Same with Sans when he said his line about "having a badtime". I FELT LIKE HE WAS TALKING TO ME. Therfore, a little creeped out I reset the Genocide route and haven't touched Undertale since yesterday.
See, that was the power of this game. Undertale made me happy, sad, angry, creeped out. It made me feel and connect.
I would reccomend Undertale to ANYONE who wants a Unique game experience. And if you don't like it, thats fine.We all have opinions. But, I'd just give it a try.
And as my friend said about this same game:
"10 bucks os super cheap for a game of this strature. It will exeed ALL your expectations"

Watch out for other players, who can be as friendly as they are deceiving. Only a few shots from a Eoka Pistol or a few pokes from a spear are needed to render your naked body useless. Possibly the most positively impacting game in my life to date. Undertale has a brilliant, lovable ensemble cast with whom you will laugh, cry, and battle with as you explore the quirky upbeat world of the Underground.
The fantastic soundtrack has 101 individual themes (according to the official soundtrack) which come together to form an incredible score. These themes are in turn composed of various shared leitmotifs that tie the world and its inhabitants together musically.
The gameplay is curious and clever, building on a mashup of rpg exploration and bullet curtain shooter mechanics with no two enemies fighting with the same patterns. Bosses are a treat subverting the player's expectations  and the established game mechanics themselves to create an ongoing fresh and rewarding experience. The ACT menu makes this even more enjoyable, providing the player with a variety of ways to interact with the Underground's inhabitants and actually avoid fighting at all!
Underneath it all, Undertale is a remarkably introspective game. Through your choices and actions, you will not only determine the outcome of an entire world, but learn a lot about who you are at your core if you play true to your heart.
Undertale is one of my favourite games of all time. You would be missing out on a brilliant, unique experience by passing this game by.
Don't give up and STAY DETERMINED!

Tempted to hate it due to the popularity? That's fine, I don't blame ya.
I do dare anyone who plays it to say it wasn't an interesting (and touching) experience, no matter what type of gamer or person you are. So there you go. Play it, judge it for yourself, and then shut up about it forever if you don't like bandwagoning.
I hate doing such a circumstantial review that has more about the fandom than the game, but hopefully it's functional and draws in people, because this really needs to be addressed: far too many people are dismissing this as "overrated" by just seeing the fandom, and it's a feeling I totally understand, but for the love of God, don't let it stop you from playing this game. I mean come on, what are you, a 14 years old that just found out about contrarianism?
The other reason for the review not being much about the game is because of something you definitely already heard a million times: it's one of those games where the experience is better if you go there without knowing anything about it.
Usually, I'm not for this kind of argument: the whole concept of "spoilers" annoys me, because it implies that you can ruin something by simply giving someone a piece of information, as if to say that the highest value of that something resided in merely shock value and not within the journey to get to whichever event was spoiled... however, I must say that in this case the "blind experience" is at least heavily tied to the nature of the game. Not that the experience would be bad without it, but it would be extremely enhanced with it.
Anyway, if you really want to go in it knowing at least something about the gameplay and want to have an idea of what to expect and to see if it might be your kinda thing, here it comes, but beware: it's almost secondary to what this game is about.
The game is an earthbound-styled JRPG that manages to make the old-school battle system of such games (in my opinion, a bit obsolete) way more bearable by making it about timing/rhytm when you attack, and bullet-hell-like when you are attacked. You also have the choice to not fight and have enemies not fight you by using diplomacy, which is usually arbitrary commands to be performed in a certain order to convince them to stop fighting.
No, the peaceful playthrough mechanic is NOT complex dialogue choices nor complex at all, it's just picking an option and reading some flavor text until you get it right.
No, the fighting itself is not hard: the game is extremely easy, save for two major exceptions that are extremely hard and are locked behind a lot of farming.
So yeah, if you look at this from a gameplay-perspective, you might find it not appealing, but I warned you: there's something more to this game, and there are precise reasons behind all of those game-design choices.
Also yeah it's very good. Subverts the player's expectations consistently enough and has enough details to keep you entertained even after your first playthroughs.

I have been playing rust since it started back with the old single map format. Since then the game has changed massively and for the better. Gone are the rad towns with the zombies, to the current and to be released soon XP system.
Basic premise of the game is to survive, not only against the wild, but again other people. To survive you need to kill wildlife, knock down trees and gather resources to build a shelter, a home or a castle if you so wish. Building bigger buildings comes at a cost, you can be raided. Other player can exploit weaknesses in your design and use that to enter your house and take your stuff! The world resources regen fairly slowly, forcing the pvp aspect as time moves on. Although there are many low pop community servers which cater to new players with friendly no KOS rules. Personally i would start there to get the hang of the game before moving on.
This Game is still in alpha, due to a change in engine half way through the original alpha release. Meaning sometime servers have to be wiped to place the new version. this is a good and bad thing, reset for an even playing field, but also a loss of your hard work up to that point.
Pro's
Decent single player experience.
Strong Team play experience.
decent crafting progression.
Strong sense of danger (bloody choppers)
Con's
Some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s out there. (its the internet so no shock)
resource regen is a bit iffy.
still a way to go before a stable game is made.

My friend bought this game in a 4 pack and was nice enough to give me a copy.  So I loaded this baby up to see what all the fuss was about.  I came to on a debris strewn coastline with not a damn thing on and anatomically correct lady bits (but I'm a guy???).
I proceeded to explore my surroundings and found a wonderful pumpkin patch.  I was pretty excited, because, who wouldn't be?  I picked a few pumpkins and then noticed up stream there was a rickety old cabin type building.  My curiosity got the best of me.  I started making my way there when I heard a sound.  In a fury I turned myself around, rock at the ready.  There standing before me was a man.  But this was no ordinary man.
It was the devil himself.  Decked out in terrifying clothes no doubt made from the marijowannas.  Atop his shoulders sat a carved out pumpkin.  My heart sank.  I knew it was the end for me.  As he shot me in the face with his fully automatic crossbow, I removed myself from my desk chair.  Curled up into a ball.  And began crying.  My attacker must have heard this, for all I heard after were the sounds of his terribly laughter.
It will haunt me for the rest of my life.

Rust is an action survival game developed by Facepunch Studios. Stranded naked and alone, players must scavenge an island in search of food and resources. Every server features a procedurally generated map, with multiple environments to explore, from snow-capped mountains to densely wooded forests. Collect wood to forge a spear and hunt boars for meat and cloth. Create an extensive number of items, from hunting bows to padded locks, to arm yourself and secure your goods. Protect yourself from the elements by constructing a home, using a robust building utility that makes almost any design possible. Watch out for other players, who can be as friendly as they are deceiving. Only a few shots from a Eoka Pistol or a few pokes from a spear are needed to render your naked body useless. Arm yourself with weapons and gear to raid player fortresses, in pursuit of loot or an epic firefight.

Welcome back to Pandora, more or less where you last left off if you finished Borderlands.
Needless to say, if you enjoyed the first Borderlands, you'll have no trouble loving the sequel all over again. It keeps the fast paced, trigger happy combat, brings forth new (as well as old) enemies to fight, and a vast landscape to get lost in all at once.
Personally, I've never found this game very good with stealth, as the assassin's class seems a bit more like "accurate gunman". Nevertheless, I still thoroughly enjoy it, as well as sniping and cutting throats along with being a gunzerker.
Overall, I love Borderlands 2. The design is stunning, especially in the style that 2K provides, the gameplay will keep you hooked for hours, and you'll keep coming back for more. Like the first, enemies are in countless numbers, so you get to replay the same stuff over again as much as you like. It's a fun game, and it's definitely worth a buy.

For a somewhat more indepth review:
But to summerize, this is more of an "evolution" then a "revolution" sort of sequel.  In hindsight, the original was a bit of a glorified tech demo, a bunch of concepts thrown together to form a functional game.  Anthony Burch is not quite the writer he is made out to be in the Gearbox promos but the story is solid and at times geniunely entertaining.  And of course, the fact that the game improves on pretty much everything that made the original so popular helps too.  There is more diversity between guns, shields, and grenade mods then there was previously, all four core characters have tighter skill trees... Basically everything you would have liked about the first game has been upgraded and fine-tuned.  One of the few games to defeat the lingering curse that hangs over sci-fi action-RPGs.

This is my first ever review and if it helps at least one person, it would have been worth the time to write it. This is a game of heavy cons and very little pros. Playing this game is like walking through the desert in the nude during a sandstorm and getting extremely happy when half a drop of rain drops on your butt cheek. It is beyond brutal.
I started playing this game early last year and i fell in love with not the game, but my own ego. This is a game that breeds this sort of ego driven gameplay "I am better than X, my group is better than yours". If you want to spend countless hours talking in all chat convicing other players you are a god amongst them, this will be a game you will also sink well over 1,000 hours into. If you on the other hand are a humble player looking to build a base and maybe make friends with your neighbor.. THIS IS NOT THE GAME FOR YOU.
The community is beyond cancer and revels in the fact it is so crappy. You will get killed by any and all players regardless if you are a threat to their survival or not. If you even try to tell them you are friendly or you are unarmed they will shout "kill yourself" in their mics while slaughtering. But you can't really blame a community that is driven by content creators debuting the PvP of this game, it is a highlight - and the only redeeming factor outside of it's amazing AFK crafting simulator you will dedicate at least 80% of your time to if you aren't in a group with a dedicated crafter.
If you want to play this game efficiently do the following:
1. Say goodbye to your loved ones, and your dog
2. Watch every video on the subreddit as fast as possible to learn any new exploit to raid people with
3. Talk really big in chat, this will make the game more interesting as players will want to raid you
4. Remember that this is Rust, and anything you do gets deleted in 1 week, 2 weeks, 4 weeks, whenever the admin drops his coffee and decides the server needs to be culled
5. Prepare yourself for endless hours of frustra-Fun. I mean fun.
This is a game with a very very niche playerbase, and it isn't for everyone.

For a year now, I've been wanting to write a good review of this game. In spite of its broken mechanics, the promise of really fun open world survival game loomed in the distance. The problem is that every time you think things might get better, the developers find some way of fussing things up. The  build on which I'm writing this review is .59, which is by far the best build since the game's inception. That being said, I don't believe I'll be playing DAYZ any more.
First off, Alpha-schmalfa. Two years into development Bohemia is nowhere near acheiving a completed title. At the current rate of progress, the game won't be ready until some time in 2017. This snail's pace might be tolerable if it wasn't the case that every single build they release has some murderously unplayable quality to it. One of the most frustrating is admin abuse, which combined with a new feature of .59 was enough to make me give up hope. I'll walk you through the most recent turd sandwich:
A group of friends and I have been working hard over the last week to get a vehicle working and build a base. We didn't want an empty server, so we chose what seemed like a somewhat busy server as our surrogate home. We finally had our car (an offroad with everything), we got into some adventures, lost the car, got it back, and earlier today, after a helicopter hunt, we were returning to home base to sign off with some quality loot. All of us were suddenly kicked for no reason. This wouldn't have been a problem if we'd been walking, but if you're kicked in a car, you die. so there went a week of colaborative effort along with any desire to play this game again.
There is no real way to report admin abuse. The server providers depend on the admins renting the servers, so they don't really care what they do with them as long as they're paying. In other words, if you want to enjoy this game, you have to pay for a server. The offending server BTW is "nipples in despair" IP: 68.232.179.127:2362
But that's not all. Just read through the reviews. As much as I have (at times) personally enjoyed this game, most people seem to hate it. I went though 5 pages of reviews without seeing a single positive one. I wanted to be the exception. I wanted to say, as someone with over 1200 hours of game time, that if you stuck in there long enough, the dream would come true. Well, I hate to busrt your bubble but the dream is dead. Let the dream die. All that lies ahead is frustration, dissatisfaction, and dissafection.
I feel like a battered spouse that has put up with a loser for years, believing they would get better, only to be left with a bad taste in my mouth. I enjoyed the good times, but DAYZ, you're just another loser, and I want a divorce.

I could feel the sweat on my palms as I gripped the cool, metallic stock of my Hyperion sniper rifle. There were a lot of them. The bandits had sprawled out in their camp, lounging about and making disgusting jokes amongst themselves whilst jeering at the hostages they had captured from friendship gulag. I knew that I wouldn't be able to get off more than a few rounds before my rifle would no longer be effective at range, and that I would then have to use my revolver, a fine Jakobs that I wouldn't part with for my life. much as I despised the workers at Hyperion, the captured foreman had something I needed. I calculated carefully, aiming at the ugliest looking bandit. A sharp crackle followed, blasting through the air quickly and efficiently, and I watched through my scope in satisfaction as the bandit's head burst like a watermelon, showering brains and gore all over, while the rest of his body dissolved from the acid my rifle's bullet had spewed.
The rest of the bandits flew into a panic, diving behind cover, yelling and screaming at each other while firing disorganized shots in my direction. I emptied one magazine on the poor suckers, and slung the rifle over my shoulder. I slid down the dusty hill that encroached over their camp, where I had been sniping, and came to rest behind a tent, pulling out my revolver in the process. "Now, my dear," I rasped softly to my revolver through the flanging device on my mask,"let's put your beautiful barrel to work."
Whipping around the tent, I fired three swift shots into the nearest bandit, and noted with satisfaction my accuracy. One to the face, one to the neck, and one to the left ear. He dropped like a rock. I heard one bandit shout out "that guy owed me money!", so I rendered him unable to collect with a swift shot to the jugular. Then the largest tent opened, and a lumbering brute staggered out, swinging a saw bladed axe wildly about himself, screaming in a berserking rage.Quickly, I threw out my decoy. The psycho charged at it, hacking and slashing, enraged that he hit nothing but a hologram. Meanwhile, I was invisible. And I charged him. It only took moments-- a few swift steps, a short leap, and I was upon him. Pulling my electrified katana from its scabbard, I plunged it into his heavily tattooed chest, spurting blood out as it happened. And in mid thrust, I became visible. The psycho shrieked with pain and rage, and swung his axe wildly, knocking me to the ground. With a swift roll, I was on my feet, blade ready. This asylum-ready freak was going to go down. He lunged, spitting curses and screaming. All the while, the Hyperion prisoners had been watching in amazement, cheering, but now they were silent with tension. I ducked and rolled beneath his swipe, whipping my sword around and stabbing it through his neck. The blood gushed out in a waterfall of crimson, and his decaptitated spinal cord from the neck up flopped out and plopped on the ground. He sunk to the ground with a moan. I sheathed my sword and turned, ready to scour the prisoners for the foreman. That's when I heard it: "Now, boys! Shoot!" And immediately bandits popped out from cover everywhere. My personal shield absorbed most of the bullets, but I cursed myself for being so unobservant. A large beeping noise indicated that my shield was depleted, and less than an instant afterwards, I felt my body being pierced by many malicious chunks of led, sapping my strength and draining my energy. I sunk to the ground in despair,ready to let the darkness close in. But to my amazement, I saw something that I couldn't believe. A dwarf of a man, not much larger than a midget, dove into the fray yelling and ranting, wielding two heavy machine guns, spraying the bandits with bullets. The bandits cried out in fear, many fleeing while still more fell to this---Gunzerker's--- guns. Then A beautiful woman stepped out from cover, and used some uncanny power akin to the force to throw several of the bandits fifty feet into the air, while they screamed in fear and despair. Then she turned to me. "Hold still," She said simply, and quickly patched up my wounds and gave my shield a quick partial recharge. Then things quieted down, and I staggered to my feet. I looked at them both. "Thanks."  The small dwarf-like man grinned and chuckled. "Call me... Your Salvador," He smirked. The woman gave me a sweet smile. "I'm Maya. Me and Salvador were looking for the vault. Wanna come?"

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place. (Review at the end)
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

I have been playing rust since it started back with the old single map format. Since then the game has changed massively and for the better. Gone are the rad towns with the zombies, to the current and to be released soon XP system.
Basic premise of the game is to survive, not only against the wild, but again other people. To survive you need to kill wildlife, knock down trees and gather resources to build a shelter, a home or a castle if you so wish. Building bigger buildings comes at a cost, you can be raided. Other player can exploit weaknesses in your design and use that to enter your house and take your stuff! The world resources regen fairly slowly, forcing the pvp aspect as time moves on. Although there are many low pop community servers which cater to new players with friendly no KOS rules. Personally i would start there to get the hang of the game before moving on.
This Game is still in alpha, due to a change in engine half way through the original alpha release. Meaning sometime servers have to be wiped to place the new version. this is a good and bad thing, reset for an even playing field, but also a loss of your hard work up to that point.

I wanted to wait 2 years or so until I decided to write a review for this game. I finally feel I have played enough to write a review with the background play time to support it.
As stated, this game is two years old now, and for awhile, they didn't do crap with the game, it seemed that they took the money and ran. For two years, the game was very poorly optimized that you had to AVOID going to the towns, because you couldn't turn without doing two full 360s, and by the time, you're probably bleeding out or dead. Now, as of December of 2015, I can say that they have FINALLY optimized the game, so I can play with higher settings, with very minimal frame droppage. The game is beautiful, I feel I was kinda jipped for the first couple years, but ALPHAAAAA!
If you play this game, you gotta stick through it and be support. With ownership switch, I think they're finally getting things situated to know where the hell they go with the "great idea, horrible action" they were left with.
The Community. Horrible. It was fantastic at the beginning, entertaining even. Now its KOS, doesn't matter if you're a new spawn with nothing but a mining helment on. I wouldn't say it "difficult" to find loot, but it's difficult to gather enough food and water to get to where you need to go to get the good loot, which is perfectly okay, you don't wanna play a game for 30 minutes and be stacked. Then what? And I think that's what happened with the community, for awhile, they didn't have the drop rates stabalized, you could get everything you needed within an hour, and then you're left with nothing to do except kill people because quite frankly, for a zombie game, there are hardly any zombies.
Until you fire your weapon.
My friends and I just recently played, and after a few hours and only us and one other person being in the server, we were in Cherno and decided to shoot the one zombie we saw. All the sudden another one showed up, and another, and about 20 more! We had to run away, and it was fun! I wish there was more of that difficulty rather than just be quiet and there is no issue. They (the devs) need to work on difficulty. If you watched TWD, you'd see that Zombies react to any kinda of noise, I wish they would implement that in DayZ. Hopefully thats in updates to come, I do know they are adding hostile animals (wolves) that will add to the fun!
I do hope they add more cities or military bases, they deleted two and the most major places on the coast side, Balota and the NE Airstrip. Theres maybe one building there, which was really dissapointing for me. Now you HAVE to go up north to get the good supplies, which isn't horrible, but it would still be nice to have more places to go rather than going the same loop. Up through stary, stop here and there to see if a truck spawned, get to NW, head south to the secret base, and you're pretty much done.
All in all, now they are showing that they are working on the game, and they haven't just taken our money and ran, I would suggest this game, its a great time killer. Its more fun to play with friends I think personally, but everyone likes their own thing. I will add, it would be nice to be able to have atleast two players, one for if you wanna play with your friends, and one for if your friends aren't on and you wanna play solo for a bit and not have to worry about finding you way back to your group.
Its still a work in process, so if you're not patient, I would reccommend you just wait for another 4 years for this game to be finished or in Beta.. lol.

This game... This DAMN game... I have so much to tell you, but I'll try (and probably fail) to make it brief.
So, at first there was a kickstarter, but not many people cared about that (even though it raised 10 times its goal of $5,000). Then, many youtubers have played the game near its launch, including the Game Grumps, and that's where my personal experience with the game started. I did hear of the game before, but not too much, definately not enough to know anything that's considered a spoiler. I came to the let's play expecting another indie game that's making jokes and subverting gameplay elements just because, but by the first boss battle I knew this game was something special. One lets play and a pirated playtrough later, I decided I needed to support Toby Fox for all he's done to me. This miight not sound like much, but I normally don't buy games I've already finished, especially ones that beg me not to play it anymore (yep, that actually happens).
Of all the things I wanna say about this game, the thought that I consider this to be the best horror game of 2015, if not of the 2010's so far. "But Paul", you ask,"this game doesn't look scary at all!", but that's the point. One minute you might be convincing a bisexual lizard scientist to make out with a buff fish warrior that tried to kill you, and whose house you burned down while trying to cook... something, while being in a pity date with the aforementioned lizard, and the next you might be reading about the implications of time travel via ressurection and failed experiments on... I think I've said too much already.
Now, among what I HAVE heard about the game prior to watching it was the fact that it messes with the fourth wall in a way only a videogame could, and that's literally my favorite trope in any media ever. From MGS2's "fission mailed" sequence and the entirety of Eternal Darkness: Sanity's Requiem (a horror game dor the Gamecube), to even the simplest ones, like pretending to reset your game in, say, Animal Crossing. And let me tell you, it doesn't do this often, but you will be impressed every time it happens, especially because the game is almost entirely made in GameMaker because, to quote Toby "Radiation" Fox himself, "I don't know how to program lol".
That's not to say this game doesn't have any shortcomings. There's only one or two bosses that doesn't take a fixed amount of turns or attacks, because you just HAD to insert a dialogue into every boss, didn't you, Toby? And also let's not forget the hype backslash, because the game is so hyped for people who haven't played it yet, that they're either going to not play it out of spite, or they're going to be massively dissapointed. See, this game was as good as it was, because it was unexpected, Nobody expected it to be such a success, or that it'd be that good, maybe except for the kickstarter backers, but who cares about them? (Note: I care about them immensly, because the game wouldn't exist without them)
To finish off this surprisingly lenghty review, I just want to say this: If you were't spoiled yet, and you like games like Earthbound, or just feel-y games in general, get this game right now, or at least download the demo. (Note: The demo was made 2 years before launch and while it is very similar to the released game, some functions, like the in-game manual, aren't in the finished product)

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place. (Review at the end)
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

Gearbox has done a rare thing here: made a sequel that is in almost every measure better than the first game.   Weapon system, mission system, co-op system, plot, characters, skills, loot... all of it a marked improvement over the first.  Think of a problem with the first Borderlands; Borderlands 2 probably fixed it.  With all those improvements, the game is VERY fun, both for solo and multiplayer endeavors.
Now the game isn't without its faults.  Finding legendary loot by accident is almost impossible in this game; generally you're only going to get it after several hours of killing the same boss over and over and over.  When you do, some of it is quite a letdown.  There's also issues with storage space, namely why you can carry more in your backpack than in the gigantic steel-door vault back at the main hub.  Beyond that there's minor issues with balance here and there, some class skills, a few other things.
Still, all of the above issues are relatively minor, and even then only come out after you've played the game for about 20+ hours.  At its core, this is an incredibly good, incredibly fun game, wonderful to play with friends as well as with strangers.  If you had even a passing interest in the first game, get the second.  Do it. If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place. (Review at the end)
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

This game... This DAMN game... I have so much to tell you, but I'll try (and probably fail) to make it brief.
So, at first there was a kickstarter, but not many people cared about that (even though it raised 10 times its goal of $5,000). Then, many youtubers have played the game near its launch, including the Game Grumps, and that's where my personal experience with the game started. I did hear of the game before, but not too much, definately not enough to know anything that's considered a spoiler. I came to the let's play expecting another indie game that's making jokes and subverting gameplay elements just because, but by the first boss battle I knew this game was something special. One lets play and a pirated playtrough later, I decided I needed to support Toby Fox for all he's done to me. This miight not sound like much, but I normally don't buy games I've already finished, especially ones that beg me not to play it anymore (yep, that actually happens).
Of all the things I wanna say about this game, the thought that I consider this to be the best horror game of 2015, if not of the 2010's so far. "But Paul", you ask,"this game doesn't look scary at all!", but that's the point. One minute you might be convincing a bisexual lizard scientist to make out with a buff fish warrior that tried to kill you, and whose house you burned down while trying to cook... something, while being in a pity date with the aforementioned lizard, and the next you might be reading about the implications of time travel via ressurection and failed experiments on... I think I've said too much already.
Now, among what I HAVE heard about the game prior to watching it was the fact that it messes with the fourth wall in a way only a videogame could, and that's literally my favorite trope in any media ever. From MGS2's "fission mailed" sequence and the entirety of Eternal Darkness: Sanity's Requiem (a horror game dor the Gamecube), to even the simplest ones, like pretending to reset your game in, say, Animal Crossing. And let me tell you, it doesn't do this often, but you will be impressed every time it happens, especially because the game is almost entirely made in GameMaker because, to quote Toby "Radiation" Fox himself, "I don't know how to program lol".
That's not to say this game doesn't have any shortcomings. There's only one or two bosses that doesn't take a fixed amount of turns or attacks, because you just HAD to insert a dialogue into every boss, didn't you, Toby? And also let's not forget the hype backslash, because the game is so hyped for people who haven't played it yet, that they're either going to not play it out of spite, or they're going to be massively dissapointed. See, this game was as good as it was, because it was unexpected, Nobody expected it to be such a success, or that it'd be that good, maybe except for the kickstarter backers, but who cares about them? (Note: I care about them immensly, because the game wouldn't exist without them)
To finish off this surprisingly lenghty review, I just want to say this: If you were't spoiled yet, and you like games like Earthbound, or just feel-y games in general, get this game right now, or at least download the demo. (Note: The demo was made 2 years before launch and while it is very similar to the released game, some functions, like the in-game manual, aren't in the finished product)
There are endless amount of weaponry available to blow people apart into chunks, I highly recommend this game.

This game is all-around a very solid and enjoyable game. One of the aspects that enjoy hte most is the breaking of the 4th wall (which is one thing I enjoy in games like Metal Gear Solid). The game is, at times, aware that it is a game and even addresses your actions and your motives for the actions that you take, mainly in the Genocide story path. Even if  you decide to go the Pacifist route after a Genocide run, the game is aware of your past actions and will adapt as so in ways you may not see until you think about it.
For the gameplay, it is a refreshing style that is a big nostalgia factor. It is fairly simple but challenging in its own ways. Every battle in the last parts of hte game tests your skills as well as your memory if you have to keep dying. Each boss fight brings a level is awe and fun that makes you want to go through the game over and over to see if you can go through these fights flawlessly.
Overall, the game is a refreshing and fun experience with great music that fits the game's themes and feel very well. It will leave you scratching your head if you dive in with prior knowledge and makes the game just that more enjoyable. If you wish to experience the game in its entirety, I would recommend doing the True Pacifist route first, then slowly make your way down to the Genocide path. If you go in the other direction, in hte words of Sans, "You are going to have a bad time." The game is defintely worth the price tag and will keep you hooked to it for weeks to come.

Don't get biased because of the horrible fanbase like I did at first, this is a great game. Undertale is an RPG based on Earthbound and various other SNES RPGs. As a matter of fact, The creator of this game, Toby Fox made an Earthbound Halloween ROM Hack a few years prior to this game's release. The combat system is fairly unique, instead of it mostly being Text-Based like most RPGs, it has more of a Bullet-Hell theme where you have to dodge attacks with the arrow keys. One of the main gimmicks of the game is that you can either kill or spare enemies. If you kill all the enemies in the game you get the Genocide ending, if you spare every enemy in the game you get the Pacifist ending and if you do a mix you get the Neutral ending. The plot is fairly simple, thousands of years ago a war broke out between Humans and Monsters, Humans won and the Monsters were banished underground. There is alot more to it, but I don't want to spoil the game. Overall, I'd give the game a 9/10.

Gearbox has done a rare thing here: made a sequel that is in almost every measure better than the first game.   Weapon system, mission system, co-op system, plot, characters, skills, loot... all of it a marked improvement over the first.  Think of a problem with the first Borderlands; Borderlands 2 probably fixed it.  With all those improvements, the game is VERY fun, both for solo and multiplayer endeavors.
Now the game isn't without its faults.  Finding legendary loot by accident is almost impossible in this game; generally you're only going to get it after several hours of killing the same boss over and over and over.  When you do, some of it is quite a letdown.  There's also issues with storage space, namely why you can carry more in your backpack than in the gigantic steel-door vault back at the main hub.  Beyond that there's minor issues with balance here and there, some class skills, a few other things.
Still, all of the above issues are relatively minor, and even then only come out after you've played the game for about 20+ hours.  At its core, this is an incredibly good, incredibly fun game, wonderful to play with friends as well as with strangers.  If you had even a passing interest in the first game, get the second.  Do it.
