Rust will never be forgotten, and it will never be at peace. I told myself I would wait to do this review, that I would let it settle, that it would one day be finished and then I could write my thoughts. Well, too much time has passed for me to wait any longer, and for some reason, today seems to be the day.
I'm not even sure now how I discovered this, "new game with a cool idea". A friend, DayZ-exploring, a flashing Steam store page, who knows. But once I installed it, and loaded it up, I had found a new, exciting video game. The music when loading was incredible, eerie and atmospheric; and this was 'alpha' music? Once I loaded into the world, an island of apparently great size, I enjoyed the experience from the start. Nature, trees, vast distances, animals, ruins, and...people.
For that is what makes Rust tick, people. The first moment, not knowing whether to hide, fight, or try to communicate, is telling, and this is a common thread. And with these first moments, come the first deaths, both expected and not. And so comes the first rule of Rust, don't trust anyone. And with this rule comes the choice you have to make, do you strive to live a solo life? Do you have Steam friends that play and can band together? Or do you try to find some team to take you in? Be ready, you are going to die, a lot.
I made a shelter, and built, and harvested, and hunted. I ventured into dangerous places and survived. Or died. In the end, it was a great experience. Then came the version changes, at first it was good, bugs were fixed. Then, they started over from scratch, and things started getting different from what made it good in the first place. It was good, then bad, then good, then bad.
The game today is worse than it was, a new thing we are seeing in games when they are made to be a service. A game with a golden age, something we used to only see in MMOs. That is why I can no longer recommend this game. I am going to give it a thumbs up, because of my experiences, and that it was worth the money I paid, but now is a different time. Rust is over for me.
Graphics:
Apart from certain updates and small periods, Rust has always looked fantastic. As they moved into Beta and the modern Rust era, the game both looks great, and takes a great system to run. It's one of the games that gets my PC as hot as it can get. Beware!
Sound:
Great music and sounds at first, but inconsistent sound production. Seemed like the staff never settled on consistant sounds/music during the process. To me, this shows a lack of focus, which has been clear from every player since the beta started. This developmental blurriness seems to coincide with when Rust had already made huge sales. Pretty much the team had success, and just went in slow-patch mode. It was less about a work of art, a work that could have defined the team of producers and developers for the rest of their lives, and more about making the project akin to updating the software in automatically flushing toilets.
Community:
It's a multiplayer game, and the community can be tight-knit if you're in good, but overall it's as toxic as it gets. The sadness with Rust comes from both the community and the developers. Nobody is happy, ever. This has bred conflict between players I've never witnessed before. In short, Rust has the worst community of players I have ever seen, and the clear lack of maturity in most players is almost depressing.
Overall:
Rust was a pioneer, and flagship in a tattered lot, but what made it great also destroyed it. When new games are made in its shadow, I hope that someone can capture that essence just once again, and hold it tight until a perfect time to share it with the world.

The experience I had with Undertale feels like a whole new era of storytelling, a revolution. The level of storytelling in Undertale is out of this world. I don't think I have had this much emotional investment with a game before, and each individual's experience deserves to take it in their own hands.
As a gamer since the late 90's, growing up with PS1 and PS2, i've played through many, many classic masterpieces from that era, like Metal Gear Solid 1-3, Spyro the Dragon 1-3, Rayman, Oddworld and Resident Evil, just to name a few.
Each of these games have a very iconic feel to them, defining the intense quality and revolution of games for the decade, both graphically, storywise and in gameplay, and Undertale as one of the best of this decade.
When considering to buy this game, let go of prejudice like I did, and become immersed. Undertale is not an experience to miss out on, especially considering its price. You will have a more enjoyable experience out of this game than most Triple A $60 games out there.

The experience I had with Undertale feels like a whole new era of storytelling, a revolution. The level of storytelling in Undertale is out of this world. I don't think I have had this much emotional investment with a game before, and each individual's experience deserves to take it in their own hands.
As a gamer since the late 90's, growing up with PS1 and PS2, i've played through many, many classic masterpieces from that era, like Metal Gear Solid 1-3, Spyro the Dragon 1-3, Rayman, Oddworld and Resident Evil, just to name a few.
Each of these games have a very iconic feel to them, defining the intense quality and revolution of games for the decade, both graphically, storywise and in gameplay, and Undertale as one of the best of this decade.
When considering to buy this game, let go of prejudice like I did, and become immersed. Undertale is not an experience to miss out on, especially considering its price. You will have a more enjoyable experience out of this game than most Triple A $60 games out there.

I bought it to play on single player, so take this review as a point of view from a single-player guy.
I found this game profoundly irritating and boring, mainly because of the enemies constantly respawning. This may sound like a minor problem, but it hurt my experience badly. Sometimes after clearing an area of enemies, you have to fight the exact same enemies on your way back if you take too much time on that particular area. So, the game kind of encourages you to rush the areas, which is a real shame because the world itself is gorgeous. It's a world i wanna explore, but the game won't let me, because i know i must not take too much time on each area.
You might say "oh, why don't you just run ignore and run through them?" Well, ignoring enemies in this game can cause your death. I felt like the enemies were easy to fight when you are trying to kill them, but if you try to run through a group of them without fighting back, you may die. So, one or way or another, i felt like the games was always forcing me to fight the exact same enemies over and over again, which was boring to say the least.
The enemies constantly respawning also means that you will not have moments of rest, not even after defeating bosses, which is profoundly annoying.
The enemies themselves also seem to be designed around co-op, i found a lot of them OP for just 1 player. So, unless you have someone to play with, i don't think you should consider get this. There is a matchmaking system where you can join games of other people online, but my experience with that was stressful. Might been just bad luck, but all my "partners" wanted always all the loot for themselves, even when was me doing the most work on killing the enemies.
If you want a good singleplayer rpg/fps game, allow me to recommend RAGE. I played RAGE after Borderlands 2 and RAGE doesn't have all the problems Borderlands 2 has.

Borderlands 2 is the sequel to the 2009 game Borderlands, it continues the story of another vault opening in pandora and more vault hunters trying to retrieve its goods. You play as either an assassin, a siren, a gunzerker, or a commando. Borderlands 2 has guns, a lot of guns. There are literally (almost) infinite types of different guns; the game uses a complex algorithm to produce thousands of different guns, inserting different prefixes and stats each time. This game is well designed with stunning comic book style graphics. I would definitely recommend this to anyone fond of the action fps sub-genre. 91/100

I wish I got this game sooner! Great gaming value - you definitely get your money's worth!!
If you enjoyed the 1st Borderlands, you'll love it! It is a fantastic upgrade on what was already an enjoyable gaming experience. The weapons are similar but improved in varied and amusing ways, the characters are new as well as old, and enemy AI is quite challenging at times. The driving, however, is the one downside - it's still the same mundane lack-lustre experience. However, this wasn't designed to be a car racer, and it more than makes up for this in spades in all other aspects of the game.
If you have never played Borderlands, you're in for a well polished and thoroughly enjoyable gaming experience.
Great graphics, very comical characters and voice acting, awesome boss battles remniscent of old school shoot em ups, and then there's the LOOT!!!! Wow, I never thought I could be so addicted in striving for loot, but 2K/Gearbox Software have done very well to get the loot rewards/discovery items and their occurences (or rarity) JUST RIGHT. You'll never discover the same item twice!
Enjoyable storyline and side missions kept me entertained for hours (almost 30 hours and only about halfway in to the main game!) - and that's just the vanilla game!!!
This is a fantastic gaming experience, and I am surprised this has not rated higher on Metascore.
Even if you only purchase the Bordelands 2 game only, prepare yourself for hours of entertainment.
I would recommend the GOTY edition, simply because it's just great bang-for-buck. The DLC's included are pretty much separate games in themselves (requires the base Borderlands 2 game to play it), and I suspect they will provide 10's, if not hundreds, of hours of great quality gameplay that will keep you searching for the ultimate weapon/loot.
Even for a game that's over a year old, it looks fantastic, the gameplay is enjoyable, the loot is as rewarding as ever, and the game never gets boring (especially co-op with other players).
9.5/10

This game is going nowhere, and very slowly. I wouldn't recommend for anyone to buy this game, unless you are ABSOLUTELY deadset on staying with the developers every few months, as they add worthless garbage into the game instead of fixing the fundamental aspects of it that would allow for an enjoyable experience. I wont be picking this game back up until (if they do) manage to fix its current outstanding flaws, and I suggest you spare yourself the pain of being subjected to the same torturous hours of running across the "wasteland" of Chernaurus, and spend your money on something more enjoyable.

I have been a fan ever since the mod. I just loved the concept of you being thrown in the middle of this post-apocalyptic world. Your survival depending solely on the decision you are going to make. It was something that was never done before and people were super stoked about it! When they announced they'd be making it into a standalone game with the developers of ArmA 2 actually working with the mod creators I was first in line. Got the alpha on release day.. and yeah it was pretty bad, bugged, glitched and all that.. but I was still having fun with the game and even concinced a friend to buy it saying "it's gonna be awesome dude, they'll be adding all this cool stuff.. it'll be ground breaking!"
Yeah.. I regret that now. This game was released in December 2013.. today, it is December 2015 - 2 years later. And the game is STILL completely broken. They've added very little to none of the things they were promising, only raising the price without actually offering you your money's worth. All you get is one disappointment after the other.. and that's coming from somebody who was defending the game from people saying all this stuff.
Overall - don't buy this game! It could've been a complete game changer. Yet, what this game became is the number one example of why steam early access simply doesn't work! You give all your money to the developers - and in return you get a broken, sorry excuse for a game with 3 new hats added every month.
If you're as stoked about this genre as I was 2 years ago - don't buy this game! And especially don't buy any of the steam rip-offs that tried to build on the game's success. They're all the same.
My recommendation is go play the ArmA 2 mod.. after all this time it's still the most enjoyable of them all. And that's really saying something.

Undertale is a roleplaying game developed by Toby Fox, releasing on Steam in September 2015.
You play Undertale from a top down perspective, as you control a child. You navigate through “Underground”. Scattered around the Underground, you will encounter plenty of different enemies. The “combat” system in Undertale is where this game will differ from other RPG games of this type. First of all, the regular attacking in combat is done via a QTE sort of mechanic as you have to hit the action button in the right spot to do more damage. This adds a skill level to the combat rather than just relying on stats and equipment. Secondly, the other options when in a fight are much more diverse, such as sparing an enemy, which means letting them live, or you can simply talk to the enemy, whether it be flirting with them, joking, or complimenting them. Each way of interacting with the enemy will result in a different outcome at the end of the fight.  When the enemy attacks you though, you have to again take part in a small mini game, which usually requires you to dodge out of the way of certain objects which are flying at your LV (your love…the game will explain at the beginning). I am not normally a fan of QTEs but Undertale does a good job of masking the mechanic by portraying it in an original way.
Visually, this game is by no means a good looking game. It’s the basic of basics of 8 bit graphics. If you grew up playing games with these sorts of graphics, I can probably see you getting a huge nostalgia hit, but if you missed that era, and then you will probably not fully enjoy the art style. Personally I didn’t like it at all. It is way too basic and minimalistic for me. I need something more pleasing to look at. The sound track of this game is brilliant though, composed by the developer himself, there is some absolutely awesome tracks to be heard throughout the game. If you are the sort of person that really appreciates video game music, I would recommend you pick up the Soundtrack for sure!
Where most people will say Undertale succeeds brilliantly, is the story. I am not going to go into any spoilers at all as I know it is a touchy subject, but you meet some very original characters, some quirky and hilarious as you progress through the game.  The way your story pans out will be determined by your actions throughout the game.  Undertale has three different endings. It’s nice to see a game where your choices really do have a lot of weight behind them, as we have come all too familiar with games giving us the illusion that our choices matter, when in fact we just end up in the same place at the end anyway.
I wouldn’t say Undertale is a hugely difficult game. The puzzles are easy enough once you take a step back and think it through clearly. If you are fighting enemies, the combat is fairly easy too; you just have to be good at QTEs to be able to progress without any real problems.  Completing one of the endings took me just over three hours. I am not sure whether I feel like I want to go into Undertale again to see the other endings, because the game is fairly slow paced and I am really not a fan of the art style and graphics. I think I would be more tempted to way a play through on YouTube of the other endings as I would only be doing it for the story element. Obviously if you are a fan of the gameplay you can probably get about ten hours of content from Undertale.
Sadly, as surprisingly as it sounds, I had technical problems with Undertale – and I wasn’t the only one. The game simply wouldn’t launch. This was fixed using the following Steam community post -
The game can be played using either keyboard or controller. I would personally favour the controller though, given the QTEs and simple controls other than those.
To sum up, I’m not going to say Undertale is a must play game like most people. Yes I can see why people see it as being earth shatteringly good, but I really don’t see what all the fuss is about. The game play is slow paced and bland and graphically it is just awful.  What you are getting with Undertale is a fantastic sound track, and hugely original plot. I can quite happily say I could have got the same experience out of Undertale from just watching a play through online. Credit where credit is due though, the story is really good and it is probably Undertale’s biggest selling point. The game has a good price point at £6,99 so even if you are on the fence, it’s not like you are going to break the bank with trying it out.

It always refreshing to see a game that allow you take a pacifist route over a typical "beat everything you see" route. But Undertale, its almost heartbreaking to do anything but a pacifist route.
Story:
Monster and humans once lived together on the surface, but a war broke out between the two and the monster lost. They were sealed underground and barrier was raised to keep them there. One day a child fall down into the underground world of the monsters. Now you must guide him out and back to the surface.
The story is pretty straight forward at first glance, but it soon made apparent that nothing in this game will be as straight forward as other RPGs. You'll be met with many jokes, unique characters, and quite a few jokes and comments that breaks the 4th wall. The monsters are so colorful, funny, and charming in their own way. The characters you encounter (and possibly befriend) makes this game great for me and really immerse me in the atmosphere of this world. Their antics and crazy personality just fit so well with this game.
Gameplay:
The game consist of going to various areas to solve puzzles. Sometime as you're walking you may encounter a monster. The game is a turnbase RPG. When you encounter a monster, you are given 4 options:
-Fight: You attack the monster. The amount of damage you do is dependent on your weapon and if you can land the cursor on a good spot in the attack minigame (just a cursor going from 1 side to the other and you can stop it)
-Act: This will give you various option depending on the enemy. All these options are none lethal and pretty ridiculous, ranging from petting to telling jokes. Generally choosing the right Acts will lead to a peaceful ending with the encounter
-Item: Use some type of item doing a fight, generally an healing item
-Mercy: Here you're given 2 options. Spare or Flee. Flee end the encounter with you fleeing. Spare will generally do nothing unless you've either weaken the enemy in fighting or did the right Acts. If you met those conditions then the enemy name will be yellow mean that Spare will end the fight, and letting the monster live.
You'll also meet various NPCs where you can buy items and others that you can befriend. Now whether you kill everything you encounter or peacefully end all encounter depends on you, but whichever you do will affect not only the ending, but also how other characters will react to you. So choose wisely...
Soundtrack:
Very catchy and fun tracks in them. It really set the mood of each areas you'll go to and really fit perfectly with each character you encounter.
Final Comments:
This is truly a fun game that I will easily remember. It when a game have a cast of characters that all have such vibrant personalities to go with their interesting designs that really make you remember those characters and as such this game. The areas themselves, while some are memorable others are forgettable, but these are few. This is a great RPG that you will spend much time on, if for any other reason to see some of the endings, especially if you went with anything but the true pacifist ending. Personally I love this game and haven't had this much fun with a game cast in a while. This game goes about $9.99 at the time of this review and honestly I think it worth every penny.  I hope to see you all in the Underground soon. Also watch out for talking flowers.

There is an irony to success in Rust: the better you are at surviving, the less that will actually happen. Just before writing this, I spent a couple hours upgrading my building, building new weapons and ammunition, and collecting extra supplies to keep behind a new electronic lock. I have windows that afford me a view in every direction, and a kind of parapet on the third floor from which I can shoot down at anyone who starts trying to batter down my walls. I spend most of my time hiding from other players now, or hiding from the helicopter, or watching out for bears and wolves. When I think about a typical session of Rust, it’s a catalog of things that didn’t happen, of risks successfully avoided and bets wisely hedged. The brilliance of Rust is that it demands a lot of suspenseful work, attention, and planning to make sure that it remains uneventful.

I don't like Undertale, and I would not recommend it.  And it's not because it's so popular with everyone, or even that there seems to be an excess to idiotic people trying to gain "Internet popularity" by referencing it or making fake guides for it.  It bores me, and I have no interest in the characters.
My first playing, I didn't make it to that goat-woman's house.  I just didn't have interest in playing.  Days later, I thought it deserved a more fair chance, so I reset and tried again.  It was a bit fun to fight the flower and dodge his "love bullets" and hear his comments.  By this time, I'd watched a few Internet videos (none of which wanted to give away the "truth" behind the story.) and the word "pacifist run" kept coming up.  Most of the people who said I have to play this game were in love with the idea of a game where "you don't have to kill anything."  I attempted this, but quickly grew bored with the tedium of fights, trying to figure out the "personalities" of the monsters.  I went traditional RPG on them.
I liked how goat-mama remembered a decision I made from the previous game.  It's nice to have a game that remembers what you did on former playthroughs.  But at her house.  Ugh!  I wanted to explore.  I wanted to find out the actual story behind everything.  Why do people like this game so much?  She wanted to keep me prisoner.  So, by HER choice to block my path instead of letting me leave when I tried, literally 30 times, I killed her.  Lemonhead was free, and I wasn't bothered by killing her off.  I kept killing monsters.
After this, Sans was a little entertaining.  He and Papyrus broke the tedium with a little humor.  But still, I found myself not caring.  Over five and a half hours of gameplay without trying to "power-level," and I still didn't care.  The game was ungripping.
Also, I am not a keyboard gamer.  Pressing Z on a keyboard is not as fast for me as mashing A on a controller.  And I have to keep my hands up in front of me all the time on a keyboard.  Using an XBox360 controller, control did not work well.  Slightly moving one direction would often make me move continually, definitely not helping with puzzles.
So, while there will be some who say I "have to finish the game to appreciate it" I say this:  I spent over 5 times more time on this game than I give an anime series to impress me.  I could have formed opinions on up to 3 movies in this time period.  If I played FFVII with Aeris on my team for over 20 hours, and still didn't care when she died, how will I start caring for this game by playing another 15 hours?  The 5 already feel wasted.
I will not argue whether or not this is a GOOD game, or deserving of its massive popularity.  I simply would not tell anyone else they "have to" play it.  At the same time, I would not prevent anyone from choosing to play Undertale.  It apparantly takes a certain type of person to enjoy it.

Hell, they removed the damn zombies eight months ago and they haven't put them back in because they'd rather patch in helmet skins than focus on fixing the damn AI pathing.
If the absence of ZOMBIES in a ZOMBIE game weren't bad enough, the graphical optimization is just god awful. If I want to get anywhere, I look at the sky, because when I look anywhere near the horizon, frame rate barely breaks twenty in a game that really isn't demanding for my mid-line PC.
Save yourself $35.00 and don't support this broken game any more than it already has been. Better yet, go spend it at a museum or on a date or something. At least then you'll get something for your money.

I just thought I should come and write a review, after seeing that some of the negative reviews are misleading.

Going into it I had prepared myself to the thought of being owned, that I would be killed on sight and stand a good chance to be raided and thus I have had a magnificent experience.

It is hilarious playing this game as you run into such funny situations here is a small list of somethings that I have come across in my short time -

- a group of naked men blasting reggae music through the mic and spreading positive vibes.
- a group of guys travelling around looking for other people to have rap battles with and also giving you all their valuable items.
- good members of the community teaching me how to build, and giving me tips after breaking into my house, leaving as friends.

it's survival of the fittest and if you want a post apocalyptic survival game you can't be surprised that it sometimes resorts to killing on sight and that you can't trust anybody.
I have been raided, killed and I have lost everything, its heart breaking and very terrifying. but not as much as it is a learning experience.
I can't wait to sink more hours into this.

You won't regret buying this game, I say get it.

2 years ago i heard about a game which sounded almost 100% like what I'd been looking for, based on character interaction, with survival the only goal, a true sandbox with it's story content made by the players themselves.
Dayz SA appeared to be this game, so i bought it, at release it was pretty terrible, something stupid like 4 guns in game, basically no content, but this was ok, it was alpha and a year or two down the line it would be taking shape.
The game sold over 2 million copies, and the devs got rich, awesome, they can speed up the development with all this dollah and still be loaded! This did not happen.
2 Years down the line and the game has barely been developed. Lets look at the things which this game potentially requires to make it interesting.
Character interaction - Right now, with no real threat from zombies, starvation or the elements, there is no reason to seek help from your fellow man, and as such, most people shoot each other without uttering a word. Without a pre determined group to play with, you will find little interaction, and when you do, you will quickly realise you are doing nothing other than what you would do alone.... loot for hours on end, to potentially lose it all to a 500km sniper shot you don't even hear/falling from a 3m drop.
Base building - this endgame content could realistically require people to form groups and interact to complete tasks too daunting to face on their own, possibly a future savior of the game... But 2 years and $100m down the line and we have basically none of this. Right now you can lock a door in a house (which can be opened by hitting it with an axe ONCE), or hide items in unlockable barrels/tents which are regularly wiped by the servers/updates.
Vehicles - a smaller version of basebuilding, getting a vehicle working could be a reason to group together for a cause, the only problem is, right now a vehicle takes on average longer to repair than to run across the entire map, then when repaired are probably the worse iteration of vehicles i have ever seen in a game. Though they are right now possibly the only reason to band together with fellow survivors.
Survival - Perhaps the challenge of survival against the elements/zombies could be a draw to the game? No.
zombies finally made their re-appearance to experimental build after the massive drop in player numbers without them, and are a minor threat, but are so sparse and easy to outrun, they are nothing more than a hinderance. Food/the elements are a joke, you can find enough food and drink in any town to survive for an untold ammount of time even on a full pop server, the elements take the form of the heat and the cold. both implemented in the most irritating way possible, you often have to stop running for 10 mins to sit in a pool of water naked to cool yourself down because you got hot from running too much, cold is the reverse, you didnt run enough, now sit next to a fire you spent 5 mins crafting, great fun...
Gunplay - Ok so perhaps this will be a great shooter game? It COULD be, it's more tactical then most other stuff on the market, and your aim matters less than your intelligence and positioning, it's the thinking mans shooter. However, to really compete you are going to need to spend 3/4 hours getting a military grade weapon, and probably only have a firefight every hour or two. It just takes too long for a quick pvp fix
There is much much more but tbh I am getting irrate writing this review as it reminds me of the massive dissapointment this game has been so far. I personally believe the Devs have given up, they're about a year behind their last "roadmap", and were suppossed to be releasing a beta by jan, if the game went to beta in this state it would be a travesty, but then again, taking this long with the budget they had is also a travesty. I think they will probably get it to the bare minimum of playability and hand it to the community to finish, which is pathetic, but probably the games only hope.
One day this game could be amazing, but it will not be in the hands of the devs

Almost... 3 years since early access release, a big staff of developers, and the optimization is still TERRIBLE.
By checking the recommended system requirements, you'd think that you wouldn't experience low fps at all. I don't really care about the servers swallowing weapons or items that you drop on the ground, what I care about is if the game is playable at all. But the optimization just makes me sad.
To be honest, I don't know if this game will ever be optimized at all. I feel like there is something seriously wrong with the engine they are using. IMO they should seriously develop or just use a different engine, I don't care if they even go for a more cartoonish/animated style, as long as the game is optimized.

It's terrible to look around and aim in this game, no matter how good PC you have, you will miss how good it feels to turn around and aim in a different FPS game.

Undertale is one of those games where you only can find one or twice per generation. Many of yours might say that it's thanks to the old-shcool style in the visual and gameplay. I tell you they are sadly mistaken.
Undertale is a game with a simple promise: you, as the protagonist, finds himself caught in the Underground, where the monsters live after being banned by humans. At first you might think that simply just go through dungeons, face hordes of monsters and solve puzzles to complete your journey.
But then you discover what is Undertale indeed.
The way in which the game features the characters, the plot and even the monsters you should defeat you create an emotional bond as rarely seen. Combine this with the constant breaking of the fourth wall and you inevitably will treat the game as if it were a separate dimension, where the power to save or eradicate all (and taking the consequences of it being thrown in your face at all times) is in your hands. In short, Undertale is a game that captivates you deeply.
If you had been wanting to give a chance to him, give! You will not regret.
If you are just curious and looking a good story, be sure to check. It's a short game, but it really worth the time played.
But if you are one of those who intend to neglect the game only because of fandom's fame, I can only regret, for you lose the opportunity to experience good things because of a pathetic prejudice. But really I can't expect much from someone who lives attached to such a thought, and still thinks that you're a example of decency, isn't it?

It always refreshing to see a game that allow you take a pacifist route over a typical "beat everything you see" route. But Undertale, its almost heartbreaking to do anything but a pacifist route.
Story:
Monster and humans once lived together on the surface, but a war broke out between the two and the monster lost. They were sealed underground and barrier was raised to keep them there. One day a child fall down into the underground world of the monsters. Now you must guide him out and back to the surface.
The story is pretty straight forward at first glance, but it soon made apparent that nothing in this game will be as straight forward as other RPGs. You'll be met with many jokes, unique characters, and quite a few jokes and comments that breaks the 4th wall. The monsters are so colorful, funny, and charming in their own way. The characters you encounter (and possibly befriend) makes this game great for me and really immerse me in the atmosphere of this world. Their antics and crazy personality just fit so well with this game.
Gameplay:
The game consist of going to various areas to solve puzzles. Sometime as you're walking you may encounter a monster. The game is a turnbase RPG. When you encounter a monster, you are given 4 options:
-Fight: You attack the monster. The amount of damage you do is dependent on your weapon and if you can land the cursor on a good spot in the attack minigame (just a cursor going from 1 side to the other and you can stop it)
-Act: This will give you various option depending on the enemy. All these options are none lethal and pretty ridiculous, ranging from petting to telling jokes. Generally choosing the right Acts will lead to a peaceful ending with the encounter
-Item: Use some type of item doing a fight, generally an healing item
-Mercy: Here you're given 2 options. Spare or Flee. Flee end the encounter with you fleeing. Spare will generally do nothing unless you've either weaken the enemy in fighting or did the right Acts. If you met those conditions then the enemy name will be yellow mean that Spare will end the fight, and letting the monster live.
You'll also meet various NPCs where you can buy items and others that you can befriend. Now whether you kill everything you encounter or peacefully end all encounter depends on you, but whichever you do will affect not only the ending, but also how other characters will react to you. So choose wisely...
Soundtrack:
Very catchy and fun tracks in them. It really set the mood of each areas you'll go to and really fit perfectly with each character you encounter.
Final Comments:
This is truly a fun game that I will easily remember. It when a game have a cast of characters that all have such vibrant personalities to go with their interesting designs that really make you remember those characters and as such this game. The areas themselves, while some are memorable others are forgettable, but these are few. This is a great RPG that you will spend much time on, if for any other reason to see some of the endings, especially if you went with anything but the true pacifist ending. Personally I love this game and haven't had this much fun with a game cast in a while. This game goes about $9.99 at the time of this review and honestly I think it worth every penny.  I hope to see you all in the Underground soon. Also watch out for talking flowers.

Undertale is a game that has filled me with tons of satisfaction ;)
Feel free to take this one for a spin or two for its great music, story, and gameplay.

Honest in a way that this sort of game hasn't been in the past. There is alot at play in Undertale, but it's ability to genuinely capture your affection, to subvert your expectations and engender hysterical laughter or absurd dissapointment in equal measure is a rare treat.
Punches above it's weight class in terms of what it can do with such an otherwise seemingly limited framework Undertale is worth every moment. And if you have truly managed to avoid the info out there and can start a brand new blind playthrough I urge you to do it.

Has truly been an experience I am so thankful to of had. It is simply a breath of fresh air in what feels very stale regarding AAA titles. Although it may not be for everybody, if you have the desire and "determination" to play till the end I believe the journey will be well worth the ride.
Case short, this is a masterpeice of witty, and emotional story telling, combined with "out of the box" game mechanics that I will look forward to playing again many year later down the road; hopefully along with my children when the time is right.

I bought this months ago knowing that this was an early Alpha game but still wanted to try it out as I like an Open-World Zonbie game, oh how I was fooled.
Graphics - Not bad but the performance issues are crippling PC's begging to run it at full settings, I have a GTX 970 and an AMD FX-8350 and can't maintain a decent fps even on medium settings.
Performance - I covered a bit about this previosuly but yes the performance is still just terrible, Don't feel bad if you have a half-decent rig like myself and can't run it well.
Gameplay - Awful, very stuttery gameplay leads to a poor gameplay experience. 1st person mode is ok but the akward gameplay hampers thr real fun such as trying to pick up any object you sometimes glide over it.
Combat - This isn't suppossed to be funny but the combat is a joke. When you start your game from the beginning you're basically like a newborn baby, not a single thing to protect you from the harsh world, that's not a problem but when the first town you come across is riddled with Z's then you don't really have much of a choice other than skip it ( I tried hand to hand and it's pathectic, it's basically like a boxing match on a PS1 game). The combat is poor, you can't block attacks and it's pretty much you attack Z first then they attack you over and over untill either one of you falls.
Zombies - Poor enemies, they will run after you if they spot you until you lose them, this makes it almost impossible at the start as you begin already hungry and on the edge of thrist so even if you manage to outrun them you'll be basically dead in a short while without a pit stop. Also the enemy animations are so poor it makes me cringe that this game is sitting at £22.99.
World - The best thing about this game and the only best thing. The world itself if actually decent and is HUGE. There are many cities, towns and villages to come across.
Difficulty - This game can be quite difficult if you don't know what you are doing, it took me a good few hours to cath the basics since this game doesn't have any tutorials which is a bad thing imo as there is so much features in this game. When you start you start with nothing, only your clothes and hunger. Any nearby villages have nothing so don't bother investigating ( I spent multiple respwans checking these out and you don't get anything worthwhile). This game has a very steep learning curve and can be very frustrating for new players so my advice would be if you're serious about picking this look online for a beginners guide, you'll need it.
Overall - I've spent a good few hours tinkering about and honestly I can't recommend this game just yet, it just isn't finished yet to meet the quality that we deserve, it is playable right now but hold off until some further updates.

I'm less than 10 hours in and totally impressed by this game. It's akin to Bioshock and Fallout but it all feels more smooth and less tedious to play. The combat system is simplier and more streamlined than FallOut, you spend less time opening containers and searching deadbodies leaving more time to kill and blow stuff up. It manages to truncate all the best elements of the most popular FPS elements into one game. Most importantly sorting through the best weapons/equipment is almost effortless. One of the most important parts of any FPS games is getting the right character build to suit your style of play, it never feels like a chore, and the developers don't punish you for making mistakes as much as some other games, for example, if you sell one of your favourite weapons to a trader by accident, you can buy it back straight away at the same price (a nice touch) Although I like Bioshock FallOut I feel Borderlands 2 so far to be just that little bit better, and I haven't even touched on multiplayer yet!

I HAVE 20 HOURS ON RECORD. I KNOW WHAT I'M TALKING ABOUT. So I had originally written a review for this game awhile back, but I hand't done a pascifist (Isn't that something babies put in their mouths? No, you're thinking of a pedophile!) so I felt like I needed to revamp and rewrite this bad boy.
GAMEPLAY:
This, is what I really liked about Undertale, but also is one of the things that frustrates me the most. So the gist of it is that when enemies attack you, you take control of a little heart and dodge their attacks, their attacks take the form of numerous shapes and sizes. This introduces a new layer of skill that most JRPGs don't have, and I love it. Unfortuneately, this is about all I liked about combat. The gimmick (Gimik? Gimick? Gimmic?) of the game is that you don't have to kill anything. That's right kiddos, you don't have to 'kill' an in game entity. You're really not supposed to kill anyone, because the way the game is written makes it so you only get the 'good' ending if you don't kill anyone. Unfortuneately, not killing anyone punishes you a lot. You get no XP for this, therefore no health upgrades. But that's fine, because if you're halfway decent at the game, you'll be able to dodge most attacks. But when there's maybe 3 different monsters per 'zone' it just get repettitive. I'm not smiling and chuckling to myself after the 7nth time Aaron flexes himself off the screen (Don't ask. Just no.), even tho the first time he did it I thought it was funny. At this poin't your probably saying "Than why not just go full combat mode if all you care about is mechanics?" because there are... I think 3 weapons in the whole game. That's all I found at least, there may be more. Each weapon has a different way of attacking, which all basically comes down to pressing a button at the right time. So in the end, the gameplay innovates but doesn't give enough variation to make sure those inovations feel fresh. Although I will say that fighting bosses never got old, they always mixed it up and they were always pretty fun to fight.
STORY:
I feel like I shouldn't put anything here because I probably would have enjoyed the game more had I gone in completely blind. But I think I need to say something about it because story is also the reason I wouldn't reccomend this game. To all the people who liked the game and are still reading this review for whatever reason, THE STORY IS NOT BAD. In fact the story is very above par. But that's clearly not a negative, and this is a negative review so of course I have a qualm with it. So here's the rundown: The entire story hinges on weather or not you like the characters. If you don't like the characters, you just won't like this game. There's a part in the pascifist ending (Spoiler free here bud) where all my "Friends" are in danger. Except I didn't actually care because I only liked one of them. The game forced me to do things with them to get it's stupid ending. While yes, I did feel more attatched to some of them, for the most part I hated all their stupid faces. If you don't like the characters, pascifist ending will not be worth it for you at all. In fact, I much enjoyed the nueteral ending to pascifist.
And yes, I realize to some extent every game relies on you liking it's characters, I get that. But not every game is devoid of enjoyment if you don't like the characters to the extent Undertale was. And yes, I realize the fandom idolizes EVERY SINGLE CHARACTER. This doesn't make them good, this just means a bunch of children have bad tastes. The characters are shallow, with maybe on defining personality feature, overexagerated, and quite frankly feel like Toby Fox wanted to have quirky characters for the sake of having quirky characters, but overlooked the fact that he was bad at quirky writing. Oh yeah, and about the fandom: Just don't listen to them on anything story in this game. The majority of them haven't played Nintendo games and aren't even old enough to catch most of the reffrences or see what this game is trying to do. "You're litterally 10, you aren't even old enough to have Earthbound nostalgia."
NOTE: I'm doing genocide now, and I'm actually having a lot more (Although repettitive) fun utilizing the raw mechanical abillities of the game. Some people will tell you genocide defeats the  point of the game, or that you haven't finished the game if you haven't done pascifist. They're wrong. The point of the game and it's story is that your choices impact stuff for a different ending, with every end boss running commentary on your actions throughout the game. Not to "not kill people" although I must say, the game feels really preachy about how the genocide path is the 'Bad Guy Path' I mean jayz, let me formulate my own opinions on what I'm doing, don't try and cram Pascifist down my throat.
GRAPHICS:
There's not much to say here. I was neither impressed nor dissapointed. What you see in the screenshots is what you get the whole game. Although I will say that the end boss fights graphics were friggin amazing. I feel like I'm reving the end fight up too much if not spoiling it, but I cannot stop praising it.
SOUND:
The soundtrack is a mixed bag for me. Some songs I was sitting there in my chair thinking "Holy ♥♥♥♥, this is amazing!" other songs I had heard so many times that they basically put me in a trance. Basically, if you're not in a boss fight, the music gets really old really fast. And if you're wondering about the sound effects, they aren't anything special at all. Not that sound effects would be a selling point for a game.
Alright so now we're at the end of this review. I'm still kinda trying to find what works for me in my serious, non-meme reviews so I changed up the format a little bit for this one, I'm also changing the grading system. Not that anyone cares, since I don't write a lot of serious reviews... Anyways, on to the Pros, Cons and Notes.
PROS:
-A good, solid, well done soundtrack.
-Inovates in all the right ways.
-I got a good chuckle out of several of the jokes.
-Above par story.
-The end boss fight.
-No seriously, that fight makes me almost want to reccomend the game.
-It's that good.
-Okay I'm done.
CONS:
-Some of the soundtrack is dull and repetitive.
-Alot of the game can get dull and repetitive.
-The entire game hinges on you likeing the characters, if you don't like them there's nothing for you in this game.
-The graphics are neither good nor bad, they are 'meh', and this is a con for me.
-The game feels like it's dragging on a lot of times.
-Combat is never fleshed out, and when you spare someone you get the same dialogue every time.
-You have to slog through nine hours to get to the final boss.
NOTES:
-I didn't dislike the game, but I didn't like it.
-I actually did like some of the characters, but I don't seem to like them as much as the majority of the fandom.
-The steam forums will give you aids.
-Everyone keeps telling me Im wrong when I say this game was made by one guy "It was made by a team" Well you know what? The game feels like it was made by one guy.
-You could do a lot worse for 10.00$
[C] - In the end, I think this game is a bit overhyped. It's not a bad game by any means, but it just doesn't have that extra umph needed to make it a good game. It's just a 'meh' game to me.

I'm less than 10 hours in and totally impressed by this game. It's akin to Bioshock and Fallout but it all feels more smooth and less tedious to play. The combat system is simplier and more streamlined than FallOut, you spend less time opening containers and searching deadbodies leaving more time to kill and blow stuff up. It manages to truncate all the best elements of the most popular FPS elements into one game. Most importantly sorting through the best weapons/equipment is almost effortless. One of the most important parts of any FPS games is getting the right character build to suit your style of play, it never feels like a chore, and the developers don't punish you for making mistakes as much as some other games, for example, if you sell one of your favourite weapons to a trader by accident, you can buy it back straight away at the same price (a nice touch) Although I like Bioshock FallOut I feel Borderlands 2 so far to be just that little bit better, and I haven't even touched on multiplayer yet!

This game. There are no words for it.
So let me make some.
This is one of the few games I've played where choice actually mattered to the endgame. Most games will toss out previous events in favor of a few final options that ignore everything you've done. You don't get that here. Your choice starts within the first few rooms and that first choice is the start of the impact to the ending, and it's somewhat hinted that these choices will impact everything overall.
Not to mention the way the game reacts if you do different things, even from your first battle. From making a flower angry that you knew what was up, to a dummy that flies away if you don't take either of the normal methods out.
The cast was very colorful, every NPC was unique in their own right, even the minor ones that you might've skipped over in other RPGs, as well as the enemies themselves! This is also the only game ever that will ever be able to get away with using the comic sans font, because it did actually add to the character that uses it.
I have played through this game several times (at present, 77.4 hours on record) and I'm still finding new things. The game is actually not that long either (6-8 hours for first-timers, I think?), yet it still can surprise me!
I highly recommend this game to anyone that loves story-based games, anyone that loves games that change depending on how you play them, and anyone willing to find out mysteries in a game (several mysteries are still out there, and the game is at least a half year old!).
My biggest suggestion? Buy the game and soundtrack together. The soundtrack is amazing. Take a look at the track list, and go to Youtube and take a listen to a few songs, like "Bonetrousle," "Undyne," and "Spider Dance." I won't spoil everyone's favorite song. ;) But if you're someone that likes to listen to music when doing stuff, a lot of this music will give you that little extra to keep you going. And while I recommended listening to the songs on Youtube, it's better to support the creator by actually buying it if you like it.
I can't foresee any games coming out anytime soon with as much awesomeness as Undertale. Why are you still reading this? Go buy this and the soundtrack bundle now!

This game. There are no words for it.
So let me make some.
This is one of the few games I've played where choice actually mattered to the endgame. Most games will toss out previous events in favor of a few final options that ignore everything you've done. You don't get that here. Your choice starts within the first few rooms and that first choice is the start of the impact to the ending, and it's somewhat hinted that these choices will impact everything overall.
Not to mention the way the game reacts if you do different things, even from your first battle. From making a flower angry that you knew what was up, to a dummy that flies away if you don't take either of the normal methods out.
The cast was very colorful, every NPC was unique in their own right, even the minor ones that you might've skipped over in other RPGs, as well as the enemies themselves! This is also the only game ever that will ever be able to get away with using the comic sans font, because it did actually add to the character that uses it.
I have played through this game several times (at present, 77.4 hours on record) and I'm still finding new things. The game is actually not that long either (6-8 hours for first-timers, I think?), yet it still can surprise me!
I highly recommend this game to anyone that loves story-based games, anyone that loves games that change depending on how you play them, and anyone willing to find out mysteries in a game (several mysteries are still out there, and the game is at least a half year old!).
My biggest suggestion? Buy the game and soundtrack together. The soundtrack is amazing. Take a look at the track list, and go to Youtube and take a listen to a few songs, like "Bonetrousle," "Undyne," and "Spider Dance." I won't spoil everyone's favorite song. ;) But if you're someone that likes to listen to music when doing stuff, a lot of this music will give you that little extra to keep you going. And while I recommended listening to the songs on Youtube, it's better to support the creator by actually buying it if you like it.
I can't foresee any games coming out anytime soon with as much awesomeness as Undertale. Why are you still reading this? Go buy this and the soundtrack bundle now!
